4. Stop when your body is almost parallel to the floor.
5. Pull back to the start by bending your knees and using the cable for help.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and torso in a straight line throughout.
2. Lower slowly and resist the descent with your hamstrings.
3. Use only enough cable assistance to control the movement.
4. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit at the pulldown machine with your thighs secured under the pads.
2. Grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip and arms fully extended overhead.
3. Lean back slightly and keep your chest up.
4. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
5. Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull with your back, not just your arms.
2. Avoid swinging your torso to move the weight.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades down as you pull.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench set between two low cable pulleys.
2. Grasp a handle in each hand with arms bent at your chest sides.
3. Press the handles up and together in an arc over your chest.
4. Extend your arms until the handles meet above you.
5. Lower the handles back down to the sides of your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat on the bench.
2. Squeeze your chest as the handles come together.
3. Control the lowering phase, do not let the cables yank your arms.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand side-on to the machine and grasp the handle with the far hand so the cable crosses in front of your body.
2. Bend at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your knees slightly bent and your back flat.
3. Let the working arm hang straight down toward the cable.
4. Raise the handle out to the side until your hand reaches shoulder level, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
5. Lower the handle slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and under control through the full range.
2. Lead with the elbow and turn the pinky up at the top to bias the rear delt.
3. Keep the torso still and avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Brace your core to keep the bent-over position stable.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Face the machine and grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend at the hips until your torso is near 90 degrees, knees slightly bent and back flat.
3. Let your arms extend with the cable holding the bar.
4. Pull the bar to your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and down.
5. Extend the arms slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout.
2. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Avoid jerking the weight with the lower back.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Face the machine and grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend at the hips until your torso is near 90 degrees, knees slightly bent and back flat.
3. Let your arms extend with the cable holding the bar.
4. Pull the bar to your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back.
5. Extend the arms slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout.
2. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Avoid using momentum from the lower back.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ-bar to a low pulley. Stand facing the machine and grasp the bar with a semi-supinated underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, back straight and core braced.
3. Hold the bar at arm's length in front of your thighs.
4. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar slowly until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
2. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
4. Control the negative instead of dropping the weight.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low pulley. Stand facing the machine and grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width.
2. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, back straight and core braced.
3. Hold the bar at arm's length in front of your thighs.
4. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar slowly until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
2. Keep the wrists neutral to avoid strain.
3. Keep your elbows close to your torso.
4. Move under control and avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads.
2. Grasp the close-grip handle with palms facing each other and arms fully extended overhead.
3. Pull the handle down toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your back at the bottom, then slowly let the handle rise until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive with your elbows, not your hands, to keep tension on the lats.
2. Keep your chest up and shoulders down to avoid rounding your back.
3. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
4. Move slowly and avoid using momentum or leaning back excessively.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing away with the cable between your legs.
2. Hold the bar with an overhand grip, arms extended down in front of your thighs.
3. Stand upright with your core engaged and a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height.
5. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso still and avoid swinging or using momentum.
2. Exhale as you raise the bar, inhale as you lower it.
3. Keep your shoulders down, not shrugged toward your ears.
4. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the front delts.

instructions:
1. Stand in the middle of a cable machine with a handle attached to each low pulley.
2. Hold the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, cables crossing in front.
3. Stand upright with your arms extended and a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Raise the handles out to your sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows and keep your wrists neutral.
2. Exhale as you raise the handles, inhale as you lower them.
3. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Keep your traps relaxed to isolate the side delts.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley and hold it in your outside hand.
2. Grip the machine with your inside hand and lean away until your arm hangs across your body.
3. Position your feet together with a stable stance.
4. Raise the handle out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lean away from the machine to load the side delt through a longer range.
2. Lead with your elbow and keep a slight bend throughout.
3. Exhale as you raise the handle, inhale as you lower it.
4. Move slowly and avoid swinging from the hips.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to the lowest position and grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward.
2. Step forward into a staggered stance with arms extended down and out to your sides.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your chest up.
4. Bring the handles up and together in front of your body in a wide arc, palms turning up.
5. Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as you bring the handles together at the top.
2. Keep the bend in your elbows fixed; do not turn it into a press.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together, inhale as you return.
4. Keep your shoulders retracted to protect the shoulder joint.

instructions:
1. Sit at the low cable row station with feet braced on the platform and knees slightly bent.
2. Grasp the handle with both hands and sit upright with a straight back.
3. Extend your arms fully and let the weight stretch your shoulder blades forward.
4. Pull the handle to your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid swinging back to move the weight.
2. Lead the pull with your elbows, not your hands.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach a handle to a low pulley and lie on a flat bench with your head near the pulley.
2. Grasp the handle and extend your arms over your chest with a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Lower the handle in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch through your lats and chest.
4. Pull the handle back over your chest in the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Drive the movement from your lats and chest, not your arms.
3. Stop the stretch before your lower back arches off the bench.
4. Exhale as you pull over and inhale as you lower behind your head.

instructions:
1. Set a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and lie back with feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp a handle in each hand and press them up over your chest with a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
4. Bring the handles back together over your chest in the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows so it stays a fly, not a press.
2. Squeeze your chest as the handles meet at the top.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the chest.
4. Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you lower them.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the cable and lie on a flat bench with your head near the pulley.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
3. Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Extend your arms back up until they are nearly vertical, squeezing your triceps.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and move only your forearms.
2. Point your elbows up and slightly in to keep tension on the triceps.
3. Stop the bar near your forehead, not on it.
4. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set a flat bench beside a low cable pulley with the head of the bench near the stack.
2. Lie back, grasp a straight bar with an overhand grip, and extend your arms over your shoulders.
3. Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar behind your head until you feel a triceps stretch.
4. Press the bar back up until your arms are nearly vertical, squeezing your triceps.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only your forearms.
2. Position the bench close enough that the cable stays loaded at the stretch.
3. Let the bar travel behind your head to load the long head of the triceps.
4. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set both cable pulleys to a high position and attach a handle to each.
2. Stand in the centre, grasp a handle in each hand, palms facing forward, arms extended up and out to the sides.
3. Stagger your feet shoulder-width apart and keep your back straight.
4. Pull the handles down and together in front of your hips in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
5. Slowly return the handles to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your lower chest as the handles meet at the bottom.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced to resist leaning.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together, inhale on the return.
4. Move slowly and keep tension on the chest throughout.

instructions:
1. Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position and attach a handle to each.
2. Stand in the centre, grasp a handle in each hand with an underhand grip, arms extended down and out to the sides.
3. Stagger your feet shoulder-width apart and keep your chest up.
4. Sweep the handles up and together in front of your chin in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
5. Slowly lower the handles back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Focus on squeezing your upper chest as the handles meet near chin level.
2. Keep your shoulders slightly retracted and chest puffed out.
3. Exhale as you raise the handles, inhale on the return.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.

instructions:
1. Set both cable pulleys to mid-chest height and attach a handle to each.
2. Stand in the centre, grasp a handle in each hand, arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height, palms forward.
3. Place one foot in front of the other, knees slightly bent, back straight.
4. Pull the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as the handles meet at the centreline.
2. Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows throughout.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together, inhale on the return.
4. Brace your core to resist the cables pulling you backward.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to the low pulley of the cable machine.
2. Sit on a chair facing the machine, feet together and flat on the floor, knees bent about 90 degrees.
3. Grasp the rope in both hands and hold it close to your chest for support.
4. Push through your heels and extend your legs to stand up tall.
5. Slowly bend your knees and lower back down to the seated position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to engage the glutes and quads.
2. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine.
3. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you sit down.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping into the chair.

instructions:
1. Attach a handle to a mid-height pulley on a cable machine.
2. Grasp the handle with your left hand in a neutral grip and step back to create tension.
3. Bend slightly at the hips, back straight, core braced, and tuck your upper arm against your side with the elbow bent 90 degrees.
4. Extend your forearm straight back by straightening the elbow, keeping the upper arm still.
5. Slowly return to the start with control, then finish all reps and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm pinned to your side so only the forearm moves.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale on the return.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the triceps.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Hold it in your left hand and step back to create tension.
2. Bend forward at the hips with your back flat and knees slightly bent. Rest your right hand on your right knee.
3. Let your left arm hang straight down toward the floor.
4. Pull the handle to your lower ribs, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade in.
5. Lower the handle slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding the spine.
2. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the cable.
4. Lead with the elbow, not the hand, to target the back.

instructions:
1. Set a pulley to mid-chest height. Stand side-on with feet just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Bend at the hips and knees and lean toward the floor. Rest your left hand on your knee.
3. Hold the handle in your right hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, with a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Bring the handle across in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping the elbow bend fixed.
5. Return slowly to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbow throughout.
2. Squeeze your chest as the handle crosses your body.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting.
4. Move from the shoulder joint, not the elbow.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand facing the machine.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand with your palm facing forward.
3. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and let your arm hang straight down.
4. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still and close to your body.
5. Lower slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbow pinned to your side.
2. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
4. Avoid swinging the torso to lift the handle.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley. Stand facing away from the machine and step forward to create tension.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand with your palm facing back.
3. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and let your arm hang by your side.
4. Raise the handle straight in front of you to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow.
5. Lower slowly under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Raise to shoulder height, no higher.
2. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the cable.
4. Control the lowering phase, do not let the cable pull your arm down.

instructions:
1. Set a pulley to shoulder height. Stand side-on with your right side toward the machine.
2. Hold the handle in your right hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing up.
3. Keep your upper arm parallel to the floor and still.
4. Curl the handle toward your head by bending your elbow.
5. Extend slowly back to the start under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm fixed at shoulder height.
2. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you extend.
4. Move only at the elbow.

instructions:
1. Sit at the cable machine with feet flat and knees under the pads. Grasp a single handle on the high pulley with your right hand, arm fully extended overhead, palm facing forward.
2. Pull the handle down toward your right shoulder, driving your elbow down and back.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blade down as you reach the bottom.
4. Slowly extend your arm back overhead under control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch to the left hand.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down and inhale as you extend back up.
2. Keep your torso facing forward and resist any twisting.
3. Lead with the elbow, not the hand, to load the lat.
4. Use a full stretch at the top for the most range.

instructions:
1. Stand between two cable pulleys set at the highest position. Grasp a handle in each hand, palms facing up, arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and back straight.
3. Curl the handles toward your head by bending your elbows, keeping upper arms fixed.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Slowly extend your arms back out under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you curl in and inhale as you extend out.
2. Keep your upper arms still at shoulder height throughout.
3. Move only at the elbows, not the shoulders.
4. Use a controlled tempo to keep tension on the biceps.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to the high pulley. Stand with your back to the machine and grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing each other.
2. Step forward to create tension and raise your arms overhead, elbows close to your head.
3. Extend your arms straight up by contracting your triceps.
4. Bend your elbows to lower the rope behind your head, keeping upper arms still.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
3. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a single handle to a mid-height pulley and hold it with your right hand, palm facing down.
2. Bend slightly at the hips and knees with a straight back, and extend your right arm forward.
3. Pull the handle toward your torso, rotating your palm up as your elbow draws back close to your side.
4. Slowly extend your arm forward, rotating your palm back down.
5. Finish all reps, then switch to the left hand.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the end of the pull.
2. Keep your torso square and resist twisting toward the cable.
3. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.
4. Start light to control the palm rotation cleanly.

instructions:
1. Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley and sit with feet flat. Attach a straight bar and grasp it with both hands shoulder-width apart, palms up.
2. Rest your upper arms on the bench pad and extend your arms fully.
3. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to full extension under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your upper arms flat on the pad the whole set.
3. Control the lowering phase for a full stretch.
4. Keep wrists neutral to avoid strain.

instructions:
1. Sit at the pulldown station with knees secured under the pads and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder-width, arms fully extended overhead.
3. Keep your chest up and pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
5. Slowly extend your arms back overhead with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
2. Lead with the elbows, not the hands, to load the lats.
3. Avoid leaning back or using momentum.
4. Keep your chest tall and shoulders down throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit at the pulldown station with knees secured under the pads and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the pro lat bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width, arms fully extended overhead.
3. Keep your chest up and pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and out.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
5. Slowly extend your arms back overhead with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
2. The wide grip emphasizes back width, so focus on driving the elbows down.
3. Avoid leaning back or jerking the weight.
4. Keep your chest tall and shoulders down throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with a straight bar on the high pulley.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder-width and pin your elbows to your sides.
3. Keep your back straight and your forearms parallel to the floor.
4. Push the bar down by extending your elbows until your arms are straight.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your upper arms still and only move at the elbows.
3. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
4. Keep your wrists straight to keep tension on the triceps.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with a straight bar on the high pulley.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder-width, arms nearly straight and extended forward.
3. Hinge slightly at the hips and keep your back straight with knees soft.
4. Pull the bar down to your thighs in an arc, keeping your arms straight.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your arms straight so the lats drive the movement, not the triceps.
3. Feel the stretch in the lats at the top.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso steady.

instructions:
1. Set both cable pulleys to chest height and stand in the center.
2. Cross the cables, holding the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand.
3. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and arms extended in front with a slight elbow bend.
4. Pull the handles apart and out to your sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
6. Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull the handles apart, inhale as you return.
2. Keep the slight elbow bend fixed so the rear delts do the work.
3. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
4. Avoid shrugging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to shoulder height and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your right hand, palm down, arm bent 90 degrees and held in front of you parallel to the floor.
3. Drive your elbow out to the side while straightening your arm, pulling the cable across your body.
4. Squeeze your rear shoulder and upper back at the end of the movement.
5. Return your arm to the start under control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and keep the upper arm moving back, not just the hand.
2. Keep the torso still and avoid using momentum.
3. Exhale as you drive the arm out, inhale as you return.
4. Keep the wrist neutral throughout.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to shoulder height and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your right hand, palm down, arm bent 90 degrees and held in front of you parallel to the floor.
3. Keep the elbow bent at 90 degrees and drive it out to the side, pulling the cable across your body.
4. Squeeze your rear shoulder and shoulder blades at the end of the movement.
5. Return your arm to the start under control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow fixed at 90 degrees so the rear delt does the work.
2. Pull the shoulder blade back rather than just moving the arm.
3. Keep the torso still and avoid swinging.
4. Exhale as you drive out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley and sit with your knees secured under the pads, feet flat.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and extend your arms overhead.
3. Keep your back straight and pull the bar down behind your neck by driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your back at the bottom of the movement.
5. Extend your arms back overhead under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light load and avoid forcing the bar low behind the neck to protect the shoulders.
2. Drive the movement with the elbows, not the hands.
3. Keep the core tight and avoid leaning or using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you extend up.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, palms down, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended down.
3. Keep your upper arms still against your sides and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze the forearms at the top.
5. Lower the bar back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrists firm and straight throughout.
2. Keep the elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging.
3. Use a lighter load than a standard curl since the grip is weaker.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to shoulder height on a cable crossover and stand in the center.
2. Grasp the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand so the cables cross in front of you.
3. Stand with a slight bend in your elbows and arms extended in front at shoulder height.
4. Pull your arms out and back in a wide arc until they are level with your shoulders.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows and keep a fixed slight bend in the arms.
2. Pull the shoulder blades together at the end of each rep.
3. Keep the torso upright and avoid using momentum.
4. Use a light load to keep tension on the rear delts.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and tuck your elbows against your sides.
4. Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
5. Return the bar slowly until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Use a controlled tempo and avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Sit at the cable row station with feet braced and knees slightly bent.
2. Attach a straight bar to the pulley and grasp it with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Sit upright with your back straight and arms extended.
4. Pull the bar to your upper abdomen, driving your elbows down and back.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
6. Extend your arms slowly to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid using momentum.
2. Lead with the elbows to load the back, not the arms.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a high pulley on the cable crossover.
2. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and tuck your elbows against your sides.
4. Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
5. Return the bar slowly until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Keep your torso steady and avoid leaning into the bar.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and tuck your elbows against your sides.
4. Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
5. Return the bar slowly until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Use a controlled tempo and avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ bar to the high pulley of a cable machine.
2. Grasp the EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and tuck your elbows against your sides.
4. Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
5. Return the bar slowly until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. The angled bar eases wrist strain, so grip it firmly.
3. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor facing a low cable pulley with a straight bar attached.
2. Extend your legs forward with a slight bend in the knees and brace your feet against the frame.
3. Grasp the bar with both hands shoulder-width apart, palms down, and sit upright with arms extended.
4. Pull the bar to your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and chest lifted throughout.
2. Do not use momentum or lean back to move the weight.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seated cable row machine with feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Attach a single handle to the low pulley and grasp it with your right hand, arm extended.
3. Sit upright with your back straight and rest your left hand on your left knee.
4. Pull the handle to your lower abdomen by driving your elbow back, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
5. Extend your arm back to the start with control, then switch hands.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso square and resist twisting toward the working arm.
2. Avoid using momentum to start the pull.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the top of each rep.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench between two low cable pulleys with single handles attached.
2. Grasp the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand so the cables cross.
3. Bend forward at the hips with a straight back until your chest is near your knees.
4. Raise both handles out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight elbow bend.
5. Lower the handles back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the rear delts.
2. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding the spine.
3. Do not swing the torso to lift the handles.
4. Exhale as you raise and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seated cable row machine with feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Attach a V-bar to the low pulley and grasp it with both hands, palms facing each other.
3. Sit upright with your back straight and arms extended toward the machine.
4. Pull the handle to your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back, keeping your upper arms close to your body.
5. Extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your back.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
3. Do not use momentum or lean back excessively.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seated cable row machine with feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and grasp it with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Sit upright with your back straight and arms extended toward the machine.
4. Pull the bar to your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back close to your sides.
5. Extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to bias the lower lats and biceps.
2. Keep your chest up and back straight throughout.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to the highest position and attach a handle to each.
2. Stand in the center, grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward.
3. Step forward with one foot, keep your back straight and arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Pull the handles down and inward until they meet in front of your hips.
5. Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest as the handles meet in front of your hips.
2. Keep the elbow bend fixed so the chest does the work, not the arms.
3. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
4. Use a weight that lets you control the full range of motion.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley and grasp it shoulder-width with palms facing down.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
3. Lean your torso slightly forward, keep your back straight and arms extended at shoulder height.
4. Keep your arms straight and pull the bar down to your thighs in an arc.
5. Slowly return the bar to shoulder height with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight so the lats drive the movement.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
3. Squeeze your lats as the bar reaches your thighs.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ bar to the high pulley and grasp it with both hands.
2. Turn so your back faces the machine, feet in a staggered stance.
3. Step forward to create tension and extend your arms overhead, elbows close to your ears.
4. Bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Extend your arms back overhead with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and close to your ears.
2. Brace your core to protect your lower back from overextending.
3. Squeeze your triceps at full extension.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach a V-bar to the high pulley and grasp it with both hands, palms facing each other.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
3. Lean slightly forward with a straight back and bend your elbows to about 90 degrees, flared out to the sides.
4. Push the bar down to your thighs by straightening your elbows.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom of each rep.
2. Keep your torso steady and avoid leaning into the bar.
3. Use a moderate weight to protect your elbow joints.
4. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ bar to the high pulley and grasp it shoulder-width with palms facing down.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
3. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees with your upper arms close to your body.
4. Push the bar down to your thighs by straightening your elbows.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides throughout.
2. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom of each rep.
3. Keep your torso steady and avoid using momentum.
4. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the EZ bar on the high pulley with palms down, hands closer than shoulder-width.
3. Tuck your elbows to your sides and bend them to about 90 degrees.
4. Push the bar down by straightening your elbows, keeping upper arms still.
5. Slowly return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Move only at the elbows, no leaning or swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the EZ bar on the high pulley with palms down, hands wider than shoulder-width.
3. Tuck your elbows to your sides and bend them to about 90 degrees.
4. Push the bar down by straightening your elbows, keeping upper arms still.
5. Slowly return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Move only at the elbows, no leaning or swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the straight bar on the high pulley with palms down, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Tuck your elbows to your sides and bend them to about 90 degrees.
4. Push the bar down by straightening your elbows, keeping upper arms still.
5. Slowly return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Move only at the elbows, no leaning or swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the V bar on the high pulley with palms facing each other.
3. Tuck your elbows to your sides and bend them to about 90 degrees.
4. Push the bar down by straightening your elbows, keeping upper arms still.
5. Slowly return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.
4. Move only at the elbows, no leaning or swinging.

instructions:
1. Sit upright on the bench with thighs secured under the pads.
2. Grip a handle in each hand with palms facing each other and arms fully extended overhead.
3. Keep your chest up and a slight lean back.
4. Pull the handles down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to full stretch with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive with your elbows, not your hands.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and together at the bottom.
3. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways to the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Set the pulley to shoulder height and grasp the handle with both hands, arms extended in front.
3. Twist your torso away from the machine, pulling the handle across your body with straight arms.
4. Slowly return to the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to keep tension on the obliques.
2. Exhale as you twist away and inhale as you return.
3. Keep your hips facing forward so the rotation comes from your torso.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways to the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Set the pulley to a high position and grasp the handle with both hands, arms extended diagonally toward it.
3. Twist your torso down and across, pulling the handle toward your opposite hip with straight arms.
4. Slowly return to the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to keep tension on the obliques.
2. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
3. Pivot through the torso and keep the arms straight so the core does the work.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways to the cable machine, feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, knees bent and hips back.
2. Grasp the handle at hip height with the hand nearest the machine, holding it at your shoulder.
3. Twist your torso away while pressing the handle up and across your body.
4. Straighten your legs to stand tall as you finish the press.
5. Slowly return to the semi-squat with the handle back at your shoulder.
6. Finish all reps, switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Start light and add resistance as your form holds.
2. Drive through the legs and hips to power the press.
3. Exhale as you twist and press, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your core braced throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the cable machine, left foot forward and right foot back, knees bent.
2. Set the pulley low and grasp the handle with your right hand, palm down. Lean forward so your upper body is near parallel to the floor.
3. Extend your arm toward the pulley, keeping your back straight and core braced.
4. Pull the handle to your torso, rotating your wrist until your palm faces up.
5. Slowly extend your arm back to the start with control.
6. Finish all reps, switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.
2. Keep your feet planted for a stable base.
3. Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
4. Lead with the elbow and squeeze the back at the top.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with feet flat and knees under the pads.
2. Grasp the wide bar with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width, palms facing back.
3. Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning back excessively.
2. Drive with the elbows rather than yanking with the arms.
3. Exhale as you pull down and inhale as you return.
4. Control the bar on the way up for a full stretch.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to the lowest position and attach a handle to each.
2. Stand in the center, grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward, and step forward into a staggered stance.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your chest up.
4. Pull the handles up and inward until they meet in front of your upper chest.
5. Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your upper chest, not your arms.
2. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows the whole set.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return.
4. Use a controlled tempo to keep tension on the chest.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ bar to the low pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand tall with arms extended and the bar resting against your thighs.
4. Pull the bar up toward your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the bar close to your body.
5. Lower the bar back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows higher than your wrists throughout.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid swinging.
3. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
4. Stop pulling if you feel pinching in the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Stand tall with arms extended and the bar resting against your thighs.
4. Pull the bar up toward your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the bar close to your body.
5. Lower the bar back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows higher than your wrists throughout.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid using momentum.
3. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
4. A narrower grip emphasizes the traps; widen it to shift to the delts.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and place a bench in front of it.
2. Sit on the bench and grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just beyond your knees, letting the bar hang.
4. Curl the bar upward by flexing your wrists.
5. Lower the bar back down with control until you feel a stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearms flat on your thighs and only move your wrists.
2. Squeeze the forearms at the top of each rep.
3. Use a full range of motion, letting the wrists extend at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set both pulleys to the lowest position and attach a handle to each.
2. Grasp the handles so the cables cross, holding the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left.
3. Step back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended down in front of you.
4. Raise the handles up and out overhead into a "Y" shape, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
5. Lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back.
2. Lift with your shoulders, not by shrugging your neck.
3. Use a light weight and controlled tempo for proper form.
4. Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a wall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on the wall at shoulder height.
2. Step your right foot back and keep the back leg straight.
3. Place your left forefoot against the base of the wall with the heel on the floor.
4. Press the back heel into the floor and push the front forefoot against the wall to deepen the stretch.
5. Hold 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back knee fully straight to target the upper calf.
2. Keep the back heel pressed flat on the floor.
3. Keep your spine neutral, no arching or rounding.
4. Breathe slowly and steadily to relax into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended out to the sides at shoulder level.
2. Lift your heels off the floor as high as possible.
3. At the same time bring your straight arms forward to clap in front of you.
4. Lower your heels and return your arms to the sides.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your eyes forward to hold your balance.
2. Squeeze the calves fully at the top.
3. Keep the arms straight and level with the shoulders.
4. Move with control to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand on the edge of a step with your heels hanging off the edge.
2. Hold a chair for balance and set your feet hip-width apart with toes firm on the step.
3. Lower your heels below the edge to feel a stretch in the calves.
4. Raise your heels as high as possible.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the chair for balance only, let the calves do the work.
2. Move slowly and with control.
3. Drop the heels below the step for a full stretch.
4. Pause briefly at the top of each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a wall with feet hip-width apart and flat on the floor.
2. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height for support.
3. Raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower your heels under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift the heels fully and pause at the top to maximize activation.
2. Use the wall for balance, not to push yourself up.
3. Keep the toes pointed straight ahead.
4. Move slowly on the way down.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a wall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on the wall at shoulder height.
2. Step one foot back, keeping the back leg straight and the front leg slightly bent.
3. Press the back heel into the floor.
4. Lean forward toward the wall to deepen the calf stretch.
5. Hold 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back leg straight and the heel pressed flat.
2. Stretch both legs equally.
3. Lean from the hips, keeping the spine neutral.
4. Breathe slowly and steadily.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both legs straight on the floor.
2. Loop a rope under the ball of your right foot and hold a handle in each hand.
3. Keep your right knee straight and your back flat on the floor.
4. Pull the rope to flex your foot and bring your toes toward your shin.
5. Hold the stretch, then release and switch to the left foot.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the knee fully straight to target the upper calf.
2. Pull with steady tension, not sudden jerks.
3. Breathe slowly and relax into the stretch.
4. Feel the stretch in the calf, not the lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand on a step with the balls of both feet on the edge and heels hanging off.
2. Hold the railing or wall for balance.
3. Keep your legs straight and your body upright.
4. Slowly lower your heels below the step until you feel a calf stretch.
5. Hold the stretch, then raise your heels back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees straight to target the upper calf.
2. Lower the heels slowly and under control.
3. Use the railing for balance, not to take the load off your legs.
4. Stretch when your muscles are warm.

instructions:
1. Place your forearms on the arm pads and grip the handles.
2. Press your back against the back pad and let your legs hang straight down.
3. Brace your core.
4. Raise your knees in front of you until your thighs reach parallel to the floor.
5. Lower your knees back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
2. Lift with the abs, not by swinging.
3. Curl the pelvis up at the top to engage the lower abs.
4. Keep your back against the pad throughout.

instructions:
1. Place your forearms on the arm pads and grip the handles.
2. Press your back against the back pad and let your legs hang straight down.
3. Brace your core.
4. Raise your straight legs in front of you until they reach parallel to the floor.
5. Lower your legs back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your legs as straight as possible to increase the load.
2. Press your back into the pad to stop swinging.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.

instructions:
1. Start in a lunge with your right leg forward and left leg back.
2. Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
3. Explosively push off the floor and switch leg positions in the air.
4. Land softly back into a lunge with the left leg forward.
5. Keep switching legs at a steady, rhythmic pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee aligned over the toes.
2. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
3. Use your arms to help balance and drive.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Exhale and round your back upward toward the ceiling.
3. Tuck your chin toward your chest and draw your navel toward your spine.
4. Hold and feel the stretch along your spine.
5. Inhale and return to the flat tabletop position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and control the rounding of the spine.
2. Exhale as you arch up and inhale as you return.
3. Keep wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
4. Keep the neck relaxed as you tuck the chin.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Inhale and gently arch your back, dropping your belly toward the floor.
3. Lift your chest and look up toward the ceiling.
4. Hold and feel the stretch through the front of the torso and neck.
5. Exhale and return to the flat tabletop position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Arch only as far as is comfortable.
2. Inhale as you lift and exhale as you return.
3. Place a mat under the knees for comfort.
4. Lift the chest rather than cranking the neck back.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms reaching straight overhead.
2. Bend your elbows and pull your arms down toward your hips.
3. At the same time, thrust your hips forward by squeezing your glutes.
4. Reverse the motion and return arms overhead with hips back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement by squeezing the glutes, not the lower back.
2. Keep the core braced throughout.
3. Keep your feet planted for stability.
4. Move with a controlled, coordinated rhythm.

instructions:
1. Anchor one end of a resistance band to a sturdy chair and the other to your left ankle.
2. Stand facing the chair with your right foot planted.
3. Step your left foot back and lower into a lunge, bending both knees.
4. Keep your right knee stacked over your right ankle and your left knee just above the floor.
5. Push through your right heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Use a lighter band until your form is solid.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the ankle.
3. Brace your core to resist the band pulling you off line.
4. Hold the chair for balance if needed.

instructions:
1. Anchor one end of a resistance band to a sturdy chair and the other to your right ankle.
2. Stand facing the chair with your left foot planted.
3. Step your right foot back and lower into a lunge, bending both knees.
4. Keep your left knee stacked over your left ankle and your right knee just above the floor.
5. Push through your left heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Use a lighter band until your form is solid.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the ankle.
3. Brace your core to resist the band pulling you off line.
4. Hold the chair for balance if needed.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a chair, facing away from it.
2. Rest the top of your left foot on the seat behind you.
3. Place your right foot flat on the floor, a comfortable stride ahead.
4. Bend your right knee and hip to lower down, keeping your torso upright, until your right thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your right heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Brace your core to stop your hips from twisting toward the working leg.
3. Lower under control instead of dropping.
4. Lean the torso slightly forward to bias the glute.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a chair, facing away from it.
2. Rest the top of your right foot on the seat behind you.
3. Place your left foot flat on the floor, a comfortable stride ahead.
4. Bend your left knee and hip to lower down, keeping your torso upright, until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your left heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Brace your core to stop your hips from twisting toward the working leg.
3. Lower under control instead of dropping.
4. Lean the torso slightly forward to bias the glute.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your left heel on the edge of a chair.
2. Lift your right leg and hold it bent toward the ceiling.
3. Place your arms by your sides, palms down.
4. Drive through your left heel and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
5. Pause at the top, then lower your hips with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute hard at the top rather than arching your lower back.
2. Keep your hips level so the working side does not drop.
3. Brace your abs to resist pelvic rotation.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both heels on the edge of a chair, knees bent.
2. Place your arms by your sides, palms down.
3. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
4. Pause at the top with your body in a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Lower your hips back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glutes at the top instead of arching the lower back.
2. Keep your heels firmly planted on the chair.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the glutes.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your heels on the edge of a chair.
2. Bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall out to the sides.
3. Place your arms by your sides, palms down.
4. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
5. Pause at the top, then lower your hips with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees pushed out to keep tension on the glutes.
2. Squeeze the glutes at the top instead of arching the lower back.
3. Keep your heels planted on the chair throughout.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a chair and grip the front edge next to your hips.
2. Slide your hips off the chair and extend your legs forward with heels on the floor.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your body until they reach about 90 degrees.
4. Press through your palms to extend your elbows and lift back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back close to the chair to protect your shoulders.
2. Keep your elbows pointing back, not flaring out.
3. Lower under control and avoid dropping into the bottom.
4. Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on the bench with your eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
2. Set your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and drive them into the floor.
3. Retract your shoulder blades and pull them down into the bench.
4. Keep a natural arch in your lower back with glutes on the bench.
5. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep a stable base.
2. Keep your feet planted and push them into the floor throughout.
3. Keep your head in contact with the bench.
4. Keep your shoulder blades pinched together for stability.

instructions:
1. Grasp the parallel bars with palms facing in and arms fully extended.
2. Lift your body off the floor and cross your ankles behind you.
3. Lean your chest forward and bend your elbows to lower your body.
4. Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Press through your palms to extend your elbows and lift back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lean forward to shift the work onto the chest.
2. Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
3. Lower under control and do not bounce out of the bottom.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seated dip machine and grasp the handles with both hands.
2. Place your feet flat on the floor and keep your chest up.
3. Lean slightly forward to load the chest.
4. Push the handles down by extending your elbows until your arms are straight.
5. Bend your elbows under control to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lean forward slightly to keep tension on the chest.
2. Exhale as you push down and inhale as you return.
3. Move under control rather than letting the handles snap up.
4. Keep your shoulders pulled down throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench and grip the front edge next to your hips.
2. Slide your hips off the bench and extend your legs forward with heels on the floor.
3. Lean your chest slightly forward and bend your elbows to lower your body.
4. Lower until your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
5. Press through your palms to extend your elbows and lift back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back close to the bench to protect your shoulders.
2. Lean forward slightly to bring the chest into the movement.
3. Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
4. Lower under control and do not drop into the bottom.

instructions:
1. Grip the parallel bars with palms facing inward and arms fully extended.
2. Lift your body off the floor and cross your ankles behind you.
3. Lean your torso forward about 30 to 45 degrees.
4. Bend your elbows and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep leaning forward to load the chest instead of the triceps.
2. Let your elbows flare out to about 45 degrees.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach the added weight with a dip belt and grip the bars with palms facing inward.
2. Press up to full arm extension and cross your ankles behind you.
3. Lean your torso forward about 30 to 45 degrees.
4. Bend your elbows, letting them flare out, and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forward lean to maximize chest activation.
2. Use a load you can control through the full range.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your shoulders pulled down throughout.

instructions:
1. Attach the added weight with a dip belt and grip the bars with palms facing inward.
2. Press up to full arm extension and cross your ankles behind you.
3. Lean your torso forward about 30 to 45 degrees.
4. Slowly bend your elbows and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both the lowering and lifting phases slow and controlled.
2. Maintain the forward lean to keep tension on the chest.
3. Use a load you can control through the full range.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grip the parallel bars with palms facing inward and arms fully extended.
2. Lift your body off the floor and cross your ankles behind you.
3. Lean your torso forward about 30 to 45 degrees.
4. Bend your elbows and lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Pause at the bottom for two seconds, then push up to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hold the bottom pause without bouncing.
2. Keep leaning forward to load the chest.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band above head height behind you.
2. Stand facing away from the anchor, one foot forward for balance.
3. Hold a handle in each hand with arms out to the sides at shoulder height and a slight elbow bend.
4. Pull the handles down and together in an arc, meeting at lower chest level.
5. Slowly return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Squeeze the lower chest as the handles meet.
3. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
4. Use a band tension that lets you keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band low behind you. Stand facing away, a handle in each hand, palms forward.
2. Stagger your stance, one foot forward, both knees slightly bent. Hold your arms down and slightly out to the sides.
3. Sweep both hands up and together in an arc to about chin height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Lower your arms back to the start with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you sweep up, inhale as you lower.
2. Squeeze your upper chest at the top of each rep.
3. Keep your torso upright and core braced, do not lean back.
4. Use a lighter band if your form breaks down.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together, arms out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows bent.
2. Step your right foot out to the side and bend the knee slightly.
3. At the same time, sweep your elbows together in front of your chest.
4. Step back to the start and open your arms wide again.
5. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control.
2. Squeeze your chest as your elbows meet in front.
3. Keep your chest up and core braced during each step.
4. Push through the heel of the stepping foot.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Place your hands behind your head, elbows wide.
2. Brace your core and curl your upper body off the floor.
3. At the top, rotate your torso toward the right.
4. Rotate back to center, then lower your upper body to the floor.
5. Repeat, alternating the rotation side each rep.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, do not pull on your neck.
2. Keep your elbows wide so your core does the work.
3. Press your lower back into the floor throughout.
4. Exhale as you curl and rotate up.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back straight, shoulders relaxed.
2. Interlace your fingers behind your back and straighten your arms.
3. Lift your arms slightly and push your chest forward.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your shoulder blades together to deepen the stretch.
2. Keep your neck relaxed and in line with your spine.
3. Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold.
4. Stop if you feel any sharp pain in the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band behind you at chest height. Stand facing away, a handle in each hand, palms down.
2. Stagger your stance, one foot forward, both knees slightly bent.
3. Start with your elbows bent and hands at chest level, arms parallel to the floor.
4. Press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
5. Return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press forward, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your wrists straight and firm.
3. Drive through your chest, not just your arms.
4. Brace your core to stay stable against the band.

instructions:
1. Attach the band to a high anchor point. Stand facing away from the anchor, holding a handle in each hand.
2. Stagger your stance with one foot forward, both knees slightly bent.
3. Start with elbows bent and hands at chest height.
4. Press the handles forward and down in a diagonal line until your arms are straight near your hips.
5. Return to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
3. Squeeze your chest at the bottom of the press.
4. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.

instructions:
1. Attach the band to a low anchor point. Stand facing away from the anchor, holding a handle in each hand.
2. Stagger your stance with one foot forward, both knees slightly bent.
3. Start with elbows bent and hands near your chest sides.
4. Press the handles forward and up in a diagonal line until your arms are straight at shoulder height.
5. Return to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back.
3. Drive the press from your upper chest.
4. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lean slightly forward at the hips.
2. Hold both arms in front of your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Pull your right arm back, bending the elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine.
4. Return your right arm to the front while keeping your left arm steady.
5. Switch arms and repeat the pull on the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine at the end of each pull.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull back, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees with forearms parallel to the floor and elbows tucked to your sides.
3. Rotate your forearms upward and outward until they point toward the ceiling and your upper arms reach shoulder level.
4. Reverse the motion back to the starting position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows bent at 90 degrees throughout the movement.
2. Move slowly to control the rotation and protect your shoulders.
3. Keep your shoulder blades down and back.
4. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you rotate up.

instructions:
1. Kneel on all fours with knees under your hips and hands under your shoulders.
2. Place your right forearm on an exercise ball to your side, elbow bent at 90 degrees.
3. Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch across the front of your chest.
4. Hold the position.
5. Return to the start and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower only as far as is comfortable and do not force the stretch.
2. Move slowly into and out of the stretch.
3. Relax your chest and shoulder to deepen the stretch.
4. Keep your hips aligned over your knees for a stable base.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest to just above the floor.
3. Push through your palms explosively so both hands leave the floor.
4. Tap your chest with both hands in the air.
5. Land softly with hands back under your shoulders.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep your hips level through the jump.
2. Land with soft elbows to absorb the impact.
3. Exhale hard as you push off the floor.
4. Keep your neck neutral, eyes down.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with your big toes touching and knees apart.
2. Sit your hips back onto your heels.
3. Walk your hands forward and lower your torso between your thighs.
4. Rest your forehead on the floor with arms extended, palms down.
5. Hold and breathe deeply.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Sink your hips toward your heels to deepen the lower back stretch.
2. Breathe slowly and let your spine relax.
3. Place a cushion under your hips if your knees feel tight.
4. Keep your neck relaxed with the forehead supported.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows bent.
3. Push your hips back toward your heels and straighten your arms.
4. Reach your arms forward and let your chest sink down.
5. Hold and breathe deeply.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your hips back to lengthen the lats and spine.
2. Move slowly and with control.
3. Breathe deeply throughout the hold.
4. Keep your arms active to feel the stretch through the sides.

instructions:
1. Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and core braced.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your chin above the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down to engage your lats and biceps.
2. Control the descent instead of dropping.
3. Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Step onto a box and grip the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
2. Pull or step up until your chin is above the bar.
3. Hold the top position with elbows bent and shoulder blades down.
4. Slowly lower yourself over 3 to 5 seconds until your arms are fully extended.
5. Step back up to reset.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your muscles engaged during the hold, do not just hang.
2. Resist the descent to maximise time under tension.
3. Keep your core braced to stop swinging.
4. Breathe steadily through the hold and the lowering phase.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down to start the movement.
4. Drive your elbows down and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The narrow grip loads the biceps hard, so keep the pull smooth without swinging.
2. Lower slowly to keep tension on the lats and biceps.
3. Keep your shoulders pulled away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows and drive them down toward your ribs.
2. Lower slowly to maximise muscle activation.
3. Keep your shoulders pulled away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The wider grip shifts emphasis to the lats and upper back.
2. Drive your elbows down and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Lower slowly and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a parallel-grip handle with palms facing each other, hands close together.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The neutral grip is shoulder-friendly and loads the biceps and brachialis hard.
2. Drive your elbows straight down and keep your torso steady.
3. Lower slowly and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your arms and place your fingertips on your shoulders, elbows pointing out.
3. Draw circles with your elbows, moving them forward, up, back, and down.
4. Keep the motion smooth and controlled.
5. After several circles, reverse the direction.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly to improve shoulder mobility and control.
2. Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
3. Keep your core braced so your torso stays still.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together and knees slightly bent.
2. Place your hands on your knees for support.
3. Keep your knees together and circle them slowly to one side.
4. Make small controlled circles in one direction.
5. Switch and circle in the other direction.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and stay in control.
2. Keep your knees close together.
3. Stop if you feel any knee pain.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended overhead.
2. Step your right foot behind and across your left leg.
3. Bend both knees to lower into a curtsy and bring your hands down to your sides.
4. Push through your left heel to stand back up and clap your hands overhead.
5. Repeat on the other side, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back straight.
2. Lower under control to protect your knees.
3. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot.
4. Push through the heel of the front foot.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together and arms out to your sides.
2. Jump your feet out to a wide stance.
3. At the same time bring your arms in front and clap your hands at chest level.
4. Jump your feet back together and open your arms back out.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees slightly bent to absorb impact.
2. Exhale as you jump out and clap.
3. Hold a steady rhythm.
4. Land softly through the balls of your feet.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Bend your elbows and lower until your chest is just above the floor.
4. Push explosively so your hands leave the floor.
5. Clap your hands in front of your chest, then land with hands back down.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive hard through your chest, shoulders, and triceps.
2. Land softly to protect your wrists.
3. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag.
4. Exhale as you push and clap.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank on the floor with your hands under your shoulders.
2. Place a padded stool just in front of you.
3. Brace your core and place your right hand, then left hand, onto the stool.
4. Step your hands back down to the floor one at a time.
5. Keep alternating which hand leads.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders stacked over your hands.
2. Move under control and grip the stool firmly.
3. Set the stool on a non-slip surface.
4. Keep your hips level and core braced.

instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up.
3. Walk both hands about 20 cm to one side to rotate your body around, then perform another push-up.
4. Keep walking your hands in the same direction to complete the full circle, doing a push-up at each position.
5. Brace your core so your hips stay level throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips from sagging by squeezing your glutes and bracing your abs.
2. Move your hands with control to protect your wrists and shoulders.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to your torso, not flared out.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on the bench with feet planted on the floor and eyes under the barbell.
2. Grip the bar with hands slightly closer than shoulder-width, palms facing away.
3. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with straight arms.
4. Lower the bar to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
5. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
2. Tuck your elbows close to your sides to load the triceps.
3. Lower the bar under control to your lower sternum.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands close together under your chest and arms straight.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
4. Press through your palms to push back up to straight arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs to load the triceps.
2. Lower under control to maximize muscle engagement.
3. Brace your core so your hips do not sag.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
