1. Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
3. Pull your body up by driving your elbows down and contracting your biceps until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down and pull your chest to the bar.
2. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell on the floor, gripping it overhand just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Pull the bar from the floor, then explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug to drive it upward.
3. Drop under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders while squatting until your thighs pass below your knees.
4. Drive up out of the squat and continue pressing the bar overhead until your arms are straight.
5. Lower the bar back to your shoulders, then to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body during the pull.
2. Catch the bar with elbows high and your torso upright.
3. Use leg drive to start the overhead press, not just your arms.
4. Brace your core throughout to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows close to your sides.
3. Let your hips settle to the floor and press through your palms to lift your chest, arching your upper back into the cobra position.
4. Bend your arms to lower your chest back down, then press back up to the plank.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your palms and squeeze your chest and triceps to press up.
2. Move with control through each transition between plank, push-up, and cobra.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs straight and hands flat on the floor at shoulder level, elbows close to your sides.
2. Press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor and straighten your arms into the cobra position.
3. Keep your hips on the floor and hold briefly at the top.
4. Bend your elbows to lower your chest back to the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift the chest by extending your upper back, not by yanking with your arms.
2. Keep your hips pinned to the floor throughout.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs straight and hands flat on the floor at shoulder level.
2. Press through your palms to lift your chest into the cobra position, keeping your hips on the floor.
3. Slowly rotate your torso to the right and look over your right shoulder, then return to center.
4. Slowly rotate your torso to the left and look over your left shoulder, then return to center.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate slowly and only as far as feels comfortable.
2. Keep your hips pinned to the floor.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Breathe steadily, exhaling into each rotation.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs straight and hands flat on the floor at shoulder level.
2. Press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor and straighten your arms into the cobra position.
3. Keep your hips on the floor and chest lifted.
4. Hold the position while breathing steadily.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift through your upper back rather than shrugging your shoulders.
2. Keep your hips pinned to the floor.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Breathe deeply and steadily during the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with legs straight and arms extended overhead on the floor.
2. Lift your legs while bringing your arms forward toward your knees, curling your body into a tight cocoon.
3. Squeeze your abs at the top.
4. Lower your legs and arms back to the start with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use your abs to curl up, not momentum.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
3. Lie on a mat to protect your back.
4. Exhale as you curl in, inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Grip the bar with both hands close together, palms facing each other, one hand in front of the other.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and body straight.
3. Pull your body up and lean your head to one side of the bar until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower under control until arms are fully extended.
5. Pull up again, leaning your head to the other side of the bar.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body straight and resist rotation on every rep.
2. Lower slowly to control the movement.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and rest your right elbow against the inside of your right thigh.
3. Let the dumbbell hang with your arm fully extended.
4. Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, keeping your elbow against your thigh.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the biceps at the top of the curl.
2. Keep your upper arm still against your thigh.
3. Use a weight you can control through a full range of motion.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and raise your legs overhead until your feet reach toward the floor behind your head.
2. Hold one foot with both hands.
3. Release the other leg and lift it straight up until it points to the ceiling.
4. Hold the position and keep your balance.
5. Lower the leg back to the start and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and keep control of each leg.
2. Keep your shoulders on the floor and do not strain your neck.
3. Exhale as you lift the leg, inhale as you lower it.
4. Use a mat to support your back.

instructions:
1. Stand in a semi-lunge with your left leg bent and your right leg extended behind you.
2. Raise your right arm overhead and lower your left arm to your side.
3. Brace your core and rotate your torso to face the opposite side.
4. As you rotate, lower your right arm and raise your left arm overhead.
5. Rotate back to the start, switching arm positions again.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate with control to protect your lower back.
2. Keep your feet planted and stay balanced.
3. Keep the movement smooth and deliberate.
4. Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a wall corner with your feet shoulder-width apart, about 30 cm from the corner.
2. Place your forearms and palms flat on each wall at shoulder height.
3. Lean your body forward into the corner.
4. Push your chest toward the corner until you feel a stretch across your chest and shoulders.
5. Hold the position.
6. Step back to release and repeat.
tips:
1. Increase the lean gradually as the muscles loosen.
2. Stop at a gentle stretch, not pain.
3. Keep your palms and forearms flat against the wall.
4. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet much wider than shoulder-width and your toes pointing slightly out.
2. Shift your weight onto your right leg and bend the right knee, keeping the left leg straight with the toes up.
3. Lower your hips toward your right heel while keeping your chest tall and the right knee tracking over the toes.
4. Push through the right heel to return to the wide standing position.
5. Shift to the left leg and repeat the movement on that side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back flat the whole time.
2. Sit back into the hip rather than letting the knee collapse inward.
3. Control the descent to load the inner thigh of the straight leg.
4. Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand tall on your right foot and bend your left knee so the lower leg lifts behind you.
2. Extend your arms forward to act as a counterbalance.
3. Bend your right knee and hinge slightly forward, lowering until the back knee nears the floor.
4. Keep the right knee tracking over the toes and the pelvis level.
5. Drive through the right foot to return to standing, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the forward arm reach to stay balanced and upright.
2. Keep the working knee tracking in line with the toes.
3. Lower under control instead of dropping into the bottom.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you descend.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands behind you with the fingers pointing toward your body.
3. Press through your palms and feet to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your head in line with your spine and squeeze your glutes at the top.
5. Hold the position, then lower your hips back down.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes hard.
2. Keep the shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
3. Distribute weight evenly between hands and feet.
4. Breathe steadily while holding the position.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent, feet flat, and hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your body.
2. Press through your palms and feet to lift your hips into a tabletop position.
3. Lift your right hand and left foot off the floor at the same time.
4. Twist your torso and reach your right hand toward your left foot.
5. Return the hand and foot to the floor, then repeat on the opposite side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your trunk, not just your arm.
2. Keep the hips lifted as you twist.
3. Move under control to keep your balance.
4. Exhale as you reach across, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor and step your right foot forward into a low lunge.
2. Keep the right knee stacked over the ankle and the left knee resting on the floor.
3. Sink your hips forward and down to stretch the front of the left hip and thigh.
4. Lengthen your spine and keep your chest tall.
5. Hold the stretch, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Tuck the pelvis slightly to deepen the hip flexor stretch.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot, not past the toes.
3. Avoid arching the lower back; stay tall through the spine.
4. Breathe slowly and ease deeper on each exhale.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended in front at hip height, palms facing in.
2. Cross your right arm over your left, then your left over your right.
3. Keep alternating the cross as you raise both arms upward.
4. Continue until your hands reach head height.
5. Cross your arms in the same way as you lower them back to hip height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead the lift with your shoulders, not momentum.
2. Move at a steady, controlled pace through the whole range.
3. Keep shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and hands behind your head, elbows out.
2. Do a light jump and cross your legs in mid-air, landing crossed, then jump back to the wide stance.
3. Lift your right knee and twist your torso to bring your left elbow toward it.
4. Return to the start and do another light leg cross.
5. Lift your left knee and bring your right elbow toward it.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Drive the twist from your obliques, not your arms.
2. Bring elbow and knee together with control.
3. Exhale as you twist and lift, inhale as you return.
4. Land softly with bent knees on each jump.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wide apart and arms extended out to the sides at shoulder level.
2. Do a light jump and cross your legs in mid-air while bringing both arms straight in front of your chest.
3. Land with legs crossed and arms crossed in front.
4. Jump again to return to the wide stance with arms out to the sides.
5. Repeat, alternating which leg and arm cross on top.
tips:
1. Land softly with knees slightly bent to absorb impact.
2. Keep a steady rhythm to maintain cardio output.
3. Squeeze your inner thighs as your legs cross.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wide apart and arms bent out to the sides at shoulder level, hands facing each other.
2. Do a light jump and cross your legs in mid-air while crossing both arms in front of your chest.
3. Land with legs crossed and arms crossed in front.
4. Jump again to return to the wide stance with arms bent out to the sides.
5. Repeat, alternating which leg and arm cross on top.
tips:
1. Land softly with knees slightly bent to absorb impact.
2. Keep shoulders down and away from your ears.
3. Squeeze your inner thighs as your legs cross.
4. Keep a steady rhythm and breathe throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands by your sides or under your lower back.
2. Lift both legs slightly off the floor and engage your core.
3. Cross your right leg over your left, then your left over your right in a scissor motion.
4. Keep crisscrossing as you raise your legs to a 45-degree angle.
5. Lower your legs back to just above the floor while still crisscrossing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
2. Keep legs straight and move them smoothly.
3. Exhale as you raise the legs, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping the legs.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bring your right arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
3. Place your left hand on the right upper arm.
4. Gently pull the right arm toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the back of the shoulder.
5. Hold, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the stretched arm straight and relaxed.
2. Do not pull on the elbow joint; pull on the upper arm.
3. Keep both shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Breathe slowly and stay relaxed during the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms crossed over your chest.
2. Shift your weight onto your left leg with a slight knee bend.
3. Kick your right leg straight forward, keeping it as straight as you can.
4. Lower the right leg back to the floor with control.
5. Kick your left leg forward in the same way.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright; do not lean back as you kick.
2. Brace your core to stay balanced.
3. Move with control, no jerking.
4. Exhale as you kick, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your left knee on the floor and your right foot flat in front, both legs bent about 90 degrees.
2. Brace your core and rotate your torso toward the right leg.
3. Reach both hands to the outside of the right thigh.
4. Push your hips forward while keeping your back straight to feel the stretch in the left hip.
5. Hold, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee stacked over the ankle.
2. Move into the stretch slowly with control.
3. Keep your back straight, do not arch the lower back.
4. Breathe slowly throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand with legs wide in a semi-lunge, turned to the right, left leg extended back and right knee bent.
2. Bend forward at the hips and place your hands on the floor for balance.
3. Keep the left leg straight and press the left heel down toward the floor.
4. Feel the stretch in the left calf and hold.
5. Switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back leg straight to target the calf.
2. Keep your back flat and shoulders relaxed.
3. Ease the heel down with control.
4. Breathe slowly during the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Extend your arms straight overhead, in line with your ears.
3. Brace your core and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, reaching your arms toward the ceiling.
4. Lower your shoulder blades back down with control, keeping the arms extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use your abs to lift, not your neck or momentum.
2. Keep the arms straight to add load to the abs.
3. Use a mat to support your back.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
3. Exhale and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, curling your upper body toward your knees.
4. Lower your shoulder blades back down with control while inhaling.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Move slowly and with control to keep tension on the abs.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and lean back slightly with your arms extended to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Extend your legs straight out, parallel and just above the floor.
3. Exhale and pull both knees toward your chest while crunching your upper body up to meet them.
4. Bring your arms toward the sides of your knees as you crunch.
5. Extend your legs and open your arms back out with control while inhaling.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your abs, not momentum.
2. Keep your lower back stable and do not let it arch.
3. Exhale as you crunch in, inhale as you extend out.
4. Squeeze your abs hard at the top of each rep.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Extend your arms straight overhead with hands together, in line with your ears.
3. Exhale and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, keeping your arms extended.
4. Lower your shoulder blades back down with control while inhaling.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and locked next to your ears throughout.
2. Lift with your abs, not momentum from your arms.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet just off the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
3. Exhale and lift your shoulder blades off the floor while bringing your knees toward your head.
4. Lower your upper back and legs back to the start with control while inhaling, keeping your feet off the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Use a mat to support your back.
3. Exhale as you lift shoulders and knees, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your feet off the floor to maintain tension on the lower abs.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with your knees bent at 90 degrees and your lower legs resting on a stability ball.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
3. Exhale and lift your shoulder blades off the floor, curling your upper body toward your knees.
4. Lower your shoulder blades back down with control while inhaling, keeping your legs on the ball.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your legs steady on the ball to challenge your core stability.
2. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Move slowly to maximize ab tension.

instructions:
1. Sit on a BOSU ball with your feet flat on the floor and knees bent.
2. Lean back so your lower back rests on the dome and your torso extends back over the ball.
3. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out.
4. Curl your shoulder blades up toward your knees by contracting your abs.
5. Lower your torso back over the ball with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Use the full range the ball allows by stretching back at the bottom.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the abs.

instructions:
1. Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the floor and knees bent.
2. Walk your feet forward and lean back until your lower and mid back rest on the ball.
3. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing out.
4. Curl your shoulder blades up toward your knees by contracting your abs.
5. Lower your torso back over the ball with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Stretch back over the ball at the bottom for a full range of motion.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your feet planted to stay balanced on the ball.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with your legs extended straight up toward the ceiling.
2. Keep your feet together and reach your arms straight up over your chest.
3. Curl your shoulder blades off the floor and reach your hands toward your toes.
4. Squeeze your abs at the top for a brief moment.
5. Lower your shoulder blades back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck or using momentum.
2. Keep your legs pointing straight up throughout the set.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Press your lower back into the floor to protect your spine.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Hold a medicine ball in both hands with your arms extended straight over your chest.
3. Curl your upper back off the floor by contracting your abs.
4. Press the ball toward the ceiling and squeeze your abs at the top.
5. Lower your upper body back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling your head forward.
2. Keep your feet flat and your knee angle steady.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the abs.
4. Pick a ball weight that lets you keep good form.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
2. Step your right leg behind and across your left leg.
3. Bend both knees to lower into a curtsy, keeping your front knee over your ankle.
4. Push through your front heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat on the other side, alternating legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright to hold your balance.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot, not collapsing inward.
3. Push through the front heel to drive the glutes.
4. Control the descent instead of dropping down.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place a towel under your right foot.
2. Slide your right foot behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy lunge.
3. Keep your front knee in line with your front ankle and your chest tall.
4. Push through your left heel and slide your right foot back to the start.
5. Finish all reps on one side, switch the towel to the other foot.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to keep balance.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot.
3. Push through your heel to drive the glutes.
4. Use a smooth floor so the towel slides freely.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under your left foot.
2. Hold the band with both hands at shoulder height or by your sides.
3. Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a lunge.
4. Push through your left heel to return to the start, bringing your right leg back to center.
5. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back straight.
2. Move slowly and with control against the band.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep tension on the band the whole rep.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips or by your sides.
2. Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower.
3. Keep your front knee in line with your front ankle and point your back knee toward the floor.
4. Push through your left heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat on the other side, stepping your left leg behind your right, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to keep balance.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot.
3. Push through your heel to drive the glutes.
4. Keep your torso upright throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your arms extended straight up toward the ceiling.
2. Lift your legs with your knees bent at 90 degrees.
3. Brace your core and slowly lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor, keeping your back flat.
4. Return your right arm and left leg to the start.
5. Repeat with your left arm and right leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Stop the limbs just above the floor to keep tension.
3. Move slowly so your back does not arch.
4. Breathe out as you extend, in as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your right arm extended overhead on the floor and your left arm by your side.
2. Bend your right knee toward your chest and extend your left leg out, keeping both lower legs near parallel to the floor.
3. Brace your core and switch: sweep your right arm to your side while extending your right leg past hip level.
4. At the same time sweep your left arm overhead and draw your left knee toward your chest.
5. Keep your lower back flat and continue alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced so your lower back stays flat.
2. Stop the moving leg just above the floor to keep tension.
3. Breathe out as you extend, in as you return.
4. Use a mat to support your back.

instructions:
1. Stand under a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Lift your feet off the floor and let your body hang with arms fully extended.
3. Relax your shoulders and keep your grip firm.
4. Hold the position and breathe steadily.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders relaxed and do not shrug them toward your ears.
2. Breathe deep and steady throughout the hold.
3. Use a bar high enough that your feet clear the floor.
4. Use chalk if your grip starts to slip.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench and secure your feet under the footpads.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body toward your knees.
4. Lower your torso back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not pull on your neck; lift with your abs.
2. Move with control to keep tension on the abs.
3. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
4. Spread your knees slightly to reduce hip flexor takeover.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench and secure your feet under the footpads, hips near the edge.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body toward your right knee, twisting your torso.
4. Lower back down with control.
5. Lift toward your left knee, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged to protect your lower back.
2. Do not pull on your neck; lift with your abs and obliques.
3. Twist fully at the top to load the obliques.
4. Exhale as you crunch and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Secure your feet at the end of a decline bench and lie back with knees slightly bent.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand close to your chest.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body, twisting your torso to the right.
4. Squeeze your obliques at the top.
5. Lower back down, then lift while twisting to the left, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you twist and crunch, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your lower back supported and core tight.
3. Use a weight you can control with good form.
4. Keep your feet anchored to stabilize your body.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your head at the higher end and grip the side edges for stability.
2. Bend your knees to 90 degrees with thighs perpendicular to the bench.
3. Engage your core and lift your hips, curling your knees toward your chest.
4. Lower your hips back down with control, keeping knees bent.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged to support your lower back.
2. Lift with your abs, not momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl your hips up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the movement small and controlled to stay on the lower abs.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a chair and your hands on the floor close together, forming a diamond shape with thumbs and index fingers.
2. Brace your core so your body makes a straight line from head to heels.
3. Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
4. Push through your hands to straighten your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stop your hips from sagging.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your body to load the triceps.
3. Use a stable chair so it cannot slip.
4. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor close together in a diamond shape, hips raised toward the ceiling.
2. Set your body in an inverted V with straight legs and torso.
3. Lower your head toward your hands by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
4. Push through your hands to straighten your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips high and legs straight to hold the pike position.
2. Keep your elbows tucked to load the triceps and front shoulders.
3. Move under control on the way down.
4. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your knees on a low step and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
2. Set your body in a straight line from head to knees.
3. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows to about 45 degrees from your body.
4. Push through your hands to straighten your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared wide.
2. Move under control through the full range.
3. Keep your hips in line with your shoulders and knees.
4. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your knees on a box and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
2. Set your body in a straight line from head to knees.
3. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows to about 45 degrees from your body.
4. Push through your hands to straighten your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared wide.
2. Move under control through the full range.
3. Use a stable box so it cannot shift.
4. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet hooked under the footpads.
2. Hold your torso parallel to the floor, raised off the bench.
3. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
4. Curl your upper body toward your knees without pulling on your neck.
5. Lower back to the parallel position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso off the bench so the abs stay loaded.
2. Do not yank on your neck; let the abs do the work.
3. Use a stable bench so it cannot move.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
2. Form a straight line from head to heels and brace your core.
3. Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower your chest toward the floor.
4. Push through your hands and straighten your arms back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips in line with your body and do not let them sag.
2. Lower under control to load the chest.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a stable bench so your feet do not slip.

instructions:
1. Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart and walk your feet up a wall.
2. Form a straight line from head to feet with your feet pressed into the wall.
3. Brace your core to keep your body rigid.
4. Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower your chest toward the floor.
5. Push through your hands and straighten your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hands under your shoulders as you lower.
2. Lower under control to stay stable in the steep position.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Press your feet firmly into the wall to stay secure.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
2. Form a straight line from head to heels and brace your core.
3. Lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder while keeping your hips level.
4. Return your right hand to the floor.
5. Lift your left hand and tap your right shoulder, then return it.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square and resist twisting as you tap.
2. Set your hands a little wider for a stable base.
3. Move slowly so the core does the work, not momentum.
4. Use a stable bench so your feet do not slip.

instructions:
1. Lie back on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper body toward your knees.
4. Raise until your torso is near upright, keeping your back straight.
5. Lower under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.
3. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your feet anchored under the pads for stability.

instructions:
1. Lie back on a decline bench with your feet secured and knees slightly bent.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand against your chest.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper body off the bench.
4. Continue until you reach a seated position and feel your abs contract.
5. Lower under control back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not momentum.
2. Hold the dumbbells firmly against your chest throughout.
3. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your feet anchored to stay stable.

instructions:
1. Place two dumbbells on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width and grip the handles.
2. Set your body in a plank, with a straight line from head to heels and feet together.
3. Brace your core and keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your torso.
4. Bend your elbows and lower your chest below the level of the handles for a deep stretch.
5. Press through the handles until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level so your body stays in a straight line.
2. Lower under control to use the full deep range of motion.
3. Inhale as you lower and exhale as you press up.
4. Stop the deficit shorter if your shoulders feel strained.

instructions:
1. Set the cable handle at chest height and stand with your right side to the machine.
2. Place your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the handle with both hands.
3. Extend your arms so the handle is in front of your chest.
4. Pull the handle down and diagonally across your body, rotating your torso and pivoting your back foot.
5. Return to the start under control, then finish your reps and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your torso, not just your arms.
2. Keep your arms long and move the handle in one smooth diagonal line.
3. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
4. Use a lighter weight if your form breaks down.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
2. Extend your arms out from your chest.
3. Rotate your torso and chop your hands diagonally down toward your left hip.
4. Bend your knees slightly and pivot your right foot as you turn.
5. Return to the start under control with your hands back in front of your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stabilize your spine and drive the rotation.
2. Pivot your foot to get full range without straining your knee.
3. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
4. Keep a slight knee bend throughout for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
2. Extend your arms out from your chest.
3. Rotate your torso and chop your hands diagonally down toward your right hip.
4. Bend your knees slightly and pivot your left foot as you turn.
5. Return to the start under control with your hands back in front of your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stabilize your spine and drive the rotation.
2. Pivot your foot to get full range without straining your knee.
3. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
4. Keep a slight knee bend throughout for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together and your arms extended out at shoulder level.
2. Step your right foot diagonally forward at about 45 degrees.
3. Lower into a lunge, rotate your torso right, and reach your left hand toward your right foot.
4. Press through your right heel and rotate back to center as you return to standing.
5. Repeat on the left side, then alternate.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, not past them.
2. Brace your core and rotate smoothly to protect your spine.
3. Push through the heel of the stepping leg to drive back up.
4. Exhale as you lunge and inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, elbows bent and pointing outwards, hands near your chest.
2. Slide your right hand across your left forearm, moving both arms in opposite diagonal directions.
3. Keep your elbows bent and your shoulder blades active throughout.
4. Return your hands to the center.
5. Repeat the slide with your left hand across your right forearm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the motion smooth and controlled.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades as you open the arms.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso still.
4. Breathe steadily through each repetition.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, hands in a guard near your face.
2. Rotate your torso to the right and extend your right arm in a diagonal punch across your body.
3. Return your right hand to the guard as you rotate back to center.
4. Rotate your torso to the left and punch diagonally across your body with your left arm.
5. Return to center.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate your hips and shoulders fully to drive each punch.
2. Keep your free hand up to protect your face.
3. Exhale sharply as you punch.
4. Start slow to set technique before adding speed.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat and place your hands close together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
2. Lean forward over your hands with a straight back and braced core.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward your hands, keeping elbows close to your body.
4. Press through your hands to push back up to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tracking back, not flared out.
2. Hold a straight line from head to knees.
3. Inhale as you lower and exhale as you press up.
4. Keep your core tight to stop your hips sagging.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a couch and grip the edge next to your hips.
2. Press into your hands to lift your hips off the couch with arms straight and knees bent.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your body while lifting one bent knee toward your chest.
4. Press through your hands to raise your body and lower the leg back down.
5. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep your grip secure for balance and control.
2. Move slowly in both directions.
3. Coordinate the arms and legs so you lift the knee as you lower.
4. Brace your core to keep the torso stable.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your back to a chair and place your hands on the seat edge, fingers pointing toward your body.
2. Bend your knees with your heels on the floor.
3. Press into the chair to lift your hips off the floor with arms straight.
4. Bend your elbows to lower your body until they reach about 90 degrees.
5. Press through your hands to lift back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Set your hands firmly on the chair for a strong base.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
3. Stop at about 90 degrees to protect the shoulders.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Place two sturdy chairs parallel, slightly wider than shoulder-width, with the backs facing each other.
2. Stand between them and grip the top of each chair back.
3. Lift your body off the floor by straightening your arms.
4. Keep your torso upright and lower by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees.
5. Press through your hands to push back up to full arm extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Check that both chairs are stable and will not slide or tip.
2. Keep your torso upright to keep tension on the triceps.
3. Lower under control and avoid dropping into the bottom.
4. Breathe out as you press up.

instructions:
1. Place your forefeet on the edge of a step with your heels hanging off.
2. Bend at the hips and hold a bench in front of you, keeping your back flat and legs straight.
3. Press through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels below the step until you feel a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your legs straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
2. Move through a full range, raising high and stretching low.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo.
4. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Keep your back flat and your neck neutral.
3. Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, drive your right heel up toward the ceiling.
4. Lift until your thigh is in line with your torso.
5. Lower under control without touching the knee to the floor, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your glute, not momentum.
2. Keep your hips square and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Squeeze the glute hard at the top.
4. Keep your gaze down to protect your neck.

instructions:
1. Stand in a doorway and grip both sides of the frame at about hip height.
2. Step one foot forward and lean back to load your arms.
3. Curl your elbows to pull your body toward the frame.
4. Keep your elbows close to your sides.
5. Lower under control until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line and avoid swinging.
2. Pull with your biceps, not your shoulders.
3. Step further forward to increase resistance.
4. Keep a firm grip to protect your wrists.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands in front of your chest.
2. Lower into a squat, keeping your chest up and weight in your heels.
3. Stand back up, then immediately squat down again.
4. Explode upward into a jump.
5. Land softly with bent knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back straight throughout.
2. Land softly through the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
3. Move fluidly between squats and jumps.
4. Drive up explosively through your heels and forefeet.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and both arms bent at your sides.
2. Lift your right knee toward your chest and twist your torso right, bringing your left elbow to the knee.
3. Tap the elbow to the knee twice.
4. Lower the leg and return your torso to face forward.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning too far forward.
2. Rotate from the torso, not just the shoulders.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on one leg.
4. Exhale as the elbow meets the knee.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your fists near your sides.
2. Punch both arms forward while lifting your right knee to about waist height.
3. Return your arms and leg to the start.
4. Punch both arms forward again while lifting your left knee.
5. Continue alternating legs with each set of punches.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the punches from your shoulders and finish with the triceps.
2. Brace your core to stay balanced as you lift each leg.
3. Keep your chest tall and avoid leaning back.
4. Exhale as you punch and lift.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours, then lift your hips to form an inverted V with straight arms and legs.
2. Keep your hands flat and your head between your arms.
3. Drive one heel down toward the floor while the other lifts.
4. Switch feet quickly in a running motion.
5. Keep alternating at a steady pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and press the floor away through your hands.
2. Brace your core to stop your hips from sagging.
3. Keep a steady rhythm as you switch feet.
4. Breathe evenly throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
2. Let your arms hang at your sides.
3. Drag the dumbbells up along your torso by pulling your elbows back.
4. Lift until the dumbbells reach chest height and squeeze your biceps.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly along your torso.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbells close to your body the whole time.
2. Pull your elbows back rather than forward.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a handle in each hand, palms facing forward, arms extended down.
3. Keep your back straight and your chest up.
4. Drag the handles up along your torso by pulling your elbows back.
5. Lift until your hands reach chest level, then lower slowly.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the handles close to your torso throughout.
2. Pull your elbows straight back, not out to the sides.
3. Use a band tension that lets you keep control.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands straight over your chest.
3. Curl your head, shoulders, and upper back off the floor by contracting your abs.
4. Keep your arms straight as you lift the dumbbell toward the ceiling.
5. Squeeze your abs at the top, then lower your upper body under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Lead with your abs, not your neck.
3. Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.
4. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Start with both arms extended straight up over your chest, palms facing forward.
3. Lower the right dumbbell toward your chest by bending the elbow while the left arm stays extended.
4. Press the right dumbbell back up by extending the elbow and squeezing your chest.
5. Repeat with the left arm while the right stays extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower each dumbbell under control without bouncing.
2. Breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting while one arm works.
4. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down on the bench.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
2. Let your arms hang straight down by your sides.
3. Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the right dumbbell toward your shoulder, palm staying inward.
4. Squeeze at the top, then lower the dumbbell under control.
5. Repeat with the left arm while the right stays extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
2. Lift with your arm muscles, not by swinging.
3. Keep your back against the bench to stay stable.
4. Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Face your palms forward with elbows bent.
3. Brace your core and press the right dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat with the left arm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to resist leaning to one side.
2. Breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower.
3. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
4. Avoid arching your lower back as you press.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Face your palms toward each other with elbows pointing down.
3. Press the right dumbbell overhead while leaning slightly to the opposite side until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.
5. Press the left dumbbell overhead with the same slight lean to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core hard to control the lean and resist twisting.
2. Breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower.
3. Move at a steady pace without using momentum.
4. Keep your wrist straight and stacked over your forearm.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended and palms facing your body.
2. Pull the dumbbells up toward your armpits by bending your elbows.
3. Drive your elbows high and out to the sides as you lift.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control to the starting position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
2. Keep your back straight and chest up.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a controlled tempo and avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench with feet on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended at your sides.
2. Raise the dumbbells in an arc over your torso and back behind your head, keeping arms long.
3. Bring the dumbbells back over your chest in an arc to the start.
4. Keep the motion smooth and controlled throughout.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move from the shoulders, not momentum.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Inhale as you lower behind your head, exhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Lift the dumbbells in a wide arc out to your sides, keeping arms long.
3. Continue the arc until the dumbbells meet above your head.
4. Lower them back down the same wide arc to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
2. Brace your core and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Use a light weight to keep the motion controlled.
4. Keep wrists straight throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, holding one dumbbell vertically with both hands in front of your hips.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your chest up and the dumbbell close to your body.
4. Drive through your heels to stand and squeeze your glutes at the top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Track your knees in line with your toes.
2. Keep your weight on your heels and midfoot.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you stand.
4. Keep your torso upright throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest.
2. Keep feet flat on the floor and maintain a natural arch in your lower back.
3. Lower the dumbbells to chest level by bending your elbows at about 45 degrees to your torso.
4. Press the dumbbells back up until your arms are extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
2. Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to protect your shoulders.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press.
4. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down on the bench.

instructions:
1. Sit on a flat bench with back support, feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
3. Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight and your back against the pad.
2. Keep wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep elbows slightly in front of your body, not flared straight out.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back to a bench, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
3. Bend your knees and hips to lower down, keeping your chest up and back straight.
4. Lower until your buttocks lightly touch the bench.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up and extend your hips and knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to engage glutes and quads.
2. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you stand up.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Touch the bench lightly without fully sitting and relaxing.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees, palms facing your body.
3. Keep your core tight and back straight.
4. Raise your upper arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
5. Lower your arms back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid swinging or using momentum.
2. Keep your elbows bent at a steady angle throughout.
3. Lead the movement with your elbows, not your hands.
4. Stop at shoulder height to protect the shoulder joint.

instructions:
1. Lie across a bench with only your upper back supported and hips slightly lowered.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands above your chest, elbows slightly bent.
3. Keep your feet flat on the floor and core tight.
4. Lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head until you feel a stretch in your lats and chest.
5. Pull the dumbbell back over your chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a steady slight bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Keep your upper back in contact with the bench.
3. Move slowly and control the stretch at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you pull the dumbbell back up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
2. Hinge at your hips and knees until your torso is near parallel to the floor, back straight.
3. Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders, elbows slightly bent.
4. Pull the dumbbells up toward your face, driving your elbows high and wide.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
2. Lead with your elbows up and out, not straight back.
3. Use a lighter weight to keep form clean.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a supinated grip, palms facing forward.
2. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly until your torso is near parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders with your arms straight.
4. Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower the dumbbells under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows tucked close to drive the lats and biceps.
2. Hold a flat back and braced core throughout.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Move under control, do not swing the weights.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
2. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly until your torso is near parallel to the floor. Keep your back flat.
3. Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders with your arms straight.
4. Pull the dumbbells toward your torso, leading with your elbows.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower the dumbbells under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
2. Keep a flat back and braced core throughout.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid jerking; control both the lift and the descent.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
2. Curl the dumbbells to your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping upper arms still.
3. Rotate your palms to face forward and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
5. Reverse the curl to return the dumbbells to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core and keep ribs down during the press.
2. Exhale as you press overhead, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the movement smooth between the curl and press.
4. Start light to control the transition.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a stability ball with your forefeet on the floor for support, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Extend one arm overhead and let the other arm hang at your side.
3. Curl the hanging-arm dumbbell to your shoulder while bending the overhead arm to lower its dumbbell behind your head.
4. Return both arms to the start under control, keeping your balance.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stay balanced on the ball.
2. Move slowly and with control to avoid losing position.
3. Keep the overhead upper arm steady during the extension.
4. Exhale on the effort, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a box, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Place the top of one foot on the box behind you.
3. Lower your body by bending your front knee until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your torso upright and let your back knee drop toward the floor.
5. Push through your front heel to return to the start.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Brace your core to stay stable on one leg.
3. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.
4. Lean slightly forward to bias the glutes, stay upright to bias the quads.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
3. Lower your body by bending your front knee until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your front heel to stand back up, keeping your torso upright.
5. Finish all reps on one side, switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Drive through the front heel, not the back foot.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced through the whole rep.
4. Start light to master balance before adding load.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the footpads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest.
3. Lower the dumbbells slowly to your chest, keeping your upper arms at about 45 degrees to your body.
4. Press the dumbbells back up by straightening your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet locked under the pads to stay stable.
2. Move under control, no bouncing off the chest.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press.
4. Drive the dumbbells slightly inward at the top to load the lower chest.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest.
3. Lower the dumbbells slowly to your chest, keeping your upper arms at about 45 degrees to your body.
4. Press the dumbbells back up by straightening your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and your upper back tight on the bench.
2. Move under control, no jerking.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press.
4. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

instructions:
1. Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline and sit back with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your upper chest.
3. Lower the dumbbells slowly to chest level, keeping your upper arms at about 45 degrees to your body.
4. Press the dumbbells back up by straightening your arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a 30 to 45 degree incline to target the upper chest.
2. Keep your upper back and hips against the bench.
3. Move under control through the full range.
4. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press.

instructions:
1. Lie crosswise on a bench with your upper back supported and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands above your chest, elbows slightly bent.
3. Lower the dumbbell in an arc over and behind your head until you feel a stretch.
4. Pull the dumbbell back over your chest along the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a firm two-hand grip on the dumbbell.
2. Stop the descent when you feel a stretch, do not overstretch the shoulders.
3. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
4. Brace your core to keep your hips steady.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 to 45 degrees and lie face-down with your chest and stomach supported.
2. Plant your feet on the floor and let your arm hang down holding a dumbbell, with a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Raise the dumbbell out and up in a wide arc toward the back, squeezing the rear shoulder and upper back.
4. Pause briefly at the top without using momentum.
5. Lower the dumbbell slowly along the same arc to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light weight and keep the movement strict to target the rear delts.
2. Keep a fixed slight bend in the elbow throughout.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top of each rep.
4. Breathe out as you raise and in as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a close grip at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
3. Engage your core and sit up while pressing both dumbbells overhead.
4. Lock the dumbbells out overhead at the top of the sit-up.
5. Lower your torso back down while bringing the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to protect the lower back.
2. Press straight up so the dumbbells finish over your shoulders.
3. Keep your feet planted to anchor the sit-up.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a close grip, palms facing forward.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders at the same time.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows fixed to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not swing or use momentum.
3. Control the lowering phase.
4. Keep your wrists straight.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet close together, holding a dumbbell with both hands in front of your thighs.
2. Keep your back flat and a slight bend in your knees.
3. Hinge at the hips and lower the dumbbell along your legs.
4. Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbell close to your legs throughout.
2. Brace your core to support your spine.
3. Lead the movement with your hips, not your back.
4. Keep your back flat, never rounded.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back and lift your legs off the floor, almost parallel to the floor with knees straight.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended over your hips.
3. Lift your shoulder blades off the floor into a crunch, pushing the dumbbell over your thighs.
4. Hold the crunch position while keeping your lower back pressed down.
5. Lower your shoulders back to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your lower back into the floor throughout.
2. Keep your core braced to hold the legs up.
3. Exhale as you crunch up.
4. Start light to keep good form.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
2. Curl both dumbbells up to shoulder height.
3. Rotate your palms to face forward and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.
4. Lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending the elbows, then extend your arms back overhead.
5. Reverse the press to bring the dumbbells back to your shoulders, then lower to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move through each phase with control, no swinging.
2. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back during the overhead phases.
3. Keep elbows pointing forward during the triceps extension.
4. Exhale as you press overhead, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
2. Keep your elbows close to your torso.
3. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, rotating your palms to face up at the top.
4. Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the start, rotating to a neutral grip.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move in a controlled manner, no swinging or jerking.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body and stop them from flaring out.
3. Keep your wrists straight.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
2. Keep your elbows close to your torso.
3. Curl one dumbbell up toward your shoulder, rotating your palm to face up at the top.
4. Squeeze the biceps briefly, then lower the dumbbell slowly back to the start.
5. Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move in a controlled manner, no swinging or jerking.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body and stop them from flaring out.
3. Keep your wrists straight.
4. Brace your core to stop your torso from rocking side to side.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step your right leg behind and across to the left of your left leg.
3. Lower your hips until your back knee hovers just above the floor.
4. Push through your left heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat with the left leg stepping behind and across, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and core braced for balance.
2. Move with control, focusing on stability.
3. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot, not collapsing inward.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, elbows bent, palms facing forward.
2. Press the left dumbbell up until your arm is straight while keeping the right at chest level.
3. Lower the left dumbbell back to the start.
4. Press the right dumbbell up until your arm is straight, then lower it back.
5. Keep alternating arms with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
2. Move slowly and under control.
3. Keep your core tight to stay stable as one arm presses.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, elbows bent, palms facing forward.
3. Press both dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended over your chest.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control until your elbows reach chest level.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet locked under the pads to stay stable.
2. Lower the dumbbells slowly and keep the press controlled.
3. Drive through your chest, not your shoulders.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other, with a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Open your arms in a wide arc, lowering the dumbbells out to your sides until you feel a stretch across your chest.
4. Bring the dumbbells back up in the same arc until they meet above your chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Squeeze your chest at the top of the arc.
3. Control the lowering phase and do not overstretch.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing each other.
3. Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control back to your sides.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your palms facing each other the whole time.
2. Tuck your elbows close to your body to load the triceps and lower chest.
3. Control the lowering phase.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand by your side, palm facing in, and grip the bench with your free hand.
3. Press the dumbbell up over your chest until your arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbell under control back to your side.
5. Switch arms and repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stop your torso from twisting toward the loaded side.
2. Keep your palm facing in and elbow close to your body.
3. Hold the bench firmly with your free hand for balance.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie back on a decline bench with your feet secured under the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell in both hands with your arms extended overhead.
3. Curl your torso up, keeping the dumbbell extended above your head, until you are sitting upright.
4. Lower your torso back down under control to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your neck neutral and do not pull with it.
2. Move with your abs, not momentum.
3. Keep your arms straight overhead throughout.
4. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie chest down on a bench set to a decline or incline angle. Place your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Let your shoulders drop to feel a stretch in your upper traps.
4. Lift your shoulders up toward your ears and squeeze your shoulder blades.
5. Lower your shoulders back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your shoulders, not your arms.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades hard at the top.
3. Keep your head and neck neutral.
4. Exhale as you shrug up.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the footpads.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands against your chest.
3. Curl your upper body up toward your knees, keeping the dumbbell close to your chest.
4. Sit up until your torso is upright.
5. Lower your upper body back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbell close to your chest for balance.
2. Drive the movement with your abs, not momentum.
3. Keep your head and neck in line with your spine.
4. Exhale as you sit up.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended above your chest.
2. Lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
3. When your arms are near parallel to the floor, bend your elbows to bring the dumbbell toward the sides of your head.
4. Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbell back up.
5. Raise the dumbbell in an arc back over your chest to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms steady during the elbow extension.
2. Move slowly and stay in control through the arc.
3. Use a full range of motion.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms out to your sides at chest level, palms facing up.
2. Raise the dumbbells in a wide arc, twisting your wrists so your palms face back as they meet above your chest.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
4. Lower your arms back out to the sides under control, twisting your palms back to face up.
5. Stop when your arms are level with your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your chest at the top of the arc.
2. Keep your wrists aligned with your forearms during the twist.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the chest.
4. Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands extended above one shoulder.
2. Rotate your torso and pull the dumbbell diagonally across your body to the opposite hip, pivoting your feet as you turn.
3. Keep your arms extended through the chop.
4. Reverse the motion and bring the dumbbell back up to the start under control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate through your torso and pivot your feet for full range.
2. Keep a firm grip on the dumbbell.
3. Control the dumbbell instead of swinging it.
4. Brace your core throughout the chop.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended down at your sides.
2. Curl the dumbbells up while dragging your elbows backward, keeping them close to your body.
3. Continue until the dumbbells reach the front of your shoulders.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows drifting back, not forward, to keep tension on the biceps.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your shoulders still throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
2. Bend your working arm to 90 degrees with your elbow pinned to your side and forearm pointing forward.
3. Rotate your forearm outward, keeping your elbow fixed against your body.
4. Pause when your forearm points out to the side.
5. Lower the forearm back to the starting position under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light weight and strict form.
2. Keep your elbow pinned to your side the whole time.
3. Keep your wrist straight and in line with your forearm.
4. Do not rotate your torso; move only at the shoulder.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
2. Bend your working arm to 90 degrees with your elbow pinned to your side and forearm pointing forward.
3. Rotate your forearm outward, keeping your elbow fixed against your body.
4. Pause when your forearm points out to the side.
5. Lower the forearm back to the starting position under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light weight and strict form.
2. Keep your elbow pinned to your side the whole time.
3. Keep your wrist straight and in line with your forearm.
4. Do not rotate your torso; move only at the shoulder.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Bend your arms with elbows pointing out to the sides at shoulder height and palms facing the floor.
3. Press the dumbbells forward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Bring the dumbbells back to shoulder level under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest and stomach against the bench to avoid arching your back.
2. Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.
3. Use a light weight to keep the rear shoulders working.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades as you press.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Bend your arms with elbows pointing out to the sides at shoulder height and palms facing the floor.
3. Press the dumbbells forward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Bring the dumbbells back to shoulder level under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest and stomach against the bench to avoid arching your back.
2. Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.
3. Use a light weight to keep the rear shoulders working.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades as you press.

instructions:
1. Place a dumbbell on each side of your body and stand between them.
2. Squat down, grip both dumbbells, and stand up with arms straight at your sides.
3. Brace your core, lift your chest, and pull your shoulders back.
4. Walk forward in short controlled steps with an upright torso.
5. At the end of the set distance, turn around and walk back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso tall and avoid leaning forward or to either side.
2. Squeeze the handles hard to keep your grip secure.
3. Take steady, even steps and do not rush.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the carry.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms touch the floor.
5. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Move slowly and under control to keep tension on the chest.
3. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
4. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
3. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Control the lowering phase to protect your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Slowly squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Use a slow tempo on both the lowering and lifting phases.
3. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
4. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.

instructions:
1. Set a bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline and sit back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended above your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your upper chest and bring the dumbbells back up over your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows the whole time.
2. Do not let the dumbbells touch at the top.
3. Keep your back against the bench and your shoulders pulled down.
4. Control the lowering phase to protect your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand racked on your shoulders with elbows up.
2. Keep your chest tall and step forward with your right leg.
3. Bend both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee is just above the ground.
4. Push through your right heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat on the left leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbells racked tight to your shoulders with elbows pointing forward.
2. Brace your core to stay upright and resist twisting.
3. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
4. Push through the front heel, not the toes.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand resting against your thighs, palms facing back.
2. Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height with arms nearly straight.
3. Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your thighs.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a controlled tempo and do not swing the weights.
2. Keep your torso still and core braced.
3. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the front delts.
4. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand racked on your shoulders with elbows pointing forward.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
3. Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping knees in line with your toes.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up, fully extending hips and knees.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows up to hold the dumbbells stable on your shoulders.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
3. Brace your core to stay upright.
