4. Keep your spine neutral and chest tall.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Place a dumbbell across your hips and hold it with both hands.
3. Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top and hold briefly.
5. Lower your hips back down with control without resting on the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to load the glutes.
2. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
3. Keep knees aligned with toes, not splaying out.
4. Keep your spine neutral and ribs down, do not arch the lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows down.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
3. Descend until your thighs are just below parallel to the floor.
4. Hold the bottom position for 2 seconds with your chest up.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
2. Keep your weight on your heels through the hold.
3. Stay tight in the bottom position, do not relax during the pause.
4. Keep your spine neutral and chest tall.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keep your elbows pointed down.
2. Step your right foot behind and across to the outside of your left foot.
3. Bend both knees and lower until your right knee almost touches the floor. Keep your chest up.
4. Push through your left heel to return to the start.
5. Switch sides and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front.
2. Drive through the heel of the front foot to load the glutes.
3. Brace your core to control the diagonal movement.
4. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you stand up.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows down.
2. Step your right foot forward into a split stance, left heel raised.
3. Bend both knees and lower until your right thigh is about parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your chest up and your right knee over your ankle.
5. Push through your right heel to return to the start.
6. Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright to load the quads.
2. Lower under control until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
4. Brace your core to support the front-loaded weight.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows down.
2. Place your right foot on a low step and extend your left leg back, heel raised.
3. Bend the front knee and lower until your left knee nearly touches the floor.
4. Keep your chest up and the front knee over your ankle.
5. Push through your right heel to return to the start.
6. Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Use a step low enough to keep balance and control.
2. Keep an upright torso to bias the quads.
3. Drive through the front heel on the way up.
4. Brace your core to control the deeper range.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keep your elbows down.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your weight on your heels.
3. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping the dumbbell close to your chest.
4. Keep your chest up and your back neutral.
5. Push through your heels and stand up, extending your hips at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes and not caving in.
2. Keep the dumbbell tight to your chest to stay upright.
3. Brace your core against the front load.
4. Inhale as you descend, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward, arms extended at your sides.
2. Curl the dumbbells up to a 90-degree elbow angle for 7 reps.
3. Curl from the 90-degree angle up to the top for 7 reps.
4. Curl through the full range for 7 reps.
5. Lower under control after each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and your elbows at your sides.
2. Do not swing or use momentum.
3. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your right knee on the floor and left foot flat in front, knee over ankle.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
3. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your torso upright.
4. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your ribs down and core braced so your lower back does not arch.
2. Squeeze the down-side glute to stabilize the split stance.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows through the press.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Use a neutral grip, palms facing your torso, arms hanging at your sides.
3. Curl the right dumbbell up toward your shoulder, keeping your elbow tucked.
4. Lower it under control until your arm is fully extended.
5. Repeat with the left arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides; do not swing the weight.
2. Hold a firm neutral wrist throughout the curl.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced to prevent leaning.
4. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Use a neutral grip, palms facing your torso, arms hanging at your sides.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders at the same time, elbows tucked.
4. Squeeze at the top of the movement.
5. Lower both dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides; do not swing the weights.
2. Hold a firm neutral wrist throughout the curl.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced to prevent leaning.
4. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weights.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
2. Plant your feet on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
3. Let your arms hang straight down with a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Pull the dumbbells to your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed to the pad; do not push up to cheat the weight.
2. Lead with your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your neck neutral and gaze down at the pad.

instructions:
1. Sit at a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, upper arms on the pad.
3. Extend your arms fully but keep a slight bend to hold tension.
4. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
5. Lower both dumbbells under control to near-full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms flat on the pad to isolate the elbow flexors.
2. Do not let the dumbbells drop; control the lowering phase.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep a firm neutral wrist throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
2. Keep your arms extended down by your sides, upper arms and elbows pressed against the wall.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze at the top for a moment.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms and elbows against the wall to isolate the arms.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep the neutral grip fixed through the full range.
4. Brace your core and keep your back flat against the wall.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, dumbbells hanging at thigh level.
2. Hinge at the hips, lowering the dumbbells toward your knees with a flat back.
3. Explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug your shoulders to pull the dumbbells up.
4. Drop into a partial squat and rotate your elbows under to catch the dumbbells on your shoulders.
5. Stand tall by extending your hips and knees.
6. Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the lift with your hips and legs, not your lower back.
2. Move explosively on the pull and catch with control.
3. Keep the dumbbells close to your body during the pull.
4. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Raise both arms out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows high, palms facing up.
3. Curl the dumbbells inward toward your head by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze at the top for a moment.
5. Extend your arms back out to shoulder height under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed at shoulder height throughout.
2. Use a controlled motion and avoid swinging.
3. Focus on contracting the biceps at the top.
4. Keep your shoulders steady and avoid shrugging.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
3. Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top for a moment.
5. Lower your hips back to the starting position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press through your heels to maximize glute activation.
2. Keep a neutral spine and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
4. Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down at lockout.

instructions:
1. Sit on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging down and palms facing forward.
2. Curl the right dumbbell up toward your shoulder by bending your elbow.
3. Squeeze at the top for a moment.
4. Lower the right dumbbell under control while starting to curl the left dumbbell.
5. Continue alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary to isolate the biceps.
2. Let the arms stretch fully at the bottom for a longer range.
3. Move under control and avoid swinging.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit back on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging down and palms facing each other.
2. Curl the right dumbbell up toward the shoulder, rotating the wrist so the palm faces up.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
4. Lower the right dumbbell with control back to the start.
5. Repeat on the left arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms back against the bench to stretch the biceps.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weight.
3. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
4. Keep the wrist firm through the rotation.

instructions:
1. Sit back on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging down and palms facing each other.
2. Curl the right dumbbell up toward the shoulder, keeping the palm facing in.
3. Squeeze at the top.
4. Lower the right dumbbell with control, keeping the neutral grip.
5. Repeat on the left arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms back against the bench for a full stretch.
2. Hold the neutral grip throughout to load the brachialis and forearm.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Lie back on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level with palms facing forward.
2. Press the right dumbbell up until the arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the right dumbbell with control to chest level.
4. Press the left dumbbell up while keeping the right in position.
5. Continue alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.
2. Brace the core to resist twisting as you press one side.
3. Keep the non-working dumbbell steady at the chest.
4. Use a weight you can control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Lie back on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level with palms facing forward.
2. Press both dumbbells up until the arms are fully extended.
3. Bring the dumbbells together near the top without clashing them.
4. Lower both dumbbells with control to chest level.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.
2. Keep the shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
3. Lower until you feel a stretch in the upper chest.
4. Use a weight you can control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Sit back on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging down and palms facing forward.
2. Curl both dumbbells up toward the shoulders by bending the elbows.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
4. Lower both dumbbells with control until the arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms back against the bench to stretch the biceps.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weights.
3. Keep the wrists straight and aligned with the forearms.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Press the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your upper chest.
4. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Lower under control and feel the stretch before reversing.
3. Drive the chest, not the shoulders, to bring the dumbbells together.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Press the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until your upper chest is stretched.
4. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows fixed at a slight bend the whole set.
2. Control the lowering phase and pause briefly at the stretch.
3. Lead with the chest to close the arc, keeping the shoulders down.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball and walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on the ball, feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Lift your hips so your torso is roughly horizontal and hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent.
3. Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until your chest is stretched.
4. Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back together above your chest along the same arc.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core and keep your hips raised to stay stable on the ball.
2. Keep elbows fixed at a slight bend throughout.
3. Move slowly and control the dumbbells on the way down.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight, palms facing down.
2. Keeping your arms straight, raise both dumbbells in front of you until they reach shoulder height.
3. Pause briefly at the top.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Raise with your front shoulders, not momentum.
2. Keep your arms straight with only a slight elbow bend.
3. Stay pressed into the bench to isolate the delts.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle and lie back with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other in a neutral grip, elbows bent.
3. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
2. Press in a smooth path without flaring the elbows wide.
3. Drive the shoulders and upper chest through the press.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit back on an incline bench set to 45 degrees with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping palms facing in.
4. Squeeze at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
5. Lower under control until arms are fully extended. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the bench to block momentum.
2. Keep wrists straight and neutral throughout.
3. Control the lowering phase to load the stretch.
4. Keep upper arms still; only the forearms move.

instructions:
1. Lie chest-down on an incline bench set to 45 degrees with feet braced on the floor.
2. Let your arms hang straight down, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
3. Raise both dumbbells forward and up until your arms reach shoulder height.
4. Keep a slight bend in your elbows at the top.
5. Lower under control to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
2. Use a slow, controlled motion without swinging.
3. Stop at shoulder height; do not go higher.
4. Keep the bench supporting your chest to isolate the front delts.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie on your side along it, lower arm resting on the bench.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, arm down at your side, palm facing your body.
3. Raise the dumbbell out in an arc until your arm reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower under control to the start.
5. Finish the set, then switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
2. Hold the bench with your free hand for stability.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout.
4. Lead with the elbow, not the hand.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and sit back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height, palm facing forward.
3. Brace your core and hold the bench with your free hand.
4. Press the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended over your upper chest.
5. Lower under control to shoulder height.
6. Finish the set, then switch arms. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to resist twisting toward the loaded side.
2. Press the weight over your upper chest, not your face.
3. Keep your wrist stacked over your elbow.
4. Choose a weight you can control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and sit back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing back toward you.
3. Press both dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended over your upper chest.
4. Keep the palms-back grip throughout the movement.
5. Lower under control to shoulder height. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows tucked closer to your sides to protect the shoulders.
2. Press over your upper chest, not your face.
3. Keep wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.
4. Use a slow, controlled lowering phase.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie chest-first against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold briefly with arms parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use light weight and let the chest support remove all momentum.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and lead with the rear shoulders, not the hands.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the rear delts.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie chest-first against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down, palms facing down.
3. Row both dumbbells back by bending the elbows and pulling them toward your sides.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells with control until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull with the back, not the arms, and drive the elbows back.
2. Keep the chest pinned to the pad to remove momentum.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top of each rep.
4. Use a controlled tempo on the way down.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and sit back against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended at your sides, palms facing each other.
3. Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears without bending the elbows.
4. Hold briefly at the top.
5. Lower the shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift the shoulders straight up, not in a circular or forward motion.
2. Keep the arms straight and let the traps do the work.
3. Exhale as you shrug up, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a controlled tempo to avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and sit back against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms facing forward.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending the elbows.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells with control until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms back and still to maximize the stretch on the long head.
2. Lift with the biceps, not the shoulders.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo and avoid swinging.
4. Keep the wrists straight.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, pressed together just above the chest.
3. Press the dumbbells up by extending the arms while keeping them squeezed together.
4. Fully extend the arms at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to the chest with control, keeping them in contact.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press the dumbbells hard against each other through the whole movement.
2. Keep the elbows tucked toward the torso.
3. Focus on driving with the upper chest.
4. Use a controlled tempo on the lowering phase.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Press a single dumbbell flat between your palms and hold it just above your chest, elbows close to your torso.
3. Push the dumbbell upward by extending your arms, squeezing your palms together throughout.
4. Fully extend your arms at the top while keeping the squeeze on the dumbbell.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to your chest with control, maintaining the squeeze. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the dumbbell hard the whole set to keep tension on the chest.
2. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your elbows tracking close to your body.
4. Start light to groove the palm squeeze before adding load.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended straight up, palms facing each other.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head with control.
4. Stop when your forearms reach roughly parallel to the floor.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back to the top, keeping your upper arms still. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed so only the forearms move.
2. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo to keep tension on the triceps.
4. Let the dumbbells stretch the triceps behind the head for full range.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, arms slightly bent, palms facing up.
3. Raise the dumbbells over your chest in a wide arc, rotating your palms to face backward as you lift.
4. Pause briefly at the top with the dumbbells over your chest.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down in a wide arc, rotating your palms to face up again. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Drive the movement from the chest, not the shoulders.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the upper chest.
4. Stop short of letting the dumbbells touch at the top.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, gripping the handle, arms extended straight above your shoulders.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head with control.
4. Stop when your forearms reach roughly parallel to the floor and feel the triceps stretch.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back to the top, keeping your upper arms still. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed so only the forearms move.
2. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo to protect the elbows.
4. Grip the dumbbell securely with both hands to keep it stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms in front of your chest with palms facing each other.
2. Keep your back straight and squat down, lowering your hips.
3. Drive up to stand while opening your arms out to the sides to shoulder level, forming a T.
4. Pause at the top with arms parallel to the floor, palms facing forward.
5. Bring your arms back in front of your chest as you squat down again. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum to swing the dumbbells.
2. Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced through the squat and raise.
4. Start light to coordinate the squat and lateral raise.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat, keeping your chest up and back straight.
3. Drive through your heels and jump straight up, extending your legs fully.
4. Land softly on the balls of your feet and bend your knees to absorb the impact.
5. Lower straight into the next squat. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes on the descent and landing.
2. Land soft and quiet to reduce joint impact.
3. Brace your core to control the dumbbells through the jump.
4. Use a moderate weight so you can land under control.

instructions:
1. Place your right knee and right hand on a bench, with your left foot flat on the floor.
2. Lean forward until your torso is parallel to the floor and keep your back flat.
3. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent to 90 degrees.
4. Straighten your elbow to extend the dumbbell back until your arm is fully extended.
5. Slowly bend your elbow to return to the start, keeping your upper arm still. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm pinned to your side to isolate the triceps.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the dumbbell.
4. Keep your back flat and core braced to stop your torso twisting.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with your knees shoulder-width apart and your torso upright.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing your body and elbows bent.
3. Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height while rotating your palms back toward your body.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and core braced to stop your back arching.
2. Move smoothly and let the rotation flow with the press.
3. Squeeze your shoulders at the top of each rep.
4. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

instructions:
1. Kneel on both knees with a dumbbell in each hand held at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
2. Step one foot forward and plant it flat to form a 90-degree angle at the knee.
3. Drive through the front foot to stand up, bringing the other foot in to stand tall.
4. Step one foot back and lower that knee to the floor, then the other, returning to kneeling.
5. Alternate the leading leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee aligned over your ankle.
2. Drive through the heel of the front foot to stand.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso upright through the transition.
4. Use a controlled tempo on the way down to the floor.

instructions:
1. Kneel with both knees on the floor and your torso upright from knees to shoulders.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
3. Push your hips back and sit down toward your heels, keeping your torso upright.
4. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to upright.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard as you drive your hips forward.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
3. Brace your core throughout the movement.
4. Control the descent to protect your knees.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing in.
2. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height, keeping a slight elbow bend.
3. Lower back to your sides under control.
4. Raise the dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height.
5. Lower back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
2. Lift with the shoulders, not by swinging the body.
3. Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears.
4. Use a light weight to keep both movements controlled.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, feet flat on the floor.
2. Lean your torso forward, keeping your back flat.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
3. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
4. Keep the back flat and chest leaning forward.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, holding a dumbbell in your left hand by your side, right arm raised straight overhead.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the left knee slightly, keeping the right leg straight.
3. Lower the dumbbell toward your left foot, keeping the back flat and the right arm pointing up.
4. Rotate the torso to follow the movement, going as low as form allows.
5. Push through the left foot and rotate back up to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep the back flat and avoid rounding the spine.
2. Keep the raised arm locked and stacked over the shoulder.
3. Drive the movement from the hips, not the waist.
4. Move slowly and stay controlled throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
2. Step forward with the right foot and lower into a lunge until the left knee hovers just above the floor.
3. Keep the right knee over the right ankle.
4. Push through the right heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat with the left leg, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the torso upright and core braced.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
3. Move at a steady, controlled pace for balance.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
2. Step forward with the right foot and lower into a lunge until the left knee hovers just above the floor.
3. Pulse up and down a few centimetres for 2-3 small reps, keeping tension on the legs.
4. Push through the right heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat with the left leg, alternating each set.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
2. Keep the pulses small and controlled.
3. Keep the torso upright and core braced.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
2. Step forward with your right foot and lower into a lunge until both knees bend about 90 degrees and your left knee hovers just above the floor.
3. As you lunge, press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Push through your right heel to stand, lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
5. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front shin vertical so the knee tracks over the ankle.
2. Brace your core to stay stable while the weights are overhead.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move at a controlled pace to keep your balance.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with knees slightly bent for stability and support your head with your lower hand.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, keeping the upper arm against your side and the elbow bent 90 degrees.
3. Start with your forearm across your abdomen.
4. Rotate your shoulder to lift the dumbbell until the forearm points toward the ceiling, keeping the elbow pinned to your side.
5. Slowly lower back to the start with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm glued to your side to isolate the rotation.
2. Use a light weight, as these are small stabilizing muscles.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weight.
4. Exhale as you rotate up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, forearm parallel to the floor, and support that elbow with your free hand.
3. Keep the upper arm still and extend your elbow to lift the dumbbell toward the ceiling.
4. Lower the dumbbell back with control until the forearm is parallel to the floor again.
5. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm vertical and stationary so only the elbow moves.
2. Support the working elbow with your free hand for stability.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the triceps.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with your legs bent and feet on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang straight down from your shoulder, and hold the bench with your free hand.
3. Keep your elbow slightly bent and raise the dumbbell out to the side up to shoulder level.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
5. Slowly lower the dumbbell back down with control.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and avoid using momentum.
2. Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbow throughout.
3. Squeeze the rear shoulder and shoulder blade at the top.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with knees bent and feet flat, supporting your head with your lower hand.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with the elbow resting on your side, bent 90 degrees, and the palm facing your head.
3. Slowly rotate your forearm, turning your palm down toward your knees, keeping the upper arm and elbow still.
4. Rotate back to the start with control.
5. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm and elbow fixed against your side.
2. Use a light weight to protect the wrist and elbow.
3. Move slowly through the full rotation.
4. Exhale as you pronate, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging straight down.
2. Keep your chest pressed to the bench and your head neutral.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your ribs, flaring your elbows out and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms hang straight.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows and drive them up and back to hit the rear delts.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Keep your chest down and do not lift your torso off the bench.
4. Use a controlled tempo instead of swinging the weights.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging straight down, palms facing each other.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are level with your torso.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the rear delts.
2. Keep your neck neutral and your chest on the bench.
3. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the rear delts.
4. Use light weight and a slow tempo to avoid swinging.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging down by your sides, palms facing forward.
2. Keep your upper arms still against your sides.
3. Curl the dumbbells up by bending your elbows, supinating so your palms face you.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Let the dumbbells fully stretch the biceps at the bottom.
3. Supinate the wrist fully for a stronger peak contraction.
4. Use a controlled tempo with no momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended over your chest, palms facing each other.
2. Keep your upper arms vertical and still.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
4. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Lower under control to feel the stretch in the triceps.
3. Keep your wrists neutral throughout.
4. Tuck your elbows in rather than letting them flare wide.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended over your chest, palms facing each other.
3. Keep your upper arms still and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
4. Stop when your upper arms touch the floor.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed and only move your forearms.
2. Use the floor to limit the range and protect your elbows.
3. Keep your wrists neutral throughout.
4. Control the lowering phase instead of dropping the weights.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet close together, about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower your body.
4. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up and straighten your legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep weight on your heels and mid-foot, not your toes.
2. Track your knees over your toes, do not let them cave inward.
3. Breathe in on the way down, breathe out as you stand up.
4. Keep your torso upright to emphasize the quads.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand over your chest with a slight bend in the elbow, palm facing inward.
3. Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc until your upper arm touches the floor.
4. Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbell back over your chest in the same arc.
5. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbow throughout.
2. Keep your back flat on the floor.
3. Brace your core to resist your torso rotating toward the working side.
4. Lead the movement with your chest, not your shoulder.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with your legs straight.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended straight up, palm facing forward.
3. Bend your elbow and lower until your upper arm touches the floor, keeping the elbow about 45 degrees from your body.
4. Press the dumbbell back up by extending your elbow.
5. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and supported on the floor.
2. Brace your core to resist your torso rotating toward the working side.
3. Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.
4. Drive through the heel of your hand on the press.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand by your side, palm facing your thigh.
2. Keeping your arm nearly straight, lift the dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height with your palm facing down.
3. Pause briefly at the top.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to your side.
5. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Do not swing or use momentum to lift the weight.
2. Brace your core to resist your torso rotating toward the working side.
3. Stop the lift at shoulder height.
4. Lower the dumbbell under control.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench and place your upper arm flat on the arm pad, holding a dumbbell in a neutral grip, palm facing inward.
2. Keep your elbow pressed against the pad.
3. Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder by bending your elbow.
4. Squeeze at the top.
5. Slowly lower the dumbbell until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm pressed firmly against the pad.
2. Move slowly and under control through the full range.
3. Do not swing or use momentum.
4. Keep your wrist neutral and firm throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand in a split stance, left foot forward, and lean your torso forward to near parallel with the floor.
2. Rest your left hand on your left knee for support and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
3. Pin your right upper arm against your side, parallel to the floor, with the forearm hanging down.
4. Extend your elbow to drive the dumbbell back until the arm is fully straight.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm fixed and only move the forearm.
2. Move slowly and squeeze the triceps at full extension.
3. Brace your core to stop the torso twisting.
4. Do not swing or use momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing in.
2. Place your other hand on your hip.
3. Keep a slight bend in the working elbow.
4. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until the arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
2. Keep the torso upright and do not lean toward the weight.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging.
4. Stop at shoulder height.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your hip.
2. Place your other hand on your hip for balance.
3. Keep a slight bend in the working elbow.
4. Sweep the dumbbell up and across your body in a wide arc to chest height.
5. Squeeze the chest at the top, then lower under control. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow bend fixed through the arc.
2. Drive the movement from the chest, not the hand.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Keep the torso upright and core braced.

instructions:
1. Sit at a preacher bench with one arm over the pad, holding a dumbbell in an overhand grip.
2. Press the back of your upper arm into the pad.
3. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder by bending the elbow.
4. Squeeze at the top, keeping the wrist firm.
5. Lower under control until the arm is straight. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm flat on the pad to isolate the forearm.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep the wrist locked in the overhand position.
4. Do not let the shoulder lift to help.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm facing down.
2. Hold a dumbbell in an overhand grip with the wrist past the knee.
3. Let the wrist drop so the dumbbell lowers toward the floor.
4. Raise the dumbbell by extending the wrist as high as possible.
5. Lower under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearm pinned to the thigh and only move the wrist.
2. Use the full range, down and up.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Use a lighter weight to keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Stand beside a rack and place your left hand on it for support.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip, arm hanging straight down.
3. Step your right foot back, bend the knees slightly and hinge forward with a flat back.
4. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, driving your elbow back and close to your body.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until the arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders square to the floor and do not rotate your torso.
2. Drive the elbow back and down to load the lats, not the arm.
3. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the shoulder blade.
4. Breathe out as you pull, breathe in as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip.
3. Rest your right forearm on your right thigh so the wrist extends past the knee.
4. Curl the dumbbell up by flexing the wrist and squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control by extending the wrist.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearm pinned to the thigh and move only at the wrist.
2. Use a slow, controlled tempo without momentum.
3. Allow a full stretch at the bottom of each rep.
4. Breathe out as you curl up, breathe in as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell on the floor between them.
2. Hinge down and grasp the dumbbell with your right hand, back flat and core tight.
3. Drive through the floor and explosively extend the hips, knees and ankles.
4. Pull the dumbbell up close to your body and shrug as it rises.
5. Punch your hand up to catch the dumbbell overhead with a straight arm.
6. Lower under control to the floor and repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power from the hips and legs, not the arm.
2. Keep the dumbbell close to your body as it travels up.
3. Keep the back flat throughout the lift.
4. Exhale on the drive up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and press the arm straight overhead.
3. Place your left hand on your hip for support.
4. Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping the upper arm still.
5. Extend the arm back to straight and squeeze the triceps.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow pointing forward and close to your head.
2. Move only at the elbow and keep the upper arm fixed.
3. Control the lowering phase for a full triceps stretch.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench with feet firmly on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand pressed straight above the shoulder, palm facing forward.
3. Lower the dumbbell out and down with the elbow wide until it drops below chest level.
4. Press the dumbbell back up over the shoulder and squeeze the chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow flared to load the chest with the wide path.
2. Keep the wrist straight and stacked over the elbow.
3. Brace the core to stay stable against the one-sided load.
4. Lower under control for a full chest stretch.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with the palm facing up.
3. Rest the forearm on the thigh so the wrist hangs just past the knee.
4. Curl the dumbbell up by flexing the wrist as high as possible.
5. Lower the dumbbell slowly by extending the wrist fully, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearm pressed against the thigh and still.
2. Move only the wrist, not the elbow.
3. Lower under control with no swinging.
4. Let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips at the bottom for a full range.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench and rest the back of one upper arm on the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell with an underhand grip, palm facing up.
3. Curl the dumbbell up toward the shoulder, keeping the upper arm still.
4. At the top, rotate the wrist to face the palm down.
5. Lower the dumbbell slowly with the overhand grip, then rotate back to palm up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm flat on the pad throughout.
2. Rotate the wrist slowly and fully at the top.
3. Use a lighter weight to control the pronated lowering.
4. Resist the descent on the eccentric to load the forearms.

instructions:
1. Kneel in front of a bench and lay both forearms across it.
2. Hold the dumbbells with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
3. Let the wrists hang just off the edge so the dumbbells drop.
4. Raise the dumbbells by extending the wrists upward as high as possible.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly by dropping the wrists fully.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearms flat and still on the bench.
2. Move only the wrists.
3. Lift and lower under control with no jerking.
4. Use a lighter weight than a palms-up wrist curl.

instructions:
1. Kneel in front of a bench and lay both forearms across it.
2. Hold the dumbbells with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
3. Let the wrists hang just off the edge so the dumbbells drop.
4. Raise the dumbbells by flexing the wrists upward as high as possible.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly by extending the wrists fully.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearms flat and still on the bench.
2. Move only the wrists.
3. Let the dumbbells roll to the fingertips at the bottom for full range.
4. Lift and lower under control with no jerking.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with the back supported.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands and press it fully overhead.
3. Bend the elbows to lower the dumbbell behind the head until the forearms are about parallel to the floor.
4. Press the dumbbell back up by straightening the elbows.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows pointed forward and close to the head.
2. Keep the upper arms vertical and still.
3. Lower under control to feel the stretch on the triceps.
4. Grip the dumbbell firmly for stability.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one dumbbell with both hands.
2. Press the dumbbell overhead until your arms are straight.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Lower until your forearms pass parallel to the floor.
5. Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbell back overhead.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointed forward and close to your head.
2. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
3. Brace your core so your lower back does not arch.
4. Lower under control to feel a stretch in the long head.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Press the dumbbells overhead with arms straight and palms facing each other.
3. Step forward with one foot and lower your hips until both knees bend about 90 degrees.
4. Keep the back knee just above the floor and the dumbbells locked overhead.
5. Push through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbells stacked over your shoulders the whole time.
2. Keep your torso upright and ribs down.
3. Drive through the front heel, not the toes.
4. Brace your core to resist tipping side to side.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands and press your arms straight overhead.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper body up into a seated position.
4. Keep the dumbbell directly overhead, in line with your shoulders.
5. Lower your upper body back to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbell stacked over your shoulders, not drifting forward.
2. Lift with your abs, not momentum.
3. Exhale as you sit up and inhale as you lower.
4. Start light to keep the overhead position stable.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench and rest your upper arm on the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell with an underhand grip and let your arm hang straight.
3. Curl the dumbbell up by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm on the pad.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully straight.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm flat on the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weight.
3. Straighten the arm fully at the bottom for full range.
4. Keep your shoulder relaxed and down.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor facing an exercise ball.
2. Lean forward so your chest rests on the ball and your upper arms lie across it.
3. Hold a dumbbell with both hands using an underhand grip.
4. Curl the dumbbell up by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms on the ball.
5. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower under control until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed into the ball to isolate the biceps.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your core tight to stay steady on the ball.

instructions:
1. Sit at a preacher bench and rest the back of your left upper arm flat on the pad, twisting your torso slightly to the right.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand with an underhand grip, arm hanging straight down.
3. Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm pressed to the pad.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm flat against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not use momentum; move slowly and with control.
3. Use a full range of motion at the bottom and top.
4. Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands at your chest.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. At the bottom, press the dumbbell forward to full arm extension, then bring it back to your chest.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes and do not let them cave inward.
2. Press the dumbbell in a straight line at chest height.
3. Brace your core throughout the movement.
4. Keep your chest up and back flat in the squat.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench with feet planted on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
2. Extend your arms so the dumbbells are above and slightly behind your head, upper arms angled about 45 degrees.
3. Keeping your elbows fixed, bend your arms to lower the dumbbells behind your head.
4. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back up to full arm extension.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only your forearms; keep your upper arms still.
2. Keep your elbows tucked and pointing forward.
3. Lower the weight under control and do not swing.
4. Use a weight you can fully extend with good form.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest first against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight down and palms facing forward.
3. Keeping your upper arms still, curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to maximize biceps tension.
2. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
3. Do not swing the weights or lift your chest off the pad.
4. Let your arms fully extend at the bottom for a full stretch.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest first against the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight down and palms facing each other.
3. Keeping your upper arms still, curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders with a neutral grip.
4. Squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your palms facing each other through the whole movement.
2. Move slowly and with control.
3. Do not swing the weights or lift your chest off the pad.
4. Keep your wrists straight and firm.

instructions:
1. Lie with your upper back on an exercise ball, feet flat on the floor, knees bent at 90 degrees.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plate, arms extended above your chest.
3. Lower your hips toward the floor while at the same time lowering the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
4. Drive your hips back up by squeezing your glutes while pulling the dumbbell back over your chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Keep your back firmly supported on the ball.
3. Do not lower the dumbbell past torso level to protect your shoulders.
4. Exhale as you extend your hips and pull the dumbbell back.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plate, arms extended above your chest.
3. Lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until your upper arms reach the floor.
4. Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
2. Exhale as you pull the dumbbell back over your chest, inhale as you lower it.
3. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
4. Use a weight you can control through the full arc.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
2. Bend your knees into a quarter squat, keeping your torso upright.
3. Drive explosively through your legs and press the dumbbells overhead, locking out your elbows at the top.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use leg drive to start the press, then finish with your shoulders.
2. Keep your core braced to transfer force from legs to arms.
3. Keep your torso vertical during the dip.
4. Use a weight you can control on the way down.

instructions:
1. Stand on your right leg with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your left hand, arm extended by your side.
2. Hinge at your hips, lowering the dumbbell toward the floor while raising your left leg straight behind you in line with your torso.
3. Continue until your torso is parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
4. Hold this position for the set duration.
5. Return to standing and repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at your hips, do not round your back.
2. Keep your shoulders back and chest lifted.
3. Keep your standing foot flat and weight balanced.
4. Keep a soft bend in your standing knee.

instructions:
1. Place your right knee and right hand on a bench, with your left foot planted on the floor and your torso parallel to the ground.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand with an overhand grip, arm hanging straight down.
3. Row the dumbbell up and out to the side, letting your elbow flare while squeezing your shoulder blade.
4. Hold briefly with your upper arm parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Flare your elbow out to the side to target the rear delts.
2. Exhale as you row up, inhale as you lower.
3. Use a controlled pace, do not swing the weight.
4. Keep your torso still and avoid rotating.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand behind your back, palms facing back.
2. Let your arms hang straight and keep your shoulders relaxed.
3. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
4. Squeeze the upper back at the top for a moment.
5. Lower the shoulders slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only the shoulders; keep your arms straight and elbows soft.
2. Do not roll the shoulders; lift straight up and down.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your neck relaxed throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
2. Hinge at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and let the dumbbells hang down.
4. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows to target the rear deltoids.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced throughout the hinge.
3. Do not swing or use momentum; control the weight.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
2. Step your right foot back and lower into a lunge, front knee over the ankle.
3. Lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
4. Push through the front heel to return to standing, bringing the back foot forward.
5. Repeat on the other leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
2. Push through the front heel to drive back up.
3. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on a step with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
2. Step your right foot back off the step and lower into a lunge.
3. Let the back knee drop below the level of the step for a deep stretch.
4. Push through the front heel to return to standing on the step.
5. Repeat on the other leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the step's added range to load the glutes and hamstrings more.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
3. Control the descent; do not drop into the bottom.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with each hand on a dumbbell, feet wide for stability, body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Row the right dumbbell up toward your hip, elbow close to your body.
4. Lower the dumbbell back to the floor with control.
5. Repeat with the left arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square; do not let them rotate as you row.
2. Spread the feet wider for a more stable base.
3. Press hard through the supporting hand to stay stable.
4. Exhale as you row, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie chest-down on an incline bench set near 45 degrees, feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down, palms facing each other.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed against the bench to stay stable.
2. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
3. Use a light weight and avoid swinging.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
2. Let the dumbbells hang by your sides.
3. Keep your upper arms close to your body and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight throughout the movement.
2. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
3. Use lighter weight than a standard curl since this grip is weaker.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing your body.
2. Step backward with your right foot and lower until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee is just above the floor.
3. Push through your left heel to return to standing, bringing your right foot back beside your left.
4. Repeat with the left leg, alternating sides.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot, not collapsing inward.
3. Drive through the front heel to engage the glutes and hamstrings.
4. Move with control to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing your body.
2. Step backward with your right foot and lower until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee is just above the floor.
3. Perform two small pulses by raising and lowering a few cm while holding the lunge.
4. Push through your left heel to return to standing, bringing your right foot back beside your left.
5. Repeat, alternating legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced through the pulses.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.
3. Drive through the front heel to load the glutes and hamstrings.
4. Keep the pulses small and controlled.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with your chest supported and forefeet on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down, arms hanging straight toward the floor.
3. Keep your upper arms still and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed against the bench to stop momentum.
2. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
3. Use lighter weight than a standard curl due to the reverse grip.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
3. Rest your forearms on your thighs so your wrists hang just past your knees.
4. Lower the dumbbells by letting your wrists drop down.
5. Raise the dumbbells by extending your wrists upward as far as possible.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weight.
2. Keep your forearms pressed flat against your thighs.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a light weight to feel the extensors work.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
2. Keep a slight bend in your knees and a neutral spine.
3. Hinge at the hips and push your hips back, lowering the dumbbells down the front of your legs.
4. Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, around knee level.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips, do not round your lower back.
2. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs throughout.
3. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your knees.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet lifted off the ground.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands at chest level.
3. Lean back slightly to form a V-shape with your torso and thighs.
4. Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the dumbbell beside your hip.
5. Return to center, then rotate to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine straight, do not round your back.
2. Move with control instead of using momentum.
3. Keep your feet steady and legs together.
4. Exhale on each twist.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees with upper arms near parallel to the floor.
3. Swing the dumbbells outward and up in an arc until your arms extend just above shoulder height.
4. Reverse the arc to bring the dumbbells back in front of your face.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows out to the sides to hit the lateral delts.
2. Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.
3. Use a light weight and high reps to control the arc.
4. Exhale as you press out and up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees with upper arms near parallel to the floor.
3. Swing the dumbbells outward and up in a wide arc until your arms extend just above shoulder height.
4. Reverse the full arc to return the dumbbells to the front of your face.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Trace a wide, smooth arc to keep tension on the delts.
2. Lead with the elbows out to the sides.
3. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Use a light weight to control the full path.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
2. Raise your right arm straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Lower your right arm back to the start with control.
4. Raise your left arm to shoulder height in the same way.
5. Lower your left arm back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
2. Do not swing your torso or use momentum.
3. Keep the wrist neutral and the dumbbell level.
4. Stop at shoulder height; no need to go higher.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
2. Press the right dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height with control.
4. Press the left dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
5. Lower the left dumbbell back to shoulder height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
3. Press in a controlled line without jerking.
4. Do not shrug the shoulders up toward the ears.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing forward, elbows out.
2. Press the right dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder level as you start pressing the left dumbbell up.
4. Press the left dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
5. Lower the left dumbbell back to shoulder level.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press in a controlled manner without jerking.
2. Keep the shoulders down; do not shrug during the press.
3. Brace the core to keep the torso upright.
4. Keep wrists stacked over the forearms.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor, holding one dumbbell with both hands behind your head.
2. Start with elbows bent and pointed up, upper arms close to your head.
3. Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbell overhead until the arms are fully straight.
4. Lower the dumbbell back behind your head with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows close to your head; do not flare them out.
2. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
4. Control the lowering phase for a full stretch.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with the balls of your feet on a weight plate and heels on the floor, feet hip-width apart.
2. Rest a dumbbell on each knee, holding them in place with your hands.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as possible.
4. Pause and squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels back down with control for a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the dumbbells balanced on your knees throughout.
2. Use a full range of motion, deep stretch at the bottom and full squeeze at the top.
3. Move slowly; do not bounce or use momentum.
4. Keep the balls of your feet firmly on the plate.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
3. Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, rotating your palms up as you bend your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top and hold for a second.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and do not swing.
2. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the biceps.

instructions:
1. Sit upright on a bench with your back supported and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs, palms facing back.
3. Raise both dumbbells in front of you with near-straight arms until they reach shoulder height.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Do not swing or use momentum.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the front delts.

instructions:
1. Sit upright on a bench with your back supported and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
3. Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your palms facing inward.
4. Squeeze at the top with your elbows close to your body.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the bench for stability.
2. Do not swing the weights or use momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lean forward from your hips with a straight back.
3. Raise your upper arms until they are parallel to the floor, elbows bent 90 degrees.
4. Extend your elbows to straighten your arms behind you, keeping upper arms still.
5. Squeeze your triceps, then bend your elbows back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and do not round your shoulders.
2. Keep your upper arms fixed in place.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
4. Use a controlled motion and squeeze the triceps at full extension.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift and lower with control, no momentum.
2. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
3. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the side delts.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
3. Rest your forearms on your thighs with wrists hanging just past your knees.
4. Curl the dumbbells up by flexing your wrists.
5. Hold briefly at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep forearms pinned to your thighs and move only at the wrists.
2. Use a full range of motion at the top and bottom.
3. Control the lowering phase, do not let the weight drop.
4. Use a weight that lets you keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing forward.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on the ball.
4. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stabilize on the unstable surface.
2. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep feet planted firmly for balance.
4. Move smoothly, do not swing or jerk the weights.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your right forefoot on a weight plate.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and rest it on your right thigh near the knee.
3. Push through your forefoot to raise your heel as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calf briefly at the top.
5. Lower your heel under control below the plate for a full stretch.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Use a full range, deep stretch at the bottom and full squeeze at the top.
2. Rest the dumbbell on the thigh, not directly on the knee joint.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
4. Keep your core engaged for balance.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the support pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms up.
3. Extend your arms over the pad so the dumbbells hang in front of you.
4. Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms on the pad.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep upper arms pressed into the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
3. Control the lowering phase, the stretch at the bottom is where the load is highest.
4. Use a weight you can curl without leaning back.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a reverse grip, palms facing your body.
2. Position the dumbbells near your shoulders with elbows bent and close to your torso.
3. Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead, keeping palms facing inward.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back firmly against the bench for stability.
2. Keep elbows tucked close to the torso through the press.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move under control, do not swing the weights.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat and legs spread.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with an overhand grip, palm facing down.
3. Lean forward and brace your right elbow against the inside of your right thigh, arm hanging straight.
4. Curl the dumbbell up by bending the elbow, keeping the palm facing down.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrist firm and straight to load the forearm.
2. Move only at the elbow, no swinging.
3. Use a lighter weight than a normal curl.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back supported.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
3. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back firmly against the bench.
2. Brace your core to stay stable.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep wrists stacked over your elbows.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
3. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back pressed against the bench.
2. Brace your core to stay stable.
3. The neutral grip is easier on the shoulder joint.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs, arms straight.
3. Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
4. Squeeze at the top for a moment.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and avoid momentum.
2. Lift straight up, do not roll the shoulders.
3. Keep your arms straight throughout.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand at your side, arm straight. Place your left hand behind your head.
