3. Bend slowly to your right, lowering the dumbbell toward the floor.
4. Bend as far as is comfortable, feeling a stretch in your left side.
5. Return upright with control. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
2. Bend straight to the side, not forward or back.
3. Keep your head and neck neutral.
4. Exhale as you bend, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet together, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Take a large step to the right, bending the right knee and pushing your hips back.
3. Lower until the right thigh is near parallel to the floor, keeping the left leg straight and the left foot flat.
4. Push through the right heel to return to the start.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back flat; do not round forward.
2. Sit your hips back so the working knee tracks over the foot.
3. Keep the trailing leg straight to stretch the inner thigh.
4. Push through the heel, not the toes.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet together, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step out to one side, bending that knee and pushing your hips back.
3. Lower until the working thigh is near parallel to the floor, keeping the other leg straight and its foot flat.
4. Push through the heel to return to the start.
5. Complete your reps on one side, then switch to the other.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and back flat; do not round forward.
2. Sit your hips back so the working knee tracks over the foot.
3. Keep the straight leg extended to stretch the inner thigh.
4. Push through the heel, not the toes.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet together, holding one dumbbell with both hands at your chest.
2. Step out to one side, bending that knee and pushing your hips back.
3. Lower until the working thigh is near parallel to the floor, keeping the other leg straight and its foot flat.
4. Push through the heel to return to the start.
5. Complete your reps on one side, then switch to the other.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hold the dumbbell tight to your chest to keep your torso upright.
2. Sit your hips back so the working knee tracks over the foot.
3. Keep the straight leg extended to stretch the inner thigh.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the weight.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side on a bench or the floor, legs stacked, lower arm supporting your head.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, arm resting along your side.
3. Raise the dumbbell toward the ceiling with a near-straight arm until your arm is roughly vertical.
4. Lower the dumbbell back to your side with control.
5. Complete your reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and keep a slight bend to protect the joint.
2. Move slowly to keep tension on the side delt and avoid swinging.
3. Keep your core tight so your torso does not roll back.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set up in a side plank on one elbow, elbow under the shoulder, body in a straight line.
2. Hold a dumbbell in the top hand, arm hanging down toward the floor.
3. Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
4. Raise the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc until your arm is near parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the dumbbell with control while holding the plank.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips lifted and body straight; do not let the hips sag.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades to drive the fly, not momentum.
3. Use a light weight so trunk stability stays solid.
4. Brace your obliques throughout to resist collapsing.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes slightly out, holding a dumbbell at your chest.
2. Shift your weight to the right leg, bend the right knee and push the hips back into a side squat.
3. Keep the left leg straight and the chest up.
4. Push through the right heel to return to center.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working knee tracking over the toes, not caving inward.
2. Sit the hips back rather than letting the knee drift forward.
3. Keep the chest tall and core braced for balance.
4. Exhale as you push back up to center.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended, palms facing forward.
2. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending the elbows.
3. Keep the upper arms still and squeeze the biceps at the top.
4. Lower both dumbbells under control to full extension.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms pinned to your sides; do not swing.
2. Drive the lift with the biceps, not momentum.
3. Lower slowly to load the muscle on the way down.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, elbow resting on the floor at about 45 degrees from your body.
3. Press the dumbbell straight up until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower under control until the elbow lightly touches the floor.
5. Finish all reps on the right, then switch to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrist stacked straight over the elbow.
2. Let the elbow tap the floor without bouncing.
3. Brace your core to resist rotation toward the loaded side.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with the elbow tucked close to your body and resting on the floor.
3. Press the dumbbell straight up until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower under control, bringing the elbow back to your side and touching the floor.
5. Finish all reps on the right, then switch to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow tucked tight to maximize triceps work.
2. Stack the wrist over the elbow throughout.
3. Brace your core to resist rotation toward the loaded side.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Press the dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
3. Keep the wrist straight and the dumbbell stacked over the shoulder.
4. Walk forward in a straight line, keeping the weight steady overhead.
5. Lower the dumbbell, switch to the left hand, and walk back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the biceps near the ear and the arm locked out.
2. Brace the core to stop the torso leaning to either side.
3. Take short, controlled steps.
4. Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Press the dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
3. Step forward with your right foot and lower until both knees bend to about 90 degrees.
4. Push through your front heel to return to standing, keeping the dumbbell locked overhead.
5. Finish all reps on one side, then switch arms and legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working arm locked out and the dumbbell stacked over your shoulder.
2. Brace your core to stop your torso leaning toward the loaded side.
3. Keep your chest up and front shin near vertical.
4. Inhale as you descend, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back, arms and legs spread wide in a star shape, dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Keep your left hand and right leg on the floor.
3. Brace your core and lift your left leg and right arm at the same time toward each other.
4. Reach the dumbbell toward your left foot and squeeze your abs at the top.
5. Lower under control to the start, finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your abs, not your neck.
2. Move slowly and controlled in both directions.
3. Keep the resting arm and leg pressed to the floor for balance.
4. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand using an underhand grip, palm facing forward.
2. Let the arm hang straight at your side.
3. Raise the dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height with a near-straight arm.
4. Pause when your arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower under control to the start, finish all reps, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbow.
2. Lift with the front shoulder, not a swing from the hips.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso still.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your right side to a wall, right hand on the wall, a dumbbell in your left hand.
2. Lift your right foot off the floor and balance on your left leg.
3. Press through the ball of your left foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
4. Pause and squeeze the calf at the top.
5. Lower the heel under control to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Move slowly and get full range at the top and bottom.
2. Keep your supporting knee straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
3. Stay upright and use the wall only for balance.
4. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
2. Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot slightly off the floor.
3. Hinge at the hips, extending your right leg straight behind you as the dumbbells lower toward the floor.
4. Keep a slight bend in your left knee and a straight line from head to right heel.
5. Drive through your left heel to stand back up, keeping the right foot off the floor.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and hinge from the hips, not the lower back.
2. Fix your eyes on a point ahead to hold balance.
3. Brace your core to stop your hips and torso rotating.
4. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
2. Extend your left leg straight, in line with your right thigh.
3. Drive through your right heel and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top and pause briefly.
5. Lower your hips with control, keeping the left leg extended. Switch legs after each set. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep shoulders, hips, and knee in a straight line at the top.
2. Drive through the heel to load the glutes.
3. Keep your core braced so the lower back does not arch.
4. Keep the pelvis level and avoid letting the working hip drop.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back to a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Rest the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
3. Keep your torso upright and bend your right knee to lower your body.
4. Lower until your left knee is just above the floor, keeping the right knee tracking over the foot.
5. Push through your right heel to return to the start. Switch legs after each set. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright to load the quads.
2. Lean the torso slightly forward to shift load to the glutes.
3. Keep the front foot flat and drive through the heel.
4. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.

instructions:
1. Stand on your right leg, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Lift your left leg off the floor and extend it straight in front of you.
3. Bend your right knee to lower your body, keeping the left leg extended off the floor.
4. Lower until your right thigh is parallel to the floor, keeping the knee aligned over the foot.
5. Push through your right heel to stand back up. Switch legs after each set. Repeat.
tips:
1. Start light or bodyweight to master balance before adding load.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
3. Fix your gaze on a point ahead to hold balance.
4. Keep the working knee tracking over the foot, not collapsing inward.

instructions:
1. Stand beside a lifting cage and hold the bar for support with your right hand. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand at your side.
2. Set your feet hip-width apart.
3. Lift your right leg off the floor and extend it forward.
4. Bend your left knee to lower your body as far as you can control.
5. Press through your left heel to return to standing. Switch sides after each set. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning forward.
2. Use the support lightly for balance, not to pull yourself up.
3. Move slowly and under control.
4. Keep the working knee tracking over the foot.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a sturdy platform, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Place your right foot fully on the platform.
3. Push through your right heel to drive your body up, bringing your left foot to meet your right.
4. Step down with your left foot, then your right, returning to the start.
5. Switch legs after each set. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a stable, secure platform.
2. Keep your chest up and shoulders back.
3. Drive through the heel of the working leg for stronger glute engagement.
4. Control the step down rather than dropping.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step one foot forward and the other foot back into a split stance, feet hip-width apart.
3. Lower straight down by bending both knees until the front thigh is parallel to the floor and the back knee hovers just above it.
4. Push through the front heel to stand back up to the split stance.
5. Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and brace your core throughout.
2. Drive through the front heel, not the toes.
3. Keep the front knee tracking over the middle of the foot.
4. Lower under control instead of dropping into the bottom.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep your chest up and brace your core.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
4. Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping weight on your heels.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up and squeeze your glutes at the top. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and weight on your heels.
2. Let your knees track in line with your toes.
3. Keep your chest up so the torso does not collapse forward.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing each other.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Drive through your heels to stand up.
4. As you reach standing, press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders and descend into the next squat. Repeat.
tips:
1. Time the press to start as your legs finish extending.
2. Brace your core to keep the torso upright during the squat.
3. Exhale as you press overhead, inhale as you squat.
4. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms facing each other.
2. Press the right dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height.
4. Press the left dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended, then lower it back.
5. Continue alternating sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to resist leaning or twisting toward the working side.
2. Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Press in a controlled line, not a jerk.
4. Exhale on the press, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing back.
2. Raise the right dumbbell straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Lower the right dumbbell back to your side under control.
4. Raise the left dumbbell to shoulder height, then lower it back.
5. Continue alternating sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a controlled motion and do not swing the weight.
2. Keep your torso still and avoid leaning back.
3. Stop the raise at shoulder height.
4. Keep a steady neutral neck, eyes forward.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand resting against the front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
2. Brace your core and keep a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Raise the right dumbbell straight in front of you until it reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower it back down with control.
5. Repeat with the left arm, then continue alternating.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and do not swing the weights or use momentum.
2. Keep your torso still and avoid leaning back.
3. Stop the raise at shoulder height.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand behind your neck, palms facing forward, elbows bent and flared out.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Press both dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to behind-neck height with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press only within a comfortable shoulder range to protect the joint.
2. Keep your core tight to stop your lower back from arching.
3. Move under control and do not bounce at the bottom.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, knees slightly bent.
2. Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
3. Tuck your upper arms against your sides with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
4. Extend both elbows to drive the dumbbells straight back until your arms are straight.
5. Bend your elbows to return to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and pinned to your sides.
2. Keep your back flat and do not round the shoulders.
3. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep your posture straight and core engaged.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Hold the top briefly and squeeze your calves.
5. Lower your heels back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid bouncing at the top or bottom.
2. Rise as high as you can onto your toes for a full contraction.
3. Keep your knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
4. Keep your torso upright throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand on a step with the balls of your feet on the edge and heels hanging off, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep your posture straight and core engaged.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Hold the top briefly and squeeze your calves.
5. Lower your heels below the step edge to feel a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Make sure the step is stable before you start.
2. Let the heels drop fully for a complete stretch each rep.
3. Move slowly and avoid bouncing.
4. Keep your knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Bend your knees slightly and lean your torso forward, placing your left hand on your left knee for support.
3. Let your right arm hang straight down.
4. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still.
5. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm fixed to isolate the biceps.
2. Lift and lower slowly with control.
3. Do not swing or use momentum.
4. Keep your back flat while leaning forward.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
2. Curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders.
3. Rotate your palms to face you at shoulder level.
4. Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
5. Reverse the press, rotate back, then lower to the curl and back to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and control the wrist rotation.
2. Keep your core braced and avoid leaning back.
3. Do not use momentum to drive the press.
4. Keep a slight bend in your knees for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down.
2. Let your arms hang straight in front of your hips.
3. Raise both dumbbells in front of you with arms straight.
4. Continue lifting until the dumbbells are above your head.
5. Pause briefly, then lower under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Brace your core and avoid arching your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
2. Let the dumbbells hang at your sides.
3. Drag the dumbbells up close to your torso by pulling your elbows back.
4. Continue until the dumbbells reach lower-chest level.
5. Squeeze, then lower under control to full arm extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drag the dumbbells up your body instead of curling them out.
2. Keep a neutral grip and the dumbbells close to your torso.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Bend your knees and hinge at the hips to lean forward.
3. Brace your right elbow against the inside of your right thigh and place your left hand on your left knee.
4. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control to full extension.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Isolate the biceps and keep your shoulder still.
2. Brace your elbow firmly against your thigh.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your back flat while hinged forward.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and stand behind it.
2. Drape your right upper arm over the top of the incline pad, holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip and arm extended.
3. Keep the upper arm fixed against the pad and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat, then switch to the left arm.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm pinned to the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not swing the dumbbell; move only at the elbow.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Use the same reps on both arms to balance strength.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Press the dumbbell overhead until the arm is fully extended, palm facing forward.
3. Keep the upper arm close to your head and stationary.
4. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending the elbow.
5. Extend the arm back to the top.
6. Repeat, then switch to the left arm.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm vertical and still; move only at the elbow.
2. Brace your core to stay upright.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the descent to protect the elbow.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
2. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
3. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. Keep wrists straight and stacked over the elbows.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Press in a straight vertical path.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at head height, palms facing each other.
2. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
3. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to head height under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to avoid arching your lower back.
2. The neutral grip is easier on the shoulders; keep wrists straight.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move under control to protect the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Stand behind a preacher bench, holding a dumbbell in one hand with a supinated grip.
2. Rest the back of your upper arm flat on the angled pad.
3. Start with the arm fully extended.
4. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, keeping the arm pressed to the pad.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control until the arm is fully extended.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm flat on the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Do not use momentum; move only at the elbow.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the bottom to protect the elbow.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip (palms facing back).
2. Let your arms hang straight at your sides and keep your upper arms still.
3. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping palms facing down.
4. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides.
2. Do not swing the weight or use momentum.
3. Keep your wrists firm and straight throughout.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward.
2. Let your arms hang straight at your sides and keep your upper arms still.
3. Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Pause and squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms close to your body and stationary.
2. Do not swing the dumbbells; move them under control.
3. Fully extend at the bottom for a complete range of motion.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip.
2. Let your right arm hang in front of your body and place your left hand on your hip.
3. Raise the dumbbell diagonally across your body toward your left shoulder, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Stop at shoulder height and pause briefly.
5. Lower the dumbbell slowly to the start, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced to resist rotation.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbow to protect the joint.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on your left foot with your right foot lifted off the floor, holding a dumbbell in one or both hands.
2. Keep your standing leg slightly bent and your torso upright.
3. Press through the ball of your left foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
4. Pause and squeeze your calf at the top.
5. Lower your heel under control to the start, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range of motion, lifting the heel as high as possible.
2. Do not bounce; move slowly and under control.
3. Hold a wall or rack for balance if needed.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in the calf.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands behind your head.
2. Bend your elbows so the dumbbell hangs behind your head, keeping upper arms close to your ears.
3. Extend your arms by pressing the dumbbell straight overhead.
4. Pause briefly at the top with arms straight.
5. Lower the dumbbell behind your head under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your ears.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso upright.
3. Move the dumbbell under control through a full range.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down and angled slightly wider than your shoulders.
2. Keep elbows pinned to your sides and upper arms still.
3. Curl both dumbbells up at the same time along their outward angle until they reach shoulder height.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower under control until arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep upper arms still; only the forearms move.
2. Do not swing or use body momentum.
3. Maintain the slight outward arm angle through the whole rep.
4. Exhale curling up, inhale lowering.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands using an underhand grip, palms facing forward.
2. Let arms hang straight down in front of your hips.
3. Keep upper arms and elbows still against your body.
4. Curl your wrists upward as far as possible toward your forearms.
5. Squeeze, then lower the dumbbell under control until wrists are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Only the wrists move; keep elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Use a full range of motion, letting the wrists extend fully at the bottom.
3. No momentum; keep the tempo slow and controlled.
4. Use a weight that keeps form clean.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with arms and legs spread wide in a starfish position, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Lift your right arm and left leg toward each other, crunching and rotating your torso to bring the dumbbell across toward your left foot.
3. Lower back to the spread position under control.
4. Repeat on the other side, lifting your left arm and right leg.
5. Continue alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from the core, not by swinging the limbs.
2. Rotate the torso so the obliques work, not just a straight crunch.
3. Keep the lower back from arching off the floor.
4. Exhale as you crunch, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step your right foot forward and your left foot back into a split stance.
3. Lower straight down by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nears the floor.
4. Push through your right heel to return to standing, keeping your feet in place.
5. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright through the whole rep.
2. Track the front knee over the foot, not collapsing inward.
3. Drive up through the front heel.
4. Keep the descent controlled, not a drop.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Place your right foot fully on the bench.
3. Push through your right heel to drive your body up, bringing your left foot up to meet it.
4. Step down with your left foot first, then your right, back to the start.
5. Finish all reps, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive with the front leg; do not push off the trailing foot.
2. Keep the whole front foot flat on the bench.
3. Stand farther from the bench to bias glutes, closer to bias quads.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping down.

instructions:
1. Stand in front of a bench, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Place your right foot flat on the bench.
3. Push through your right heel to stand up on the bench and drive your left knee up toward your chest.
4. Lower your left foot back to the floor, then step your right foot down.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the foot on the bench, do not push off the back foot.
2. Place your whole foot on the bench to stay stable.
3. Control the step down slowly.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
2. Keep your legs nearly straight with only a slight knee bend.
3. Hinge at your hips and lower the dumbbells toward the floor, keeping your back flat and the weights close to your legs.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat, do not round your shoulders.
2. Brace your core throughout to protect your spine.
3. Hinge from the hips, not the waist.
4. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended straight above your chest.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper back off the floor, pushing the dumbbell straight up toward the ceiling.
4. Keep your arms straight throughout.
5. Lower your upper back to the floor with control.
Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight, do not bend the elbows.
2. Push the dumbbell straight up, not forward.
3. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a light weight and move with control.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended straight above your chest.
3. Lift your upper body off the floor while twisting your torso to the right, bringing the dumbbell toward your right side.
4. Lower your upper body back to the floor with control, arms still extended.
5. Repeat the movement twisting to the left, alternating sides.
Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight, do not bend the elbows.
2. Use a light weight to keep control.
3. Exhale as you twist up, inhale as you lower.
4. Lead the twist with your core, not your arms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
2. Keep your legs straight but not locked.
3. Hinge at your hips and push your hips back, lowering the dumbbells toward the floor with a flat back.
4. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs and lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core throughout to support your spine.
2. Keep the dumbbells close to your legs.
3. Hinge from the hips, not the waist.
4. Keep your back flat, do not round it.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and extend your legs straight, raised just off the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest and lean back slightly with a straight back.
3. Rotate your torso to the right and move the dumbbell toward the floor beside your right hip.
4. Rotate back through the center, then rotate to the left and move the dumbbell beside your left hip.
5. Return to the center. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Lead the rotation with your obliques, not your arms.
2. Keep your legs raised and together for stability.
3. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you return to center.
4. Do not round your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
2. Keep your shoulders level and your posture upright.
3. Walk forward in a straight line, keeping the dumbbell close to your body.
4. Keep a neutral spine and resist leaning toward the loaded side.
5. After the set distance or time, switch the dumbbell to the other hand. Repeat.
tips:
1. Resist sideways bend; brace your core against the load.
2. Keep your shoulders level and do not let the loaded shoulder shrug.
3. Take even, controlled strides.
4. Use a weight that challenges your grip without breaking posture.

instructions:
1. Stand between two benches with a wide stance and toes pointed slightly outward.
2. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, letting it hang between your legs.
3. Lower into a wide squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes; do not let them collapse inward.
2. Keep your chest up and back straight.
3. Use the extra depth off the benches to load the inner thighs.
4. Drive through your heels, not your toes.

instructions:
1. Stand on a sissy squat platform with feet shoulder-width apart and lower legs secured by the pads.
2. Hold a dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
3. Lower your body by bending at the knees and leaning back, keeping hips and torso in a straight line.
4. Lower until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your knees to return to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips straight to load the rectus femoris in the stretch.
2. Move slowly and with control on the way down.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso and hips aligned.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest.
2. Press your palms firmly into the dumbbell to engage your chest.
3. Extend your arms straight out in front at shoulder height, keeping the dumbbell squeezed between your palms.
4. Pull the dumbbell back to your chest under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep constant inward pressure on the dumbbell to load the chest.
2. Press forward in a smooth, controlled line.
3. Keep your torso tall and core braced.
4. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest, palms facing forward.
2. Flare your elbows out and lower the dumbbells in an arc toward your chest.
3. Bring the dumbbells together just above your chest, elbows pointing out.
4. Press the dumbbells back up by extending your elbows to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
2. Move slowly and under control, no momentum.
3. Keep the dumbbells facing forward through the full range.
4. Use a moderate weight so the elbows stay stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, supporting your left hand on your left knee.
3. Raise your right elbow until the upper arm is parallel to the floor, forearm hanging down.
4. Extend your elbow to straighten the arm behind you, keeping the upper arm still.
5. Lower the dumbbell back under control, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm pinned and motionless throughout.
2. Move slowly and squeeze the triceps at full extension.
3. Do not swing the weight; drive only with the triceps.
4. Keep your back flat and core braced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Raise the upper arm until the elbow is level with the shoulder, bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing down.
3. Keep the elbow fixed and rotate the forearm upward until it points up.
4. Rotate the forearm slowly back down to the start, then switch arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light dumbbell to keep form clean.
2. Move slowly and control the rotation.
3. Keep the elbow fixed at shoulder height.
4. Drive the movement from the shoulder, not momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Raise the upper arm until the elbow is level with the shoulder, bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing down.
3. Keep the elbow fixed and rotate the forearm upward until it points up.
4. Rotate the forearm slowly back down to the start, then switch arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a light dumbbell to keep form clean.
2. Move slowly and control the rotation.
3. Keep the elbow fixed at shoulder height.
4. Drive the movement from the shoulder, not momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back, legs straight, holding a dumbbell with both hands and arms extended overhead on the floor.
2. Lift your legs, upper body, and the dumbbell at the same time into a V shape.
3. Reach the dumbbell toward your feet, keeping arms and legs straight.
4. Lower your legs, torso, and dumbbell back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms and legs straight to maximize the contraction.
2. Exhale as you fold up, inhale as you lower.
3. Move under control, no jerking or momentum.
4. Keep your lower back from arching off the floor.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees and point them out to the sides in a W shape, palms facing forward.
3. Brace your core and press the dumbbells overhead in an arc until your arms are extended.
4. Bring the dumbbells slightly inward at the top so they finish over the middle of your body.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to the W position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and ribs down to protect your lower back.
2. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.
4. Use a lighter weight and controlled tempo.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell vertically with both hands cupped under the top weight plate.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body.
3. Curl the dumbbell upward toward your chin by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move the weight with your biceps and avoid swinging.
2. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
4. Keep your wrists firm to hold the dumbbell steady.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward and arms extended at your sides.
2. Keep your upper arms still and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
3. At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly in this palms-down position.
5. Rotate your wrists back to palms-up at the bottom.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower the weight slowly to load the forearms on the way down.
2. Keep your elbows close to your body.
3. Make the wrist rotation smooth and controlled.
4. Use a lighter weight than a standard curl.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and upper arms resting on the pad.
2. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
3. At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly in this palms-down position.
5. Rotate your wrists back to palms-up at the bottom.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Lower the weight slowly to overload the forearms.
3. Use a full range of motion.
4. Make the wrist rotation smooth and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your body.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, letting your arms hang down.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, keeping your elbows close and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold the contraction briefly.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your spine.
2. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
3. Lead with your elbows and drive with your back, not your arms.
4. Brace your core to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
2. Bend knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Let the dumbbells hang straight down under your shoulders.
4. Pull the dumbbells toward your lower ribs, driving elbows up and back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and chest up; do not round your back.
2. Lead with the elbows to drive the back muscles, not the arms.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the dumbbells close to your body throughout.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank gripping a dumbbell in each hand, hands under shoulders, feet slightly wider than hip-width.
2. Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Row the right dumbbell toward your hip while balancing on the left hand and feet.
4. Lower the dumbbell to the floor under control.
5. Repeat the row with the left arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep hips level and resist twisting as you row.
2. Widen your feet for a more stable base.
3. Move under control; do not let the body rock.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top of each row.

instructions:
1. Place your left knee and left hand on a bench, back flat and near parallel to the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, arm hanging straight down.
3. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, driving the elbow up and back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control to full stretch.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and torso square; do not rotate the trunk.
2. Lead with the elbow to engage the back, not the biceps.
3. Control the lowering phase for a full stretch.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Bend knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Pin your upper arms to your sides, parallel to the floor, elbows bent.
4. Extend both elbows to straighten your arms behind you, squeezing the triceps.
5. Bend the elbows to return under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep upper arms still; only the forearms move.
2. Do not swing the weights; use strict triceps action.
3. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
4. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Squat down and place the dumbbells on the floor shoulder-width apart.
3. Jump your feet back into a plank, body in a straight line.
4. Jump your feet back to the dumbbells and stand, lifting the dumbbells.
5. Press the dumbbells overhead as you jump up, then land softly.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
2. Keep your core braced in the plank to prevent hip sag.
3. Use lighter dumbbells until the movement is smooth.
4. Keep the press tight overhead, not behind the head.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Let your arms hang straight down by your sides.
3. Swing both arms upward in a wide arc until they reach overhead.
4. Swing your arms back down to your sides in a controlled motion.
5. Keep the movement fluid and continuous.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
2. Keep movements smooth and avoid sudden jerks.
3. Increase the range of motion gradually as you warm up.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand next to a wall and place your right hand on it for support.
2. Set your feet hip-width apart and keep your left leg straight but not locked.
3. Swing your left leg forward as high as your flexibility allows.
4. Swing the same leg backward in a controlled motion.
5. Continue swinging fluidly, then switch sides and repeat with the right leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
2. Control the swing rather than throwing the leg.
3. Build range of motion gradually as muscles warm up.
4. Keep the support hand light for balance only.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bring both arms behind your back and interlace your fingers.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your hands away from your hips.
4. Push your chest forward and up to deepen the stretch.
5. Hold, then return to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged to support the lower back.
2. Only lift the arms as far as is comfortable.
3. Keep your chin level and shoulders down away from your ears.
4. Breathe out as you deepen the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand or sit with your upper arm fixed and elbow bent.
2. Keep your upper arm still throughout the movement.
3. Straighten your elbow fully to extend the forearm.
4. Lower back to the bent starting position under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm stationary so only the elbow moves.
2. Move through a full range of motion.
3. Control the lowering phase.
4. Brace your core for stability.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend both arms in front of you at hip level with elbows straight.
3. Cross one hand over the other with palms open.
4. Bend your wrists upward, then extend them back down.
5. Continue the wrist curl and extension, then switch hand positions and repeat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows straight so the forearms do the work.
2. Minimize shoulder involvement.
3. Move slowly and under control.
4. Train both hand positions for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand next to a wall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your arm straight back behind you and place your palm flat on the wall at shoulder height.
3. Keep the elbow fully straight and the palm pressed to the wall.
4. Slowly rotate your torso away from the wall until you feel a stretch in the biceps and forearm.
5. Hold 15 to 30 seconds, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow locked straight to maximize the biceps stretch.
2. Turn the body away gradually, never forcing the shoulder.
3. Breathe slowly and stay relaxed through the hold.
4. Stretch both arms equally for balance.

instructions:
1. Lie face up on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Bend your elbows and tuck them close to your sides, palms down near your hips.
3. Press through your forearms and elbows to lift your upper back and torso off the floor.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower under control back to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement by retracting the shoulder blades, not by arching the neck.
2. Keep the elbows close to the body to load the upper back and triceps.
3. Move slowly and with control in both directions.
4. Keep the core braced to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Press down through your forearms to lift your hips upward.
3. Continue pressing until your torso forms a straight, stable line.
4. Hold briefly while bracing the core.
5. Lower your hips back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press the floor away through the forearms to engage the core fully.
2. Keep the hips level and avoid sagging or piking.
3. Use a non-slip surface to keep the forearms stable.
4. Breathe steadily and move with control.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Place your right hand on the floor and press up.
3. Place your left hand down to reach a high plank with arms extended.
4. Lower your right forearm back down, then your left, to return to the forearm plank.
5. Alternate the leading arm each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the hips square and avoid rotating side to side.
2. Brace the core hard throughout the transitions.
3. Place the hands directly under the shoulders when pressing up.
4. Use a non-slip surface and move with control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Reach both hands behind you and place them on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
3. Draw your elbows and shoulder blades together.
4. Gently push the hips forward and lean the upper body back until you feel a stretch across the chest and front of the shoulders.
5. Hold briefly, then return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the shoulder blades together to deepen the chest stretch.
2. Keep the core engaged and avoid overarching the lower back.
3. Lean back only as far as is comfortable.
4. Breathe deeply throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Place your hands on two elevated surfaces slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Set your feet together on the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the surfaces, keeping elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
4. Lower until your chest is level with your hands.
5. Press through your hands to extend your arms fully.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower under control to keep tension on the chest.
2. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared wide.
4. Keep your hips in line with your shoulders, do not let them sag.

instructions:
1. Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, heels hanging off.
2. Hold a stable surface for balance if needed.
3. Lower your heels below the step to feel a stretch in your calves.
4. Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
5. Lower your heels back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range, dropping the heels low and lifting high.
2. Keep your knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
3. Avoid bouncing or using momentum.
4. Make sure the step is stable before starting.

instructions:
1. Lie face down over an exercise ball with your hips on the ball.
2. Anchor your feet against a wall or stable surface for balance.
3. Place your hands behind your head with elbows pointing out.
4. Lower your upper body toward the floor by bending at the waist.
5. Lift your upper body until it forms a straight line from head to hips.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your back muscles, do not pull on your neck.
2. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you lift.
3. Keep your feet firmly anchored to stay balanced.
4. Do not overextend the back at the top.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball.
3. Continue until your back and shoulders drape over the ball.
4. Let your arms hang toward the floor and relax your spine over the ball.
5. Hold the stretch and breathe deeply.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet planted firmly for stability.
2. Use a fully inflated ball that supports your weight.
3. Relax and let your spine curve naturally over the ball.
4. Breathe slow and deep to ease into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Set your forearms on an exercise ball in a plank position.
2. Form a straight line from head to heels with your body.
3. Brace your core and roll the ball a short distance away from you.
4. Roll the ball back toward your forearms under control.
5. Keep your spine neutral throughout the motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push forward, inhale as you pull back.
2. Do not let your lower back arch or hips sag.
3. Move slowly to keep the ball stable.
4. Brace the core hard before each rep.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball in a split stance with your left foot flat on the floor in front and your right knee back.
2. Let the ball support your hips and keep your torso upright.
3. Lower your hips toward the floor until you feel a stretch in the front of your right hip and thigh.
4. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly into the stretch and stop at mild tension.
2. Keep your core braced so your lower back does not arch.
3. Breathe deeply and relax into the hold.
4. Use a firm, well inflated ball for stable support.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor in a tabletop position with an exercise ball at your right side.
2. Place your right hand on the ball with the arm bent.
3. Roll the ball forward, extending your right arm overhead and lowering your chest toward the floor.
4. Feel the stretch along your right side and back, and hold for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Roll the ball back and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips above your knees for support.
2. Sink your chest down to deepen the stretch along the lats.
3. Move slowly and stop at mild tension to protect the shoulder.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms at your sides, palms down, and heels resting on an exercise ball.
2. Brace your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels.
3. Bend your knees and roll the ball toward your glutes by pulling your heels in.
4. Keep your hips elevated throughout.
5. Slowly extend your legs to roll the ball back out.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips lifted the whole set so the hamstrings stay loaded.
2. Move slowly and with control to manage the unstable ball.
3. Exhale as you curl in, inhale as you extend out.
4. Squeeze your glutes to hold the bridge position steady.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and feet with arms and legs straight and an exercise ball under your hips.
2. Slowly lower your body onto the ball so it supports your hips and torso.
3. Let your back gently arch over the ball and feel a stretch in your lower back.
4. Hold for a moment, then return to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower onto the ball only as far as is comfortable.
2. Let your spine relax over the ball rather than forcing the arch.
3. Breathe deeply and steadily through each rep.
4. Use a well inflated ball for smooth, supported movement.

instructions:
1. Start on your hands and feet with arms and legs straight and an exercise ball under your hips.
2. Slowly lower your body onto the ball so it supports your hips and torso.
3. Let your back gently arch over the ball and feel a stretch in your lower back.
4. Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Return to the start and repeat.
tips:
1. Lower onto the ball only as far as is comfortable.
2. Relax your spine over the ball instead of forcing the arch.
3. Breathe deeply and steadily through the hold.
4. Use a well inflated ball for stable support.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with an exercise ball under your armpit and lower ribs.
2. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, foot flat on the floor for stability.
3. Extend your top arm along the line of your body and let your bottom arm rest over the ball.
4. Relax your torso over the ball until you feel a stretch along your side and lats.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe deeply and let your ribs sink over the ball as you relax.
2. Only stretch as far as is comfortable, no straining.
3. Keep your bottom hip and foot planted for stability.
4. Avoid arching your lower back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with an exercise ball under your armpit and lower ribs.
2. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, foot flat on the floor for stability.
3. Let your bottom arm rest over the ball and reach your top arm overhead along your body.
4. Relax your torso over the ball until you feel a stretch along your side and lats.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe deeply and let your ribs sink over the ball as you relax.
2. Reach the overhead arm to deepen the stretch through the lat.
3. Keep your bottom hip and foot planted for stability.
4. Avoid arching your lower back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms at your sides, palms down.
2. Place your left heel and calf on top of an exercise ball, with your right leg extended in line with your hips.
3. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from shoulders to left heel.
4. Bend your left knee to roll the ball diagonally toward your hips while raising your right leg up.
5. Extend your left leg to roll the ball back and lower your right leg, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control through each phase.
2. Exhale as you curl the ball in, inhale as you extend.
3. Keep your hips level and lifted to load the hamstrings.
4. Use a firmly inflated ball for stability.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, back straight.
2. Extend your right leg in front of you, heel on the floor, toes pointing up.
3. Hinge at your hips and lean forward with a straight back, reaching toward your right toes.
4. Feel the stretch along the back of your right thigh.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge from the hips, not by rounding your back.
2. Exhale as you lean forward into the stretch.
3. Only stretch as far as is comfortable.
4. Use a firmly inflated ball for support.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Roll forward until your upper back rests on the ball, shoulders and head relaxed, arms out for balance.
3. Bend your left leg with the foot flat on the floor for support.
4. Bend your right leg, placing the forefoot on the floor and the heel back, to stretch the front of the right thigh.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Tuck your tailbone and push your hips up to deepen the stretch.
2. Exhale as you sink into the stretch.
3. Only stretch as far as is comfortable.
4. Use a firmly inflated ball for support.

instructions:
1. Sit on an exercise ball and walk your feet forward until the ball supports your lower back and hips.
2. Set your feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart and place your hands behind your head.
3. Lean back over the ball to lengthen your abs into the start position.
4. Curl your upper body up by contracting your abs until your torso is near vertical.
5. Lower back over the ball with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your abs, not by pulling on your head.
2. Keep contact with the ball to protect your lower back.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Move slowly to avoid using momentum.

instructions:
1. Place an exercise ball between your lower back and a wall.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly in front of your hips.
3. Lower into a squat by bending your knees and hips, letting the ball roll up your back.
4. Stop when your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees stay over your toes.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Set your feet far enough forward that your knees stay above your ankles.
2. Keep your back flat against the ball.
3. Inhale as you lower and exhale as you push up.
4. Drive through your heels, not your toes.

instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
3. Press up explosively so your hands leave the floor or your body pushes up fast.
4. Land with soft elbows and absorb the impact.
5. Lower straight into the next rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the whole hand to generate power.
2. Keep your core braced so your hips do not sag.
3. Exhale hard on the explosive push.
4. Use a non-slip surface for safe landings.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet about 120 cm apart, right foot turned out 90 degrees and left foot slightly turned in.
2. Bend your right knee until it sits over your right ankle and your thigh is parallel to the floor, keeping your left leg straight.
3. Lean to the right and rest your right forearm on your right thigh.
4. Reach your left arm overhead to make a straight line from left hand to left foot.
5. Hold, then return to standing with control.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Keep your bent knee stacked over your ankle.
2. Press your back foot into the floor to stay stable.
3. Lengthen along your top side rather than collapsing into the lower arm.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand or sit with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Rotate your head toward your left shoulder, then drop your chin diagonally toward that shoulder.
3. Hold and breathe deeply to feel the stretch along the side of your neck.
4. Return your head to the neutral position.
5. Repeat the stretch toward the right shoulder.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders down and relaxed during the stretch.
2. Move into the stretch slowly and smoothly.
3. Only stretch to a comfortable range, never to pain.
4. Keep your back tall throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and core engaged.
2. Raise both arms overhead and interlock your fingers with palms turned up.
3. Reach upward, lengthening your spine toward the ceiling.
4. Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Slowly lower your arms back to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control through the stretch.
2. Breathe steadily, exhaling as you reach upward.
3. Lengthen the spine rather than arching the lower back.
4. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with a grip closer than shoulder-width, palms up, arms extended down.
2. Curl the bar up by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still and pinned to your sides.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top as the bar reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower the bar under control until the arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows fixed at your sides so the biceps do the work.
2. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the muscle.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. The close grip biases the long head, so keep the wrists neutral.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar at shoulder-width, palms up, arms extended down.
2. Curl the bar up by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still and pinned to your sides.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top as the bar reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower the bar under control until the arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows fixed at your sides throughout the curl.
2. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the muscle.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging the torso to lift the bar.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms up, arms extended down.
2. Curl the bar up by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still and pinned to your sides.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top as the bar reaches shoulder height.
4. Lower the bar under control until the arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows fixed at your sides through the curl.
2. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the muscle.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. The wide grip biases the short head, so keep the wrists steady.

instructions:
1. Attach an EZ bar to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms up, arms extended down.
3. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending the elbows, keeping the upper arms pinned to your sides.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top as the bar reaches shoulder height.
5. Lower the bar under control until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows fixed at your sides through the curl.
2. The cable keeps tension at the top, so squeeze hard there.
3. Control the lowering phase rather than letting the stack pull your arm down.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a cable crossover machine with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar on the low pulley with a wide underhand grip.
2. Keep upper arms still against your sides and let your arms hang fully extended.
3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending the elbows.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control until the arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows pinned to your sides so the biceps do the work.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging the bar.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar overhead with a narrow overhand grip and arms fully extended.
2. Keep the elbows close to your head and pointing up.
3. Lower the bar behind your head by bending the elbows.
4. Lower until your forearms are fully flexed.
5. Extend the elbows to press the bar back overhead.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows tucked close to your head throughout.
2. Move under control and do not use momentum.
3. Brace your core to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, holding an EZ bar at shoulder height with a close overhand grip and elbows pointing forward.
2. Press the bar straight overhead by extending the elbows.
3. Fully extend the arms at the top.
4. Lower the bar under control back to shoulder height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows in front of you to load the front delts.
2. Keep your back against the pad and core braced.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench holding an EZ bar with an underhand grip, palms up.
2. Rest your forearms on your thighs with the wrists just past your knees and let the bar hang down.
3. Curl your wrists upward as high as possible while keeping the forearms still.
4. Squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control until the wrists are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearms flat on your thighs the whole set.
2. Move only at the wrists, not the elbows.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo without swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip resting against your thighs.
2. Keep your arms nearly straight and core braced.
3. Raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height until level with the floor.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not swing or use momentum to lift the bar.
2. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the front delts.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with chest and hips on the pad.
2. Hold an EZ barbell with palms facing down, hands shoulder-width apart, bar near your shoulders.
3. Press the bar forward and slightly up until your arms are fully extended.
4. Pause briefly with arms straight.
5. Lower the bar back to your shoulders with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest and hips pressed to the pad throughout.
2. Move slowly to keep tension on the rear delts and upper back.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Do not swing or use momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ barbell with a close grip and palms facing up.
2. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
3. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
4. Lower the bar with control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Do not swing your torso to lift the bar.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the descent for full muscle tension.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ barbell at shoulder-width with palms facing up.
2. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
3. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
4. Lower the bar with control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides.
2. Do not swing or use momentum.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the lowering phase.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, arms at your sides.
2. Rapidly lift your feet up and down on the spot, staying on the balls of your feet.
3. Keep your core tight and knees soft to stay light.
4. Use your arms naturally for balance.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay on the forefeet for quick, light steps.
2. Keep a steady, fast turnover.
3. Hold a slight knee bend the whole time.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together, barbell resting across your upper back with an overhand grip.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat, keeping knees tracking over your toes.
3. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up, extending knees and hips.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet together for the full movement.
2. Keep your chest up and spine neutral.
3. Do not let your knees cave inward.
4. Brace your core before each descent.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced.
3. Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side until the thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Keep hips level and do not rotate the torso.
5. Lower the leg back down with control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the hip; keep the spine and torso still.
2. Squeeze the outer glute at the top of each lift.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Work on a non-slip surface for stable hand and knee contact.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced.
3. Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side until the thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Draw small controlled circles with the knee while keeping hips level.
5. Reverse the circle direction, then lower the leg and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the circles small and controlled to stay in the hip.
2. Do not let the hips tilt or the torso rotate.
3. Squeeze the outer glute throughout the circles.
4. Breathe steadily and avoid holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a fixed bar and grip it with both hands at about chest height.
2. Step back and bend your knees, keeping your arms straight.
3. Push your hips backward and let your upper body lean away from the bar.
4. Drop your chest down to deepen the stretch through the lats and shoulders.
5. Hold 15 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly.
6. Step forward to release. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move into the stretch slowly and avoid bouncing.
2. Only go as far as a comfortable stretch, never into pain.
3. Make sure the bar is secure and can hold your weight.
4. Keep the spine long rather than rounding the lower back.

instructions:
1. Set a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and attach a handle to each.
2. Lie back on the bench with feet flat on the floor.
3. Hold a handle in each hand with arms out to the sides and a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Sweep the handles up over your chest in a wide arc until they meet.
5. Squeeze the chest, then lower the handles back out with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in the elbows the whole time.
2. Drive the movement with the chest, not the arms.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you bring the handles together.
4. Keep shoulder blades pulled back and down on the bench.

instructions:
1. Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Run a resistance band under your upper back and hold a handle in each hand.
3. Bend your elbows so your upper arms rest on the floor at about 90 degrees.
4. Press the handles straight up until the arms are extended.
5. Lower the handles back until the upper arms touch the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
2. Pause briefly when the elbows touch the floor for control.
3. Choose a band tension that lets you keep clean form.
4. Drive through the chest while keeping the wrists stacked over the elbows.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides, palms down.
2. Place your hands under your hips for lower back support.
3. Lift both legs about 15 cm off the floor, keeping them straight.
4. Alternate kicking the legs up and down in small, controlled movements.
5. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your lower back into the floor to protect the spine.
2. Keep the kicks small and controlled rather than fast and loose.
3. Exhale steadily as you kick; do not hold your breath.
4. Lower the leg height if your hips take over from your abs.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under both feet.
2. Hold the handles with palms facing back and arms extended down in front of your thighs.
3. Raise your arms straight in front of you to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower your arms slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the shoulders, not momentum from the hips.
2. Keep wrists neutral to reduce strain.
3. Keep a slight knee bend for stability.
4. Control the lowering phase to use the band's tension.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
2. Let the barbell rest against the front of your thighs with arms extended.
3. Raise the barbell in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the barbell slowly back to your thighs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with the front shoulders, not by swinging the torso.
2. Keep the core braced to stop the lower back from arching.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
4. Stop at shoulder height; raising higher shifts load to the traps.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar with both hands, palms down, slightly wider than shoulders.
2. Start with the bar in front of your thighs and your back straight.
3. Raise the bar overhead and then behind your head, keeping the elbows bent.
4. Continue until you feel a stretch across the front of the shoulders and chest.
5. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral; do not arch the lower back.
2. Use a wider grip if the stretch feels too tight at first.
3. Move slowly and breathe deeply to relax the muscles.
4. Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder joint.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing each other.
3. Bend your knees and hinge at the hips to lower into a squat, pushing your knees out.
4. Lower until your thighs are just below parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up, extending hips and knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Track your knees over your toes; do not let them cave in.
2. Keep your chest up and back straight throughout.
3. Brace your core to support the spine under load.
4. Drive through the heels, not the toes, on the way up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand resting over the shoulders, palms facing forward and elbows pointing down.
2. Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
3. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat, pushing your knees slightly outward.
4. Descend until your thighs pass parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright; the front load helps you stay vertical.
2. Keep your elbows high so the dumbbells stay locked on your shoulders.
3. Track your knees over your toes and do not let them cave inward.
4. Breathe in as you descend and out as you stand.

instructions:
1. Start in a full planche with hands on the floor about shoulder-width apart and your body held parallel to the floor by your arms.
2. Extend your legs straight behind you and engage your core and glutes to hold a straight line.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your body toward the floor, keeping it horizontal.
4. Push through your hands to extend your arms and return to the planche.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your core and glutes to keep your body from sagging.
2. Protract your shoulders to keep the planche stable.
3. Use a firm, non-slip surface to protect your wrists.
4. Build the strength to hold a planche before adding the push-up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands on the handle.
2. Brace your core and keep your chest up.
3. Bend your knees and hips to lower into a squat.
4. Descend until your thighs reach parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the kettlebell pulled in close to your chest throughout.
