2. Track your knees over your toes and do not let them cave inward.
3. Keep your torso upright and brace your core against the front load.
4. Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the resistance band under both feet.
2. Hold a handle in each hand and place them against your shoulders.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat.
4. Hinge at your hips to lower your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
5. Drive your hips forward to raise your torso back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips, not the waist, and keep your spine neutral.
2. Keep a soft bend in your knees throughout.
3. Squeeze your glutes to finish each rep.
4. Exhale as you rise and inhale as you hinge.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a barbell resting across your upper back with an overhand grip.
2. Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat.
3. Push your hips back and hinge forward to lower your torso toward the floor.
4. Stop when your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
5. Drive your hips forward to raise your torso back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips, not the waist, and keep your spine neutral.
2. Keep a soft bend in your knees to protect your lower back.
3. Brace your core hard before each rep.
4. Exhale as you rise and inhale as you hinge.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with elbows bent.
2. Keep a slight bend in your knees and a flat back.
3. Hinge at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso toward the floor.
4. Stop when your torso is almost parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward to raise your torso back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and do not round your spine.
2. Hinge at the hips, not the waist.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands at chest height.
2. Keep a slight bend in your knees and a flat back.
3. Hinge at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso toward the floor.
4. Stop when your torso is almost parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Drive your hips forward to raise your torso back to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and do not round your spine.
2. Hinge at the hips, not the waist.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Position your shoulders under the pads and place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
2. Press your back flat against the backrest and release the safety handles.
3. Bend your knees to lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the platform.
4. Push through your heels to extend your legs and return to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout.
2. Track your knees over your toes.
3. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Jump both feet forward toward your hands into a squat position.
3. Jump both feet back to return to the high plank.
4. Keep your core braced and body straight throughout.
5. Repeat at a steady pace.
tips:
1. Keep your hands directly under your shoulders in the plank.
2. Brace your core to keep your hips from sagging.
3. Exhale as you jump forward, inhale as you reset.
4. Use a non-slip surface to keep your hands and feet stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of the resistance band.
2. Hold a handle in each hand with palms facing each other, arms extended down at your sides.
3. Curl both handles up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping palms facing each other.
4. Slowly lower the handles back to full arm extension.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows close to your body and do not swing.
2. Control the lowering phase against the band tension.
3. Squeeze at the top where band tension peaks.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the machine with your ankles under the leg pads and legs fully extended.
2. Hold the side handles to keep your torso stable.
3. Curl one leg by bending the knee and pulling the ankle toward your glutes.
4. Squeeze the hamstring at the top, then lower the leg with control.
5. Repeat, alternating legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips pressed into the pad through the whole set.
2. Drive the movement from the hamstring, not by swinging the leg.
3. Lower each rep slowly to keep tension on the muscle.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with feet flat and chest against the pad.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing up and rest your elbows on the pads.
3. Curl one handle up by bending the elbow toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower the handle with control.
5. Repeat, alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and pinned to the pad.
2. Keep your wrist neutral to avoid strain.
3. Control the lowering phase on every rep.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing down.
3. Press one handle forward by extending your arm.
4. Squeeze the chest, then return the handle with control.
5. Repeat, alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the pad through the set.
2. Drive the press with your chest, not just your arms.
3. Control the return so the chest stays loaded.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing down.
3. Press both handles forward by extending your arms.
4. Squeeze the chest, then return the handles with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the pad through the set.
2. Drive the press with your chest, not just your arms.
3. Control the return so the chest stays loaded.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing down.
3. Press one handle forward by extending your arm, keeping the elbow slightly bent at the end.
4. Squeeze the chest, then return the handle with control.
5. Repeat, alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the pad through the set.
2. Drive the press with your chest, not just your arms.
3. Control the return so the chest stays loaded.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the high row machine with your chest against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip one handle with an overhead reach, arm fully extended.
3. Pull the handle down and back toward your torso, driving your elbow low and squeezing your shoulder blade.
4. Pause briefly at the contracted position.
5. Slowly extend your arm back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed to the pad and back straight throughout.
2. Lead with your elbow to target the lats, not the biceps.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
4. Use a slow eccentric to keep tension on the back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both legs extended and arms at your sides.
2. Bend your right knee toward your chest until the thigh is vertical.
3. Interlace your fingers behind the thigh to support it.
4. Slowly straighten the right leg, extending the heel toward the ceiling until you feel the stretch.
5. Hold 15 to 30 seconds, then lower and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Keep the opposite leg flat on the floor.
3. Move slowly without bouncing.
4. Stretch only to mild tension, not pain.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both legs extended and arms at your sides.
2. Lift your right leg toward the ceiling, keeping it straight.
3. Hold the back of the leg with both hands, just below or above the knee.
4. Gently pull the straight leg toward your torso until you feel the stretch.
5. Hold 15 to 30 seconds, then lower and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the opposite leg flat on the floor.
2. Keep the lifted leg as straight as possible.
3. Move slowly and avoid sudden pulls.
4. Stretch only to mild tension, not pain.

instructions:
1. Place a sturdy chair behind you and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Kick up so your feet rest on the chair seat and your hips stack over your shoulders.
3. Brace your core to keep your body straight.
4. Bend your elbows to lower your head toward the floor under control.
5. Push through your hands to extend your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to prevent your lower back from arching.
2. Lower slowly and under control.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your elbows tracking slightly forward, not flared wide.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart and feet off the floor.
2. Brace your core and let your body hang straight.
3. Keeping your legs together, bend your knees and lift them toward your chest.
4. Raise your knees as high as you can while curling your pelvis up.
5. Slowly lower your legs back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Avoid swinging; use controlled movement.
2. Curl your pelvis up to engage the lower abs.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep a secure grip on the bar.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward.
2. Let your body hang straight with feet off the floor.
3. Brace your core, bend your knees, and lift them toward your right elbow while twisting your torso.
4. Raise your knees as high as comfortable.
5. Lower under control, then lift toward the left elbow. Alternate sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not swing; use controlled movement.
2. Exhale as you lift and twist, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep a firm grip on the bar.
4. Drive the twist from your obliques, not momentum.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Place your arms at your sides, palms down.
3. Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor and brace your core.
4. Reach your right hand toward your right heel by bending to the side.
5. Return to center, then reach your left hand toward your left heel. Alternate sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control.
2. Exhale as you reach, inhale as you return to center.
3. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
4. Keep your shoulders lifted the whole set.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to a high pulley on a cable machine.
2. Kneel facing the machine and hold the rope with both hands near your head.
3. Keep your hips fixed and brace your core.
4. Crunch your torso down by curling your ribs toward your pelvis, bringing elbows toward your thighs.
5. Return under control while keeping tension on the cable.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips still; flex only the spine.
2. Do not use momentum.
3. Exhale as you crunch, inhale as you return.
4. Keep constant tension on the cable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms raised to shoulder height in front, palms down.
2. Lift your right knee toward your left elbow while twisting your torso to the right.
3. Return to the start.
4. Lift your left knee toward your right elbow while twisting your torso to the left.
5. Alternate sides in a steady rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist and lift at the same time to engage the obliques.
2. Move smoothly to protect the back and hips.
3. Exhale on the twist, inhale as you return.
4. Keep your chest tall and core braced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Lift your right knee toward your chest while swinging your left arm forward.
3. Quickly switch, lifting your left knee while swinging your right arm forward.
4. Stay on the balls of your feet and keep a running rhythm.
5. Continue alternating knees while bracing your core.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your knees high while staying balanced.
2. Stay light on the balls of your feet.
3. Pump your arms to keep rhythm.
4. Keep your torso upright, not leaning back.

instructions:
1. Start on hands and knees with hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Step both feet back to extend your legs, coming onto the balls of your feet.
3. Form a straight line from head to heels with shoulders stacked over wrists.
4. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to stop your hips sagging or rising.
5. Hold the position with steady breathing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced the whole time to prevent the lower back from sagging.
2. Stack your shoulders directly over your wrists to spread the load evenly.
3. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor just ahead of your hands.
4. Breathe steadily instead of holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Attach a resistance band to a high anchor point.
2. Kneel facing away from the anchor and hold a handle in each hand near your head, elbows bent.
3. Keep your hips fixed and crunch your torso down toward your knees.
4. Pull your elbows toward your thighs by rounding your spine, not bending your hips.
5. Slowly return to the start while keeping tension on the band.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl the spine to bring the ribs toward the pelvis rather than folding at the hips.
2. Keep your hips stationary and avoid using momentum.
3. Exhale as you crunch down and inhale as you return.
4. Keep tension on the band throughout the range.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms reaching overhead.
2. Press your lower back flat into the floor.
3. Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor at the same time to form a shallow curve.
4. Brace your core and keep your lower back pinned to the floor.
5. Hold the position with steady breathing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the lower back flat against the floor; lift the legs less if it arches.
2. Lift shoulders and legs to a matching height for a balanced curve.
3. Bend the knees or lower the arms to make the hold easier.
4. Keep the neck relaxed and in line with the spine.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench at about 30 degrees between two cable stations with the pulleys low.
2. Grab a handle in each hand and lie back with feet flat on the floor.
3. Hold the handles out to your sides with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Sweep the handles up and together in a wide arc until they meet over your upper chest.
5. Squeeze your chest, then lower the handles back along the same arc with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows so it stays a fly, not a press.
2. Drive the movement with your chest by bringing the upper arms together.
3. Keep your back and head pressed against the bench.
4. Exhale as you bring the handles up and inhale as you lower them.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a bench and place your hands on its edge close together so thumbs and index fingers form a diamond.
2. Step your feet back to extend your legs and form a straight line from head to heels.
3. Brace your core to keep your body rigid.
4. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward your hands, keeping elbows close to your body.
5. Push through your hands to extend your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your body to load the triceps.
2. Move with control on the way down to keep tension on the muscles.
3. Keep your hips in line with your shoulders; do not let them sag.
4. Use a stable, non-slip bench so your hands do not move.

instructions:
1. Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline and sit back against it with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms facing forward.
3. Keep elbows back and still as you curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly to full arm extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Let the arms hang fully behind the torso to stretch the long head of the biceps.
2. Keep the upper arms stationary against the incline.
3. Lower under control instead of dropping the weight.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set a bench to a 45-degree incline and lie chest-first against it with feet planted on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms hanging toward the floor.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbows as you raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height.
4. Squeeze the rear shoulders at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the chest pinned to the bench to remove momentum.
2. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
3. Use a light weight and move slowly.
4. Avoid shrugging the traps up toward the ears.

instructions:
1. Place your hands on top of a sturdy box, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Step your feet back to form a straight line from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and lower your chest toward the box, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
4. Stop when your chest is near the box.
5. Push through your hands to extend the arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the body in a straight line, do not let the hips sag.
2. Use a box that will not slide or tip.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. The higher the box, the easier the movement.

instructions:
1. Place your hands on the seat of a stable chair, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Step your feet back to form a straight line from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and lower your chest toward the chair, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
4. Stop when your chest is near the chair.
5. Push through your hands to extend the arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a chair placed against a wall so it cannot slide.
2. Keep the body in a straight line, do not let the hips sag.
3. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move under control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs extended and arms at your sides.
2. Loop a strap around your right ankle and hold both ends in your hands.
3. Bend your right knee and pull the heel toward your glutes until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh.
4. Gently lift the right thigh off the floor to deepen the stretch in the hip flexor.
5. Hold the stretch, then release and switch to the left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe slowly and ease into the stretch rather than forcing it.
2. Keep the hips pressed into the floor for the quad stretch, then lift the thigh for the hip flexor.
3. Keep the head and neck neutral, looking down.
4. Use a longer strap if you cannot reach the ankle comfortably.

instructions:
1. Set the Smith machine bar at about waist height and lock it.
2. Lie on your back under the bar with legs extended and heels on the floor.
3. Grip the bar overhand, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
4. Keep your body straight from head to heels and pull your chest toward the bar.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
6. Lower with control until arms are straight. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement by squeezing your shoulder blades together, not just bending your arms.
2. Keep your hips up so your body stays in a straight line.
3. Raise the bar to make it easier or lower it to make it harder.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms out to the sides in a T-shape and legs extended.
2. Lift your right leg toward the ceiling, keeping it straight.
3. Lower the leg across your body toward your left hand, keeping both shoulders flat on the floor.
4. Let the leg drop as far as is comfortable, feeling a stretch in the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
5. Hold, then return to the start. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Stretch only as far as is comfortable, never to the point of pain.
2. Keep both shoulders pressed to the floor to target the spine and glutes.
3. Use a mat for comfort.
4. Bend the knee slightly if flexibility is limited.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip both handles with palms facing forward.
3. Press both handles up until your arms are nearly straight.
4. Lower the handles with control back to shoulder level. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the pad throughout.
2. Drive through your shoulders rather than letting your chest take over.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move smoothly and avoid swinging the weight.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms stretched overhead.
2. Lift your upper body and legs at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet.
3. Form a V-shape with your body at the top.
4. Lower your torso and legs with control back to the floor. Repeat.
tips:
1. Bend your knees slightly if the full movement is too hard.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Move with control instead of using momentum.
4. Keep your lower back from arching off the floor.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Lower into a squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
3. Explosively jump up, extending your legs fully and swinging your arms for momentum.
4. Land softly with knees bent and hips back, returning to the squat. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
3. Move explosively on the way up but control the landing.
4. Keep your chest up and core braced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Jump your feet out wider than shoulder-width while raising your arms overhead.
3. Form an X shape at the top with arms up and feet apart.
4. Jump your feet back together and lower your arms to the sides.
5. Land softly with a slight knee bend.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the knees to absorb landing impact.
2. Land on the balls of the feet, not flat.
3. Raise the arms to full overhead range each rep.
4. Keep the movement light and rhythmic.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, holding a kettlebell in each hand.
2. Place the top of your right foot on the bench behind you.
3. Lower your body by bending your left knee until the left thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your torso upright and your weight on the left heel.
5. Press through the left heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
2. Lower under control; do not drop into the bottom.
3. Keep the front shin near vertical.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench, holding a kettlebell in each hand.
2. Place the top of your left foot on the bench behind you.
3. Lower your body by bending your right knee until the right thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Keep your torso upright and your weight on the right heel.
5. Press through the right heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
2. Lower under control; do not drop into the bottom.
3. Keep the front shin near vertical.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your right knee on the floor and your left foot flat in front, knee at 90 degrees.
2. Rack a kettlebell at your right shoulder with the elbow bent and wrist straight.
3. Press the kettlebell straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
5. Lower the kettlebell back to the shoulder under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrist straight and the kettlebell resting on the forearm.
2. Press in a straight line over the shoulder.
3. Brace the core to stop the torso from leaning.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel on both knees with your torso upright.
2. Rack a kettlebell at your right shoulder with the elbow bent and wrist straight.
3. Press the kettlebell straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Keep your spine neutral and core braced.
5. Lower the kettlebell back to the shoulder under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the wrist straight and the kettlebell resting on the forearm.
2. Press in a straight line over the shoulder.
3. Squeeze the glutes to keep the hips stable.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides with arms straight.
2. Keep your arms fully extended and brace your core.
3. Raise both kettlebells out to the sides until your arms reach shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebells under control back to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms straight to maximise the long lever and load the side delts.
2. Use lighter weight, as the long lever greatly increases difficulty.
3. Raise smoothly without swinging or using momentum.
4. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the lateral delts.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height with elbows bent and palms facing inward.
2. Press the right kettlebell overhead while slightly leaning your torso to the left.
3. As the right arm lowers, press the left kettlebell overhead while leaning slightly to the right.
4. Keep both kettlebells moving in a continuous seesaw pattern.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press each kettlebell straight up without forward or backward drift.
2. Brace your core to resist side-to-side lean and stay stable.
3. Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Exhale as you press and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Hinge at the hips and grab it with your right hand.
2. Drive through your hips and legs to pull the kettlebell up, rotating your wrist to catch it in the front rack with elbow tucked close.
3. Press the kettlebell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
4. Lower it back to the rack, then return it to the floor.
5. Switch hands and repeat.
tips:
1. Generate the clean with an explosive hip drive, not your arm.
2. Keep the kettlebell close to your body as it travels up.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting during the single-arm load.
4. Keep your wrist straight in the rack and overhead.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell with both hands and arms extended toward the floor overhead.
2. Lift your right leg, keeping the knee bent at about 90 degrees.
3. Press through your left heel to raise your hips into a straight line from shoulders to knee, while pulling the kettlebell up and over to above your chest.
4. Lower your hips and return the kettlebell overhead together.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of the bridge.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and control the pullover arc.
3. Move the hips and kettlebell smoothly, not jerkily.
4. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you lift.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight on the floor, holding a kettlebell with both hands at your chest.
2. Brace your core and lift your upper body until your torso is vertical.
3. Press the kettlebell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the kettlebell back to your chest.
5. Lower your upper body back to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift and lower your torso with control, no jerking.
2. Keep your core engaged throughout for stability.
3. Choose a moderate weight to keep good form.
4. Press the kettlebell straight up over your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Stand tall holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides. Step one foot forward and the other back, resting on the ball of the rear foot.
2. Bend both knees to lower straight down until the front thigh is parallel to the floor and the rear knee hovers above the ground.
3. Keep your torso upright and the front knee tracking over your foot.
4. Push through the front heel to drive back up and extend both legs.
5. Finish all reps on one side, switch legs, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and core braced to avoid leaning forward.
2. Keep the front knee in line with the toes, not collapsing inward.
3. Move straight up and down rather than pushing the front knee far forward.
4. Use a stance length that lets both knees bend to about 90 degrees.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
2. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
3. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping knees tracking over your toes.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up and fully extend your legs.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees in line with your toes to prevent inward collapse.
2. Inhale as you lower and exhale as you drive up.
3. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.
4. Press through the heels to engage glutes and quads.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell at shoulder height with the bell balanced upside down over your fist. Keep your wrist straight.
2. Brace your core and grip the handle hard to keep the bell stable.
3. Press the kettlebell straight overhead until your arm is fully extended.
4. Pause briefly with the bell balanced over a vertical forearm.
5. Lower it back to shoulder height under control, keeping the bottoms-up position.
6. Finish all reps, switch arms, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Grip the handle as hard as possible to stabilize the bell.
2. Start light to master the balance and control.
3. Keep the wrist straight and the forearm vertical throughout.
4. Brace your core to resist leaning to the side.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell racked at one shoulder. The bell rests against the back of your wrist with the palm facing in and the elbow down.
2. Brace your core and keep your wrist straight.
3. Press the kettlebell straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the kettlebell back to the racked position under control.
5. Finish all reps, switch arms, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a neutral wrist to avoid strain.
2. Press without using leg drive or momentum.
3. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
4. Brace your core to resist leaning away from the load.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell at your side in one hand with the arm extended.
2. Brace your core to keep your torso level against the offset load.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up, keeping your back straight.
5. Finish all reps, switch the kettlebell to the other hand, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso square and avoid leaning toward the weighted side.
2. Keep the knees tracking over the toes.
3. Brace the core hard to resist sideways bending.
4. Use a weight that lets you keep your shoulders level.

instructions:
1. Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grasp the handle with both hands. Keep your back flat and chest up.
3. Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees together to stand tall.
4. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to lower the kettlebell back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your knees out over your toes, do not let them cave inward.
2. Keep the kettlebell close to your body throughout the lift.
3. Brace your core before each rep to protect your spine.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.

instructions:
1. Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grasp the handle with both hands. Keep your back flat and chest up.
3. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand tall.
4. As you reach standing, explosively pull the kettlebell up toward your chin, leading with the elbows and keeping them high.
5. Lower the kettlebell back down and return it to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Let the leg drive feed power into the pull, do not yank with the arms alone.
2. Keep your elbows above the kettlebell during the high pull.
3. Keep the kettlebell close to your body.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand on two stepboxes with a wide stance, toes pointed slightly out. Hold a kettlebell with both hands so it hangs between your legs.
2. Bend your knees and push your hips back to lower into a wide squat. Let the kettlebell drop into the gap between the boxes.
3. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up and squeeze your glutes at the top.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your knees out over your toes, do not let them cave inward.
2. Keep your back flat and chest up, do not lean forward.
3. Keep your weight on your heels and midfoot.
4. Brace your core throughout the squat.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, with a kettlebell on the floor about 30 cm in front of you.
2. Hinge at the hips, bend the knees slightly, and grab the handle with both hands. Keep your back flat.
3. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs to load the hips.
4. Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, keeping your arms relaxed.
5. Let the kettlebell fall and hinge at the hips to guide it back between your legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Power the swing with your hips, not your arms.
2. Keep your back flat and do not round your shoulders.
3. Snap your glutes and brace your abs hard at the top.
4. Exhale as you swing up, inhale as it swings down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, with a kettlebell upright on the floor between your feet.
2. Hinge at the hips, bend the knees slightly, and grab the handle with both hands, interlocking your fingers. Keep your back flat.
3. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs to load the hips.
4. Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, keeping your arms relaxed.
5. Let the kettlebell fall and hinge at the hips to guide it back between your legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Power the swing with your hips, not your arms.
2. Keep your back flat and do not round your shoulders.
3. Snap your glutes and brace your abs hard at the top.
4. Exhale as you swing up, inhale as it swings down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing inward.
2. Bend your hips and knees to lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Drive through your heels to stand up.
4. As you rise, press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the kettlebells back to shoulder level.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the leg drive from the squat to help start the press.
2. Exhale as you press overhead, inhale as you lower into the squat.
3. Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, stance wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grasp one kettlebell in each hand, back straight and chest up.
3. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to lift the kettlebells.
4. As you reach standing, pull the kettlebells up toward your chin, leading with your elbows pointed out.
5. Lower the kettlebells back to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout the lift.
2. Let the leg drive power the pull, not just your arms.
3. Exhale as you lift and pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the kettlebells close to your body.

instructions:
1. Kick up into a handstand against a wall with hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your head lightly touches the floor.
3. Tuck your knees toward your chest to load the kip.
4. Drive your legs up explosively and press through your hands to extend your arms.
5. Finish in a full handstand with arms locked out.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Time the leg drive with the press so the hip extension assists the push.
2. Keep your core tight to hold a stable body line.
3. Look slightly forward to help balance against the wall.
4. Place a pad under your head if needed for safety.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both legs extended.
2. Bend your right knee and draw it toward your chest.
3. Wrap both hands around your shin and gently pull the knee closer.
4. Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds, keeping your left leg relaxed.
5. Release and switch to the left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull gently and steadily, never with a jerk.
2. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
3. Breathe slowly and deeply throughout the hold.
4. Stop if you feel sharp pain in the knee or back.

instructions:
1. Kneel with your right knee on the floor and your left foot in front, left knee bent to about 90 degrees.
2. Place your hands on your hips or your left thigh and keep your back straight.
3. Gently push your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of your right hip.
4. Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Return to the start and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee stacked over your ankle.
2. Tuck your pelvis slightly under to deepen the stretch.
3. Stay tall through your torso, shoulders relaxed.
4. Move slowly and avoid bouncing.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor in a tabletop position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Reach your right arm forward along the floor, palm up.
3. Sit your hips back toward your heels and press your chest down.
4. Feel the stretch along the right side of your back and hold for 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Return to the start and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Sit the hips back to deepen the stretch through the lat.
2. Keep the reaching arm long and relaxed.
3. Breathe slowly and let the shoulder ease down.
4. Use a mat for knee comfort.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the machine with one knee on the pad and the working leg secured under the roller.
2. Hold the handles and keep your back flat.
3. Curl the working leg up by bending the knee and driving the heel toward your glutes.
4. Squeeze the hamstring at the top.
5. Lower the leg under control to the start, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and back steady through the curl.
2. Drive the heel up rather than swinging the leg.
3. Exhale curling up, inhale lowering down.
4. Control the lowering phase fully.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with knees hip-width apart and sit back onto your heels.
2. Swing your arms back and brace your core.
3. Swing the arms forward and explosively drive your hips up off your knees.
4. Bring your feet under you and land in a squat with feet shoulder-width apart.
5. Lower back down to the kneeling start position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a hard arm swing to drive the jump.
2. Land softly on the forefeet with bent knees.
3. Keep knees tracking over the toes on landing.
4. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top of the drive.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with palms flat on the ground.
2. Rotate your hands so the fingers point back toward your knees.
3. Keep the palms flat and the elbows straight.
4. Slowly shift your weight back toward your heels until you feel the stretch in the wrists and forearms.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then ease forward to release.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the palms pressed flat through the stretch.
2. Shift back slowly to control the intensity.
3. Move hands closer to the knees if the stretch is too strong.
4. Breathe steadily and stay relaxed.

instructions:
1. Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine or corner.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the free end at chest level with one hand.
3. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
4. Press the bar forward and slightly up until the arm is fully extended.
5. Lower the bar under control back to chest level, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core tight to resist twisting toward the working side.
2. Drive the bar forward and up, not just up.
3. Exhale on the press, inhale on the return.
4. Keep the wrist firm and the shoulder down.

instructions:
1. Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or secure corner.
2. Stand over the bar with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
3. Hinge at the hips and grab the bar near the loaded end with a V-handle, arms extended.
4. Pull the bar toward your chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the bar with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and brace your core throughout.
2. Drive the elbows back to engage the lats and mid back.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the movement controlled, do not jerk the weight.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the bar with hands just closer than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended overhead.
3. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold the contraction briefly, keeping your back straight.
5. Return the bar slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back excessively.
2. Lead the pull with your elbows to target the lats.
3. The close grip increases biceps involvement, control the eccentric.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended overhead.
3. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold the contraction briefly, keeping your back straight.
5. Return the bar slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back excessively.
2. Lead the pull with your elbows to target the lats.
3. Control the bar on the way up, do not let it pull you out of position.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the bar with hands wider than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended overhead.
3. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Hold the contraction briefly, keeping your back straight.
5. Return the bar slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back excessively.
2. Lead the pull with your elbows to target the lats.
3. The wide grip increases rear delt and upper-back involvement.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, elbows slightly bent and palms facing down.
3. Hold the top position briefly.
4. Lower your arms back to your sides with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders down, do not shrug.
2. Lead with your elbows to target the lateral deltoids.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the muscle.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the middle of the band, holding a handle in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward.
2. Raise both arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Rotate your palms to face forward and bend the elbows to about 90 degrees.
4. Press the handles overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Reverse the motion back to shoulder height, then lower the arms to your sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid using momentum.
2. Choose a band tension that lets you control both phases.
3. Exhale as you raise and press, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
2. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Pause briefly with your arms parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to your sides with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not raise the dumbbells above shoulder height.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
3. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
2. Lean your torso forward toward the floor with arms hanging down.
3. Raise your torso to vertical while swinging both arms out to the sides to shoulder height, bending the elbows to about 90 degrees.
4. Pause briefly with your torso upright and arms parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the dumbbells and return your torso to the leaning start position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Do not raise the dumbbells above shoulder height.
2. Use a controlled swing, not heavy momentum.
3. Brace your core as you lift the torso.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your right side toward the cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart, with a handle attached to the low pulley.
2. Grasp the handle with your left hand across your body, palm facing inward.
3. Raise the handle out to your side until your arm is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Lower the handle back to the start with control.
5. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid swinging.
2. The cable keeps tension at the bottom, so move slowly there.
3. Lead with the elbow.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand next to a sturdy upright, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
2. Grasp the upright with your left hand and lean your body away until your left arm is extended.
3. Let your right arm hang down across your body.
4. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, palm facing down, with a slight bend in the elbow.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to the start with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Lean far enough to feel a stretch in the working shoulder at the bottom.
2. Lift with control, not momentum.
3. Lead with the elbow and keep the wrist neutral.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
3. Extend your right leg forward until it is straight and parallel to the floor.
4. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds and feel the stretch along the back of the thigh.
5. Lower the leg, then repeat on the left side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the extended leg straight to target the hamstring fully.
2. Hinge slightly forward at the hips for a deeper stretch.
3. Breathe slowly and do not bounce.
4. Support the thigh with your hands if you cannot hold the leg up.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides, palms down.
2. Lift both legs about 30 cm off the floor, keeping them straight.
3. Engage your core and press your lower back into the floor.
4. Draw small circles in the air with both legs moving together.
5. Complete the circles in one direction, then reverse.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor to protect the spine.
2. Start with small circles and increase size as you get stronger.
3. Keep the legs straight to maximise hip flexor and core demand.
4. Move slowly and with control rather than swinging.

instructions:
1. Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet close together, centred on the platform.
2. Adjust the seat so your knees bend to about 90 degrees.
3. Hold the side handles and press your back into the backrest.
4. Press through your feet to extend your legs without locking the knees.
5. Bend your knees with control to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat against the backrest throughout.
2. A close stance shifts emphasis toward the outer quad.
3. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet wider than shoulder-width, high on the platform.
2. Point your toes slightly outward and keep your feet flat.
3. Adjust the seat so your knees bend to about 90 degrees.
4. Hold the side handles and press your back into the backrest.
5. Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking the knees.
6. Bend your knees with control to return, then repeat.
tips:
1. A high, wide stance shifts emphasis to glutes and hamstrings.
2. Push through your heels to drive the hips.
3. Keep your back flat against the backrest throughout.
4. Keep knees tracking over your toes.

instructions:
1. Sit in the leg press machine and place your feet wider than shoulder-width, high on the platform.
2. Point your toes slightly outward and keep your feet flat.
3. Adjust the seat so your knees bend to about 90 degrees.
4. Hold the side handles and press your back into the backrest.
5. Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking the knees.
6. Bend your knees with control to return, then repeat.
tips:
1. A high, wide stance shifts emphasis to glutes and hamstrings.
2. Push through your heels to drive the hips.
3. Keep your back flat against the backrest throughout.
4. Keep knees tracking over your toes.

instructions:
1. Support your body on a captain's chair, forearms on the pads and back against the rest.
2. Let your legs hang straight down and brace your core.
3. Keep your legs straight and lift them together until parallel to the floor.
4. Lower your legs slowly without swinging.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl your pelvis up at the top to shift load onto the abs.
2. Move under control and do not swing the legs.
3. Keep shoulders pressed down to stay stable.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight together in front.
2. Keep your back long and your toes pointing up.
3. Hinge forward at the hips and reach your hands toward your feet.
4. Reach as far as your flexibility allows and relax your head and neck.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the hips to stretch the hamstrings.
2. Allow the spine to round gently to stretch the back.
3. Use a strap around your feet if you cannot reach.
4. Breathe steadily and ease deeper on each exhale.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Extend your arms straight overhead, close to your ears, hands crossed.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper body, arms following your torso line.
4. Raise until your torso is about 45 degrees off the floor.
5. Lower slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms straight and aligned with your ears.
2. Press your lower back into the floor throughout.
3. Lead with the chest, not the neck.
4. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position and grasp a handle in each hand, palms up.
2. Step forward to create tension, feet shoulder-width apart, back straight.
3. Lean slightly forward with arms extended low and behind you, slight bend in the elbows.
4. Sweep the handles up and together in a wide arc to meet overhead.
5. Lower your arms slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the arc low to high to load the upper chest.
2. Keep the elbow bend fixed throughout.
3. Do not use momentum or shrug the shoulders.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Anchor the middle of the band to a low point in front of you.
2. Lie on a bench, feet flat, holding a handle in each hand, palms up, arms extended by your sides.
3. Curl the handles toward your shoulders by bending the elbows.
4. Keep your upper arms still throughout.
5. Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat on the bench.
2. Keep upper arms pinned and move only at the elbow.
3. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Anchor the middle of the band to a low point in front of you. Lie on a bench, feet flat on the floor, holding a handle in each hand with palms up and arms extended by your sides.
2. Bend your elbows to curl the handles halfway up until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your upper arms still against your sides.
4. Lower the handles with control back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat on the bench and do not arch your spine.
2. Move only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms fixed.
3. Control the band on the way down to keep tension on the biceps.
4. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Lift your right leg and extend it straight forward into a front kick.
3. Bring the right leg back and step it behind you into a lunge, lowering until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor.
4. Push through your left heel to stand back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee in line with your ankle during the lunge.
2. Perform the kick with control, no swinging.
3. Keep your core braced to stay balanced.
4. Exhale on the kick, inhale as you lower into the lunge.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart. Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
2. Raise your hips a few centimetres, then lower back down in a small controlled pulse.
3. Keep your core braced and balance steady throughout.
4. Push through your right heel to stand up, then switch legs.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee in line with your ankle and over the midfoot.
2. Use a controlled motion, do not bounce.
3. Keep your torso upright and chest lifted.
4. Breathe steadily through the pulses.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the middle of the band under your left foot. Hold the handles at shoulder height with elbows bent.
2. Step your right leg back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees until your right knee nears the floor.
3. Keep your left knee in line with your ankle and your torso upright.
4. Push through your left heel to return to standing, bringing the right leg forward.
5. Switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee in line with your ankle.
2. Drive through the front heel to stand up.
3. Keep your core braced for balance.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, arms bent in front of your torso.
2. Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nears the floor.
3. Rotate your torso to the right, then to the left, keeping your hips stable.
4. Return your torso to centre and push through your right heel to stand up.
5. Switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee in line with your ankle.
2. Rotate from the torso, keeping hips square and stable.
3. Keep your back straight and chest lifted.
4. Perform rotations with control, no jerking.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Step your left foot back into a lunge, lowering until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Push through your right heel to stand up, driving your left knee up toward your chest.
4. Lower your left leg back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle, not collapsing inward.
2. Drive the knee up fast but lower it with control to stay balanced.
3. Keep your torso upright and brace your core throughout.
4. Exhale as you drive the knee up, inhale as you step back.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Step your right foot back into a lunge, lowering until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Push through your left heel to stand up, driving your right knee up toward your chest.
4. Lower your right leg back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle, not collapsing inward.
2. Drive the knee up fast but lower it with control to stay balanced.
3. Keep your torso upright and brace your core throughout.
4. Exhale as you drive the knee up, inhale as you step back.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Pause for one to two seconds at the bottom.
4. Push through your right heel to return to the start.
5. Step your left foot forward and repeat the lunge and pause on that side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle, not past your toes.
2. Use the pause to control balance and keep tension in the working leg.
3. Keep your back straight and chest lifted.
4. Exhale as you push back up, inhale as you step forward.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
3. Pause briefly at the bottom.
4. Push through your right heel to return to the start, keeping the same leg forward.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle, not past your toes.
2. Keep your back straight and chest lifted to hold posture.
3. Control the return to the start to stay balanced.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Step your right foot back, keeping the right leg straight and the heel flat on the floor.
3. Bend your left knee and keep your left foot flat on the floor.
4. Lean forward, pressing your hips down until you feel a stretch in your right calf, and hold 15 to 30 seconds.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back leg straight and the heel pressed down to target the gastrocnemius.
2. Keep your front knee aligned over your ankle.
3. Use a stable, non-slip surface to avoid slipping.
4. Breathe steadily and ease deeper into the stretch on each exhale.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Anchor the band to a low point behind your head and hold the handles near your head.
3. Curl your upper body up, bringing your elbows toward your knees and lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.
4. Lower your upper body back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your feet flat for stability.
3. Pull with your abs, not your neck or arms.
4. Pause briefly at the top to feel the band tension peak.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs straight behind you and hands behind your head, elbows out.
2. Engage your core and glutes.
3. Lift your upper torso off the floor, keeping your neck neutral.
4. Squeeze your lower back at the top for a moment.
5. Lower your torso back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your neck neutral and look at the floor.
2. Lift through your lower back, not by yanking with your arms.
3. Use a comfortable, non-slip surface.
4. Start with a small range and build up as you get stronger.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a bench with your arms out to the sides, elbows bent 90 degrees.
2. Let your forearms hang off the sides of the bench, pointing down toward the floor.
3. Rotate at your shoulders to lift your forearms up until they point toward the ceiling.
4. Keep the 90-degree elbow angle the whole time.
5. Lower your forearms back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged and back flat on the bench.
2. Move slowly to keep tension on the rotator cuff.
3. Hold the elbow angle fixed at 90 degrees.
4. Use light or no weight to keep the work in the rotator cuff.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a bench with your arms out to the sides, elbows bent 90 degrees.
2. Let your forearms hang off the sides of the bench, pointing up toward the ceiling.
3. Rotate at your shoulders to lower your forearms down across your body.
4. Keep the 90-degree elbow angle the whole time.
5. Rotate back to the start position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged and back flat on the bench.
2. Move slowly to keep tension on the rotator cuff.
3. Hold the elbow angle fixed at 90 degrees.
4. Use light or no weight to keep the work in the rotator cuff.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and arms out to the sides in a T shape.
2. Bend and lift your right leg, then cross it over your body toward the left side.
3. Reach across with your left hand to gently hold your right knee down.
4. Hold the stretch, feeling it in your lower back, hip, and glute.
5. Return your right leg to the start, then repeat on the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid sudden twists.
2. Breathe deeply and steadily as you hold.
3. Do not force your knee to the floor; go only as far as is comfortable.
4. Keep both shoulders on the floor to deepen the twist.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Cross your right ankle over your left thigh, just above the knee, forming a figure-four.
3. Reach through and grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands.
4. Gently pull your left thigh toward your chest until you feel a stretch in your right glute and outer hip.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then release and switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
2. Pull only to mild tension, never into pain.
3. Use a strap around the thigh if you cannot reach comfortably.
4. Breathe steadily and let the muscle ease into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both legs straight on the floor.
2. Pull your right knee toward your chest and hold it with both hands.
3. Keep your left leg pressed straight along the floor.
4. Feel the stretch across the front of your left hip and thigh.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the straight leg flat on the floor to deepen the stretch.
2. Press your lower back gently into the floor.
3. Start with a small range and increase as flexibility improves.
4. Exhale slowly as you settle into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended straight.
2. Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
3. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Lift both arms off the floor as high as you can, squeezing your rear shoulders and upper back.
5. Hold briefly, then lower with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the backs of the hands to target the rear delts.
2. Keep your neck long and chin tucked.
3. Move slowly to avoid using momentum.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the machine with the padded lever just above your ankles.
2. Align your knees just past the edge of the bench.
3. Grasp the handles and keep your hips pressed into the pad.
4. Curl your legs up toward your glutes by bending your knees.
5. Squeeze the hamstrings at the top, then lower with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips down to isolate the hamstrings.
2. Control the lowering phase, do not let the weight drop.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Point your toes to shift more load onto the hamstrings.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides, palms down.
2. Brace your core and press your lower back into the floor.
3. Keeping your legs straight, lift them until they point toward the ceiling.
4. Lower your legs slowly, stopping just before they touch the floor.
5. Keep your lower back flat throughout. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your lower back pressed down to protect the spine.
3. Bend your knees slightly if your hip flexors take over.
4. Move slowly and control the descent.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs extended and hands flat under your shoulders.
2. Press your hands into the floor to lift your chest upward and extend your spine.
3. Keep your hips and legs relaxed on the floor.
4. Raise until you feel a stretch across your abdomen and lower back.
5. Hold 15-30 seconds, then lower your chest back down.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Roll your shoulders back and down to open the chest.
2. Breathe slowly and steadily through the hold.
3. Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
4. Use a mat for comfort.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band to a low point behind your head.
2. Lie on your back, knees bent and feet flat, holding a handle in each hand.
3. Extend your arms straight above your head, palms facing forward.
4. Keeping arms straight, pull the handles in an arc over your head until they reach your thighs.
5. Slowly return the handles overhead with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows throughout.
2. Drive the movement from your lats, not your arms.
3. Exhale as you pull over, inhale as you return.
4. Keep your ribs down and core braced to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with legs extended and arms by your sides.
2. Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grasp the ankle.
3. Gently pull the foot toward your glutes, feeling the stretch in the front of the thigh.
4. Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
5. Hold 15-30 seconds, then release and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips down to avoid arching the lower back.
2. Move slowly, no sudden pulling.
3. Use a strap around the ankle if you cannot reach the foot.
4. Breathe steadily through the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with legs extended and your head resting on your lower arm.
2. Bend your top knee and reach back with your top hand to grasp the ankle.
3. Gently pull the foot toward your glutes, feeling the stretch in the front of the thigh.
4. Keep your hips stacked and body in a straight line.
5. Hold 15-30 seconds, then release and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep hips stacked to maintain alignment.
2. Use a strap around the ankle if you cannot reach the foot.
3. Breathe steadily through the hold.
4. Bend the lower hip slightly to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit on the decline chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the handles at chest level with palms facing down.
3. Press the handles forward and down by extending your arms.
4. Squeeze your chest at the end of the press.
5. Slowly return the handles to chest level with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the pad throughout.
2. Drive through the chest, not just the arms.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
4. Control the return rather than letting the weight drop.

instructions:
1. Sit on the incline chest press machine with your back flat against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the handles at chest level, palms facing forward, elbows pointing down.
3. Press the handles up and forward until your arms are extended.
4. Squeeze your upper chest at the top.
5. Lower the handles back to chest level under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and head pressed against the pad throughout.
2. Drive through your chest, not just your arms.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a full range of motion without bouncing at the bottom.

instructions:
1. Sit on the chest fly machine with your back flat against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the handles with a slight bend in your elbows, arms out to the sides at chest level.
3. Bring the handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles.
4. Hold the contraction briefly at the center.
5. Return the handles to the sides under control until you feel a stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the pad and the elbow angle fixed throughout.
2. Lead the movement with your chest, not your hands.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together, inhale as you open.
4. Control the return; do not let the weight pull your arms back fast.

instructions:
1. Adjust the seat so the pads rest against the outside of your upper arms.
2. Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
3. Grasp the handles with your elbows bent.
4. Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
5. Lower your arms back to the starting position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stop at shoulder height; raising higher shifts work to the traps.
2. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a moderate weight and avoid jerking the arms up.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips.
2. Slowly rotate your torso to the right while keeping your hips facing forward.
3. Twist as far as is comfortable and feel the stretch through your trunk.
4. Return to the center.
5. Rotate your torso to the left in the same way.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square to the front so the rotation comes from your trunk.
2. Move slowly and do not force the twist past a comfortable range.
3. Keep your core lightly braced to protect your lower back.
4. Stand on a stable, non-slip surface.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms straight by your sides, palms down.
2. Contract your abs and lift your upper back off the floor.
3. At the same time raise your straight legs toward the ceiling and reach your arms toward your feet.
4. Pause just before your hands and feet meet.
5. Lower your upper back, legs, and arms back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move with your abs, not by swinging your legs with momentum.
2. Keep your legs as straight as you can for stronger ab engagement.
3. Exhale as you fold up, inhale as you lower.
4. Lower with control rather than dropping back down.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows and hold your hands at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
3. Press your hands straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Squeeze your shoulders at the top.
5. Lower your hands back to shoulder height with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
3. Keep your head and spine aligned, do not lean back.
4. Press in a straight vertical path.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
3. Push your hips up and back into a downward-dog position, forming an inverted V.
4. Lower your hips and bring your body forward back to the plank.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core engaged so your hips do not sag in the plank.
2. Lower your chest with control before sweeping forward.
3. Drive your hips up high with arms and legs straight in the V position.
4. Move smoothly through each phase.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Drive your right knee toward your chest.
3. Return your right foot to the plank.
4. Drive your left knee toward your chest.
5. Alternate sides at a steady pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips low and level with your shoulders.
2. Keep your core braced and shoulders stable.
3. Breathe steadily as you alternate legs.
4. Keep movements controlled to hold form.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders and feet together.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Bend your elbows at about 45 degrees and lower your chest toward the floor.
4. Stop when your chest is just above the floor.
5. Push through your hands to extend your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees to the body.
2. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your head aligned with your spine.
4. Brace your core to keep your hips from sagging.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head with elbows wide.
3. Lift your upper back off the floor and rotate to bring your right elbow toward the ceiling.
4. Squeeze your obliques at the top.
5. Lower your upper back with control, then repeat to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and rotate, inhale as you lower.
2. Do not pull on your neck, let your core do the work.
3. Focus on rotating the torso, not just lifting.
4. Keep the movement slow and controlled.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip.
2. Bend at the hips and knees, keeping your back flat and almost parallel to the floor. Brace your free hand on a bench.
3. Let the dumbbell hang straight down from your shoulder with a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, squeezing the rear shoulder.
5. Lower the dumbbell with control. Finish all reps, then switch arms. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and keep the slight elbow bend fixed throughout.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Keep your spine neutral and resist twisting toward the working side.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a weight plate with both hands, arms extended straight above your chest.
3. Brace your core and sit up, lifting your upper body toward your knees while keeping the plate overhead and your arms straight.
4. Continue until your torso is upright, keeping the plate above your head.
5. Lower back to the floor with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your arms locked straight so the plate stays directly overhead.
3. Start light to master the movement before adding load.
4. Lower under control rather than dropping back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your legs straight and together. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, arms bent behind your head near the floor.
2. Brace your core and lift your torso off the floor while bending your knees and drawing them toward your chest.
3. Bring the dumbbell up and toward your knees as you crunch together.
4. Lower your torso and legs back to the start with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep your lower back from arching as you extend.
4. Start light to master the form before adding load.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms down at your sides.
2. Raise both arms out to the sides and continue lifting them overhead.
3. Bring your palms together overhead in a clapping motion.
4. Lower your arms back to your sides with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
3. Move smoothly and avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Inhale as you raise, exhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your right arm overhead and bend the elbow, reaching your right hand down toward your upper back.
3. With your left hand, hold your right elbow and gently pull it toward the left to deepen the stretch. Hold.
4. Release and switch sides, raising your left arm and using your right hand to assist. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and do not arch your back.
2. Keep your core engaged for balance.
3. Apply gentle pressure on the elbow and do not force the stretch.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and the middle of the band under both feet.
2. Hold the handles and extend both arms overhead, elbows close to your ears, palms facing each other.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the handles behind your head until your forearms are about parallel to the floor.
4. Straighten your elbows to press the handles back overhead.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your ears and stop them flaring out.
2. Keep your shoulders down to avoid neck tension.
3. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
4. Move the band slowly to keep tension on the triceps.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your right arm overhead and bend the elbow, reaching your hand down toward your upper back.
3. Bring your left hand to your right elbow and gently pull it toward the left to deepen the stretch.
4. Hold the position while breathing steadily.
5. Release, switch arms, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and do not arch your lower back.
2. Apply gentle pressure on the elbow and do not force the range.
3. Keep your core engaged for balance.
4. Breathe slowly throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Rotate your forearms so your palms turn to face up.
3. Rotate your forearms the other way so your palms turn to face down.
4. Keep your arms long and at shoulder height throughout.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows to reduce joint strain.
3. Control the rotation rather than swinging.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your feet flat and your back pressed against the pad.
2. Place your forearms on the pads or grasp the handles with upper arms parallel to the floor.
3. Squeeze your chest to bring the handles together in front of you.
4. Slowly return to the start with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the pad through the whole movement.
2. Drive the motion from your chest, not your arms.
3. Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return.
4. Control the return to keep tension on the chest.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank, then walk your feet toward your hands and lift your hips to form an inverted V.
2. Keep your arms and legs straight and your head between your arms.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your head toward the floor.
4. Push through your hands to straighten your arms back to the inverted V.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head in line with your arms to protect your neck.
2. Keep your hips high to keep the load on your shoulders.
3. Engage your core to hold the V position.
4. Use a non-slip surface for grip.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Drive your right knee across your body toward your left elbow, twisting your torso slightly.
