4. Return your right foot to the plank position.
5. Drive your left knee toward your right elbow, then return.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Pull the knee in with your abs, not by swinging your hips.
2. Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
3. Exhale as the knee drives in, inhale as you reset.
4. Move with control to keep the obliques loaded.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Jump both feet out to the sides, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
4. Jump both feet back together.
5. Keep your upper body still throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips from bouncing as your feet move.
2. Land softly on the balls of your feet.
3. Maintain a straight line from head to heels.
4. Keep your shoulders directly over your elbows.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your shoulders over your wrists.
3. Jump both knees toward your chest, landing with feet flat under your body.
4. Jump your feet back to the plank position.
5. Keep your upper body stable throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the knees in with your abs and hip flexors.
2. Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists on each landing.
3. Land softly to protect your wrists.
4. Exhale as the knees come in, inhale as you extend back.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Step your right foot forward and plant it outside your right hand.
4. Return your right foot to the plank position.
5. Step your left foot outside your left hand, then return.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Keep your hips low and level as the foot steps up.
2. Brace the core to stop the torso from rotating.
3. Keep your shoulders over your wrists throughout.
4. Move with control rather than rushing the step.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with your elbows under your shoulders and forearms flat on the floor.
2. Tuck your toes under and brace your core.
3. Lift your body off the floor into a straight line from head to heels.
4. Squeeze your glutes and keep your hips from sagging or rising.
5. Hold the position, breathing steadily.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders stacked over your elbows.
2. Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level.
3. Pull your belly button toward your spine to brace the core.
4. Breathe steadily instead of holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Lie on your right side and prop up on your right elbow, elbow under your shoulder.
2. Raise your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
3. Reach your left arm straight up toward the ceiling.
4. Rotate your torso and reach your left arm under and across your body.
5. Rotate back and return the left arm to vertical.
6. Finish the set, switch sides, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Stack your shoulder directly over your supporting elbow.
2. Keep your hips lifted and avoid letting them drop.
3. Drive the rotation from your obliques, not momentum.
4. Exhale as you reach under, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and feet wider than hip-width.
2. Hold a water bottle in your right hand, arm straight under your shoulder.
3. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
4. Raise the bottle out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the bottle back down with control.
6. Finish the set, switch hands, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square to the floor and resist rotation.
2. Move slowly and control the bottle on the way down.
3. Lead with your rear delt, not your traps.
4. Widen your feet for a more stable base.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Set your feet about shoulder-width apart for stability.
3. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
4. Lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder.
5. Return the hand to the floor and tap with the other hand.
6. Alternate sides and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips from rocking side to side.
2. Widen your stance to make balancing easier.
3. Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
4. Move slowly to maximize anti-rotation control.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands.
2. Let your arms hang straight down in front of your hips.
3. Brace your core and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Raise the plate in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Pause briefly, then lower the plate back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift slowly and avoid swinging the plate up with momentum.
2. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
3. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the front delts.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width and arms out to your sides.
2. Bend your right knee and lower into a side lunge, keeping your left leg straight.
3. Rotate your torso to the right and reach your left hand to touch your right leg.
4. Push off your right foot to return to the wide stance and rotate back to center.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Track your bent knee over your toes.
2. Keep your trailing leg straight to stretch the inner thigh.
3. Push through the heel of your bent leg to drive back up.
4. Exhale as you lower, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, arms resting over the pad and fully extended.
3. Curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad and squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Keep your wrists straight and firm.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Lower under control to keep tension on the biceps.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold an EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
3. Rest your arms on the pad with elbows extended.
4. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. Use a weight that lets you control the full range.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid swinging the torso.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold an EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands just inside shoulder-width.
3. Rest your arms on the pad with elbows extended.
4. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. The closer grip shifts emphasis toward the outer biceps and peak.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Lower under control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Sit on a preacher bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold an EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands just outside shoulder-width.
3. Rest your arms on the pad with elbows extended.
4. Curl the bar toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
5. Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly until your arms are extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad to isolate the biceps.
2. The wider grip shifts emphasis toward the inner biceps for width.
3. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
4. Keep wrists firm and neutral on the bar.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
2. Bend your right knee and place your right foot flat on the floor outside your left thigh.
3. Rotate your torso to the right and place your left elbow against the outside of your right knee.
4. Place your right hand on the floor behind you for support.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then release and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move into the stretch slowly to avoid overstretching.
2. Use the rear hand for balance and to deepen the rotation.
3. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch.
4. Keep your spine tall rather than slouched.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a barbell below you with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms straight down.
3. Pull the barbell toward your upper abdomen, driving your elbows back and close to your body.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the barbell with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the back.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your neck neutral and gaze down.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a barbell below you with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms straight down.
3. Pull the barbell toward your lower abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your body.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the barbell with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. The underhand grip recruits the biceps more, so control the weight.
3. Drive your elbows down and back to load the lats.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms hanging straight down.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward the sides of your torso, driving your elbows back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. Lead with your elbows to target the back, not the arms.
3. The neutral grip balances lat and mid-back work.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, arms hanging straight down.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward the sides of your torso, flaring your elbows slightly.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. The overhand grip emphasizes the upper back and rear delts.
3. Lead with your elbows to target the back.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees and lie chest-down on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, arms hanging straight down.
3. Pull the dumbbells toward your waist, keeping your elbows close to your body.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed into the bench to remove momentum.
2. The underhand grip recruits the biceps more, so control the load.
3. Drive your elbows down and back to load the lats.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench set to about 45 degrees.
2. Hold a barbell with a pronated grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms hanging straight down.
3. Raise the barbell in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the barbell back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed against the bench throughout.
2. Lead the movement with your shoulders, not your arms.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a light load to keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on an incline bench set to about 45 degrees.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip, arms hanging straight down.
3. Raise the dumbbells in front of you until your arms are in line with your torso.
4. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed against the bench throughout.
2. Lead the movement with your shoulders, not your arms.
3. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a light load to keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band with both hands.
2. Extend your arms straight in front of you at shoulder height, palms facing down.
3. Pull the band apart by moving your arms out to the sides until the band touches your chest.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
5. Return your arms to the front with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms nearly straight throughout.
2. Drive the movement by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull apart, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended.
3. Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range of motion at the top and bottom.
2. Initiate the pull by depressing the shoulder blades.
3. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended.
3. Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range of motion at the top and bottom.
2. Initiate the pull by depressing the shoulder blades.
3. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and shoulder blades engaged.
3. Pull your body up by driving your elbows down and back.
4. Continue until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows toward your hips to lead with the lats.
2. Avoid swinging or kipping; keep the movement controlled.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep shoulders down and away from your ears at the top.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands shoulder-width apart and body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
3. Press back up to full arm extension.
4. Shift weight to one hand and rotate your torso, raising the other arm toward the ceiling into a side plank.
5. Return the hand to the floor and lower into another push-up, alternating the rotation each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line through both the push-up and the rotation.
2. Rotate from the torso and brace your obliques to stay stable.
3. Exhale as you press and rotate, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep feet planted to give the rotation a stable base.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
3. Press back up to full arm extension.
4. At the top, push your hands hard into the floor to round your upper back and spread your shoulder blades.
5. Release back to a flat plank.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Emphasize the final push at the top to spread the shoulder blades.
2. Keep your core braced and hips level throughout.
3. Keep elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees during the descent.
4. Move slowly to feel the upper-back rounding action.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and feet together.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower your chest toward the floor.
4. Stop when your chest is just above the floor.
5. Press through your hands back to full arm extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stop your hips from sagging.
2. Lower with control until your chest nearly touches the floor.
3. Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to spare the shoulders.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and raise your legs straight up, vertical to the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head with elbows pointing out.
3. Brace your core and lift your shoulders off the floor toward your knees.
4. Hold briefly and squeeze your abs at the top.
5. Lower your shoulders back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
3. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your legs steady and vertical throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend one elbow and reach that hand up your back, palm facing out.
3. Walk the fingers up toward the opposite shoulder blade until you feel a stretch.
4. Hold for 15-30 seconds, breathing steadily.
5. Release slowly and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly to avoid straining the shoulder.
2. Keep the spine neutral, do not arch the back.
3. Stop if you feel sharp pain in the front of the shoulder.
4. Keep shoulders down and relaxed.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band at shoulder height in front of you.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand, arms extended forward at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
3. Pull the handles out to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Pause briefly at full contraction.
5. Return slowly to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
2. Keep the torso still, do not swing.
3. Exhale as you pull apart, inhale on return.
4. Use lighter resistance to keep strict form.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend one arm straight across the body at shoulder height.
3. Use the opposite hand to gently pull the arm closer to the chest.
4. Hold for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in the back of the shoulder.
5. Release slowly and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep shoulders relaxed and down, away from the ears.
2. Do not twist the torso, keep it facing forward.
3. Move slowly and stop short of pain.
4. Pull from the elbow, not the wrist.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band at chest height to a sturdy point.
2. Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat and forward.
3. Hold a handle in each hand, arms extended forward, palms facing in.
4. Pull the handles toward the chest, driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
5. Return to the start with control, keeping tension on the band.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end of each pull.
2. Keep shoulders down, do not shrug.
3. Brace the core to stop the torso from twisting.
4. Adjust position to set band tension.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band at head height to a sturdy point.
2. Stand facing the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with arms extended forward, palms facing down.
3. Pull the handles toward the face, flaring the elbows out to the sides.
4. Keep the upper arms parallel to the floor and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
5. Extend the arms back to the start with control, keeping tension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows high, in line with the shoulders.
2. Pull the hands toward the ears, not the chin.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.
4. Exhale on the pull, inhale on return.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Place a loop band around both thighs, just above the knees.
2. Extend your right leg straight back, lifted a few cm off the floor.
3. Sweep the leg in a half-circle inward over the left leg until it lightly touches the floor, keeping the band taut.
4. Reverse the motion with control to return to the start.
5. Finish the set, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep hips and shoulders square to the floor.
2. Move slowly and control the band tension.
3. Drive the motion from the glute, not the lower back.
4. Exhale as you sweep the leg, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet together. Place a loop band around both thighs, just above the knees.
2. Rest your arms on the floor by your sides for stability.
3. Press your knees apart against the band as far as control allows, keeping the feet together.
4. Slowly bring the knees back together with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a band tension that challenges you without breaking form.
2. Drive the knees open with the glutes, not momentum.
3. Keep the feet together and flat throughout.
4. Keep the lower back relaxed on the floor.

instructions:
1. Anchor a loop band to a low point and lie on your back with legs extended toward the anchor. Loop the band over your feet.
2. Place your arms on the floor by your sides.
3. Keep both legs straight and a few cm off the floor.
4. Bend the knees and draw them up until the thighs are perpendicular to the floor.
5. Straighten the legs back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press the lower back into the floor throughout.
2. Move with control against the band, no swinging.
3. Brace the abs to drive the movement.
4. Exhale as you draw the knees up.

instructions:
1. Anchor the middle of the band at head height. Face the anchor with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold one end in each hand, arms extended in front, palms facing down.
3. Pull the band toward your face, flaring the elbows out to the sides until your hands reach the sides of your face.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, keeping the upper arms parallel to the floor.
5. Extend the arms back to the start with control, keeping band tension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
2. Pause and squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.
3. Keep the upper arms level with the floor.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms by your sides, palms down for stability.
2. Lift the legs and bend the knees to 90 degrees so the thighs are perpendicular to the floor.
3. Brace the core and curl the hips off the floor, drawing the knees toward the chest.
4. Lower the hips back to the start with control, keeping the knees bent.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with the abs, not momentum.
2. Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
3. Exhale as you curl the hips up.
4. Control the lowering phase, do not drop the legs.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms by your sides, palms down.
2. Lift your legs and bend your knees to 90 degrees, thighs vertical.
3. Extend your legs straight out, keeping them off the floor.
4. Bend your knees back in and curl your hips off the floor toward your chest.
5. Lower your hips and legs back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl your pelvis using your abs, not momentum.
2. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
3. Move slowly on the way down to keep tension on the abs.
4. Exhale as you lift your hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit at the lat pulldown machine with knees secured under the pads.
2. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder-width, arms fully extended.
3. Keep your chest up and lean back slightly.
4. Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down to your sides.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows toward your hips to keep the lats working.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades at the bottom.
3. Avoid swinging your torso to move the weight.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a handle in each hand with an overhand grip, arms extended by your sides.
3. Curl both handles up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze at the top, keeping your wrists straight.
5. Slowly lower the handles back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked and still through the curl.
2. Hold a firm pronated grip to load the forearms.
3. Lower slowly to keep tension on the band.
4. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with your right foot, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a handle in each hand at shoulder height, elbows bent.
3. Step your left foot back and lower your left knee toward the floor.
4. Keep your right knee over your ankle.
5. Push through your right heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee aligned with your toes.
2. Keep your torso upright throughout.
3. Drive through the front heel to engage the glutes.
4. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit at the machine with your chest against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp the handles with arms extended forward.
3. Pull the handles back by opening your arms wide to your sides.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
5. Return slowly to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout.
2. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades at the back.
4. Exhale as you open your arms, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back to a hip-height box or bench, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place both hands on the edge behind you, palms down, arms straight.
3. Slowly bend your knees to lower your body, keeping your arms straight.
4. Let your shoulders and chest open until you feel a stretch.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then straighten your legs to return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hands fixed and arms straight throughout.
2. Lower only until you feel a comfortable stretch, not pain.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Use a stable, non-slip surface to prevent the hands slipping.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Step your right foot forward and keep that leg straight.
3. Bend your left knee slightly and keep your back straight.
4. Hinge at the hips and lower your torso toward your right foot, reaching down with your hands.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then return and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front leg straight but not locked.
2. Hinge from the hips, do not round your lower back.
3. Keep the back heel down to add a calf stretch.
4. Use a stable, non-slip surface.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Lean back slightly so your torso and thighs form a V shape.
3. Clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
4. Rotate your torso to the right, bringing your hands beside your right hip.
5. Rotate back through the centre and to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Turn from the torso, not just the arms.
2. Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return.
3. Keep your chest up and back straight, do not hunch.
4. Lift your feet to increase the challenge.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Hold a weighted ball with both hands in front of your chest, arms slightly extended.
3. Lean back slightly and keep your back straight.
4. Rotate your torso to the right, bringing the ball beside your right hip.
5. Rotate through the centre and to the left.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist from the torso, not just the arms.
2. Move slowly and under control to resist the ball's momentum.
3. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
4. Exhale as you rotate to each side.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
2. Keep your body in a straight line and your arms straight.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, letting your chest dip slightly.
4. Push your shoulder blades apart, rounding the upper back and lifting your chest.
5. Alternate retraction and protraction with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows straight; the movement comes from the shoulder blades only.
2. Exhale as you push apart, inhale as you squeeze together.
3. Keep the body straight, no sagging or arching.
4. Move slowly to feel the shoulder blades working.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms by your sides, palms down.
2. Lift both legs about 15 cm off the floor, keeping them straight.
3. Cross your right leg over your left, then switch and cross your left over your right.
4. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor throughout.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press your lower back into the floor to protect your spine.
2. Move with control instead of using momentum.
3. Keep legs straight and toes pointed.
4. Breathe steadily and keep your core braced.

instructions:
1. Sit at the cable row machine with feet on the platform, knees slightly bent. Grasp the V-bar with both hands.
2. Sit upright with a straight back and arms extended in front of you.
3. Pull the V-bar to your lower abdomen, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly extend your arms back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back to swing the weight.
2. Lead with your elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.
3. Keep your core braced to stabilize your spine.
4. Control the return phase rather than letting the weight pull you forward.

instructions:
1. Sit on the calf machine with your forefeet on the platform and knees secured under the padded lever.
2. Hold the handles and lower your heels as far as possible to stretch the calves.
3. Press through your forefeet to lift your heels as high as possible.
4. Lower your heels slowly back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and torso still throughout.
2. Maintain tension in the calves from start to finish.
3. Use a full range, lowering heels for a deep stretch.
4. Lower slowly to emphasize the eccentric.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your forefeet on the edge of a plate, heels hanging off.
2. Place a dumbbell on each knee and hold them securely with your hands.
3. Lower your heels to fully stretch the calves.
4. Press through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible.
5. Lower your heels slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement through your calves, not your hands.
2. Keep the tempo slow and controlled.
3. Avoid bouncing or using momentum.
4. Hold the dumbbells firmly so they stay balanced on the knees.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with legs extended straight in front of you, back straight.
2. Keep your right leg straight and slightly bend the left knee.
3. Reach forward and grasp the toes of your right foot with both hands.
4. Gently pull your toes toward you until you feel the calf stretch.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight to deepen the stretch.
2. Move slowly and do not force the range.
3. Use a towel or strap around the foot if you cannot reach your toes.
4. Keep your shoulders relaxed and down.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
2. Bend your right knee and cross your right ankle over your left thigh.
3. Bend your left knee and place your left foot flat on the floor.
4. Keep your back straight and lean your chest forward over the crossed leg.
5. Hold and feel the stretch in your right glute, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight as you lean forward instead of rounding it.
2. Move slowly into the stretch and avoid bouncing.
3. Keep the bent knee stable and aligned with your hip.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with back support, feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand at shoulder height, palm facing forward.
3. Press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height with control.
5. Finish the set, then switch to your left arm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the backrest and avoid arching.
2. Press the dumbbell in a straight vertical line.
3. Brace your core to resist leaning toward the working side.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the edge of a bench with feet flat and a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Lean forward at the hips until your chest is near your thighs.
3. Let your arms hang down, palms facing each other, with a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.
2. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
3. Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift the weights.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
2. Place your hands behind your head with elbows pointing out.
3. Brace your core and curl your torso toward your thighs.
4. Keep your legs straight and flat on the floor.
5. Lower your torso back with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use your abs to curl up, not your hands pulling the neck.
2. Keep your legs straight on the floor for stability.
3. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the abs.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs extended straight in front of you.
2. Lean back slightly and grip the sides of the bench for support.
3. Lift both legs a few centimetres off the bench, keeping them straight.
4. Kick your legs up and down in a small alternating scissor motion.
5. Keep your core braced throughout the movement.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
2. Use a stable, non-slip bench to prevent slipping.
3. Keep the movement small and controlled.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the set.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and legs extended. Set the leg pad to rest just above your heels and the thigh pad snug over your thighs.
2. Grip the handles and keep your torso firm against the seat.
3. Curl your heels down and back by bending your knees as far as possible.
4. Pause briefly at the bottom.
5. Slowly straighten your legs back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you curl and inhale as you return.
2. Control the return; do not let the stack drop.
3. Keep your hips and back pressed into the seat to isolate the hamstrings.
4. Point your toes back slightly to reduce calf takeover.

instructions:
1. Sit at the row machine with your chest against the pad and feet on the footrests.
2. Grip the handles with an overhand grip, arms extended forward.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced.
4. Pull the handles toward your torso, driving your elbows back past your sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows to engage the back, not the arms.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
3. Keep your torso still; do not swing.
4. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and feet together. Loop the band around the soles of your feet and hold a handle in each hand, arms extended forward, palms facing each other.
2. Sit tall with your back straight, chest up, and core braced.
3. Pull the handles toward your torso, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly extend your arms back to the start under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight; do not slouch or round forward.
2. Brace your core to stop your torso from rocking.
3. Use a controlled tempo in both directions.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight and your back upright.
2. Place both hands flat on the floor about 30 cm behind your hips, fingers pointing back.
3. Keep your arms straight and lean your torso back slightly.
4. Press your chest up and draw your shoulder blades together until you feel a stretch across the front of the shoulders and chest.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and hands firmly planted.
2. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
3. Perform on a non-slip surface to prevent your hands sliding.
4. Breathe steadily and ease deeper into the stretch on each exhale.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with a backrest, feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width and rest it on your upper chest.
2. Brace your core and keep your back against the backrest.
3. Press the barbell straight overhead by extending your elbows.
4. Fully extend your arms with the bar over your head.
5. Lower the barbell back to your upper chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
2. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
3. Press the bar in a straight vertical line, keeping it close to your face.
4. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back straight.
2. Hold the edge of the bench with your left hand for support.
3. Reach your right arm up overhead.
4. Lean your torso to the left until you feel a stretch down the right side of your body.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, return to center, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move into the stretch slowly and stay in control.
2. Keep your supporting hand firm on the bench for stability.
3. Lengthen up through the reaching arm rather than collapsing sideways.
4. Breathe steadily and relax deeper on each exhale.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
2. Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
3. Keep your right leg straight.
4. Reach forward toward your right foot with both hands, keeping your back straight.
5. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge from the hips instead of rounding your back.
2. Keep the straight leg long without forcing the knee.
3. Move in gradually and stop at a mild stretch.
4. Breathe out as you reach a little deeper.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
2. Keep your right leg straight and reach forward to grasp the toes of your right foot.
3. Gently pull your toes toward you until you feel a stretch in your calf.
4. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working leg straight so the stretch reaches the calf.
2. Hinge from the hips and keep your back long.
3. Pull the toes back slowly and stop at a mild stretch.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your hands on the floor behind you for support.
2. Lean your torso back slightly and engage your core.
3. Lift your legs and draw your knees toward your chest while bringing your torso up to form a V shape.
4. Hold briefly and squeeze your abs.
5. Lower your legs and torso back with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift into the V and inhale as you lower.
2. Use your abs to raise your legs, not momentum.
3. Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your back.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the core.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, one foot slightly forward and knees soft.
2. Raise your hands to guard position with elbows close to your body.
3. Throw punches in the air, alternating jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts.
4. Rotate your hips and shoulders to drive each punch.
5. Move around with light footwork, stepping forward, back, and side to side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate through the hips and pivot the rear foot to generate power.
2. Keep your hands up in guard between punches.
3. Exhale sharply with each punch.
4. Stay light on your feet and move continuously.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and palms facing down.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the arms back to your sides with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid swinging the arms.
2. Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.
3. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Roll the shoulders backward in small circles.
3. Gradually widen the circles while keeping a steady pace.
4. Continue the circular motion with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the motion smooth and controlled.
2. Keep the neck relaxed throughout.
3. Breathe steadily during each circle.
4. Use the shoulder muscles, not momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and arms straight at your sides.
2. Raise both arms straight forward and continue up overhead.
3. Keep the arms straight and parallel.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the arms back to your sides with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.
3. Move with control, no momentum.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold one handle in each hand, arms down at your sides, palms facing in.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
4. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and palms facing down.
5. Lower the arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Choose a band tension that challenges you without breaking form.
2. Lead with the elbows and keep the wrists neutral.
3. Keep the torso still, no swinging.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped in front for balance.
2. Take a wide step to the right and bend the right knee, keeping the left leg straight.
3. Sit the hips back and keep the right foot flat.
4. Push through the right heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat on the left side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bent knee tracking over the foot.
2. Keep the back flat and chest up.
3. Push the hips back rather than letting the knee drift forward.
4. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you push back up.

instructions:
1. Lie on your left side with legs stacked and body in a straight line. Rest your head on your left arm.
2. Extend your right arm overhead, reaching past your ear.
3. Reach long through the fingertips and let your top ribs lengthen until you feel a stretch down the side of your back.
4. Hold 15 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
5. Return to the start and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the reaching arm long to lengthen the lat and side ribs.
2. Tuck the pelvis slightly so the lower back does not arch.
3. Ease into the stretch, never force the end range.
4. Use a padded, non-slip surface.

instructions:
1. Lie on your right side with legs extended and stacked. Rest your head on your right arm and place your left hand on your hip.
2. Lift your left leg straight up, keeping it in line with your body.
3. Pause at the top and squeeze the outer hip.
4. Lower the leg slowly under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with the hip, not momentum.
2. Keep the leg straight and in line with the torso.
3. Stop the lift before the hips roll back.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your left side with legs extended and stacked. Rest your head on your left arm and place your right hand on your hip.
2. Lift your right leg straight up, keeping it in line with your body.
3. Pause at the top and squeeze the outer hip.
4. Lower the leg slowly under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with the hip, not momentum.
2. Keep the leg straight and in line with the torso.
3. Stop the lift before the hips roll back.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your right side with legs stacked. Prop up on your right elbow, elbow under your shoulder.
2. Brace your core and lift your hips off the floor into a straight line from head to feet.
3. Hold the position, keeping the body straight and tight.
4. Lower your hips under control.
5. Switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow directly under the shoulder.
2. Hold a straight line, no sagging hips.
3. Keep the head in line with the spine.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Set up in a side plank on your right side, elbow under your shoulder, left hand on your hip.
2. Brace your core and lift your hips into a straight line.
3. Lower your hips toward the floor without touching it.
4. Drive the hips back up, squeezing the obliques at the top.
5. Switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly with control, no swinging.
2. Keep the elbow under the shoulder for support.
3. Squeeze the top obliques hard at the top of each rep.
4. Exhale as you lift the hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your right side with your legs straight and stacked, propped on your right elbow under your shoulder.
2. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from head to feet. Raise your left arm toward the ceiling.
3. Lower your hips with control until they nearly touch the floor.
4. Drive your hips back up to the straight line position.
5. Finish one side, then switch to your left side. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in one straight line, do not let your hips sag forward or back.
2. Move the hips slowly and with control.
3. Exhale as you lift the hips, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder for support.

instructions:
1. Lie on your right side with your legs bent and stacked. Place your right arm across your chest and your left hand on the floor in front of you.
2. Press your left hand into the floor to push your upper body up.
3. Hold briefly at the top, feeling the triceps and chest contract.
4. Lower your upper body back down with control.
5. Finish one side, then switch to your left side. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
2. Plant the supporting hand firmly for stability.
3. Drive through the triceps, do not use momentum.
4. Keep your core braced to protect the spine.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, knees slightly bent. Hold your fists up in a guard position.
2. Rotate your torso left and punch across your body with your right hand, extending the arm fully.
3. Return to the guard position.
4. Rotate your torso right and punch across your body with your left hand.
5. Keep alternating sides at a steady pace. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive each punch from torso rotation, not just the arm.
2. Keep your legs and hips stable while the torso turns.
3. Exhale sharply on each punch, inhale as you reset.
4. Keep the non-punching fist up to guard.

instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, body in a straight line.
2. Lower your body while leaning toward the right, bringing your chest near your right hand.
3. Push through both hands back to the start.
4. Lower again while leaning toward the left, bringing your chest near your left hand.
5. Keep alternating sides each rep. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your body in one straight line, do not let the hips drop.
3. Plant both hands firmly for stability.
4. Brace your core to control the side-to-side shift.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your right arm across your torso at chest height, keeping the forearm parallel to the floor.
3. Grasp your right hand with your left hand and gently pull the wrist backward.
4. Hold the stretch and feel it in the right wrist and forearm.
5. Release slowly, then switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull slowly, never jerk the wrist.
2. Breathe deeply and steadily through the hold.
3. Relax into the stretch to let the forearm lengthen.
4. Stop if you feel sharp pain in the joint.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to a mid position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your left hand, arm extended toward the machine.
3. Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back, and lean forward a little for balance.
4. Pull the handle to your torso, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine.
5. Extend your arm back to the start under control.
6. Repeat, then switch to the right arm.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square to resist trunk rotation.
3. Lead with the elbow and squeeze the back, not the arm.
4. Avoid swinging your torso for momentum.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to a mid position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your right hand, arm extended toward the machine.
3. Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back, and lean forward a little for balance.
4. Pull the handle to your torso, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine.
5. Extend your arm back to the start under control.
6. Repeat, then switch to the left arm.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square to resist trunk rotation.
3. Lead with the elbow and squeeze the back, not the arm.
4. Avoid swinging your torso for momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and anchor one end of the band under your left foot.
2. Hold the other end with your right hand and raise that arm overhead, elbow close to your head.
3. Start with your elbow bent and your hand behind your head.
4. Extend your arm straight up, fully straightening the elbow.
5. Lower your hand back behind your head under control.
6. Repeat, then switch to the left arm.
tips:
1. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your upper arm fixed and close to your head.
3. Brace your core so your lower back does not arch.
4. Control the band on the way down for full range.

instructions:
1. Set the cable pulley to a low position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grasp the handle with your left hand, arm extended down toward the machine.
3. Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back, and lean forward a little for balance.
4. Pull the handle to your torso, driving your elbow back and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine.
5. Extend your arm back to the start under control.
6. Repeat, then switch to the right arm.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square to resist trunk rotation.
3. Lead with the elbow and squeeze the back, not the arm.
4. Avoid swinging your torso for momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one dumbbell with both hands under the top plates, palms facing up.
2. Let the dumbbell hang in front of your hips with arms extended.
3. Curl the dumbbell up toward your chest by bending your elbows.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still against your sides.
2. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
3. Use a controlled tempo instead of swinging the weight.
4. Keep your wrists firm and neutral throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand in front of your thighs.
2. Keep your back flat and shoulders back.
3. Bend at your hips and knees to lower the kettlebell toward the floor.
4. Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand up.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control. Switch hands. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
3. Hinge at the hips, do not round your lower back.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the loaded side.

instructions:
1. Sit in the leg press machine and extend one leg, placing the forefoot on the lower edge of the platform with the heel hanging off.
2. Keep a slight bend in the knee.
3. Press through the forefoot to push the platform up by extending your ankle.
4. Squeeze your calf at the top.
5. Lower the heel below the platform edge for a full stretch under control. Switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the knee throughout.
2. Let the heel drop fully at the bottom for a deep stretch.
3. Pause briefly at the top contraction.
4. Move at a steady pace to keep tension on the calf.

instructions:
1. Sit in the 45 degree leg press and place one foot flat on the platform, mid-foot centered.
2. Keep your back against the seat and release the safety handles.
3. Press through your foot to extend the leg and push the platform up.
4. Stop just short of locking the knee.
5. Lower the platform under control until your knee nears your chest. Switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your knee tracking over your toes.
3. Press through the whole foot, not just the toes.
4. Keep your hips and lower back flat against the seat.

instructions:
1. Stand on your right leg holding a dumbbell in your right hand, knee slightly bent.
2. Hinge at the hip and extend your left leg straight back.
3. Lower the dumbbell toward the floor until your torso and back leg are parallel to the ground.
4. Keep your back flat and hips level.
5. Drive through your standing heel to return to standing. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee.
3. Keep your hips square to the floor, do not let them open.
4. Practice without weight first to learn balance.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band low and hold the free end in your right hand.
2. Stand on your left leg with the knee slightly bent.
3. Hinge at the hip and extend your right leg straight back.
4. Lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor against the band tension.
5. Drive your hips forward to return to standing. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you hinge forward, inhale as you return.
2. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee for balance.
3. Keep your back flat and shoulders down.
4. Keep your hips level, do not let the pelvis rotate.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
3. Brace your core and curl your torso up off the floor.
4. Keep lifting until your chest is close to your knees.
5. Lower your back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced through the whole movement.
2. Move slowly and avoid yanking with your hands or neck.
3. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.
4. Anchor or relax your feet to reduce hip flexor takeover.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
2. Reach up and grip one handle overhead with each hand.
3. Pull one handle down toward your hip while the other arm stays high.
4. Drive that arm back up as you pull the opposite handle down.
5. Keep alternating arms in a steady skiing rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge slightly at the hips and drive the pull with your lats, not just your arms.
2. Use a full range, finishing each pull near your hip.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
4. Breathe steadily with the rhythm.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together, holding a rope handle in each hand by your sides.
2. Keep your core braced and posture upright.
3. Turn the rope with small wrist circles and jump lightly off the floor.
4. Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
5. Keep jumps low and quick in a steady rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep jumps low to reduce joint impact.
2. Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
3. Stay relaxed through the shoulders.
4. Breathe steadily and rhythmically.

instructions:
1. Set the Smith bar across your upper back and grip it with both hands.
2. Place one foot back on a bench about 40 cm high, front foot planted ahead.
3. Lower by bending your front knee, keeping your torso upright.
4. Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your front heel to stand back up.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
2. Stay upright; lean slightly forward to bias glutes.
3. Drive through the front heel, not the toes.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the Smith bar across your upper back and grip it with both hands.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels high.
4. Pause at the top, feeling the calves contract.
5. Lower your heels slowly below the start for a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range, stretching at the bottom and rising onto the toes at the top.
2. Keep your knees nearly straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
3. Move slowly and controlled, no bouncing.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set a decline bench under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest.
2. Lie on the bench with your feet hooked under the pads. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Unrack the bar and lower it under control to your lower chest.
4. Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
2. Lower the bar to the lower chest, not the upper chest.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your hips on the bench and feet anchored.

instructions:
1. Set a flat bench under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your mid chest.
2. Lie on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Unrack the bar and lower it under control to your mid chest.
4. Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pinned to the bench.
2. Drive your feet into the floor for a stable base.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Touch the chest lightly, do not bounce the bar.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench at about 30 degrees under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your upper chest.
2. Lie on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Unrack the bar and lower it under control to your upper chest.
4. Press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades retracted against the bench.
2. Lower the bar to the upper chest, just below the collarbone.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your back flat, do not arch off the bench.

instructions:
1. Place an upright bench under the Smith machine and set the bar to shoulder height.
2. Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Unrack the bar and press it straight up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Lower the bar under control back to shoulder height.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back against the pad and core braced.
2. Drive the bar straight up, not forward.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
4. Lower until the bar reaches just above your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with your chest supported.
2. Grip a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and let your arms hang straight down.
3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms vertical and stationary throughout.
2. Control the lowering phase, do not let the bar drop.
3. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top of each rep.
4. Keep your chest pinned to the pad to remove momentum.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, arms hanging straight down.
3. Keep your upper arms still and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms vertical and stationary throughout.
2. Use a full range of motion at the bottom for a strong stretch.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the lowering phase, do not let the weights drop.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to about 45 degrees and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
2. Hold an EZ bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms hanging straight down.
3. Keep your upper arms still and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms vertical and stationary throughout.
2. Use the angled grip to reduce wrist strain.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the lowering phase for full tension.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Keep your core tight and feet hip-width apart.
3. Bring your right knee toward your right elbow, keeping your hips level.
4. Return your right foot to the start.
5. Bring your left knee toward your left elbow, then return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and resist torso rotation.
2. Brace your abs the whole time.
3. Exhale as you draw the knee in, inhale as you return.
4. Move slowly and with control rather than rushing.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointing slightly out.
2. Place your hands on your hips.
3. Shift your weight onto your right leg, bending the right knee while keeping the left leg straight.
4. Lean your torso slightly forward until you feel a stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg.
5. Hold for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bent knee tracking over the toes, not past them.
2. Ease into the stretch slowly without bouncing.
3. Breathe steadily and let the inner thigh relax.
4. Increase depth gradually as flexibility improves.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing you.
2. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
3. Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
4. Fully extend your arms at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down, rotating your palms to face you again.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate your wrists smoothly through the whole movement.
2. Keep your core braced to support your spine while standing.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Do not arch your lower back at the top.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together and arms by your sides.
2. Hinge at your hips and lower your torso toward your legs, reaching your hands toward the back of your feet.
3. Keep your back straight and your knees soft.
4. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, feeling the stretch along the back of your legs.
5. Return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and stop at mild tension, never pain.
2. Hinge from the hips rather than rounding your lower back.
3. Keep your weight even across both feet for balance.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways to a cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart, handle set at mid height.
2. Grasp the handle with both hands and bend your arms slightly, keeping them close to your torso.
3. Brace your core and twist your torso away from the machine, pulling the handle across your body.
4. Rotate until your shoulders face away from the machine.
5. Return slowly under control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your obliques, not your arms.
2. Keep your hips facing forward so the twist comes from the torso.
3. Keep your feet planted firmly throughout.
4. Exhale as you twist away from the machine.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, looping a resistance band under your forefeet.
2. Hold the band handles by your sides with slight tension.
3. Push through your forefeet and lift your heels as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels slowly under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the balls of your feet, not the toes.
2. Pause at the top to maximize the contraction.
3. Keep your knees straight to emphasize the gastrocnemius.
4. Control the descent for full range of motion.

instructions:
1. Set the Smith machine bar across your upper back and unrack it.
2. Place your forefeet on a low platform with heels hanging off, feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Push through your forefeet and raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels slowly below the platform for a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the balls of your feet, not the toes.
2. Keep your knees straight to emphasize the gastrocnemius.
3. Pause briefly at the top and bottom for full range.
4. The fixed bar path lets you focus purely on the calves.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
2. Brace your core and press the right dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
3. Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height under control.
4. Press the left dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
5. Lower it back to shoulder height, alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working arm.
2. Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your shoulders down rather than shrugging.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand resting in front of your thighs, palms facing back.
2. Brace your core and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise both dumbbells straight in front of you until your arms are parallel to the floor.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso still and avoid swinging or using momentum.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your wrists neutral and shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Use a weight you can control through a full range of motion.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a bench, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place your right heel on the bench with the toes pointing up. Keep your left foot flat on the floor.
3. Keep your right leg straight and lean your torso forward from the hips.
4. Hold the stretch and feel tension in your right calf.
5. Switch legs and repeat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the stretched leg fully straight to target the gastrocnemius.
2. Hinge from the hips, do not round your back.
3. Ease into the stretch slowly, no bouncing.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band in both hands.
2. Place the center of the band under your right forefoot.
3. Extend your right leg in front of you, heel on the floor and toes pointing up.
4. Pull the band gently and hinge your torso forward, keeping your back straight.
5. Hold the stretch, then switch legs and repeat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the stretched leg straight and toes pulled toward you.
2. Keep the standing leg slightly bent for balance.
3. Hinge from the hips, do not round your spine.
4. Increase tension gradually as flexibility improves.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley.
2. Hold the bar with both hands, arms extended, palms facing down.
3. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward a little at the hips.
4. Keep your arms straight and pull the bar in an arc down to your thighs, contracting your lats.
5. Return the bar slowly to the start, keeping tension in your lats.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your lats, not your arms.
2. Keep your elbows nearly straight throughout.
3. Brace your core to keep your lower back stable.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Brace your core and stand tall.
3. Place your right hand behind your head and keep your left arm down by your leg.
4. Bend your torso to the left until you feel a stretch along your right side.
5. Hold the stretch, then return and repeat on the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and do not push them sideways.
2. Move slowly and hold without bouncing.
3. Keep your spine long, do not round forward.
4. Increase the bend gradually as flexibility improves.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a raised surface about hip height with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place your right heel on the surface with the leg straight and toes pointing up.
3. Keep your back flat and hinge at the hips toward your right leg.
4. Reach toward your right foot until you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh.
5. Hold 20-30 seconds, return to start, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elevated leg straight and toes pulled toward the shin.
2. Hinge from the hips, do not round the lower back.
3. Keep the standing leg slightly bent for balance.
4. Ease into the stretch, do not bounce.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands behind your head, elbows out.
2. Engage your core and stand tall.
3. Lift your right knee up while bending your torso to the right to bring elbow and knee together.
4. Lower the leg and straighten the torso back to start.
5. Repeat on the left side, alternating.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you crunch, inhale as you return.
2. Drive the side bend from the waist, not the shoulders.
3. Keep the standing leg slightly bent for balance.
4. Move under control, do not swing.

instructions:
1. Stand with your right side near a wall, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your right arm to the side at shoulder height and place your palm flat on the wall.
3. Slowly turn your body away from the wall, keeping the arm fixed.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds where you feel a stretch across the chest and front shoulder.
5. Return to start and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working arm straight and the palm flat on the wall.
2. Keep shoulders down, away from the ears.
3. Turn gradually to avoid overstretching.
4. Adjust arm height to target different parts of the chest.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms straight in front at shoulder height, palms down.
2. Raise your right arm overhead while lowering your left arm to your side.
3. Keep both arms straight throughout.
4. Return to start, then swap, raising the left arm and lowering the right.
5. Continue alternating in a controlled rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe steadily as the arms move.
2. Keep both arms straight and the torso square.
3. Use a smooth, controlled motion.
4. Move through a full range without forcing the end position.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a stable surface for balance if needed.
2. Bend your right knee and bring the heel toward your glutes.
3. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
4. Keep knees together and gently pull the heel up until you feel a stretch along the front of the thigh.
5. Hold 20-30 seconds, release, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the torso upright, do not lean forward.
2. Keep the supporting leg slightly bent for balance.
3. Tuck the pelvis slightly to deepen the stretch.
4. Pull gently and hold steady, do not bounce.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a stable surface for balance if needed.
2. Bend your right knee and bring your heel toward your glutes.
3. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand and keep your knees close together.
4. Pull your ankle gently upward until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
5. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, release, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to reduce injury risk.
2. Keep the supporting leg slightly bent for balance.
3. Keep your torso upright and do not lean forward or back.
4. Tuck your pelvis under to deepen the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and posture upright.
2. Clasp your hands behind your back and interlock your fingers.
3. Straighten your arms and slowly lift your hands upward until you feel a stretch in your shoulders and chest.
4. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
5. Lower your hands and release the clasp.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight without bending the elbows.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed and down, away from your ears.
3. Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching.
4. Open your chest forward to increase the stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Keep your palms facing forward and elbows pointing down.
3. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
2. Brace your core and keep your back straight to avoid arching the lower back.
3. Press in a smooth path, keeping the dumbbells over your shoulders.
4. Keep your neck relaxed and let the shoulders do the work.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hands on your hips for balance.
2. Shift your weight onto your left leg.
3. Slowly lift your right leg out to the side as high as is comfortable, keeping it straight.
4. Hold briefly, then lower your right leg back down with control.
5. Finish your reps, then switch to the left leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean to the side.
2. Keep the supporting leg slightly bent for balance.
3. Lift through the hip, not by swinging the leg.
4. Start with a smaller range and increase it as strength improves.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and posture upright.
2. Raise your right arm overhead and let your left hand hang at your side.
3. Gently lean your torso to the left, reaching your right arm over your head.
4. Feel the stretch along the right side of your torso and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
5. Return to the start, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and do not push them out to the side.
2. Keep your shoulders relaxed, away from your ears.
3. Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching.
4. Increase the lean gradually as flexibility improves.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your left arm up and your right arm down, palms forward.
2. Keep your core braced and posture tall.
3. Smoothly raise your right arm overhead while lowering your left arm, with a slight core rotation.
4. Keep both arms straight throughout.
5. Continue alternating arms in a controlled swimming motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stay balanced.
2. Move smoothly and avoid jerky swings.
3. Keep arms straight the whole time.
4. Breathe steadily through each cycle.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Lift your right leg straight up to hip height while raising your left arm to touch your right toes.
3. Keep the lifted leg as straight as possible.
4. Lower your leg and arm back down with control.
5. Repeat on the opposite side, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both the lifted leg and reaching arm straight.
2. Keep your support leg slightly bent for balance.
3. Brace your core to stay stable.
4. Exhale as you reach for the toe.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended forward and parallel.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise both arms diagonally overhead to form a Y shape.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back at the top.
5. Lower your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and controlled for full muscle activation.
2. Keep arms in a clean diagonal line, no swinging.
3. Drive the lift from your shoulders and mid-back.
4. Exhale as you raise the arms.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with arms and legs spread to form an X shape.
2. Press your lower back into the floor and brace your core.
3. Crunch your abs to lift your shoulders and legs, reaching your hands toward your ankles.
4. Lower your arms and legs back down with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift using your abs, not momentum.
2. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the movement controlled at both ends.
4. Use a mat to cushion your back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Bend your knees slightly into a half-squat to load the jump.
3. Explode upward, spreading legs out to the sides and extending arms overhead into a star shape.
4. Land softly with feet together and arms down, bending your knees to absorb impact.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the jump from your legs and glutes.
2. Land with knees bent to absorb impact.
3. Keep your core braced in the air.
4. Start with smaller jumps to lock in form.

instructions:
1. Adjust the seat so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
2. Sit upright with a straight back and grip the handlebars lightly.
3. Place the balls of your feet on the pedals.
4. Pedal in a smooth circular motion, pushing down and pulling up.
5. Set the resistance to match your target intensity and keep pedaling.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Start at low resistance and raise it as your endurance improves.
3. Breathe steadily and deeply throughout.
4. Drive through the whole pedal stroke, not just the downward push.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a sturdy chair with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Place your left foot fully on the chair seat.
3. Push through your left heel to lift your body up until both feet are on the chair.
4. Step down with your right foot, then your left foot.
5. Switch the leading leg each set.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you step up, inhale as you step down.
2. Drive through your heel to load the glutes and quads.
3. Make sure the chair is stable before starting.
4. Keep your torso upright and avoid pushing off the trailing foot.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to the high pulley and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms down.
2. Step back, bend your knees slightly and hinge your torso forward a little.
3. Keep your arms nearly straight with a soft elbow bend.
4. Pull the bar down to your thighs in a wide arc, squeezing your lats.
5. Slowly return the bar overhead under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down, inhale on the return.
2. Keep your arms straight so the lats do the work, not the biceps.
3. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.
4. Move only at the shoulders, keeping the torso still.

instructions:
