1. Sit at the cable row station with feet on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the straight bar with a close grip, palms down.
3. Sit tall with a straight back and braced core.
4. Pull the bar to your abdomen, keeping elbows close and squeezing your shoulder blades.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you extend.
2. Lead with the elbows to drive lat engagement.
3. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.
4. Keep your torso still and avoid swinging for momentum.

instructions:
1. Sit at the cable row station with feet on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the straight bar just wider than shoulder-width, palms down.
3. Sit tall with a straight back and braced core.
4. Pull the bar to your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Slowly extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you extend.
2. Drive your elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades.
3. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging.
4. Keep your torso still and avoid swinging for momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, and place the band under both feet.
2. Hold an end of the band in each hand between your legs at hip level.
3. Bend your knees and push your hips back, keeping your chest up and back straight.
4. Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you drive up.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes, pushing them out.
3. Keep your weight on your heels, not your toes.
4. Keep your chest up and torso upright.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, and place the band under both feet.
2. Hold an end of the band in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward and elbows down.
3. Bend your knees and push your hips back, keeping your chest up and back straight.
4. Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your heels to stand back up while keeping the band at your shoulders.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you drive up.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes, pushing them out.
3. Keep your weight on your heels, not your toes.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced under the band load.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with your arms reaching forward and legs extended behind you.
2. Lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor together as high as is comfortable.
3. Squeeze your lower back and glutes at the top.
4. Lower with control back to the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the lift from your lower back and glutes, not momentum.
2. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a mat for comfort.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with your arms reaching forward and legs extended behind you.
2. Lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor together as high as is comfortable.
3. Hold the position for 5 to 10 seconds while squeezing your lower back and glutes.
4. Lower with control back to the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the lift from your lower back and glutes, not momentum.
2. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
3. Breathe steadily during the hold instead of holding your breath.
4. Use a mat for comfort.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with a band anchored low in front of you, holding an end in each hand with arms extended forward and legs extended behind.
2. Lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor together, squeezing your lower back and glutes.
3. Bend your elbows and pull the band toward your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Extend your arms back out while keeping tension on the band.
5. Lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead the pull with your elbows and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
2. Keep your chest and legs lifted throughout the row.
3. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you extend.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with a resistance band held in both hands, arms extended in front and legs straight behind.
2. Lift your arms and chest off the floor, engaging your lower back and glutes.
3. Holding the lift, bend your elbows and pull the band back toward your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Extend your arms forward again while staying lifted.
5. Lower your chest and arms back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and pull, inhale as you extend and lower.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades hard at the top of the pull.
3. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
4. Move slowly and avoid jerking the band.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your elbows at your sides with forearms pointing up and hands relaxed.
3. Press your elbows into the floor and lift your upper back and shoulders off the ground.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and hold briefly.
5. Lower your upper back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
2. Drive the movement by retracting your shoulder blades, not by shrugging.
3. Use a mat to cushion your back and elbows.
4. Keep the lift smooth and controlled.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height.
2. Place your feet in the handles and assume a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on the floor.
3. Brace your core to keep your body in a straight line.
4. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
5. Push through your hands to straighten your arms back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your hips level and core tight to stop your body from sagging.
3. Make sure your feet are secure in the handles before starting.
4. Lower under control to manage the added instability.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles overhead.
2. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and hang with arms straight and feet off the floor.
3. Brace your core and pull your knees up toward your elbows.
4. Curl your pelvis up and bring your knees as close to your elbows as possible.
5. Lower your legs back to the hanging position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl your pelvis up to drive the move with your abs, not your hip flexors.
2. Exhale as you raise your knees, inhale as you lower.
3. Avoid swinging by lowering slowly and staying tight.
4. Start with a smaller range and increase it as you get stronger.

instructions:
1. Set one suspension trainer handle close to the floor.
2. Stand beside it, place your right foot in the handle, and keep your left foot flat on the floor.
3. Bend your left knee and push your hips back into a squat while reaching both hands toward the floor.
4. Keep your right leg straight and let it extend out to the side.
5. Push through your left heel to stand back up, keeping the right leg extended.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Exhale as you stand up, inhale as you lower.
2. Keep your working knee tracking over your toes.
3. Keep your chest up to protect your lower back.
4. Control the slide of the suspended foot to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and back flat against the bench.
2. Press your palms hard against the flat sides of a weight plate at chest level, fingers pointing up.
3. Squeeze the plate and press it straight out until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep squeezing the plate throughout to maximise chest tension.
5. Bring the plate back to your chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press through your chest, not your shoulders.
2. Squeeze the plate hard the whole time to keep the chest loaded.
3. Keep your back flat against the bench.
4. Breathe out as you press, in as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and back against the bench.
2. Press your palms hard against the flat sides of a weight plate at chest level, fingers pointing up.
3. Squeeze the plate and press it straight out until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep squeezing the plate throughout to maximise chest tension.
5. Bring the plate back to your chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press through your chest, not your shoulders.
2. Squeeze the plate hard the whole time to keep the chest loaded.
3. Keep your back flat against the bench.
4. Breathe out as you press, in as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie on an incline bench set to about 30 degrees with your back against the bench.
2. Press your palms hard against the flat sides of a weight plate at chest level, fingers pointing up.
3. Squeeze the plate and press it straight out until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep squeezing the plate throughout to maximise upper chest tension.
5. Bring the plate back to your chest under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press through your upper chest, not your shoulders.
2. Squeeze the plate hard the whole time to keep the chest loaded.
3. Keep the angle near 30 degrees to bias the upper chest.
4. Breathe out as you press, in as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of a trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your hips and knees and grip the handles with a neutral grip.
3. Brace your core, keep your chest up and back flat.
4. Push through your heels and drive up, extending hips and knees together.
5. Stand tall, then lower the bar to the floor under control by bending hips and knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout.
2. Push the floor away through your heels.
3. Keep the bar handles in line with your mid-foot.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of a trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your hips and knees and grip the handles with a neutral grip.
3. Stand tall with the bar at arm's length, core braced and back flat.
4. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears and squeeze at the top.
5. Lower your shoulders back down under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Shrug straight up, do not roll your shoulders.
2. Squeeze your traps at the top for a moment.
3. Keep your neck relaxed and your arms straight.
4. Breathe out as you shrug up, in as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the cable to a low position and grip the handle in one hand.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back flat and knees slightly bent.
3. Pin your upper arm against your side with the elbow bent at 90 degrees.
4. Straighten the elbow to extend your arm fully behind you, keeping the upper arm still.
5. Lower under control back to the bent position, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the elbow; keep the upper arm locked in place.
2. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.
3. Keep your core braced to stop the torso swinging.
4. Use a light weight to keep the motion strict.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine and adjust the seat so your upper arms are parallel to the floor at the handles.
2. Grip the handles with elbows bent and tucked close to your sides.
3. Keep your torso upright to keep tension on the triceps.
4. Press the handles down by straightening your elbows fully.
5. Return slowly to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows tucked to your sides throughout.
2. Stay upright; leaning forward shifts work to the chest.
3. Press through full extension and squeeze the triceps.
4. Control the negative; do not let the weight drop.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Raise your right arm to shoulder height and bring it across your chest.
3. Use your left hand to hold the right arm just below the elbow.
4. Draw the arm across your chest until you feel a gentle stretch in the triceps and rear shoulder.
5. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso facing forward; do not twist.
2. Breathe slowly and relax into the stretch.
3. Pull gently; the stretch should not hurt.
4. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Interlace your fingers and extend your arms straight ahead at shoulder height, palms facing away.
3. Round your upper back and push your hands forward, separating your shoulder blades.
4. Drop your chin toward your chest to deepen the stretch.
5. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, feeling the stretch between the shoulder blades.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe slowly and relax into the stretch.
2. Keep your shoulders down, not shrugged toward your ears.
3. Push the hands away to spread the shoulder blades.
4. Keep the stretch gentle and pain-free.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip about shoulder-width.
2. Let the bar hang against your thighs with arms straight.
3. Pull the bar up the front of your body by lifting your elbows.
4. Raise until the bar reaches chest height, keeping elbows above the wrists.
5. Lower the bar slowly back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead the movement with your elbows.
2. Keep the bar close to your body throughout.
3. Exhale lifting, inhale lowering.
4. Do not swing or use momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing back.
2. Let your arms hang straight down so the band is taut.
3. Pull the handles straight up toward your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the band close to your body.
4. Raise until your elbows are slightly above shoulder height and pointing out to the sides.
5. Lower the handles back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, keeping them higher than the wrists.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the torso upright and avoid swinging.
4. The band tension peaks at the top, so control the lockout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your thighs.
2. Let the dumbbells rest against the front of your thighs.
3. Pull the dumbbells straight up toward your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the weights close to your body.
4. Raise until your elbows reach shoulder height and your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, keeping them higher than the wrists.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the dumbbells close to the body throughout.
4. Avoid using momentum to swing the weight up.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
2. Let the bar rest against your thighs with arms fully extended.
3. Pull the bar straight up along the front of your body, leading with your elbows.
4. Raise until the bar reaches chest height, keeping the elbows higher than the wrists.
5. Lower the bar back down with control until arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows to drive the shoulders and traps.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the bar close to the body throughout.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent 90 degrees with upper arms raised out to the sides, parallel to the floor.
2. Start with your forearms pointing down toward the floor.
3. Rotate your forearms upward until your hands point toward the ceiling, keeping the upper arms fixed.
4. Slowly rotate the forearms back down to the starting position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms still and parallel to the floor throughout.
2. Move slowly and controlled to engage the rotator cuff.
3. Squeeze the rear shoulders at the top of the rotation.
4. Keep the neck relaxed and the wrists neutral.

instructions:
1. Lie sideways on a 45 degree hyperextension bench with one hip against the pad and feet anchored under the footrests.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
3. Lower your torso sideways toward the floor by bending at the waist.
4. Raise your torso back up by contracting the obliques on the upper side until your body is straight.
5. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Move in a slow, controlled lateral arc without twisting.
2. Drive the movement from the obliques, not the arms.
3. Keep the neck neutral and in line with the spine.
4. Avoid bouncing at the bottom of the bend.

instructions:
1. Set your feet on the footrests and press your thighs against the padded platform.
2. Place your hands behind your head and lean forward from the hips.
3. Raise your torso by extending your back.
4. As you rise, twist your torso to one side.
5. Lower under control and return to the start, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist smoothly and avoid jerking to protect the spine.
2. Keep the core braced throughout to support the lower back.
3. Exhale as you lift and twist, inhale as you lower.
4. Stop the extension when your torso is in line with your legs.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel with both hands on the floor in front of you.
2. Keep your arms straight and your back flat.
3. Roll the wheel forward until your body forms a straight line, keeping your core braced.
4. Pull the wheel back to the start using your core.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core braced to protect the lower back.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Do not let the lower back sag at full extension.
4. Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel with both hands on the floor in front of you.
2. Keep your arms straight and your back flat.
3. Roll the wheel forward halfway, keeping your core braced.
4. Pull the wheel back to the start using your core.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core braced to protect the lower back.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Stop before the lower back sags.
4. Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel with both hands on the floor in front of you.
2. Keep your arms straight and your back flat.
3. Roll the wheel forward and to the left, keeping your core braced.
4. Pull the wheel back to the start using your core.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Roll out only as far as you can control to spare the lower back.
2. Keep the obliques tight to resist twisting.
3. Move slowly and avoid momentum.
4. Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel with both hands on the floor in front of you.
2. Roll the wheel forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
3. Hold this position with the core braced and the body stable.
4. Pull the wheel back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the spine neutral and do not let the lower back sag.
2. Brace the whole core to hold the position.
3. Keep the obliques tight to stop the torso twisting.
4. Breathe steadily during the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your arms extended overhead, holding the ab wheel with both hands.
2. Brace your core and lift your upper back slightly off the floor into a small crunch, keeping your arms straight and the wheel overhead.
3. Pulse up and down in a short range, keeping constant tension on your abs.
4. Keep your lower back flat and your neck relaxed.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the range small and controlled to keep tension on the abs.
2. Brace your core to keep the lower back flat against the floor.
3. Do not pull on your neck; lift with your abs.
4. Exhale as you pulse up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a mat holding the ab wheel on the floor in front of you, arms straight and back neutral.
2. Brace your core and roll the wheel forward and to the right, extending your body into a diagonal line.
3. Keep your hips slightly back and resist your torso twisting toward the floor.
4. Pull the wheel back to the start using your core and lats.
5. Repeat to the right side, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Roll out only as far as you can keep your lower back from sagging.
2. Resist rotation; keep the torso square as the wheel tracks to the side.
3. Drive the return with your abs and lats, not your arms.
4. Inhale as you roll out, exhale as you roll back in.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet off the floor in a tabletop position.
2. Hold the ab wheel overhead with both hands and arms straight.
3. Crunch up and bring the wheel toward your shins, then place it gently on your shins.
4. Lower your upper body back to the floor, keeping your legs in tabletop.
5. Crunch up again, grab the wheel from your shins, and lower back down.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shins parallel to the floor throughout the movement.
2. Lift with your abs, not momentum.
3. Keep your neck relaxed and chin slightly tucked.
4. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Raise your arms toward your knees at shoulder height.
3. Brace your core and lift your upper back off the floor, reaching forward.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your neck relaxed and do not pull on it with your hands.
2. Lift with your abs, not momentum.
3. Keep your lower back in contact with the floor.
4. Exhale as you crunch up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Adjust the seat and resistance, then sit on the machine and set your feet on the footrests.
2. Grab the handles with your elbows pointing forward.
3. Brace your core and crunch forward, curling your chest toward your knees.
4. Hold briefly at the bottom of the crunch.
5. Return slowly to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you crunch forward, inhale as you return.
2. Move with your abs, not momentum.
3. Keep your lower back against the backrest.
4. Control the return; do not let the weight pull you back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or reach forward.
3. Exhale and curl your upper back off the floor.
4. Hold the top contraction for 2 to 5 seconds.
5. Inhale and lower slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back on the floor and curl only the upper spine.
2. Keep your neck relaxed and do not pull on your head.
3. Squeeze the abs hard during the hold.
4. Move slowly and under control.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders.
2. Brace your core and keep a flat back.
3. Walk your hands forward to extend the body into a long reach.
4. Keep hips from sagging as you reach full extension.
5. Walk your hands back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stop the lower back from arching.
2. Do not let the hips drop at full extension.
3. Move slowly and control the reach.
4. Breathe out as you extend forward.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees.
3. Drive your arms forward and back in a running rhythm.
4. Keep your core tight and shoulders relaxed.
5. Continue for the set time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep elbows bent at about 90 degrees.
2. Drive from the shoulder, not the hands.
3. Keep your torso still and core braced.
4. Match a steady running cadence.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Let your arms hang relaxed at your sides.
3. Swing both arms across your body to one side.
4. Swing them back across to the other side.
5. Let your torso rotate slightly with each swing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Let the torso rotate to engage the obliques.
2. Keep the swing smooth and controlled.
3. Keep your core braced throughout.
4. Keep your shoulders relaxed.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Let your arms hang at your sides.
3. Walk forward at an easy pace.
4. Swing your arms forward and back with each step.
5. Keep your shoulders relaxed and core tight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Swing the arms naturally with each step.
2. Drive the movement from the shoulders.
3. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
4. Keep a steady walking pace.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and heels on the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head, elbows wide.
3. Lift your chest and twist your torso, bringing one elbow toward the opposite knee.
4. Lower under control back to the floor.
5. Twist to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Move slowly and avoid pulling on your neck.
3. Exhale as you twist, inhale as you lower.
4. Drive the rotation from your core, not your arms.

instructions:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a handle in each hand, arms extended down, palms facing forward.
3. Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right handle toward your shoulder.
4. Lower it under control to the start.
5. Curl the left handle the same way, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight throughout.
2. Move slowly so the band controls you, not momentum.
3. The band tension peaks at the top, so squeeze hard there.
4. Keep your back straight and shoulders down.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing each other.
3. Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right dumbbell toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
5. Curl the left dumbbell the same way, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists neutral and straight.
2. Control the lowering phase, no swinging.
3. Keep your torso upright and still.
4. Focus on the squeeze at the top.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing each other.
3. Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right dumbbell toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
5. Curl the left dumbbell the same way, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists neutral and straight.
2. Brace your core to stop your torso swaying.
3. Control the lowering phase, no momentum.
4. Keep your back straight and shoulders back.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended about 45 degrees off the floor and arms reaching overhead.
2. Lift your shoulders off the mat and brace your core.
3. Pull your right knee toward your chest while swinging both arms in an arc to your sides.
4. Straighten the leg and lower your arms and shoulders to the start.
5. Repeat with the left leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
2. Move slowly and with control, no momentum.
3. Exhale as you crunch the knee in, inhale as you extend.
4. Keep the extended leg from dropping too low if your back arches.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms resting on the floor by your sides.
2. Press your lower back into the floor and lift both legs straight up to a 90-degree angle with your torso.
3. Lower one leg under control until just before it touches the floor.
4. Raise it back to the top, then lower the other leg the same way.
5. Keep both legs straight throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to protect your spine.
2. Move slowly and with control, no swinging.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Stop the lower leg before it touches the floor to keep tension on the abs.

instructions:
1. Sit with legs extended forward and palms on the floor behind your hips.
2. Press through your hands and heels to lift your hips into a straight line from shoulders to feet.
3. Keeping the hips lifted, raise one straight leg as high as you can.
4. Lower it under control, then raise the other leg.
5. Hold the hips steady the whole time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a straight line from head to heels, do not let the hips sag.
2. Squeeze your glutes to hold the hips up.
3. Move the legs slowly and with control.
4. Exhale as you raise each leg.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms resting on the floor by your sides.
2. Lift your head and shoulder blades off the floor and hold them up.
3. Raise both legs straight up to a 90-degree angle with your torso.
4. Lower one leg under control until just before it touches the floor.
5. Raise it back up, then lower the other leg the same way.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades lifted the entire set to load the upper abs.
2. Press your lower back into the floor to protect your spine.
3. Move slowly with no swinging.
4. Exhale as you lift each leg.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended straight and arms by your sides.
2. Press your lower back into the floor.
3. Raise one straight leg toward the ceiling while the other stays near the floor.
4. Lower it under control, then raise the other leg.
5. Keep both legs straight throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back in contact with the floor to avoid arching.
2. Move with control, no swinging.
3. Exhale as you raise each leg.
4. Keep the resting leg just off the floor to maintain tension.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your right hand behind your head and your left hand on the floor for support.
3. Crunch up and twist your torso, bringing your right elbow toward your left knee.
4. Lower under control to the start.
5. Switch hands and repeat to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Twist using your obliques, do not pull on your neck.
2. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
3. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
4. Exhale as you crunch and twist.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands up in a guard near your chin.
2. Punch forward with your right arm, rotating your torso slightly.
3. Return your right hand to guard.
4. Punch forward with your left arm, rotating your torso slightly.
5. Return to guard and alternate sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to control torso rotation.
2. Snap each punch out and return the hand fast to guard.
3. Keep a slight bend in your knees for stability.
4. Exhale sharply on each punch.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Step your right leg back into a lunge, bending both knees while reaching your hands toward your left foot.
3. Push off your right foot to return to standing.
4. Step your left leg back into a lunge, reaching your hands toward your right foot.
5. Return to standing and alternate sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front shin near vertical and weight on the front heel.
2. Brace your core to stay balanced.
3. Move with control rather than rushing.
4. Drive through the front foot to stand up.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet on the floor.
2. Prop your upper body up on your elbows.
3. Raise your right knee toward your chest, keeping the knee bent.
4. Lower your right foot to tap the floor as you raise your left knee toward your chest.
5. Keep alternating knees in a steady rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.
2. Move with control and tap the floor lightly.
3. Keep the bend in your knees consistent.
4. Exhale as each knee rises.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended at your sides, palms facing forward.
2. Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
3. Squeeze the bicep at the top, then lower the dumbbell with control.
4. Curl the left dumbbell up the same way.
5. Lower with control and alternate arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and let only the forearms move.
2. Work both arms evenly to avoid imbalances.
3. Control the lowering phase, do not drop the weight.
4. Use a weight you can curl without swinging your torso.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent with fists at your chest.
2. Curl your right heel toward your glutes while punching forward with your left arm.
3. Lower your right leg and return your left arm to your chest.
4. Curl your left heel toward your glutes while punching forward with your right arm.
5. Return to the start and alternate sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the hamstring as you curl the heel up.
2. Keep a steady rhythm so both sides work evenly.
3. Stay tall and brace your core to protect your back.
4. Snap each punch out and return the hand quickly.

instructions:
1. Start in a downward dog position with hands and feet on the mat and hips lifted into an inverted V.
2. Press the floor away to keep the shoulders strong and the spine long.
3. Draw the right knee toward the chest while balancing on both hands and the left foot.
4. Extend the right leg back to the start.
5. Draw the left knee toward the chest, then return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core braced to hold the hips stable.
2. Keep the hips square to the mat and avoid twisting.
3. Move slowly and with control.
4. Press evenly through both hands to protect the shoulders.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and hands by your sides or behind your head.
2. Press your lower back into the mat.
3. Raise one leg straight toward the ceiling without bending the knee.
4. Lower that leg under control while raising the other leg.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the lower back pressed into the mat throughout.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the legs straight and the movement slow.
4. Lower the leg only as far as you can without the back arching.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in the knees.
2. Clasp your hands in front of your chest.
3. Step one foot out to the side into a wider stance, bending into the supporting hip.
4. Push off and return to the starting position.
5. Step out with the other foot and return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the chest up and torso upright.
2. Push the hips back as you step out.
3. Drive through the heel to return to center.
4. Keep a steady rhythm for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on the hips for balance.
2. Pull the toes of both feet up toward the shins.
3. Hold briefly at the top of the lift.
4. Lower the toes back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core engaged for balance.
2. Move slowly to isolate the shin muscles.
3. Keep the legs still and drive the movement from the ankles.
4. Lift the toes as high as possible without rocking back on the heels.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on the hips for balance.
2. Rise onto the toes, lifting both heels off the floor.
3. Hold briefly at the top.
4. Lower the heels back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
2. Rise as high onto the toes as possible.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
4. Hold a wall or rail if balance is an issue.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hands on hips.
2. Lift one foot off the floor a few cm.
3. Rotate the ankle slowly in small controlled circles.
4. Reverse direction and circle the other way.
5. Lower the foot and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the leg still and move only the ankle.
2. Make the circles as large as the joint allows.
3. Move slowly for control.
4. Do equal circles in both directions on each side.

instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line.
2. Bend the right elbow to lower the chest toward the right hand.
3. Keep the left arm extended straight out to the side.
4. Push back up to the start.
5. Lower toward the left hand while extending the right arm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep shoulders and hips level throughout.
2. Exhale on the push, inhale on the descent.
3. Keep the extended arm straight to load the working side.
4. Brace the core to resist twisting.

instructions:
1. Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
4. Rotate the thumbs up at the top to externally rotate the shoulders.
5. Lower the arms back to the sides under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
2. Keep the torso still and avoid swinging.
3. Control the lowering phase.
4. Stop the raise at shoulder height.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a mat with arms extended to the sides and legs straight.
2. Lift the arms, chest, and legs off the floor into a Superman position.
3. Sweep the arms in a circular motion from the sides around to the front.
4. Bring the arms back to the sides, keeping the chest and legs lifted.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glutes to support the lower back.
2. Move the arms slowly and with control.
3. Keep the chest and legs lifted the whole time.
4. Keep the neck neutral by looking down.

instructions:
1. Sit on the AirBike and adjust the seat height.
2. Place feet on the pedals and grip the moving handles.
3. Begin pedaling while pushing and pulling the handles in time with the legs.
4. Increase pedal speed and arm effort to a fast pace.
5. Hold the fast pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Breathe steadily and keep a consistent rhythm.
2. Drive evenly with both legs and arms.
3. Keep the torso braced and movements controlled.
4. Push through the heels on the pedals.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seat and adjust its height so your knees have a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
2. Place your feet on the pedals and grip the handles.
3. Pedal at a steady, moderate pace while pushing and pulling the handles in rhythm with your legs.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
5. Hold the steady pace for the set time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive evenly with arms and legs to share the load.
2. Keep your back tall and core engaged to stay stable on the seat.
3. Breathe in a steady rhythm matched to your pace.
4. Keep movements smooth and controlled.

instructions:
1. Sit on the seat and adjust its height so your knees have a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
2. Place your feet on the pedals and grip the handles.
3. Drive the pedals as fast as possible while pushing and pulling the handles hard in rhythm with your legs.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
5. Hold maximum effort for the set time, then ease off.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive explosively with both arms and legs to reach top speed.
2. Brace your core hard to keep your torso stable during the sprint.
3. Use short, sharp breaths to sustain the effort.
4. Stay seated and avoid bouncing on the seat.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench or box facing away from it.
2. Rest the top of your back foot on the bench and hold a stable support with one hand for balance.
3. Keep your chest upright and your front foot flat on the floor.
4. Lower by bending your front knee and hip until your back knee is near the floor.
5. Drive through your front heel to stand back up, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
2. Keep your front shin near vertical to load the quads and glutes.
3. Keep your hips square to avoid leaning to one side.
4. Control the descent and pause briefly at the bottom.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine.
2. Grasp the handles with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull your body upward until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull.
2. Set the assistance so you can complete clean reps with full range.
3. Pull with your back and biceps rather than swinging.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine.
2. Grasp the parallel handles with palms facing each other, about shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull your body upward until your chin clears the handles.
4. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tracking close to your body as you pull.
2. Set the assistance so you can complete clean reps with full range.
3. Drive your elbows down to lead with your back muscles.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg and hold a sturdy support with both hands for balance.
2. Extend the other leg straight forward and keep it off the floor.
3. Bend the standing hip and knee to lower slowly, keeping your chest up and the free leg straight.
4. Descend until your glutes are near your heel.
5. Push through the heel to stand back up, switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower under control and do not collapse at the bottom.
2. Keep the free leg straight and roughly parallel to the floor.
3. Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
4. Keep weight on the mid-foot and heel of the working leg.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the assisted pull-up machine pad and grip the handles overhand, just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Let your arms extend fully and your shoulder blades rise.
3. Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, driving the elbows down.
4. Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tracking down and slightly in, not flared wide.
2. Set the assistance so you can complete clean reps with control.
3. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
4. Pull your shoulder blades down and back at the top.

instructions:
1. Set up in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line.
2. Have a partner place a weight plate on your upper back.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
4. Push through your palms to straighten your arms back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a straight line from head to heels and brace your core.
2. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.
3. Make sure the plate is centered and secure on the upper back.
4. Keep elbows around 45 degrees, not flared to the sides.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with your lower abdomen on an exercise ball.
2. Plant your feet firmly on the floor with legs extended.
3. Place your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
4. Bend at the waist to lower your upper body over the ball.
5. Squeeze your lower back and glutes to lift your torso until your body is straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet firmly planted for stability.
2. Lift with your lower back and glutes, not your neck or arms.
3. Do not hyperextend at the top; stop at a straight line.
4. Move slowly and keep the ball steady.

instructions:
1. Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull and tuck so your head drops toward the floor and your legs lift overhead.
3. Pass your legs under the bar and lower into a horizontal position.
4. Hold your body straight and parallel to the floor, facing down.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to hold a straight line.
2. Keep your arms straight and your grip firm throughout.
3. Breathe steadily during the hold.
4. Build with tuck and straddle progressions before the full lever.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is about 45 degrees, keeping your back straight.
3. Let your arms hang down with palms facing back.
4. Raise your straight arms back and up until they are roughly level with your torso.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
6. Lower under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and lead with the rear shoulders.
2. Do not swing or use momentum; move slowly.
3. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.
4. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.

instructions:
1. Stand on the balance board with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Brace your core to steady the board.
3. Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee and hip into a squat.
4. Push back to centre through the heel.
5. Repeat to the other side. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working knee in line with the toes.
2. Brace your core to control the unstable surface.
3. Fix your eyes on a point ahead to hold balance.
4. Move slowly and stay in control.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold an exercise ball tight against one side with that arm.
2. Extend the other arm forward for balance.
3. Bend at the hips and knees to lower into a squat, keeping your chest up and back straight.
4. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your heels to stand. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Press the ball firmly to your side to keep your torso square.
2. Do not let the ball pull you sideways; resist the lean.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Brace your core throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a slam ball with both hands.
2. Lift the ball overhead, fully extending your body.
3. Forcefully slam the ball to the floor, hinging at the hips and crunching your torso down.
4. Squat to pick the ball back up.
5. Stand and lift it overhead again. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the slam with your abs and lats, not just your arms.
2. Hinge at the hips as you slam to protect your lower back.
3. Exhale sharply on the slam.
4. Catch or trap the ball on rebound to stay in control.

instructions:
1. Stand on the centre of the band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and slightly bent knees.
3. Let your arms hang straight down with a slight elbow bend.
4. Pull the handles to your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Anchor the band securely under both feet to stop slipping.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced throughout.
3. Drive with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a mat and loop a resistance band around both feet.
2. Place your hands behind your head and extend your legs, lifting your shoulders off the floor.
3. Bring your right knee toward your chest and twist your torso to move your left elbow toward it.
4. Switch sides, bringing your left knee in and your right elbow toward it in a pedaling motion.
5. Keep alternating sides in a controlled rhythm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your abs, not by pulling on your neck.
2. Twist the torso fully so the obliques engage on each rep.
3. Exhale as you crunch and twist, inhale as you switch sides.
4. Move slowly and keep your lower back pressed toward the mat.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and the resistance band under both feet.
2. Hold the band ends with a narrow grip, palms facing forward and arms straight.
3. Curl your hands up toward your shoulders, keeping your hands close together.
4. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your biceps.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides through the whole curl.
2. Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the biceps.
4. Stand on enough band to give resistance through the full range.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and the resistance band under both feet, crossed in front of you.
2. Hold each handle in the opposite hand with arms hanging at your hips.
3. Keep your right leg straight and lift it out to the side against the band.
4. Pause at the top with tension on the band.
5. Lower the leg under control back to the start, then switch to the left leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning to the side.
2. Point your toes forward to target the gluteus medius.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg with momentum.
4. Keep the standing leg slightly bent for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and the resistance band under both feet.
2. Hold a handle in each hand with arms straight down and palms facing your hips.
3. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees, keeping your back flat, until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
4. Press through your heels and drive your hips forward to stand up tall.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout the lift.
2. Drive through the hips, not the lower back.
3. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a band tension that lets you keep good form.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at ankle height to a fixed point on one side.
2. Loop the band around the ankle closest to the anchor and step out to create tension.
3. Stand tall with feet apart and the working leg out to the side.
4. Pull the working leg across your body toward the midline against the band.
5. Pause briefly, then return the leg under control to the start. Switch sides. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your pelvis level and torso upright through the movement.
2. Move from the hip, not by twisting the trunk.
3. Control the return so the band does not snap the leg back.
4. Hold a stable support if you need help with balance.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at chest height. Stand facing the anchor with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold the band with both arms extended straight forward at chest height.
3. Pull your shoulder blades back and together, keeping your arms straight.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades fully at the back of the motion.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the motion from your shoulder blades, not your arms.
2. Keep your elbows straight throughout the movement.
3. Exhale as you retract and inhale as you return.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the upper back.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band above head height. Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat for balance.
2. Hold the band with the same-side hand as the kneeling leg, arm fully extended toward the anchor.
3. Pull the band down toward your torso by bending the elbow and driving it back.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blade at the end of the pull.
5. Slowly extend your arm to return to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced to resist rotation.
2. Lead the pull with your elbow, not your hand.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the end range.
4. Avoid jerking; control both directions.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at a low point. Lie on your back facing the anchor and loop the band around one foot.
2. Bend that knee and pull it toward your chest against the band tension.
3. Keep the other leg relaxed and extended on the floor.
4. Press your foot forward and straighten the leg fully.
5. Slowly bend the knee back to the start under control.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Brace your core to keep your hips and torso still.
2. Set up so the band has tension at the start.
3. Press through the whole foot, not just the toes.
4. Control the return rather than letting the band snap back.

instructions:
1. Loop a resistance band securely around a pull-up bar. Place one or both feet in the bottom of the loop.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing forward.
3. Start in a dead hang with arms fully extended.
4. Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower yourself with control to a full hang.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull with your back and arms, not momentum.
2. Thicker bands give more assistance; pick one to match your strength.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back as you rise.
4. Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at a low point. Stand facing away with feet shoulder-width apart and the band passing between your legs, held in both hands in front.
2. Keep your knees slightly bent and your spine neutral.
3. Push your hips back and hinge forward, letting your hands travel between your legs.
4. Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand fully upright.
5. Pause briefly with glutes contracted at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips rather than squatting down.
2. Keep your spine neutral and back flat throughout.
3. Drive the movement with your glutes, not your arms.
4. Keep a slight bend in the knees the whole time.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and anchor one end of the band under the foot on the working side.
2. Hold the other end in your working hand at shoulder height, palm facing inward.
3. Brace your core and press the hand straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the hand back to shoulder height under control.
5. Finish all reps, switch sides, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrist straight and stacked over the elbow.
2. Brace your core to resist leaning toward the working side.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Anchor the band firmly under your foot so it cannot slip.

instructions:
1. Anchor the band at chest height and stand facing away from it.
2. Hold the handle in your working hand with the arm extended out to the side, palm forward.
3. Set feet shoulder-width apart with knees slightly bent.
4. Pull the hand in an arc across to the center of your chest.
5. Return the arm out to the side under control.
6. Finish all reps, switch sides, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout the movement.
2. Brace your core to stop the torso from rotating.
3. Squeeze the chest at the end of the arc.
4. Exhale as you bring the hand in, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Loop a band around your front leg just below the knee and anchor it in front at knee level.
2. Stand in a split stance with that leg forward and the other foot behind you.
3. Hold your hands together at your chest and keep your torso upright.
4. Bend both knees and lower straight down until the front thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and let the band hold you back.
2. Drive through the front heel to load the quads.
3. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
4. Set band tension before starting so it stays taut.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band in front of you at chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
2. Step back until the band is taut and set feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Lower into a squat until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
4. Drive up through your heels to stand and at the same time row both handles to your ribs.
5. Extend the arms and return to the squat in one motion.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Time the row so it finishes as you reach the top of the squat.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the row.
3. Keep your chest up and back flat in the squat.
4. Exhale as you stand and row, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band overhead and hold the handle in your working hand.
2. Stand tall with your elbow tucked at your side and bent.
3. Keep the upper arm still and push the handle down until the arm is straight.
4. Bend the elbow to return the handle to the start under control.
5. Finish all reps, switch sides, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout.
2. Move only the forearm, not the shoulder.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working side.
4. Exhale as you push down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a resistance band looped around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Place both feet flat on a raised platform about 30 cm high, knees bent, and rest a pad or bar across your hips.
3. Drive through your heels and extend your hips upward until your torso and thighs form a straight line, pushing your knees outward against the band.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, then lower your hips under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push your knees outward against the band throughout to keep tension on the glutes.
2. Tuck your chin and keep ribs down to avoid arching the lower back.
3. Pause and squeeze at the top for full hip extension.
4. Drive through the heels, not the toes.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench with feet flat on the floor and eyes under the bar.
2. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it to arms over your chest.
3. Lower the bar under control to mid-chest, keeping elbows about 45 degrees from your torso.
4. Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
5. Repeat, then rack the bar.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades pinched and flat against the bench for a stable base.
2. Drive your feet into the floor to stay tight.
3. Lower the bar with control and touch the chest without bouncing.
4. Keep wrists stacked over your elbows.

instructions:
1. Set a box behind you so that sitting on it puts your thighs roughly parallel to the floor.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell across your upper back, gripping slightly wider than shoulders.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering under control until you sit lightly on the box.
4. Keep tension, then drive through your heels and extend hips and knees to stand back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Sit back onto the box, do not drop or bounce off it.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
3. Brace your core and keep your chest up throughout.
4. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you descend.

instructions:
1. Stand about 60 cm in front of a bench with a barbell across your upper back.
2. Place the top of one foot behind you on the bench, keeping your front foot flat.
3. Keep your chest up and lower by bending the front knee until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
4. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front foot to load the quads and glutes.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting and stay upright.
4. Lower under control through a full range of motion.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell secured across your upper back.
2. Bend your knees slightly to preload tension, keeping your heels grounded.
3. Drive explosively through the balls of your feet to raise your heels and extend your ankles fully.
4. Lower your heels back to the floor under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push through the forefoot to maximize calf activation.
2. Control the descent rather than bouncing the heels down.
3. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
4. Keep knees soft and slightly bent throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a barbell over your midfoot.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip just outside your knees.
3. Set your chest up, flatten your back, and brace your core.
4. Push through your heels and extend the hips and knees together to stand tall.
5. Lower the bar back to the floor under control, keeping the back flat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your shins and thighs through the whole pull.
2. Drive through your heels and lead with your chest, not your hips.
3. Keep a neutral spine and braced core to protect your lower back.
4. Move smoothly off the floor, then extend explosively at the top.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell across the front of your shoulders with a clean grip, fingers under the bar and elbows pointing forward.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
3. Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
4. Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs reach parallel or just below.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up, keeping your elbows high.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows high so the bar stays seated on your shoulders.
2. Keep your torso upright to hold the bar over your midfoot.
3. Track your knees in line with your toes.
4. Inhale and brace before each descent, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a barbell over your midfoot.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip.
3. Set your chest up, flatten your back, and brace your core.
4. Drive through your heels to lift the bar past your knees.
5. Explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug your shoulders to pull the bar up your body.
6. Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power from your legs and hips, not your arms.
2. Keep the bar close to your body through the whole pull.
3. Finish with a full hip extension and strong shrug.
4. Keep a neutral spine and braced core throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, a barbell over your midfoot.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar just outside your legs.
3. Set your chest up, flatten your back, and brace your core.
4. Push through your heels and drive your hips forward to lift the bar to a standing position.
5. Lower the bar back to the floor under control, keeping the back flat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body the entire lift.
2. Drive your hips through to lock out, squeezing your glutes.
3. Keep a neutral spine and braced core to protect your lower back.
4. Keep your shoulders pulled back and lats tight to hold the bar in.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, a barbell over your midfoot.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder-width.
3. Set your chest up, flatten your back, and brace your core.
4. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to lift the bar.
5. As you stand, pull the bar up toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
6. Lower the bar back to the floor under control and repeat.
tips:
1. Use leg and hip drive to start the bar, then pull with the upper back.
2. Keep the bar close to your body throughout.
3. Lead the high pull with your elbows, keeping them above the bar.
4. Track your knees over your toes to protect your knees.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with a box about 30 cm high near your feet.
2. Place one foot on the box and cross the opposite ankle over that knee in a figure-four shape.
3. Rest a barbell across your hips and hold it securely with both hands.
4. Drive through the heel on the box to lift your hips until your torso forms a straight line to the working knee.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips under control.
6. Finish the set, switch sides, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Pad the bar so it sits comfortably across your hips.
2. Drive through the heel of the planted foot to bias the glute.
3. Keep your core braced to stop your pelvis from twisting.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both feet flat on a box about 30 cm high, knees bent.
2. Rest a barbell across your hips and grip it securely with both hands.
3. Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso forms a straight line to your knees.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your feet, not collapsing inward.
3. Drive through the heels to keep tension on the glutes.
4. Pad the bar across your hips for comfort.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with a box about 30 cm high near your feet.
2. Place one foot on the box and extend the other leg up toward the ceiling.
3. Rest a barbell across your hips and hold it securely with both hands.
4. Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until your torso forms a straight line to the working knee.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips under control.
6. Finish the set, switch sides, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the working foot to emphasize the glute.
2. Keep your hips level; resist letting the free side drop.
3. Brace your core to stop your torso from twisting.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with both feet on a box about 30 cm high.
2. Stagger your stance with one foot slightly forward and the other slightly back.
3. Rest a barbell across your hips and grip it securely with both hands.
4. Drive mainly through the forward heel to lift your hips until your torso forms a straight line to your knees.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips under control.
6. Finish the set, switch the lead leg, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Shift most of your weight onto the working leg; use the other as a kickstand.
2. Keep your head, neck, and shoulders relaxed throughout.
3. Brace your core to keep your pelvis stable.
4. Pad the bar across your hips for comfort.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Grip a barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width and hold it above your chest.
3. Lower the bar until your upper arms rest on the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
4. Press the bar up until your arms are straight over your chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pause briefly when your elbows touch the floor to remove momentum.
2. Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees to spare the shoulders.
3. Drive with your chest and triceps to lock out the press.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Rack a barbell across the front of your shoulders, elbows high and pointing forward.
2. Grip the bar just outside shoulder-width and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your torso upright, until your thighs reach parallel or slightly below.
4. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows high to stop the bar rolling off your shoulders.
2. Brace your core hard to hold an upright torso under load.
3. Drive your knees out in line with your toes.
4. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands just outside shoulder-width.
2. Drive through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the bar past your knees.
3. Explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug your shoulders to pull the bar upward.
4. Drop under the bar, rotating your elbows forward to catch it across your front shoulders in a squat.
5. Drive through your heels to stand, then lower the bar to the floor with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.
2. Drive power from your legs and hips, not your arms.
3. Catch with elbows high to lock the bar on your shoulders.
4. Brace your core to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Rack a barbell across your upper back and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs drop just below parallel.
4. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and spine neutral throughout.
2. Drive your knees out in line with your toes.
3. Brace your core before each descent.
4. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Rack a barbell across your upper back and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs drop just below parallel.
4. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and spine neutral throughout.
2. Drive your knees out in line with your toes.
3. Brace your core before each descent.
4. Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell in a rack at about waist height and hook your arms under it, holding the bar in the crooks of your elbows against your chest.
2. Stand up to lift the bar off the rack, then step back with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Keep a neutral spine as you push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs reach parallel or slightly below.
4. Drive through your heels to extend your hips and knees back to standing.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced to resist forward collapse.
2. Hold the bar tight in your elbow crooks throughout.
3. Drive your knees out in line with your toes.
4. Move under control and distribute weight evenly across your feet.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell at thigh level with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees slightly to lower the bar to just above the knees, keeping the back flat.
3. Explosively extend the hips, knees and ankles, shrugging the shoulders to accelerate the bar upward.
4. Pull the body under the bar and catch it on the front of the shoulders in a quarter-squat, elbows high.
5. Stand fully upright, then lower the bar back to thigh level under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the bar with the hips and legs, not the arms.
2. Keep the bar close to the body throughout the pull.
3. Catch with the elbows pointing forward to rack the bar securely.
4. Brace the core before each explosive pull.

instructions:
1. Straddle a barbell on the floor so it runs between the legs, feet roughly shoulder-width apart.
2. Grip the bar with one hand in front of the body and one hand behind, using a mixed grip.
3. Brace the core, push the hips back and bend the knees to lower into a squat with a tall torso.
4. Drive through the heels to extend the hips and knees and stand fully upright.
5. Lower the bar back to the floor under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep weight balanced evenly between both legs.
2. Drive through the heels using the glutes and hamstrings.
3. Keep the torso upright and the back flat throughout.
4. Alternate hand and stance positions between sets for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell at thigh level with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Dip slightly by bending the hips and knees, keeping the back flat.
3. Explosively extend the hips, knees and ankles to drive the bar upward.
4. At full extension, shrug the shoulders forcefully toward the ears as the body rises onto the toes.
5. Land softly and reset the bar at thigh level under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Time the shrug with full hip and knee extension.
2. Keep the arms straight and let the legs drive the bar.
3. Keep the bar close to the thighs throughout.
4. Brace the core to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across the upper back with a grip slightly wider than the shoulders.
2. Push the hips back and bend the knees to lower until the thighs are about parallel to the floor.
3. Explosively drive through the heels to jump straight up, fully extending the hips and knees.
4. Land softly on the forefeet, bending the knees and hips to absorb the impact.
5. Lower back into the squat position. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the barbell steady and centered on the upper back.
2. Keep the knees tracking over the toes on takeoff and landing.
3. Land softly to absorb impact through the legs.
4. Use a lighter load to keep the movement explosive.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with the upper back resting against a bench, knees bent and feet flat.
2. Position a barbell across the hips and hold it securely with both hands.
3. Push through the heels to lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Squeeze the glutes at the top and hold briefly with the hips fully extended.
5. Lower the hips under control, stopping just before they touch the floor. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heels to load the glutes.
2. Keep the range short and controlled, emphasizing the squeeze at the top.
3. Keep the knees tracking in line with the toes.
4. Use a pad on the bar for hip comfort.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand facing the bar, feet shoulder-width apart, and hold the loaded end with both hands at upper chest height.
3. Brace your core and press the bar forward and slightly upward until your arms are extended.
4. Lower the bar back to your chest under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists firm and the bar pointed up at the same angle each rep.
2. Brace your abs to stop your torso leaning back.
3. Press in a smooth arc, not straight up.
4. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand side-on to the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands at one hip.
3. Keep your legs and hips still and bend your torso laterally away from the bar.
4. Contract your obliques to pull the bar back upright.
5. Finish all reps on one side, switch sides, and repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the waist, not the hips or knees.
2. Lower under control rather than dropping the bar.
3. Keep your shoulders square and facing forward.
4. Brace your core throughout to protect your spine.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on a bench and hold a barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Extend your legs straight out so your feet are off the floor.
3. Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid-chest under control.
4. Press the bar back up until your arms are extended without using leg drive.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your glutes and core tight to stay stable without leg drive.
2. Lower the bar to the same point on your chest each rep.
3. Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
4. Use lighter weight than a standard bench press at first.

instructions:
1. Set a barbell low across your rear deltoids and upper traps, gripping slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Unrack the bar and step back with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, leaning your torso forward as you descend.
4. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending hips and knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar over your mid-foot throughout the lift.
2. Lead the descent with your hips to load the posterior chain.
3. Keep your chest up and back braced to protect your spine.
4. Drive your knees out in line with your toes.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip a barbell on the floor with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Brace your core, lift your chest, and pull the bar from the floor by extending your knees and hips.
3. Explosively extend your hips and shrug your shoulders to drive the bar upward, keeping it close to your body.
4. Pull your elbows under and rotate them forward to catch the bar in a front rack without re-bending the legs.
5. Lower the bar to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.
2. Drive the lift with explosive hip extension, not your arms.
3. Shrug hard before turning your elbows over the bar.
4. Keep your back flat and core braced off the floor.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell overhead with arms fully extended and a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Brace your core and keep the bar stacked over your midfoot.
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Keep the bar locked overhead throughout the descent.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up, fully extending hips and knees.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar directly over the middle of your foot to stay balanced.
2. Actively push the bar up into the shoulders to maintain a stable lockout.
3. Keep your chest tall and torso upright to hold the bar overhead.
4. Use a controlled descent to keep the bar path steady.

instructions:
1. Hold a barbell at the front of your shoulders with feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your knees into a quick, shallow dip.
3. Drive your body downward and press your arms straight to punch yourself under the bar.
4. Catch the bar overhead with locked arms in a partial squat as your feet reset.
5. Stand fully upright with the bar overhead.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Punch under the bar fast so your arms lock as your feet land.
2. Keep the bar stacked over the middle of your foot at the catch.
3. Brace your core hard to support the load overhead.
4. Keep your torso upright during the dip and catch.

instructions:
1. Stand with a barbell on the floor behind your heels, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder-width.
3. Keep your back flat, chest up, and shoulders down.
4. Brace your core and drive through your heels to stand tall, pulling the bar up behind your hips.
5. Lower the bar back to the floor with control along the same path.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the lift.
2. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top.
3. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
4. Keep your chest up to maintain a flat back.

instructions:
1. Stand beside a sturdy box or bench with a barbell across your upper back and shoulders.
2. Place the foot closest to the box flat on top of it.
3. Press firmly through that heel and drive your body up until the leg is fully extended.
4. Stand tall on top of the box with an upright torso.
5. Lower the trailing foot back to the floor with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the working leg to load the glutes.
2. Move slowly and avoid pushing off the bottom foot for momentum.
3. Choose a box height that lets you keep full control.
4. Keep your torso upright and shoulder blades pulled back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell overhand just outside shoulder-width.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is near 45 degrees, keeping your back flat.
3. Let the bar hang with your arms fully extended below your shoulders.
4. Shrug your shoulders up and back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a flat back and braced core throughout to protect your spine.
2. Pull your shoulder blades back and up rather than just elevating.
3. Pause and squeeze at the top of each rep.
4. Exhale as you shrug and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell across your upper chest or pressed overhead with arms straight.
3. Brace your core and curl your torso up toward your knees.
4. Pause briefly at the top, keeping the barbell stable.
5. Lower under control until your shoulders touch the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the barbell path vertical and the weight controlled.
2. Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower.
3. Move with your abs, not by jerking the bar.
4. Anchor your feet or have a partner hold them for heavier loads.

instructions:
1. Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms extended.
3. Lower the bar under control to about 5 cm above your chest.
4. Pause for 1 to 2 seconds without touching your chest, keeping full tension.
5. Press the bar back up to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hold the pause without resting the bar on your chest.
