2. Keep shoulder blades retracted and feet planted.
3. Maintain tightness through the torso during the pause.
4. Use a controlled descent to build pressing strength.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
2. Stagger your stance, placing one foot slightly behind so the toes align with the front heel.
3. Keeping your back flat and chest up, hinge at the hips and lower the bar along your front leg.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in the front hamstring, around mid-shin.
5. Drive through the front heel and extend your hips to stand back up.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep the barbell close to your legs throughout.
2. Hinge from the hips, not by bending the knees.
3. Load the front leg while the rear foot only assists balance.
4. Maintain a neutral spine to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a box with a barbell resting across your upper back and feet hip-width apart.
2. Place one foot fully on the box.
3. Drive through the front heel to lift your body up onto the box.
4. Bring the opposite knee up until the thigh is parallel to the floor and balance briefly.
5. Lower the raised leg back down with control and step off.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep your eyes forward to help maintain balance.
2. Step up with control, not momentum.
3. Push through the heel of the leading foot.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and feet slightly apart.
2. Hold the barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip just wider than shoulder-width.
3. Brace your core and sit tall with your chest up.
4. Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
5. Lower the bar under control back to shoulder height.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core hard to stay upright without leaning back.
2. Keep the bar path vertical over the mid-line.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Sit tall with legs straight to remove leg drive.

instructions:
1. Anchor the rope and grip one end in each hand. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees softly bent, hips back.
2. Brace your core and hold your arms at your sides with a slight bend.
3. Drive one arm up to shoulder height while the other drives down, creating a wave.
4. Quickly alternate arms, keeping a fast steady rhythm without pausing.
5. Maintain a stable braced stance for the full work interval.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate the wave from the shoulders, not just the wrists.
2. Keep your core tight to limit excess torso sway.
3. Stay light on your feet with knees bent to absorb force.
4. Breathe steadily and keep the pace consistent.

instructions:
1. Anchor the rope and grip one end in each hand. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent.
2. Raise both arms overhead while standing tall and extending the hips.
3. Slam both rope ends down hard toward the floor as you hinge slightly at the hips.
4. Let the rope rebound and immediately lift both arms back overhead.
5. Keep a fast, powerful rhythm for the full work interval.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the slam with your whole body, not just the arms.
2. Brace your core hard on each downward slam.
3. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to load power.
4. Grip firmly to keep the rope ends under control.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Tuck your toes and lift your knees about 5 cm off the floor, keeping your back flat.
3. Brace your core and step the right hand and left foot forward together.
4. Step the left hand and right foot forward, keeping the hips low and stable.
5. Continue crawling forward in this contralateral pattern for the work interval.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and avoid swaying side to side.
2. Maintain a flat back with your head in line with your spine.
3. Keep your knees hovering just off the floor throughout.
4. Move at a controlled pace to stay coordinated.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms at your sides. Place one foot on a raised surface about 30 cm high.
2. Cross the opposite ankle over the working knee to form a figure-four.
3. Brace your core and press through the working heel to lift your hips.
4. Raise until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to working knee.
5. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower under control. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the working leg, not the toes.
2. Squeeze the glute hard at the top of each rep.
3. Keep your core braced to avoid arching the lower back.
4. Keep shoulders relaxed and flat on the floor.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with arms at your sides. Place both feet on a raised surface about 30 cm high.
2. Keep one foot flat and slide the other forward so only the heel rests on the edge.
3. Brace your core and press through the flat working heel to lift your hips.
4. Raise until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower under control. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the working leg to bias that glute.
2. Squeeze the glute hard at the top of each rep.
3. Keep your hips level and core braced throughout.
4. Keep shoulders relaxed and flat on the floor.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent and feet flat about shoulder-width apart.
2. Cross your arms over your chest and brace your core.
3. Press through your heels to drive your hips up until your torso and thighs form a straight line.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked and ribs down.
5. Lower your hips under control back toward the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels, not your toes, to target the glutes.
2. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
3. Hold the top for 1-2 seconds to maximize glute contraction.
4. Keep your shins close to vertical at the top to avoid shifting load to the quads.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a mat with your arms alongside your body.
2. Bend your knees and bring your heels toward your buttocks, then reach back and grip your ankles.
3. Inhale and lift your chest and thighs off the floor by pulling your ankles up and back.
4. Open your chest, draw your shoulders back, and gaze forward, balancing on your abdomen.
5. Hold the position while breathing steadily, then release on an exhale.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Kick your feet back into your hands to lift higher rather than just pulling with your arms.
2. Keep your knees roughly hip-width to protect the lower back.
3. Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath during the hold.
4. Engage your glutes lightly to support the backbend.

instructions:
1. Set a cable pulley to the low position and attach a straight bar.
2. Stand back about 60 cm and lean slightly back so the cable pulls at roughly a 30 degree angle.
3. Grip the bar with both hands and let your shoulders relax down.
4. Shrug your shoulders up and slightly back, squeezing your traps.
5. Pause at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the shoulders; keep your arms straight throughout.
2. The angled pull biases the upper traps, so squeeze hard at the top.
3. Avoid rolling the shoulders; lift straight up and back.
4. Exhale as you shrug up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a low cable pulley with a straight bar, feet hip-width apart.
2. Hold the bar in front of your hips and keep your knees nearly straight.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
4. Pause and squeeze at the top of the movement.
5. Lower your heels slowly back to the start, feeling a stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the ankles to isolate the calves.
2. Keep the knees nearly straight to emphasize the gastrocnemius.
3. Hold the top contraction for a second.
4. Use a full range of motion, allowing the heels to drop low.

instructions:
1. Set a cable pulley to chest height and attach a single handle.
2. Stand side-on to the machine and grip the handle with both hands at your chest.
3. Step away to create tension and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
4. Brace your core and press the handle straight out in front of your chest, resisting the pull to rotate.
5. Hold for a moment, then bring the handle back to your chest under control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and shoulders square; do not let your torso twist toward the cable.
2. Brace your abs hard throughout the press.
3. Press slowly and with control rather than fast.
4. Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath.

instructions:
1. Set two cable pulleys to the high position and grab the opposite handle in each hand so the cables cross in front of you.
2. Stand tall in the centre with elbows tucked at your sides and forearms angled up.
3. Keep your upper arms still and extend both elbows, pushing the handles down and out until your arms are straight.
4. Squeeze the triceps briefly at the bottom.
5. Control the handles back up to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides so only the elbows move.
2. Drive the squeeze at the bottom of each rep.
3. Use a light weight and let the crossed cables track smoothly.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced.

instructions:
1. Set a cable pulley low and hold the attachment at chest level with both hands, elbows pointing down.
2. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and core braced.
3. Bend your hips and knees to descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels to stand back up, keeping the attachment at your chest.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked down to hold the attachment steady.
2. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
3. Track your knees in line with your toes.
4. Keep your chest up and back flat throughout.

instructions:
1. Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and secure it around your working ankle.
2. Stand facing the machine and hold the frame for balance, with a slight bend in your standing leg.
3. Keep your upper body still and curl your working foot up toward your glutes by bending the knee.
4. Squeeze the hamstring briefly at the top.
5. Lower your foot back down under control, then switch legs after the set.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the hamstring hard at the top of each curl.
2. Keep the rest of your body still and avoid swinging.
3. Hold the frame and keep a soft bend in the standing leg for balance.
4. Use a weight you can control through the full range.

instructions:
1. Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and secure it around one ankle.
2. Stand facing the machine, hold the frame, and lean your torso slightly forward.
3. Shift your weight onto the supporting leg with a soft knee bend.
4. Extend the strapped leg straight back, squeezing the glute at the top without arching your lower back.
5. Return the leg under control without resting the stack, then switch sides after the set.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and controlled to keep tension on the glute.
2. Do not swing the leg or use momentum.
3. Squeeze the glute hard at the top of each rep.
4. Keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and kneel facing the machine.
2. Grip the bar overhand slightly wider than shoulders and lean forward at the hips with arms extended overhead and a slight elbow bend.
3. Brace your core and keep your elbows nearly straight.
4. Drive the bar down in an arc toward your thighs using your lats.
5. Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then return the bar overhead under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Initiate the pull with your shoulders, not your elbows.
2. Keep a fixed slight elbow bend throughout the movement.
3. Squeeze the lats at the bottom of each rep.
4. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.

instructions:
1. Kneel facing a cable machine with a wide bar or rope attached to a high pulley.
2. Grip the attachment with both hands and extend your arms overhead, keeping your torso upright and braced.
3. Pull the attachment down and in toward your hips, driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement.
5. Return the attachment slowly to the overhead position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead the pull with your elbows, not your hands, to target the lats.
2. Keep your core tight to prevent your lower back from arching.
3. Move slowly on the return to keep tension on the muscles.
4. Exhale as you pull down and inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine, the cable between your legs.
2. Grip the rope between your thighs, step forward, and set your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Hinge at the hips, pushing your hips back and lowering your torso while keeping your back flat and knees softly bent.
4. Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top.
5. Hinge back to the start position under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your hips, not your arms or lower back.
2. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout the hinge.
3. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top without overarching.
4. Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you hinge back.

instructions:
1. Attach two handles to low pulleys on a cable machine, one on each side.
2. Stand between the pulleys and grip a handle in each hand, arms crossed in front of your body.
3. Hinge slightly forward at the hips with a flat back.
4. Retract and elevate your shoulder blades, pulling the handles back and up.
5. Squeeze your traps at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Focus on pulling your shoulder blades back and together, not just up.
2. Keep your arms relatively straight and let your traps do the work.
3. Avoid jerking the weight; move with control.
4. Exhale as you shrug and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach a handle or bar to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
2. Shift your weight onto one leg, keeping a soft bend in the standing knee.
3. Hinge at the hips, lowering your torso while extending the free leg behind you for balance.
4. Lower until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat.
5. Drive through the standing leg to return to an upright position, squeezing the glute.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square to the floor and avoid rotating your torso.
2. Maintain a neutral spine throughout the hinge.
3. Brace your core to stabilize your balance on one leg.
4. Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a low pulley cable machine and grip the bar with both hands.
2. Step back into a split stance, one foot forward and one foot behind, torso upright.
3. Hold the bar in front of you with the cable taut.
4. Bend both knees to lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
5. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle.
2. Maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
3. Lower slowly under control to protect the knee.
4. Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel or stand facing away, holding the rope beside your head.
2. Keep your hips fixed and brace your core.
3. Crunch down by flexing your spine, pulling your elbows toward your thighs.
4. Squeeze your abs at the bottom of the movement.
5. Slowly return to the upright start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the spine, keeping your hips still.
2. Pull with your abs, not your arms.
3. Exhale as you crunch down, inhale as you rise.
4. Use a controlled tempo to keep tension on the abs.

instructions:
1. Attach a single handle to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
2. Hold the handle with a neutral grip and keep your elbow tucked at your side.
3. Curl the handle up while rotating your wrist to a palms-up position.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower under control while rotating back to neutral.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm still and elbow pinned to your side.
2. Twist the wrist fully to maximize biceps engagement.
3. Control the lowering phase for constant tension.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low pulley.
2. Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with palms facing down.
3. Let your wrists hang over your knees holding the bar.
4. Extend your wrists upward, lifting the backs of your hands toward you.
5. Lower the bar slowly to a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the wrists, keeping your forearms fixed.
2. Use a full range of motion for complete extensor engagement.
3. Control the lowering phase rather than letting the weight drop.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg press machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the footplate, shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your legs, keeping a slight bend in your knees.
3. Push through your forefeet to press the footplate away, squeezing your calves at full extension.
4. Slowly lower your heels to a deep stretch.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your knees to protect the joints.
2. Use a full range of motion for deep calf activation.
3. Pause briefly at the top to maximize the contraction.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads and feet hip-width apart on the platform.
2. Place the balls of your feet on the edge with heels hanging off, toes forward.
3. Extend your legs to release the safety handles, keeping a slight knee bend.
4. Push through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible, squeezing your calves.
5. Slowly lower your heels to a deep stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout to protect the joints.
2. Use a full range of motion, lowering the heels for a deep stretch.
3. Pause at the top to maximize the contraction.
4. Exhale as you raise your heels, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Exhale and round your spine toward the ceiling, tucking your chin to your chest.
3. Draw your navel up toward your spine and engage your abdominals.
4. Hold the rounded position, breathing steadily.
5. Return to a neutral flat back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move with your breath, exhaling as you round the spine.
2. Press the floor away through your hands to spread the upper back.
3. Keep weight even across both hands and knees.
4. Round from the whole spine, not just the upper back.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair.
3. Raise both arms overhead alongside your ears.
4. Keep your chest lifted and weight in your heels.
5. Hold the position, breathing steadily.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
2. Sit your hips back to load the quads and glutes.
3. Engage your core to support an upright torso.
4. Keep weight in your heels, not your toes.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back flat against the pad and feet on the floor.
2. Grasp the handles at chest height with palms facing forward.
3. Press the handles forward until your arms are extended.
4. Pause briefly at full extension.
5. Bend your elbows to return the handles to chest level under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the pad.
2. Drive through your chest rather than shrugging the shoulders.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
4. Control the return rather than letting the weight pull your arms back.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor and sit your hips back toward your heels.
2. Fold your torso forward and rest it toward the floor.
3. Walk both hands out to one side until you feel a stretch along the opposite side.
4. Hold, breathing steadily, then walk the hands to the other side.
5. Hold the second side for equal time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips sitting back toward your heels.
2. Reach through your fingertips to lengthen the side body.
3. Relax your neck and let your head rest down.
4. Breathe into the stretched side ribs.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees apart.
2. Sit your hips back toward your heels.
3. Fold your torso forward and rest it between your thighs.
4. Lay your arms alongside your body with palms facing up.
5. Rest your forehead on the floor and hold, breathing steadily.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Let your hips sink toward your heels to deepen the stretch.
2. Relax your shoulders away from your ears.
3. Breathe slowly into your lower back.
4. Widen the knees if you need more room for your torso.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor with your knees about hip-width apart and big toes touching.
2. Place a block in front of you and rest your elbows on it.
3. Sit your hips back toward your heels and lower your chest between your thighs.
4. Reach your forearms forward over the block and relax your head down.
5. Breathe slowly and hold the stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips reaching back toward your heels to lengthen the lower back.
2. Widen your knees if your belly feels compressed.
3. Relax your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with your legs stacked and knees bent about 90 degrees, hips and shoulders aligned.
2. Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on your hip.
3. Keep your feet together and brace your core.
4. Raise your top knee as far as possible without rotating your hips or lifting your feet apart.
5. Pause, then lower your knee with control. Switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips stacked and do not roll your torso backward as you lift.
2. Drive the movement from the glute, not momentum.
3. Brace your core to keep the pelvis stable.
4. Move slowly to maintain constant tension.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands close together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
2. Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels.
3. Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping elbows close to your body.
4. Pause when your chest nearly touches your hands.
5. Press back up to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides to maximize triceps work.
2. Maintain a rigid plank; do not let your hips sag.
3. Inhale on the way down, exhale forcefully as you press up.
4. Keep your head neutral and in line with your spine.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your feet elevated on a box, knees bent about 90 degrees.
2. Place a dumbbell across your hips and hold it with both hands.
3. Brace your core and press through your heels to lift your hips.
4. Extend until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to maximize glute activation.
2. Keep the dumbbell stable on your hips; use a pad for comfort.
3. Avoid arching your lower back at the top; finish with a glute squeeze.
4. Keep your feet firmly planted on the box throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your feet on a box, one knee bent about 90 degrees and the other leg extended upward.
2. Place a dumbbell across your hips and hold it with both hands.
3. Brace your core and press through the planted heel to lift your hips.
4. Extend until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower with control. Switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the planted heel to maximize glute activation.
2. Keep your hips level; do not let the working side drop or twist.
3. Brace your core to resist rotation throughout the lift.
4. Keep the dumbbell stable on your hips; use a pad for comfort.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and place both feet on a surface about 30 cm high, one foot flat and the other staggered so only the heel rests on top.
2. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
3. Press through the lead heel and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
4. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and pause briefly.
5. Lower your hips under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of the working leg, not the toes.
2. Keep the staggered foot light to bias load onto the lead glute.
3. Pad the dumbbell with a towel for comfort.
4. Keep your core braced to prevent the lower back from arching.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Cross your right ankle over your left knee in a figure-four position.
3. Hold a dumbbell across your hips with both hands.
4. Press through the heel of the supporting foot and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
5. Lower your hips under control to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep the figure-four leg relaxed throughout.
2. Press through the heel to bias the glute.
3. Squeeze the working glute at the top.
4. Brace your core to keep the pelvis level and stop rotation.

instructions:
1. Sit with your upper back against a bench and place a dumbbell across your hips.
2. Bend your knees with feet flat, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee in a figure-four position.
3. Press through the grounded heel and drive your hips up until your torso is parallel to the floor.
4. Squeeze your glutes and hold briefly at the top.
5. Lower your hips under control until they nearly touch the floor.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Set the bench edge at mid-back height for support.
2. Hold the dumbbell firmly and pad it with a towel.
3. Keep your chin tucked and ribs down to avoid arching.
4. Drive through the heel for maximum glute engagement.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, holding a dumbbell in each hand between your legs.
2. Lower into a deep squat with your chest up.
3. Drive through your heels and explosively jump straight up, extending hips, knees, and ankles.
4. Land softly back into the squat with knees tracking over your toes.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate explosive power from the legs and hips.
2. Land with soft, bent knees to absorb impact.
3. Keep your core braced and chest up throughout.
4. Use a light dumbbell to maintain jump quality.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands, elbows down.
2. Step forward with one leg and bend both knees to descend.
3. Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee is just above it.
4. Push through your front heel to return to standing.
5. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your foot.
2. Hold the dumbbell tight to your chest to stay upright.
3. Brace your core for balance and anti-rotation control.
4. Take a long enough step to load the glute, not just the knee.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back holding a dumbbell with both hands, arms extended overhead and legs straight.
2. Brace your core and draw your navel toward your spine.
3. Exhale and curl your torso up while bending your knees toward your chest.
4. Bring the dumbbell toward your shins so your body folds like a suitcase.
5. Lower under control until your shoulders and feet nearly touch the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move with control rather than swinging the legs up.
2. Keep the dumbbell tracking over your knees, not flaring out.
3. Exhale forcefully at the top to fully contract the abs.
4. Keep your lower back lightly anchored to protect the spine.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, holding one dumbbell with both hands.
2. Hinge at the hips, pushing them back and letting the dumbbell swing between your legs.
3. Keep your back flat, shins near vertical and core braced.
4. Snap your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to drive the dumbbell up to chest height.
5. Let the dumbbell fall back and hinge again as it passes between your legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your hips, not your arms.
2. Hinge at the hips instead of squatting down.
3. Keep your back flat throughout to protect the spine.
4. Brace your core hard on every repetition.

instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with your spine straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height and cross one over the other.
3. Bend your elbows and bring the backs of your hands or palms together.
4. Lift your elbows and press your forearms forward to spread the shoulder blades.
5. Tuck your chin toward your chest and hold, breathing steadily.
6. Release, switch the arm cross, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows lifted to shoulder height for a deeper stretch.
2. Ease off if you feel pain in the upper back or arms.
3. Keep breathing steadily rather than holding your breath.
4. Round the upper back slightly to widen the stretch between the shoulder blades.

instructions:
1. Sit cross-legged with your spine tall and both sit bones grounded.
2. Inhale and lengthen through the crown of your head.
3. Exhale and rotate your torso to one side, placing one hand behind you and the other on the opposite knee.
4. Turn from the mid-back, letting the gaze follow last.
5. Hold and breathe, then return to center.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Initiate the twist from the thoracic spine, not the neck.
2. Keep both sit bones grounded to stay stable.
3. Lengthen the spine on each inhale before deepening the twist.
4. Twist only as far as feels comfortable without forcing.

instructions:
1. Place your feet on a raised surface and your hands on the floor in a pike position.
2. Keep your hips high and arms straight so your torso is near vertical.
3. Let your shoulders sink toward your ears by relaxing the shoulder girdle.
4. Push the floor away and shrug your shoulders up toward your hips.
5. Lower under control back to the sunken position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
2. Drive the motion through the shoulder blades, not the elbows.
3. Keep your hips high to load the shoulders effectively.
4. Move slowly to control the scapular elevation.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet about 120 cm apart, turn the front foot out 90 degrees.
2. Bend the front knee to a right angle over the ankle, keeping the back leg straight.
3. Lower the front forearm onto the front thigh or the hand to the floor outside the front foot.
4. Extend the top arm over the ear to form a line from heel to fingertips.
5. Hold and breathe, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee tracking over the second toe, not collapsing inward.
2. Press the back foot firmly into the floor to support the pose.
3. Roll the top shoulder back to open the chest.
4. Lengthen both sides of the waist evenly.

instructions:
1. Place a block beside the outside of the front foot.
2. Stand with feet about 120 cm apart, turn the front foot out 90 degrees.
3. Bend the front knee to a right angle over the ankle, keeping the back leg straight.
4. Rest the front hand on the block and extend the top arm over the ear.
5. Hold and breathe, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the block to keep the spine long instead of collapsing toward the floor.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the second toe.
3. Press the back foot down to engage the back leg.
4. Open the chest toward the ceiling.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands by your sides.
2. Press the lower back into the floor.
3. Bend the knees and draw them toward the chest.
4. Slowly lower the legs back toward the floor without touching.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the lower back flat to bias the abs over the hip flexors.
2. Move slowly and control the lowering phase.
3. Exhale as you lift the knees.
4. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Place the hands behind the hips, fingers pointing forward.
3. Lift the hips off the floor by straightening the arms.
4. Bend the elbows to lower the hips toward the floor.
5. Push back up by extending the elbows.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbows pointing straight back, not flaring out.
2. Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears.
3. Lower until the elbows reach about a right angle.
4. Keep the hips close to the hands.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Squat down until the hands reach toward the floor.
3. Explosively jump up and forward, extending the hips.
4. Land softly back into the squat position.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact.
2. Drive through the heels to jump explosively.
3. Keep the chest up during the squat.
4. Keep the knees tracking over the toes.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock the body into a rigid line.
3. Pull straight down on the bar with stiff arms to raise your body until it is horizontal and parallel to the floor.
4. Pause briefly with the body level, facing up.
5. Lower under control back to the hanging position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight throughout; the power comes from the lats, not the elbows.
2. Brace the abs hard to stop the hips from sagging.
3. Depress and retract the shoulder blades before each rep.
4. Use a tuck or one-leg version if the full straight-body raise is too hard.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep the body rigid.
3. Pull straight down on the bar with stiff arms to raise your body until it is horizontal.
4. Hold the horizontal front lever position, keeping the body level and facing up.
5. Lower under control back to the hang.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms locked straight; drive the movement from the lats.
2. Brace the abs and glutes to hold a flat bodyline during the hold.
3. Pull the shoulder blades down and back to support the position.
4. Regress to a tuck hold if you cannot keep the body horizontal.

instructions:
1. Kneel with hips over knees and extend one leg straight out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
2. Inhale and lengthen the spine, drawing the belly in.
3. Reach the same-side arm overhead and bend your torso toward the extended leg.
4. Rotate the chest open and turn your gaze upward, keeping the spine long.
5. Hold and breathe into the side body.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Press firmly through the kneeling shin for a stable base.
2. Lengthen the spine before bending to protect the lower back.
3. Keep the extended leg active with the kneecap facing up.
4. Lower the gaze if turning up causes any dizziness.

instructions:
1. Kneel with hips over knees and extend one leg straight out to the side, foot flat on the floor.
2. Inhale and lengthen the spine, drawing the belly in.
3. Reach the same-side arm overhead and extend it out over the straight leg.
4. Bend the torso sideways toward the extended leg, feeling a stretch along the top side body.
5. Hold and breathe into the ribs.
6. Repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Keep both hips facing forward as you side-bend.
2. Reach long through the top arm to open the side of the ribs.
3. Press the extended-leg foot into the floor to stay grounded.
4. Avoid collapsing forward; keep the chest open.

instructions:
1. Rest a barbell across your upper traps and stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Soften the knees slightly and brace your core.
3. Push your hips straight back, hinging your torso forward with a neutral spine.
4. Lower until your torso is near parallel to the floor or you feel a hamstring stretch.
5. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing the glutes at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move from the hips, not the lower back; keep the spine neutral.
2. Keep the shins nearly vertical and weight in the mid-foot.
3. Feel the stretch in the hamstrings on the way down.
4. Start light to groove the hinge pattern before adding load.

instructions:
1. Step onto the pedals and place your feet securely, then grip the moving handles.
2. Begin striding in a smooth elliptical motion, pushing and pulling the handles with your arms.
3. Build up to a fast pace while keeping movements controlled and your posture upright.
4. Drive through your legs and engage your glutes on each stride.
5. Maintain the fast pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and torso upright, do not lean on the handles.
2. Push through the whole foot to recruit the glutes and hamstrings.
3. Breathe in a steady rhythm with your stride.
4. Raise resistance or incline to increase glute activation.

instructions:
1. Step onto the pedals and place your feet securely, then grip the moving handles.
2. Begin striding in a smooth elliptical motion, pushing and pulling the handles with your arms.
3. Settle into a steady, moderate pace with controlled movements.
4. Drive through your legs and engage your glutes on each stride.
5. Maintain the steady pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and torso upright, do not lean on the handles.
2. Push through the whole foot to recruit the glutes and hamstrings.
3. Breathe in a steady rhythm with your stride.
4. Raise resistance or incline to increase glute activation.

instructions:
1. Step onto the pedals and place your feet securely, then grip the moving handles.
2. Begin striding in a smooth elliptical motion, pushing and pulling the handles with your arms.
3. Accelerate to an all-out sprint pace while keeping movements controlled.
4. Drive hard through your legs and engage your glutes on each stride.
5. Sustain the sprint pace for the set interval, then ease off.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced and torso upright, do not lean on the handles.
2. Push through the whole foot to recruit the glutes and hamstrings.
3. Match your breathing to the high effort with strong, rhythmic breaths.
4. Use short intervals to maintain sprint quality.

instructions:
1. Sit on the rower, strap in your feet, and grip the handle with an overhand grip, knees bent.
2. Drive through your legs to push your body back, keeping your arms straight.
3. As your legs near full extension, lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
4. Extend your arms first, then bend your knees to slide forward to the start.
5. Repeat the stroke at a fast pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and core braced, do not round your spine.
2. Power each stroke with your legs first, then back, then arms.
3. Exhale on the drive and inhale on the recovery.
4. Keep the recovery slower than the drive to control rhythm.

instructions:
1. Sit on the rower, strap in your feet, and grip the handle with an overhand grip, knees bent.
2. Drive through your legs to push your body back, keeping your arms straight.
3. As your legs near full extension, lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
4. Extend your arms first, then bend your knees to slide forward to the start.
5. Repeat the stroke at a steady pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back straight and core braced, do not round your spine.
2. Power each stroke with your legs first, then back, then arms.
3. Exhale on the drive and inhale on the recovery.
4. Keep the recovery slower than the drive to control rhythm.

instructions:
1. Sit on the rowing machine with feet strapped to the footrests, knees bent and shins vertical.
2. Grip the handle with an overhand grip and arms straight, leaning slightly forward from the hips.
3. Drive hard through the legs to extend the knees, then swing the torso back.
4. As the legs finish, pull the handle to the lower chest, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
5. Reverse the order: extend the arms, hinge the torso forward, then bend the knees to return.
6. Repeat at sprint pace for the set duration.
tips:
1. Keep the back flat and braced, never rounded.
2. Lead each stroke with the legs, not the arms.
3. Drive explosively and recover with control to keep stroke length.
4. Exhale on the drive, inhale on the recovery.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with the legs extended forward and the spine tall.
2. Bend one knee and place that foot on top of the opposite thigh, sole facing up.
3. Tuck the other foot under the opposite thigh in a comfortable cross-legged position.
4. Rest the hands on the knees and let both knees relax toward the floor.
5. Hold the position, breathing slowly and keeping the back upright.
6. Repeat with the legs reversed.
tips:
1. Keep the spine long and the chest open, never slumped.
2. Ease into the stretch and stop if the knees feel any pain.
3. Warm up the hips first if they feel tight.
4. Breathe deeply and stay relaxed throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Start kneeling, then step one foot forward into a low lunge with hands on the floor.
2. Shift the hips back over the rear knee and straighten the front leg.
3. Flex the front foot and point the toes toward the ceiling.
4. Hinge forward from the hips over the straight front leg, keeping the back flat.
5. Hold the stretch, breathing steadily.
6. Repeat on the other leg.
tips:
1. Hinge from the hips, not by rounding the spine.
2. Keep the front foot flexed to deepen the hamstring stretch.
3. Place hands on blocks if the floor is out of reach.
4. Ease in gradually and never bounce.

instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with the shoulders relaxed and down.
2. Drop the chin toward the chest.
3. Slowly roll the head in a half circle to bring one ear toward that shoulder.
4. Return through center to the chest, then roll to the opposite side.
5. Move slowly and only through the front lower arc, never backward.
6. Repeat for the set count.
tips:
1. Keep the motion slow and pain-free.
2. Do not roll the head backward to protect the cervical spine.
3. Let the shoulders stay relaxed throughout.
4. Breathe steadily and stop if you feel dizzy.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the leg curl machine with one ankle under the pad and grip the handles.
2. Start with the working leg fully extended and hips pressed to the bench.
3. Curl the working leg by bending the knee, pulling the ankle toward the glutes.
4. Squeeze the hamstring at the top of the movement.
5. Lower the leg slowly back to full extension with control.
6. Repeat for the set, then switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the hips pinned to the bench so they do not lift.
2. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
3. Focus tension on the hamstring throughout.
4. Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on the machine with your ankles under the leg pads and legs fully extended.
2. Hold the side handles to keep your torso stable.
3. Curl both legs by bending your knees, pulling your ankles toward your glutes.
4. Squeeze your hamstrings at the top of the movement.
5. Lower your legs back to full extension under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips pressed into the pad throughout the movement.
2. Curl through a full range without swinging.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the hamstrings.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your feet flat and the seat set so your upper arms rest on the pad.
2. Grasp both handles with palms facing up.
3. Curl both handles by bending your elbows, bringing your hands toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
5. Lower the handles back to full extension under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad throughout.
2. Hold a neutral wrist to keep load on the biceps.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Use a full range and avoid jerking the weight.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your feet flat and your upper arms resting on the pad.
2. Grasp one handle with the palm facing up.
3. Curl that handle by bending your elbow, bringing your hand toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower under control.
5. Finish your reps on one arm, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the working upper arm pressed into the pad.
2. Hold a neutral wrist to keep load on the biceps.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
4. Avoid leaning toward the working arm.

instructions:
1. Sit with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp one handle with palm facing down.
3. Press that handle forward by extending your arm, keeping the other arm still.
4. Squeeze your chest at full extension, then return under control.
5. Finish your reps on one arm, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and the working shoulder pressed into the pad.
2. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working arm.
3. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
4. Press in a smooth line without shrugging.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your chest pressed against the pad and feet flat.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing forward.
3. Pull one handle toward your torso, driving your elbow back and squeezing the shoulder blade.
4. Hold briefly, then return that handle under control.
5. Repeat on the other arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest against the pad and torso upright.
2. Lead with the elbow to engage the back, not the arms.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the end of each pull.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your feet flat and your chest firmly against the pad.
2. Grasp both handles with a neutral or overhand grip and extend your arms fully.
3. Pull the handles down and back, driving your elbows toward your hips and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Pause briefly at the contracted position.
5. Slowly return the handles to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest pressed to the pad and torso still throughout.
2. Lead with your elbows rather than your hands to target the back.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of each rep.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp both handles at chest height with an overhand grip.
3. Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly extended.
4. Squeeze your chest at the end of the movement.
5. Slowly return the handles to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the pad throughout.
2. Drive through your chest rather than your shoulders.
3. Control the return instead of letting the weight pull you back.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grasp one handle at chest height with an overhand grip.
3. Press that handle forward until your arm is nearly extended.
4. Squeeze your chest, then slowly return the handle under control.
5. Complete your reps, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and shoulders against the pad throughout.
2. Resist twisting your torso toward the working arm.
3. Drive through your chest rather than your shoulder.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Place your hands on the floor about shoulder-width apart, near a wall if needed.
2. Kick your legs up overhead until your body is inverted and vertical.
3. Stack your hips and feet over your shoulders and hands.
4. Brace your core and press the floor away to keep your shoulders active.
5. Hold the balanced position for the set time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push the floor away to keep your shoulders engaged and elevated.
2. Squeeze your core and glutes to stop your back from arching.
3. Spread your fingers and grip the floor to adjust balance.
4. Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
2. Open your knees slightly wider than your torso.
3. Reach up and grasp the outside of each foot.
4. Gently pull your feet down so your knees move toward the floor beside your ribs.
5. Keep your lower back relaxed on the floor and hold for the set time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
2. Let the stretch deepen gently rather than forcing the knees down.
3. Keep your ankles stacked over your knees.
4. Breathe slowly and evenly throughout the hold.

instructions:
1. Kneel and place your forearms on the floor, clasping your hands to form a triangle.
2. Set the crown of your head on the floor against your clasped hands.
3. Walk your feet in until your hips stack over your shoulders.
4. Engage your core and slowly lift both legs until your body is vertical.
5. Hold the position, pressing your forearms down to keep weight off your neck.
6. Lower your legs with control to exit. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press firmly through your forearms so most of your weight rests on your arms, not your head.
2. Keep your core braced to prevent the lower back from arching.
3. Never kick up with momentum; lift slowly to protect your neck.
4. Practice against a wall until your balance is reliable.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball.
2. Press the ball straight overhead with both arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep your ribs down to avoid arching your back.
4. Hold the ball steady directly above your shoulders.
5. Lower the ball with control once the hold time is complete. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the ball stacked over your shoulders, not in front of your head.
2. Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs to keep the torso stable.
3. Breathe steadily throughout the hold.
4. Choose a weight you can hold with full arm extension.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
2. Brace your core and keep your elbows tucked.
3. Press the ball straight out in front of your chest until your arms are extended.
4. Pause briefly with the ball at arm's length.
5. Pull the ball back to your chest with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the press path level and aimed at chest height.
2. Brace your abs so your torso does not lean back.
3. Move with control on the return rather than letting the ball drop in.
4. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped in front of your chest.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Jump up and land softly in a wider squat stance, thighs parallel.
4. Jump again and land back in the narrow hip-width squat.
5. Continue alternating between wide and narrow squats. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes on every landing.
3. Brace your core and keep your chest lifted throughout.
4. Move quickly but stay in control of each landing.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped in front of your chest.
2. Lower into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Jump up and land softly in a wider squat stance, thighs parallel.
4. Jump again and land back in the narrow hip-width squat.
5. Continue alternating between wide and narrow squats. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your knees tracking over your toes on every landing.
3. Brace your core and keep your chest lifted throughout.
4. Move quickly but stay in control of each landing.

instructions:
1. Sit on the iso-lateral shoulder press machine with your back flat against the pad and feet on the floor.
2. Grasp both handles at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
3. Press one handle overhead until the arm is nearly extended, keeping the other arm still.
4. Lower that handle under control back to shoulder height.
5. Press the opposite handle and continue alternating arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and head in contact with the pad throughout.
2. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working side.
3. Press in a smooth path without leaning the torso.
4. Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering.

instructions:
1. Sit on the iso-lateral shoulder press machine with your back flat against the pad and feet on the floor.
2. Grasp one handle at shoulder height with the palm facing forward.
3. Press the handle overhead until the arm is nearly extended.
4. Lower the handle under control back to shoulder height.
5. Complete all reps on one side, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back and head in contact with the pad throughout.
2. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working side.
3. Press in a smooth path without leaning the torso.
4. Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Lean slightly forward from the ankles and push off to begin moving.
3. Take short, quick strides, landing lightly on the midfoot under your body.
4. Bend your elbows about 90 degrees and swing your arms in rhythm with your stride.
5. Keep a steady, controlled pace and breathe rhythmically.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly under your hips, not out in front, to reduce impact.
2. Keep shoulders relaxed and gaze forward.
3. Breathe in a steady rhythm to manage effort.
4. Build duration and pace gradually over time.

instructions:
1. Stand tall holding a rope handle in each hand, rope resting behind your heels.
2. Swing the rope over your head using your wrists.
3. As the rope nears the floor, hop off one foot, then the other, running in place.
4. Keep hops low and land softly on the balls of your feet.
5. Maintain a steady, continuous rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Turn the rope with your wrists, keeping elbows close to your sides.
2. Keep jumps low to reduce joint impact.
3. Stay on the balls of your feet for quick rebounds.
4. Keep your core braced and posture tall.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet together, holding a rope handle in each hand and the rope behind your heels.
2. Swing the rope over your head using your wrists.
3. As the rope nears the floor, jump with both feet together, keeping the hop low.
4. Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately swing the rope again.
5. Maintain a steady, continuous rhythm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Turn the rope with your wrists, keeping elbows close to your sides.
2. Keep jumps low to reduce joint impact.
3. Stay on the balls of your feet for quick rebounds.
4. Keep your core braced and posture tall.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together, holding a rope handle in each hand and the rope resting behind your heels.
2. Turn the rope over your head using your wrists.
3. As the rope passes under your feet, perform a small jump landing on the balls of your feet.
4. Add a second smaller bounce while the rope is overhead to set the rhythm.
5. Keep a steady double-bounce pace for the set duration. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep jumps low to reduce joint impact.
2. Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
3. Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your core braced.
4. Wear supportive footwear.

instructions:
1. Loop the rope over a stable bar at about chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
2. Step back to create tension and lean back slightly with arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep your back straight.
4. Pull the rope toward your face, flaring your elbows out and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Extend your arms back to the start under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
2. Lead with your elbows high, not your hands.
3. Move under control without using momentum.
4. Make sure the bar can hold your bodyweight.

instructions:
1. Loop the rope over a stable bar at about hip height and hold a handle in each hand.
2. Step back to create tension and lean back with arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line.
4. Pull the rope toward your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
5. Extend your arms back to the start under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull.
2. Keep your body straight from head to heels.
3. Move slowly and avoid jerking the rope.
4. Make sure the bar can hold your bodyweight.

instructions:
1. Stand in a split stance, one foot forward and one back, hands at your sides.
2. Lower into a lunge until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
3. Explode upward, jumping off the ground.
4. Switch leg positions in mid-air, landing softly in the opposite lunge.
5. Immediately lower and jump again, alternating legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, not past them.
3. Stay upright and keep your core braced.
4. Use your arms to drive the jump.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg with the other leg extended out in front of you.
2. Hold your arms out for balance and brace your core.
3. Lower into a single-leg squat until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
4. Drive up explosively and jump off the ground.
5. Land softly on the same leg, absorbing the impact with a bent knee. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly and control the descent to protect your knee.
2. Keep your chest up and the non-working leg lifted.
3. Keep your core tight to maintain balance.
4. Master the standard pistol squat before adding the jump.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell in one hand at your side, feet hip-width apart.
2. Place the ball of your foot on a raised edge or stand flat on the floor.
3. Push through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as possible.
4. Squeeze your calves at the top.
5. Lower your heels slowly until you feel a stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
2. Pause at the top of each rep for full contraction.
3. Control the descent for a deep stretch.
4. Hold a wall for balance if needed.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with your legs spread, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Rest the back of your upper arm against your inner thigh.
3. Let the kettlebell hang with your arm extended.
4. Curl the kettlebell up toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still.
5. Lower it slowly back to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm braced against your thigh throughout.
2. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
4. Lower under control for full range.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep your elbows close to your torso and palms facing forward.
3. Curl the kettlebells up toward your shoulders.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebells slowly to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
2. Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.
3. Brace your core to stay stable.
4. Control the lowering phase for constant tension.

instructions:
1. Lie back on a decline bench holding a kettlebell in each hand.
2. Press the kettlebells up so your arms are extended over your chest.
3. Keep your upper arms fixed and bend at the elbows to lower the kettlebells toward your head.
4. Stop just before the kettlebells reach your forehead.
5. Extend your elbows to press the kettlebells back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and only move at the elbows.
2. Lower under control to protect your elbows.
3. Keep your wrists firm and neutral.
4. Squeeze the triceps at full extension.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell in front of your thighs with both hands or one in each hand.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your core braced.
3. Raise the kettlebell forward to shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebell slowly back to your thighs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Avoid swinging or using your hips to lift the weight.
2. Keep your wrists firm and elbows slightly bent.
3. Stop the raise at shoulder height.
4. Control the descent for constant tension.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
2. Place a kettlebell on your hips and hold it in place with both hands.
3. Brace your core and press through your heels.
4. Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push through your heels, not your toes, to keep tension on the glutes.
2. Avoid arching your lower back at the top.
3. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top before lowering.
4. Keep the kettlebell steady on the hip crease.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands.
2. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides.
3. Curl the kettlebell up toward your chest, keeping your upper arms still.
4. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebell under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides throughout.
2. Control the lowering phase, do not let the weight drop.
3. Grip the horns firmly to engage the forearms.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced.

instructions:
1. Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, stance slightly wider than hip-width.
2. Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip both kettlebells.
3. Press one kettlebell into the floor while rowing the other to your hip.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
5. Lower under control, then row the other side.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and chest up throughout.
2. Push the resting kettlebell into the floor to resist rotation.
3. Drive your elbow back, leading with the shoulder blade.
4. Avoid jerking the weight up with your lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Place a kettlebell across your hips and hold it steady with both hands.
3. Brace your core and drive through your heels.
4. Lift your hips until your thighs and torso form a straight line.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your heels to maximise glute engagement.
2. Keep your chin tucked and ribs down to protect the lower back.
3. Squeeze the glutes hard at the top of each rep.
4. Move with control rather than bouncing off the floor.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench.
2. Place a kettlebell across your hips and hold it steady with both hands.
3. Set your feet flat, hip-width apart, knees bent.
4. Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulder blades on the bench edge for a stable pivot.
2. Push through your heels to target the glutes.
3. Tuck your chin and keep ribs down to avoid arching the back.
4. Pause and squeeze at the top before lowering.

instructions:
1. Set a bench to about a 45 degree incline and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
2. Hold a kettlebell in each hand with arms hanging straight down.
3. Shrug your shoulder blades up and back toward the ceiling.
4. Squeeze the upper back at the top for a moment.
5. Lower the kettlebells under control until the shoulders fully relax.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and drive the movement from the shoulder blades, not the elbows.
2. Pull the shoulders back and up to hit the mid traps and rhomboids.
3. Keep your chest pinned to the pad to remove momentum.
4. Use a controlled tempo rather than heavy swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand tall holding a kettlebell at your chest with both hands.
2. Step wide to one side, about 90 cm, keeping both feet flat.
3. Bend the stepping leg and push your hips back while the other leg stays straight.
4. Lower until the bent knee is near a right angle.
5. Push through the heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat on both sides.
tips:
1. Keep the trailing leg straight to stretch the inner thigh.
2. Push your hips back rather than letting the knee cave inward.
3. Keep your chest up and core braced throughout.
4. Point both feet forward to load the adductors evenly.

instructions:
1. Sit at a preacher bench with the back of your upper arm resting on the pad.
2. Hold a kettlebell with an underhand grip, arm extended.
3. Curl the kettlebell up toward your shoulder.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebell slowly until the arm is straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm flat on the pad through the whole rep.
2. Lower under control to get the most from the stretch.
3. Avoid swinging or using your shoulder to lift.
4. Keep the wrist neutral to manage the off-center kettlebell load.

instructions:
1. Lie on a bench holding a kettlebell with both hands over your chest.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Lower the kettlebell back over your head until you feel a stretch in the lats.
4. Pull the kettlebell back over your chest using your lats.
5. Keep the core braced throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your lats by thinking of shoulder extension.
2. Keep the elbows in a fixed slight bend rather than flexing them.
3. Brace the abs to stop your ribs flaring.
4. Use a range that you can control without arching the low back.

instructions:
1. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Let the arm hang straight down from the shoulder.
3. Row the kettlebell up with the elbow flared out to the side.
4. Squeeze the rear shoulder and upper back at the top.
5. Lower the kettlebell under control.
6. Repeat on both sides.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow flared wide to bias the rear delt.
2. Maintain a flat back and braced core through each rep.
3. Pull with the shoulder and upper back, not the lower arm.
4. Keep the movement strict and controlled, not jerky.

instructions:
1. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides, feet hip-width apart.
2. Step one foot back about 60 cm and lower until both knees bend to roughly 90 degrees.
3. Keep the front shin vertical and torso upright.
4. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
5. Alternate legs each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your weight on the front heel to load the glutes.
2. Lower under control rather than dropping the back knee.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced.
4. Keep the kettlebells still at your sides.

instructions:
1. Place a kettlebell on the floor beside a bench.
2. Rest one knee and hand on the bench, hinge so your back is flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
3. Grip the kettlebell with the free hand, arm hanging straight down.
4. Pull the kettlebell to your hip, driving the elbow back and squeezing the shoulder blade.
5. Lower under control to full stretch.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and core braced throughout.
2. Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top.
4. Do not twist the torso to lift heavier.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with feet flat and the balls of your feet on a raised plate or block.
2. Rest a kettlebell on top of your knees, holding it in place.
3. Lower your heels below the toes to stretch the calves.
4. Press through the balls of your feet to lift the heels as high as possible.
5. Pause briefly at the top.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a full range, dropping the heels low for a deep stretch.
2. Pause and squeeze at the top of each rep.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
4. Pad the knees if the kettlebell digs in.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a kettlebell in one hand, arm hanging at your side.
2. Keep the arm straight and torso upright.
3. Move the arm backward behind your body, leading with the kettlebell.
4. Pause at the end of the range.
5. Return the arm slowly to your side.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow straight and arm controlled.
2. Avoid arching the lower back to swing the weight.
3. Move only at the shoulder.
4. Use a light load to keep form clean.

instructions:
1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
2. Keep your arms straight and core braced.
3. Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
4. Pause and squeeze at the top.
5. Lower the shoulders slowly to full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only the shoulders, not the arms.
2. Do not roll the shoulders; lift straight up.
3. Pause at the top for a strong contraction.
4. Keep the chin level and neck relaxed.

instructions:
1. Hold a kettlebell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips about 30 degrees.
2. Let the kettlebells hang with arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
3. Pull your shoulder blades up and back, shrugging toward your ears.
4. Squeeze the traps hard at the top.
5. Lower under control to a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the chest up and back flat throughout.
2. Drive the movement from the traps, not the arms.
3. Pause and squeeze at the top for a full contraction.
4. Use a controlled tempo rather than jerking the weight.

instructions:
1. Lie on a bench holding a kettlebell over your chest with one arm.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout.
3. Lower the kettlebell out to the side in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch.
4. Squeeze the chest to bring the kettlebell back over your chest.
5. Brace your core to resist rotation.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow softly bent to protect the joint.
2. Move in a smooth arc, not a press.
3. Brace hard to stop your torso twisting toward the working side.
4. Control the eccentric for a deep chest stretch.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a kettlebell in one hand with arm at your side.
2. Keep your elbow tucked against your body.
3. Curl the kettlebell up toward your shoulder, supinating the wrist.
4. Squeeze the biceps at the top.
5. Lower under control to a full stretch.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow pinned to your side to isolate the biceps.
2. Brace your core to prevent leaning or swinging.
3. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
4. Supinate the wrist at the top for a stronger contraction.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a kettlebell in one hand at your side.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Raise the kettlebell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower under control to your side.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow, keeping the wrist neutral.
2. Avoid shrugging the trap as you lift.
3. Brace your core to prevent leaning to the side.
4. Control the kettlebell, which hangs and adds instability.

instructions:
1. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Let the arm hang with a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Raise the kettlebell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor.
4. Squeeze the rear shoulder and retract the shoulder blade.
5. Lower under control.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Keep the torso fixed and avoid swinging the weight up.
2. Lead with the elbow to target the rear delt.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top.
4. Keep the neck relaxed and back flat throughout.

instructions:
1. Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, foot of the other leg on the floor.
2. Hold a kettlebell in the free hand with arm hanging straight down.
3. Keep your back flat and core braced.
4. Pull the kettlebell up toward your hip, driving the elbow back.
5. Lower under control to full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull with your back, not just your arm.
2. Keep your torso square and resist twisting.
3. Drive the elbow toward your hip for more lat engagement.
4. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the back.

instructions:
1. Hold a kettlebell in one hand at your side.
2. Stand on one foot, with the ball of the foot on the floor or a raised edge.
3. Use the free hand on a wall for balance if needed.
4. Rise up onto the toes as high as possible.
5. Lower the heel slowly to a full stretch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and control the lowering phase.
2. Get a full stretch at the bottom and full contraction at the top.
3. Keep the knee straight to emphasize the gastrocnemius.
4. Use a wall only lightly for balance, not support.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor.
2. Extend the other leg straight out.
3. Hold a kettlebell on the hip of the working side.
4. Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until the body forms a straight line.
5. Lower the hips under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute hard at the top.
2. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating the pelvis.
3. Push through the heel, not the toes.
4. Keep the core braced to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit with your upper back against a bench.
2. Plant one foot flat on the floor and extend the other leg out.
3. Hold a kettlebell across the hip of the working side.
4. Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until the torso is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower the hips under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute fully at the top.
2. Keep the chin tucked and ribs down.
3. Keep your hips level to avoid rotation.
4. Drive through the heel of the planted foot.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell in front of your thighs.
2. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee and your back flat.
3. Hinge at the hip, lowering the kettlebell while the rear leg extends behind you.
4. Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstring.
5. Drive the hip forward to return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips, do not round the back.
2. Keep your hips square to the floor.
3. Move slowly to maintain balance.
4. Keep the kettlebell close to your leg throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie on a bench holding a kettlebell with both hands, arms extended above your chest.
2. Keep your upper arms vertical and fixed in place.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell toward your forehead.
4. Press through your triceps to extend your arms back to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. Lower the kettlebell under control to protect your head.
3. Brace your core so your lower back stays flat.
4. Exhale as you extend your arms.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
2. Hinge at the hips and grip the kettlebell with one hand.
3. Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell upward.
4. Pull the kettlebell close to your body and punch your hand through at the top, locking it overhead.
5. Lower it back down between your legs with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement with your hips, not your arm.
2. Keep the kettlebell close to your body on the way up.
3. Punch your hand through to avoid the bell banging your wrist.
4. Brace your core to resist rotation.

instructions:
1. Stand with one foot slightly behind the other, most of your weight on the front leg.
2. Hold a kettlebell in front of your thighs.
3. Hinge at the hips and lower the kettlebell along your front leg, keeping your back flat.
4. Feel the stretch in the front-leg hamstring, then drive your hips forward to stand up.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
2. Maintain a flat back throughout the hinge.
3. Push your hips back rather than bending your knees.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands overhead.
2. Keep your upper arms vertical and close to your head.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell behind your head.
4. Press through your triceps to extend your arms back overhead.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms still and move only at the elbows.
2. Lower the kettlebell under control behind your head.
3. Brace your core so your lower back does not arch.
4. Exhale as you press up.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a bench, holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step onto the bench with your right foot.
3. Press through your right heel to lift your body up, bringing your left foot to meet it.
4. Step down with your left foot first, then your right.
5. Repeat, alternating the leading leg.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel of your stepping foot.
2. Keep your chest up and torso upright.
3. Place your whole foot on the bench to avoid slipping.
4. Control the step down rather than dropping.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and press a kettlebell over the shoulder with arm locked out, vertical.
2. Bend the same-side knee, place the foot flat, and extend the opposite arm and leg out at 45 degrees.
3. Drive through the bent foot and roll onto the free forearm, then up onto the free hand.
4. Sweep the straight leg back into a half-kneeling position, keeping the kettlebell overhead.
5. Stand up, then reverse each step in order to return to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell until you are standing, then fix gaze forward.
2. Keep the loaded arm locked vertically throughout every transition.
3. Move slowly and pause at each position to control balance.
4. Brace your core hard to protect the spine under load.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in front of the thighs with both hands.
2. Keep the kettlebell close to the body and pull the elbows straight up.
3. Raise it until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and elbows lead the hands.
4. Pause briefly at the top, keeping the wrists relaxed.
5. Lower the kettlebell under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows, not your hands, to target the side delts and traps.
2. Keep the kettlebell close to your torso throughout.
3. Do not shrug excessively or jerk the weight up.
4. Stop the pull if you feel shoulder pinching at the top.

instructions:
1. Set a kettlebell on the floor and take a push-up position with one hand on it, one hand on the floor.
2. Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows.
3. Press back up to full arm extension.
4. Walk both hands over the kettlebell to the other side.
5. Perform another push-up, then walk back over.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Brace your core to resist hip rotation as you walk over.
3. Keep the kettlebell stable and weighted enough not to tip.
4. Move the hands deliberately to keep shoulders square.

instructions:
1. Press a kettlebell overhead with arm locked, feet wider than shoulder-width.
2. Turn the feet about 45 degrees away from the loaded arm.
3. Push the loaded-side hip out and hinge sideways, sliding the free hand down the front leg.
4. Lower until the torso is near horizontal, keeping the kettlebell stacked overhead.
5. Drive the hip back and stand tall to return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell and the arm locked the whole time.
2. Hinge at the hip, do not just bend the spine sideways.
3. Keep both legs fairly straight to load the hamstrings and obliques.
4. Start light to master the mobility before adding load.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and rest the forearm on the thigh, palm up, with a kettlebell in the hand.
2. Let the wrist drop so the kettlebell rolls toward the fingertips.
3. Curl the wrist up by flexing as high as possible.
4. Squeeze briefly at the top.
5. Lower under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearm pressed firmly against the thigh to isolate the wrist.
