2. Use a full range, letting the kettlebell roll down then curling all the way up.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the forearm flexors.
4. Keep grip relaxed enough to allow the roll at the bottom.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm facing down, holding a kettlebell.
2. Let the kettlebell pull your wrist down toward the floor.
3. Extend your wrist to lift the kettlebell as high as possible.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your forearm flat on your thigh so only the wrist moves.
2. Use a slow, controlled tempo in both directions.
3. Start light to protect the wrist joint.
4. Squeeze at the top for a full contraction.

instructions:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Swing your body to create a controlled arch-to-hollow rhythm.
3. Drive your hips forward and pull your chest toward the bar as the swing carries you up.
4. Get your chin over the bar.
5. Push away from the bar and return to the hanging arch position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Time the hip drive with the upswing to use momentum efficiently.
2. Keep your core braced to protect your shoulders.
3. Build a strong strict pull-up before adding the kip.
4. Keep movement continuous and rhythmic, not jerky.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor or place your hands on two parallel bars or blocks.
2. Press down through your hands and lock your elbows.
3. Lift your hips and legs off the floor.
4. Hold your legs straight and parallel to the ground at a 90-degree angle to your torso.
5. Keep your core tight and hold for time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Depress and press your shoulders down to support your bodyweight.
2. Point your toes and squeeze your quads to keep legs straight.
3. Brace your abs hard to keep the torso compact.
4. Bend the knees if a full L-sit is too difficult.

instructions:
1. Stand holding the end of a landmine barbell at chest height with both hands.
2. Step back into a reverse lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor.
3. As you lunge, rotate your torso toward the front leg.
4. Twist back to center and drive through the front foot to stand.
5. Alternate legs each repetition.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Rotate from the trunk, not just the arms.
2. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
3. Brace your core to control the diagonal pull of the bar.
4. Move at a controlled pace to maintain balance.

instructions:
1. Stand holding the end of a landmine barbell at chest height with both hands.
2. Step back into a reverse lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor.
3. Drive through the front foot to stand back up.
4. Press the bar forward and upward at an angle until your arms extend.
5. Bring the bar back to your chest and alternate legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Press in a smooth arc following the landmine's path.
2. Keep your core braced throughout the lunge and press.
3. Keep the front knee aligned over the toes.
4. Exhale as you press the bar away.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Stand facing the bar with feet hip-width apart, holding the end at shoulder height in one hand.
3. Press the bar up and slightly forward until the arm is extended.
4. Lower under control back to the shoulder.
5. Switch hands and press with the other arm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to resist twisting toward the loaded side.
2. Press along the bar's natural diagonal arc, not straight up.
3. Keep your wrist firm and aligned with your forearm.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Stand beside the bar and grip the end with one hand, palm up, arm extended.
3. Keep your elbow pinned near your ribs.
4. Curl the bar up toward the opposite shoulder.
5. Lower under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arm still and move only at the elbow.
2. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top before lowering.
3. Control the lowering phase, do not let the bar drop.
4. Keep your wrist neutral to protect the forearm.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Stand facing away from the base and hold the end against your chest with both hands.
3. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and core braced.
4. Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.
5. Lower your heels slowly to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pause and squeeze the calves at the top of each rep.
2. Lower slowly for a full stretch at the bottom.
3. Keep your knees straight to bias the gastrocnemius.
4. Keep your torso upright and core tight throughout.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Stand beside the bar and grip the end with one hand, palm up.
3. Brace your working upper arm against your inner thigh or torso.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulder.
5. Lower under control to full extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm fixed so only the elbow moves.
2. Squeeze the biceps fully at the top.
3. Control the lowering phase for a full stretch.
4. Keep your wrist neutral throughout.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Stand facing the bar and hold the end at chest height with both hands, feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Step one foot back and diagonally behind the other leg.
4. Bend both knees until the front thigh is near parallel to the floor.
5. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
2. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes.
3. Squeeze the glutes as you stand back up.
4. Move with control to keep your balance in the diagonal path.

instructions:
1. Anchor a barbell in a landmine and load the free end.
2. Get on all fours facing the landmine and hook the bar end behind one knee or against the sole.
3. Brace your core and keep a neutral spine.
4. Drive the working leg back and up by squeezing the glute until the thigh is in line with your torso.
5. Lower under control without arching the lower back.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the glute at the top rather than swinging the leg.
2. Keep the hips square to the floor throughout.
3. Brace the abs to protect the lower back.
4. Move slowly to keep tension on the glute.

instructions:
1. Anchor a barbell in a landmine and hold the loaded end at your chest in a goblet grip.
2. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
3. Step one foot back and across behind the other at about 45 degrees.
4. Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor and the front thigh is near parallel.
5. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front heel planted and weight on it.
2. Keep the chest up and torso tall.
3. Control the descent to protect the front knee.
4. Brace the core for balance.

instructions:
1. Anchor a barbell in a landmine and hold the loaded end at your chest in a goblet grip.
2. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width.
3. Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee while keeping the other leg straight.
4. Push the hips back and lower until the bent thigh is near parallel.
5. Drive through the working heel to return to center.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both feet flat and pointing forward.
2. Push the hips back to load the glute.
3. Keep the chest up and back flat.
4. Feel the stretch in the straight leg's inner thigh.

instructions:
1. Anchor a barbell in a landmine and stand with your back to the anchor.
2. Hold the loaded end behind your hips or at your sides.
3. Set feet shoulder-width with toes slightly out.
4. Bend the knees and sit down until the thighs are near parallel.
5. Drive through the heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the chest up and the torso fairly upright.
2. Track the knees over the toes.
3. Drive through the whole foot, not just the toes.
4. Brace the core throughout the lift.

instructions:
1. Anchor a barbell in a landmine and kneel facing it in a half-kneeling stance.
2. Hold the loaded bar end at shoulder height with one hand.
3. Brace the core and keep the torso upright.
4. Press the bar up and forward until the arm is extended.
5. Lower under control back to the shoulder.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the hips and torso square, resisting any twist.
2. Squeeze the glute of the down knee for stability.
3. Keep the core braced to prevent leaning back.
4. Press in a smooth arc following the bar path.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and grip the end of the landmine barbell with both hands, arms extended above your chest.
2. Press your lower back into the floor and brace your core.
3. Lift your head and shoulders off the floor and raise your straight legs to about 30 to 45 degrees.
4. Hold the hollow position, keeping the bar steady and the lower back flat.
5. Maintain the hold for the set time, then lower with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor the entire time.
2. Lower the legs if the back starts to arch.
3. Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath.
4. Keep arms locked and the bar directly over the chest.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg press machine with your back flat against the pad.
2. Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the center of the platform, toes slightly out.
3. Release the safety and bend your knees to lower the platform until they reach about 90 degrees.
4. Press through your heels to extend your legs without locking the knees.
5. Lower under control back to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and lower back pressed into the seat throughout.
2. Do not let your knees cave inward.
3. Drive through the heels, not the toes.
4. Exhale as you press and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg extension machine with your back against the pad.
2. Position the padded lever just above your ankles and align your knees with the machine pivot.
3. Hold the side handles and brace your core.
4. Extend your legs to straighten the knees, squeezing the quads at the top.
5. Lower the weight under control to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and back pressed into the seat.
2. Control the lowering phase rather than letting the weight drop.
3. Pause briefly at full extension for a stronger contraction.
4. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with your legs stacked and your head supported by your lower arm.
2. Extend your top arm straight up toward the ceiling.
3. Slowly draw large circles with the top arm, keeping it straight.
4. Reverse the direction of the circles after several reps.
5. Roll to the other side and repeat with the other arm. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and keep the motion controlled.
2. Keep your core braced so your torso does not roll.
3. Start with small circles and gradually make them larger.
4. Keep the shoulder relaxed, not shrugged.

instructions:
1. Set the machine to your height and kneel with one knee on the pad.
2. Place the other leg under the padded lever, just above the heel, and rest your chest on the pad.
3. Hold the handles and keep your back flat.
4. Curl the lever by bending the knee and pulling your heel toward your glute.
5. Lower under control to the start, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest on the pad and avoid arching your back.
2. Squeeze the hamstring at the top of each rep.
3. Control the lowering phase fully.
4. Exhale as you curl and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand on the multi-hip machine platform and set the padded lever against the outside of your working thigh.
2. Grip the handles and stand tall with a slight bend in the standing leg.
3. Drive the working leg outward against the resistance, lifting it to the side as far as comfortable.
4. Pause briefly, then lower the leg slowly to the start.
5. Finish the set, switch legs, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean toward the lever.
2. Brace your core to stabilize the hips and stay balanced.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg.
4. Squeeze the outer hip at the top of each rep.

instructions:
1. Stand on the multi-hip machine platform and set the padded lever against the inside of your working thigh.
2. Grip the handles and stand tall with a slight bend in the standing leg.
3. Pull the working leg across the midline against the resistance.
4. Pause briefly, then return the leg slowly to the start.
5. Finish the set, switch legs, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and your hips square throughout.
2. Brace your core to stay balanced on the standing leg.
3. Control the return so the inner thigh stays loaded.
4. Avoid jerking or using momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand on the multi-hip machine, turn to one side, and set the padded lever behind your working thigh.
2. Grip the handles in front and hinge slightly forward at the hips with a straight spine.
3. Drive the working leg back until it lines up with your torso.
4. Squeeze the glute at the top, then lower the leg slowly to the start.
5. Finish the set, switch legs, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight bend in the standing knee for balance.
2. Squeeze the glute hard at full extension.
3. Move under control instead of swinging the leg.
4. Keep your spine neutral and do not over-arch your lower back.

instructions:
1. Sit on the push-pull chair station and reach up to grip the overhead handles.
2. Set your feet flat and keep your chest up and core braced.
3. Pull the handles down toward your shoulders, driving your elbows down and back.
4. Squeeze your back at the bottom of the pull.
5. Let the handles rise under control until your arms are extended, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows to load the lats rather than the arms.
2. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning back excessively.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the bottom.
4. Control the return rather than letting the handles snap up.

instructions:
1. Sit on the push-pull chair station and grip the front handles at chest height.
2. Set your feet flat and keep your back against the pad with your core braced.
3. Press the handles forward until your arms are extended.
4. Pause briefly at full extension.
5. Bend your elbows to return the handles slowly to your chest, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your shoulders down and back against the pad.
2. Press smoothly and squeeze the chest at full extension.
3. Control the return so tension stays on the chest.
4. Keep your core braced to avoid arching off the pad.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of the rebounder with feet hip-width apart and arms bent at 90 degrees.
2. Drive one knee up toward hip height while pushing off the mat.
3. As that foot lands, immediately drive the opposite knee up.
4. Pump your arms in time with your legs and keep your core braced.
5. Continue alternating knees at a running pace for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly through the balls of your feet to control the bounce.
2. Keep your chest tall and avoid leaning back.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced on the unstable mat.
4. Breathe rhythmically with each stride.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of the rebounder with feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and push off the mat into a jump.
3. Drive both knees up toward your chest at the top of the jump.
4. Extend your legs to land softly with bent knees.
5. Continue jumping and tucking the knees for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Engage your core to lift the knees rather than swinging the legs.
2. Land softly through the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
3. Keep your torso upright throughout the jump.
4. Exhale as you drive the knees up.

instructions:
1. Kneel upright on the centre of the rebounder with knees hip-width apart.
2. Brace your core and keep your torso tall.
3. Push down through your knees and shins to drive your body upward off the mat.
4. Absorb the rebound by softening through the hips as you settle back down.
5. Repeat the pushing rhythm for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
2. Stay upright and avoid rocking the torso.
3. Push down through the mat in a controlled rhythm.
4. Breathe steadily throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of the rebounder with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
2. Press down gently into the mat to start a small bounce.
3. Keep your feet close to the surface, barely leaving the mat.
4. Maintain an upright posture with a braced core.
5. Continue the light rhythmic bouncing for the set duration.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bounce small and controlled.
2. Land softly through the balls of your feet.
3. Keep your core engaged for balance.
4. Breathe steadily and relax your shoulders.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band across your upper back and loop the ends under each hand.
2. Set up in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and feet together.
3. Brace your core and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
4. Let the band assist as you press through your hands back to a full plank.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Lower under control until your chest nearly touches the floor.
3. Keep elbows tucked to about 45 degrees to spare the shoulders.
4. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Loop a resistance band around both thighs just above the knees and kneel on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Brace your core and keep your back flat, with one knee bent at 90 degrees and the foot flexed.
3. Drive that foot toward the ceiling, keeping the knee bent and squeezing the glute at the top.
4. Lower the leg under control to the start.
5. Finish all reps on one side, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back flat and avoid arching the lower back to push higher.
2. Move slowly and squeeze the glute at the top rather than swinging the leg.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep hips square to the floor throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit on a chair with back straight, knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor.
2. Loop a resistance band around the balls of both feet and hold the ends in your hands for tension.
3. Press the balls of your feet down, pointing the toes against the band resistance.
4. Squeeze the calves at the bottom, then flex the feet back up under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the back straight and avoid leaning forward.
2. Hold the band ends steady to keep constant tension.
3. Exhale as you press down, inhale as you return.
4. Use a slow tempo through the full range.

instructions:
1. Loop a resistance band around both thighs just above the knees and lie on your side with legs bent 90 degrees and feet stacked.
2. Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on the floor for support.
3. Keeping the feet together, lift the top knee as high as possible without rolling the pelvis back.
4. Squeeze the glute at the top, then lower the knee under control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep feet together and pelvis stacked to isolate the glutes.
2. Move slowly and avoid rocking the hips backward.
3. Exhale as you open the knee, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the head and neck aligned with the spine.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band to a high point in front of you and to one side.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handle in the opposite hand with the palm facing up.
3. Start with that arm straight and extended up toward the anchor across your body.
4. Keeping the arm straight, pull the handle down and across toward the hip on the working side.
5. Return slowly to the start, then finish reps and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from the lat, not the arm.
2. Keep the elbow only slightly bent and fixed throughout.
3. Keep hips square and resist twisting the torso.
4. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with a loop band around your ankles and another around your forearms, arms extended forward and legs straight.
2. Brace your core and glutes.
3. Lift your chest, arms and legs off the floor at the same time, spreading the legs apart against the band.
4. Squeeze the lower back and glutes at the top, keeping arms and legs straight.
5. Lower under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the neck neutral by looking at the floor.
2. Lift with the lower back and glutes rather than jerking.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep arms and legs straight throughout.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart, and place a loop band just above your knees.
2. Rest your arms by your sides with palms pressing the floor.
3. Drive through your heels and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line.
4. Holding the bridge, press your knees outward against the band as far as possible.
5. Bring your knees back together, then lower your hips with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a straight line from shoulders to knees; do not arch the lower back.
2. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top of each rep.
3. Press the knees out and feel the outer hips engage.
4. Exhale lifting and pressing out, inhale on the way down.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart, and place a loop band just above your knees.
2. Bring your hands to your chest and interlock your fingers.
3. Drive through your heels and lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line.
4. Press your knees gently outward against the band to keep tension on the glutes.
5. Hold briefly, squeezing your glutes at the top, then lower your hips with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a straight line from shoulders to knees; do not arch the lower back.
2. Push the knees outward against the band throughout the set.
3. Squeeze the glutes at the top rather than pushing with the lower back.
4. Exhale lifting, inhale lowering.

instructions:
1. Kneel upright with a loop band anchored at a low point behind you and wrapped around your hips.
2. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
3. Sit back onto your heels, keeping the band taut.
4. Thrust your hips forward, rising tall onto your knees and squeezing your glutes at the top.
5. Lower back onto your heels with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at full hip extension.
2. Keep the band securely anchored to hold steady tension.
3. Avoid over-arching the lower back; finish with a tall, neutral hip position.
4. Exhale thrusting forward, inhale sitting back.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band to a high point in front of you and to your left.
2. Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat, holding the handle in your right hand, palm facing up.
3. Extend your right arm straight overhead toward the anchor, keeping the arm straight.
4. Pull the handle down across your body toward your right hip, keeping the elbow locked.
5. Return slowly to the overhead start with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from the lat, not the arm.
2. Keep the working arm straight throughout the pull.
3. Keep hips square and resist any twisting of the torso.
4. Exhale pulling down, inhale returning up.

instructions:
1. Kneel in a tabletop position on a bench, hands gripping the edges and knees under your hips.
2. Loop a resistance band around both thighs just above the knees.
3. Extend your right leg straight back and down, kept below bench level.
4. Sweep the leg in a half-circle inward, crossing over the left leg until level with the bench.
5. Return the leg along the same path with control.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep shoulders and hips square to the floor; do not rotate the torso.
2. Move slowly and feel the outer hip and glute working.
3. Keep the band taut through the full half-circle.
4. Exhale sweeping the leg, inhale returning.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around both ankles, arms by your sides.
2. Hold something stable for balance if needed.
3. Bend your right knee and curl the heel toward your glutes, keeping the thigh still.
4. Slowly extend the leg back down with control against the band.
5. Finish all reps, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower.
2. Keep the working thigh stationary so the knee does the work.
3. Move slowly to keep tension on the hamstring, not momentum.
4. Keep a slight bend in the standing leg for stability.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Loop a band under your right foot and anchor the other end under your right hand.
3. Kick the right leg straight back until it is in line with your torso, squeezing the glute.
4. Slowly return the knee toward the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you kick back and inhale as you return.
2. Squeeze the glute at full extension rather than swinging the leg.
3. Keep your back flat and core braced to protect the lower back.
4. Keep the band taut throughout for constant tension.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs extended straight up toward the ceiling and a loop band around your ankles.
2. Place your arms by your sides on the floor for stability.
3. Brace your core and keep the legs straight with feet flexed.
4. Open the legs wide apart against the band resistance.
5. Slowly bring the legs back together with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you open the legs and inhale as you close them.
2. Keep the legs straight so the hips do the work.
3. Move slowly to keep steady tension on the band.
4. Press your lower back into the floor to stay stable.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with arms crossed under your forehead and a loop band around your thighs, just above the knees.
2. Keep your legs straight and feet together.
3. Squeeze your glutes to lift both legs off the floor.
4. While lifting, spread the legs wide apart against the band.
5. Bring the legs back together, then lower them with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and open, inhale as you close and lower.
2. Squeeze the glutes to drive the movement, not the lower back.
3. Keep the core braced to protect the spine.
4. Lift only as high as you can without arching the lower back.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on your back with arms by your sides and a loop band around your thighs, just above the knees.
2. Keep both legs extended and together.
3. Brace your core and lift your right leg straight up toward the ceiling, keeping the left leg on the floor.
4. Slowly lower the leg, stopping just before the heel touches the floor.
5. Finish all reps, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
2. Exhale as you raise the leg and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep the leg straight and move with control, not momentum.
4. Brace the abs to stabilize the pelvis.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart, and place a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Lift one leg off the floor and extend it, keeping the thigh in line with the working leg.
3. Press through the heel of the planted foot to drive your hips up until shoulders, hips and knee form a straight line.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips with control.
5. Finish the reps, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through the heel and squeeze the glute at the top, not the lower back.
2. Keep your hips level; do not let the raised side drop.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Brace your core to stop your back from arching.

instructions:
1. Loop a resistance band around both ankles and stand facing an incline bench.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and rest your hands on the top of the bench for support.
3. Engage your glutes and drive one leg up and back against the band, keeping it straight.
4. Pause at the top, then lower the leg with control to the start.
5. Finish the reps, then switch legs. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the heel and squeeze the glute at the top of each rep.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced; do not arch or rotate the hips.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg with momentum.
4. Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a band with both hands.
2. Raise your arms straight in front at shoulder height, palms down, with light tension in the band.
3. Pull the band apart by drawing your arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Pause when the band reaches your chest, then return your arms to the front with control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of each rep.
2. Keep arms straight and at shoulder height; do not let them drift up or down.
3. Keep wrists neutral and avoid shrugging the shoulders.
4. Move slowly and resist the band on the way back.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a flat bench with hips at the edge and legs hanging straight down.
2. Loop a band around your thighs above the knees and hold a stability ball between your feet.
3. Grip the sides of the bench to stay stable.
4. Squeeze your glutes and lift your legs until they are in line with your torso.
5. Lower your legs with control to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with the glutes, not by swinging the legs.
2. Keep your core braced and avoid overarching the lower back.
3. Grip the bench firmly to keep your upper body still.
4. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent about 90 degrees and feet flat, hip-width apart.
2. Loop a band around your thighs just above the knees.
3. Lean back slightly and place your hands on the floor behind you for support.
4. Press your knees outward against the band as far as you can.
5. Bring your knees back together with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Push the knees out under control and resist on the way back in.
2. Keep your feet flat and planted throughout.
3. Drive from the outer hips and glutes, not the lower back.
4. Exhale as you press out, inhale as you return.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench with knees bent at 90 degrees and a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Sit tall, brace your core, and place your hands on the bench for support.
3. Press your knees outward against the band as wide as you can.
4. Squeeze the outer hips at the end range.
5. Bring your knees back together slowly with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press the knees out, inhale as you return.
2. Drive from the outer hips, not by leaning the torso.
3. Move slowly to keep constant tension on the band.
4. Keep your back tall and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band at shoulder height to your side.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with the far hand, arm extended out to the side at shoulder height.
3. Keeping the arm straight, pull the band down and across toward your hip.
4. Squeeze the chest and lat at the bottom.
5. Return the arm to the side at shoulder height with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Move slowly and with control to maximize tension.
2. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
3. Keep the working arm straight throughout.
4. Choose a band that challenges you without breaking form.

instructions:
1. Place a loop band around your thighs just above the knees and lie on your side with knees bent 90 degrees, legs stacked.
2. Prop up on your forearm with the elbow under the shoulder, and lift your hips slightly off the floor.
3. Keeping the knees bent, raise the top knee against the band while lifting the hips until the torso is straight.
4. Squeeze the glutes at the top.
5. Lower the leg and hips back down with control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Drive from the outer glute, not by rolling backward.
2. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep a steady pace for constant band tension.
4. Keep the elbow stacked under the shoulder.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Keep your chest up and bring your hands to your chest.
3. Lower into a squat by bending the knees and pushing the hips back.
4. Push the knees outward against the band as you descend.
5. Drive through your heels to stand back up.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the chest up and lean slightly forward.
2. Press the knees out so they track over the toes.
3. Exhale as you stand, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the band taut throughout to engage the glutes.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Keep your chest up and bring your hands to your chest.
3. Lower into a squat by bending the knees and pushing the hips back.
4. Explosively jump up, extending the legs fully and pressing the knees out against the band.
5. Land softly back into the squat, absorbing through the legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with knees slightly bent to absorb impact.
2. Press the knees out against the band on takeoff and landing.
3. Exhale as you jump, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep the chest up and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around your thighs just above the knees. Place hands on hips.
2. Shift your weight onto your right leg and lift your left foot slightly off the floor.
3. Keeping the left leg straight, lift it out to the side against the band, squeezing the outer hip at the top.
4. Lower the leg back to the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch to the other leg. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift the leg and inhale as you lower it.
2. Keep a slight bend in the standing leg to stay balanced.
3. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the side.
4. Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around both wrists.
2. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees and tuck them against your sides, forearms pointing forward.
3. Rotate your forearms outward, pulling the band apart while keeping the elbows pinned.
4. Return your forearms to the start with control, keeping tension on the band. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly to maximise rotator cuff activation and protect the shoulder.
2. Exhale as you rotate out, inhale as you return.
3. Keep the elbows fixed at your sides throughout.
4. Use a light band so form stays clean.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
2. Bend your hips and knees into a half-squat, keeping your back straight and chest slightly forward.
3. Press your knees outward against the band, opening the legs as wide as possible.
4. Bring your knees back together with control, keeping tension on the band.
5. Hold the half-squat throughout. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press the knees out, inhale as you bring them in.
2. Use a band with enough tension to challenge you without breaking form.
3. Keep feet flat and weight evenly distributed.
4. Drive the knees out from the hips, not the feet.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band at hip height and stand facing the anchor, holding the free end in your right hand.
2. Reach your right arm forward toward the anchor, palm facing down.
3. Keeping the arm straight, pull the band down and back until your hand reaches your side.
4. Return your arm forward to the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch arms. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your lat and rear shoulder, not your hand.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbow to protect the joint.
3. Keep the band taut throughout the set.
4. Stay tall and avoid leaning back.

instructions:
1. Anchor a band at hip height and stand with your back to the anchor, holding the free end in your right hand.
2. Let your right arm hang back toward the anchor, palm facing forward.
3. Keeping the arm straight, raise it forward and up to about lower-chest height.
4. Lower your arm back to the start with control.
5. Finish all reps, then switch arms. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from the front of your shoulder.
2. Keep a slight bend in the elbow to protect the joint.
3. Keep the band taut throughout the set.
4. Stay tall and brace your core to avoid arching.

instructions:
1. Anchor a resistance band at a low point behind your head.
2. Lie on your back, hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, knees above your hips.
3. Hold the band with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest, pressing the band against the anchor tension.
4. Press your lower back into the floor and lower your right leg toward the ground, keeping the left leg still.
5. Return the right leg, then lower the left leg, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your lower back flat against the floor throughout.
2. Exhale as you lower the leg, inhale as you return.
3. Keep the arms steady against the band pull to engage the lats and brace the trunk.
4. Move slowly and avoid letting the pelvis tilt or rotate.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with your hands on the floor and your feet on the ab roller.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and roll the wheel toward your hands, keeping your legs straight until your hips pike up and thighs near vertical.
4. Hold briefly with the core tight.
5. Roll the wheel back under control to the plank position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pike up, inhale as you return.
2. Keep a neutral spine and brace hard to protect the lower back.
3. Start with a small range and build distance as you get stronger.
4. Use a stable, non-slip surface.

instructions:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and core engaged.
2. Lean slightly forward from the ankles and begin striding, landing midfoot under your hips.
3. Drive each knee forward and push off through the ball of your foot.
4. Swing your arms in rhythm, elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
5. Hold a steady, comfortable pace for the chosen duration or distance.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep shoulders relaxed and posture tall.
2. Breathe rhythmically to steady your effort.
3. Land softly under your center of mass to reduce impact.
4. Stay hydrated on longer runs.

instructions:
1. Sit on the hip abduction machine with your feet on the footrests.
2. Position your outer thighs against the padded levers.
3. Grip the side handles and sit upright against the backrest.
4. Press your legs outward against the resistance, pushing the pads apart.
5. Pause briefly at the widest point, then return slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back firmly against the backrest.
2. Squeeze the outer glutes at the peak of each rep.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Control the return rather than letting the pads snap back.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg extension machine with one shin behind the padded lever, just above the ankle.
2. Grip the side handles and press your back against the backrest.
3. Extend your working leg, straightening the knee to lift the lever.
4. Pause briefly at the top with the quad contracted.
5. Lower the lever slowly to the start, then complete the set and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
2. Keep your back against the backrest and hips still.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
4. Train both legs evenly to address imbalances.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg extension machine with your back against the backrest and both shins behind the padded lever, just above the ankles.
2. Grip the side handles and keep your core engaged.
3. Extend your right knee to raise the lever until the leg is nearly straight.
4. Lower the right leg under control to the start.
5. Repeat with the left leg, then alternate.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move smoothly and avoid swinging the weight up.
2. Keep your hips and back pressed into the seat.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
4. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the quad.

instructions:
1. Sit on the leg extension machine with your back against the backrest and both shins behind the padded lever, just above the ankles.
2. Grip the side handles and keep your core engaged.
3. Extend both knees to raise the lever until your legs are nearly straight.
4. Lower the lever under control to the start.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move smoothly and avoid swinging the weight up.
2. Keep your hips and back pressed into the seat.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
4. Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the quads.

instructions:
1. Sit on the hip adductor machine with your back straight and feet on the footrests.
2. Place your knees against the inner pads with your legs spread apart.
3. Squeeze your knees together against the resistance until the pads nearly meet.
4. Slowly return to the spread starting position under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid letting the pads snap back.
2. Keep your back against the seat and core braced.
3. Squeeze the inner thighs at the closed position.
4. Exhale as you close, inhale as you open.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet hip-width apart, holding a handle in each hand at head height.
2. Brace your core and hinge slightly at the hips with a soft bend in the knees.
3. Drive both handles down past your hips by pulling with your lats and extending your arms.
4. Crunch your abs to add power at the bottom of the pull.
5. Return your arms overhead under control and reset.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Initiate each pull with your lats and core, not just the arms.
2. Keep a steady hip hinge rather than squatting.
3. Breathe rhythmically with each stroke.
4. Keep the wrists firm to transfer power through the handles.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet hip-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with palms facing each other.
2. Brace your core and keep an upright posture.
3. Curl the handles up toward your face by bending your elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
4. Squeeze your biceps as the handles reach face height.
5. Extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides through the curl.
2. Move at a steady pace to keep tension on the biceps.
3. Do not shrug or use the shoulders to lift.
4. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing away from the ski ergometer, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
2. Open your arms out to the sides at shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows.
3. Pull both handles inward in an arc until your hands meet in front of your chest, squeezing your chest.
4. Pause briefly at the contraction.
5. Return your arms to the sides under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed, slight elbow bend throughout the arc.
2. Drive the movement from the chest, not the hands.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso still.
4. Move at a steady, controlled pace.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
2. Pull the handles down toward your hips while lowering into a squat, bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
3. Drive through your legs and jump up explosively, extending fully.
4. Pull the handles back up under control as you rise.
5. Land softly back into the squat and flow into the next rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
2. Coordinate the arm pull with the leg drive.
3. Brace your core to protect your lower back.
4. Breathe rhythmically across each rep.

instructions:
1. Kneel facing the ski ergometer, holding the opposite handle in each hand so the cables cross.
2. Extend your arms forward at head height with a slight elbow bend.
3. Pull both handles outward and back in a reverse fly, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Pause when your arms reach out to your sides.
5. Return your arms forward under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull out, inhale as you return.
2. Lead with your elbows to target the rear delts.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced.
4. Use a controlled tempo without swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with arms straight.
2. Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back, and lean forward.
3. Keeping your arms straight, pull both handles down and back toward your hips.
4. Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
5. Return your arms forward under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your arms straight and drive from the lats.
3. Depress your shoulder blades to engage the back.
4. Brace your core to keep the torso stable.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer, holding the opposite handle in each hand so the cables cross.
2. Extend your arms forward at head height with a slight elbow bend.
3. Pull both handles outward and back in a reverse fly, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Pause when your arms reach out to your sides.
5. Return your arms forward under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull out, inhale as you return.
2. Lead with your elbows to target the rear delts.
3. Keep your back straight and core braced.
4. Use a controlled tempo without swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet about 30 cm apart, holding both handles with arms overhead.
2. Step your right foot back into a reverse lunge, lowering until the right knee nears the floor and the left thigh is parallel to the floor.
3. As you descend, pull both handles down to your hips, driving with your back and triceps.
4. Push through the left heel to stand, bringing the right foot forward and returning your arms overhead under control.
5. Alternate legs each rep. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and do not let it cave inward.
2. Drive the pull from your lats and core, not just the arms.
3. Exhale as you pull and lunge down, inhale as you return.
4. Keep the torso upright and core braced throughout.

instructions:
1. Stand with your back to the ski ergometer, right foot a step forward and left foot back for support.
2. Hold both handles with palms facing each other and upper arms parallel to the floor.
3. Pull the handles forward by extending your elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
4. Extend until the arms are straight in front of you, engaging the triceps.
5. Return slowly to the bent-elbow start under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms stationary so the triceps do the work.
2. Brace your core to keep the torso stable in the staggered stance.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
4. Control the return rather than letting the resistance snap back.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet about shoulder-width apart, holding both handles.
2. Pull the handles down with elbows bent to 90 degrees until the elbows reach your sides, while lowering into a squat and pushing the hips back.
3. Keep the chest up and knees tracking over the toes at the bottom.
4. Return the handles in a half-circle arc as you stand back up from the squat.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Sync the arm pull with the squat so legs and back share the load.
2. Keep the core braced and back flat during the squat.
3. Breathe steadily and rhythmically with each cycle.
4. Push through your heels to stand.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet about shoulder-width apart, holding both handles, core braced.
2. Pull the handles down in a wide arc while lowering into a squat, bending the knees and pushing the hips back.
3. Continue pulling until the handles reach hip level and you are at the bottom of the squat.
4. Return the arms to the start under control as you stand back up.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the wide arc to engage the lats and rear delts strongly.
2. Keep shoulders down and relaxed, not shrugged up.
3. Drive evenly through arms and legs to share the effort.
4. Push through your heels to stand from the squat.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the ski ergometer with feet about 30 cm apart, holding both handles with palms facing each other.
2. Start with arms bent at 90 degrees and elbows pointing down at your sides.
3. Pull the handles down toward your hips by extending the elbows, keeping the upper arms still.
4. Extend until the arms are straight, engaging the triceps.
5. Return slowly to the bent-elbow start under control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms close to your body to isolate the triceps.
2. Maintain a steady pace for consistent tension.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
4. Brace the core to keep the torso upright.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an ab wheel with both hands.
2. Bend at the hips and place the wheel on the floor in front of your feet, arms extended.
3. Brace your core and roll the wheel forward, extending your body until it is nearly straight.
4. Keep your back flat and avoid letting your hips sag.
5. Pull the wheel back toward your feet using your core to return upright.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and under control through both phases.
2. Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return.
3. Keep the lower back flat, never arched.
4. Squeeze your glutes to keep the pelvis stable.

instructions:
1. Step onto the stepmill and hold the side rails lightly for balance.
2. Select a pace and begin climbing, stepping fully onto each moving step.
3. Keep your torso upright and drive through the whole foot.
4. Maintain a steady rhythm without leaning on the rails.
5. Continue for the set duration, then step off carefully.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stand tall and avoid hunching over the console.
2. Use the rails only for light balance, not to support your weight.
3. Push through the heels to emphasize the glutes.
4. Breathe steadily and keep a controlled cadence.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height.
2. Stand facing away from the anchor, holding a handle in each hand with arms in front.
3. Brace your core and lean forward, extending your arms overhead in a straight line from head to heels.
4. Lower until your arms are fully extended and you feel tension through the core.
5. Pull your arms back down to return your body to the upright start position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you fall out, inhale as you return.
2. Keep your body rigid in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Move from the shoulders and core, keeping arms straight.
4. Step closer to the anchor to make it harder.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height.
2. Sit on the floor, knees bent and feet flat, holding a handle in each hand with a neutral grip.
3. Lean back and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles, bending the elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower under control back to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
2. Lead with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades.
3. Keep the hips lifted so the body stays in a straight line.
4. Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about chest height.
2. Stand facing away from the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart, a handle in each hand.
3. Brace your core and lean forward, arms extended to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Squeeze your chest to bring your hands together in front of you.
5. Open your arms back to the sides under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you bring the hands together, inhale as you open.
2. Drive the movement with the chest, keeping a fixed elbow bend.
3. Keep the core tight so the hips do not sag.
4. Step forward to increase the difficulty.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to an overhead position and grasp them with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and feet off the floor or lightly assisting on the ground.
3. Pull your body up by driving your elbows down and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Continue until your chin clears the handles.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Depress your shoulder blades before pulling to engage the lats.
2. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your core braced to stop your body from swinging.
4. Move smoothly without jerking off the bottom.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about chest height and face the anchor.
2. Grasp the handles and walk your feet forward so you lean back with arms extended.
3. Keep your body straight from head to heels and brace your core.
4. Pull the handles toward your face, flaring your elbows out to the sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Extend your arms back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with your elbows high and wide to target the rear delts.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
4. Step closer or farther from the anchor to adjust difficulty.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about chest height and face the anchor.
2. Grasp the handles with palms facing down and walk your feet forward so you lean back with arms extended.
3. Keep your body straight from head to heels and brace your core.
4. Keeping your arms straight, raise the handles overhead until your body forms a straight line.
5. Lower the handles back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep constant tension on the straps throughout.
2. Brace your core and avoid letting your hips sag.
3. Move your feet farther forward to increase difficulty.
4. Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to an overhead position and grasp them with palms facing forward.
2. Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the floor.
3. Brace your core and lift your knees toward your chest.
4. Continue by curling your hips up to raise your knees higher.
5. Lower your legs and hips back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Curl your pelvis up rather than only lifting the legs to target the abs.
2. Move slowly to prevent swinging.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep a firm grip and steady shoulders throughout.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to an overhead position and grasp them with palms facing forward.
2. Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the floor.
3. Brace your core and raise your straight legs toward the ceiling.
4. Continue lifting your hips until your body forms a V-shape, keeping your legs straight.
5. Lower your legs back to the start under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your legs straight and curl your hips up to load the abs.
2. Move slowly to prevent swinging.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep a firm grip and steady shoulders throughout.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and stand facing the anchor with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold the handles with a neutral grip and lean back with arms extended, body straight from head to heels.
3. Pull the handles toward your face, driving your elbows high and out to shoulder level.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Extend your arms slowly to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced so your hips do not sag.
2. Lead with the elbows high to target the rear delts and mid back.
3. Do not shrug your shoulders toward your ears.
4. Adjust foot position to set the difficulty.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height and lie on your back beneath the anchor.
2. Place your heels in the handles with knees bent and arms by your sides.
3. Press your heels down and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Lower your hips slowly to the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
2. Drive through your glutes and hamstrings, not your lower back.
3. Keep your core braced to stabilize the straps.
4. Use a mat to cushion your back.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and sit beneath the anchor.
2. Hold the handles with an overhand grip and extend your legs, resting your feet on a bench.
3. Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to heels, arms extended.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower your body slowly to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
2. Lead with the back, retracting the shoulder blades before bending the elbows.
3. Keep your hips up so the body stays in a straight line.
4. Do not shrug your shoulders toward your ears.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and sit beneath the anchor.
2. Hold the handles with a neutral grip and extend your legs straight on the floor.
3. Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to heels, arms extended.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles while twisting your palms to face backward at the top.
5. Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then untwist and extend your arms to return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Exhale as you pull and twist, inhale as you lower.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades together to engage the upper back.
4. Keep your core braced to resist rotation.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and sit beneath the anchor.
2. Hold the handles with a neutral grip, knees bent and feet flat.
3. Lean back with arms extended and lift your feet, tucking your knees toward your chest.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
5. Extend your arms slowly to return to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso braced and stable while tucking the knees.
2. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you return.
3. Lead the pull with the back rather than the arms.
4. Keep the knee tuck controlled to engage the abs.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Lie on your back and place your heels in the handles with your legs extended.
2. Rest your arms on the floor at your sides for support.
3. Lift your hips off the floor and bend your knees, pulling your heels toward your glutes.
4. Slowly extend your legs back to the start with control, keeping your hips raised.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your hamstrings and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips high.
2. Keep your core braced so your lower back does not sag.
3. Exhale as you curl in, inhale as you extend out.
4. Move slowly to control the unstable straps.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height and place your feet in the handles.
2. Assume a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels.
4. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and core tight to control the unstable straps.
2. Position your shoulders directly over your hands.
3. Start slow and build speed as your coordination improves.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height and place your feet in the handles.
2. Assume a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width under your shoulders.
3. Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels.
4. Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips toward the ceiling into an inverted V.
5. Slowly lower your hips back to the plank position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your core rather than pulling with your arms.
2. Keep your legs straight and shoulders over your hands.
3. Start with a smaller range and increase as you get stronger.
4. Exhale as you lift your hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place your feet in the handles.
2. Position your hands on the floor at your sides, fingers pointing forward.
3. Press through your hands and lift your hips into a reverse plank, forming a straight line from head to heels.
4. Lower your hips toward the floor with control, stopping just before they touch.
5. Press through your hands and lift back to the reverse plank.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top to keep your hips high.
2. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag.
3. Move with a steady, controlled tempo.
4. Exhale as you lift your hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to an overhead position. Stand underneath and grasp them with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend and cross your legs for stability and hang with arms extended.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down, then drive your elbows down and back, lifting your chest toward the handles.
4. Pull until your chest is close to the handles.
5. Lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Initiate by depressing your shoulder blades before bending your elbows.
2. Keep your core tight to stop your body from swinging.
3. Start with fewer reps and build up as your strength improves.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and place your feet in them, hands under your shoulders in a push-up position.
2. Keep your body straight from head to heels and brace your core.
3. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, then press back up.
4. At the top, rotate your body to one side, stacking your feet and reaching the top arm to the ceiling in a side plank.
5. Return to the push-up position, then alternate the side plank to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a non-slip surface so your hands stay planted.
2. Move slowly through the rotation to keep your hips from dropping.
3. Exhale as you press up and during the rotation.
4. Keep your core braced throughout to protect your spine.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about chest height and stand facing the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold the handles with a neutral grip and lean back with your arms extended.
3. Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows out to the sides at shoulder height.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
5. Extend your arms back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.
2. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag.
3. Lead with your elbows wide to target the rear delts.
4. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and place your feet in them.
2. Get into a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body straight.
3. Brace your core and bend your knees, drawing them toward your chest while lifting your hips.
4. Continue until your hips are fully bent and your knees are close to your chest.
5. Extend your legs back to the plank position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you pull your knees in and inhale as you extend.
2. Start with a small range and increase it as you get stronger.
3. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
4. Move slowly to keep the straps from swinging.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles low and grasp them with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
2. Lean back with arms extended, body straight, and feet together.
3. Brace your core to hold a straight line from head to heels.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Extend your arms to lower back to the start with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move with a steady, controlled tempo.
2. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your wrists under your shoulders for alignment.
4. Drive with your back, not just your arms.

instructions:
1. Set one suspension handle to about chest height and stand facing the anchor.
2. Hold the handle with an overhand grip and lean back, arm extended, feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Pull your chest toward the handle by driving your elbow out to the side at shoulder height.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blade toward your spine until your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Extend your arm back to the start with control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the rear delt and upper back, not just the arm.
2. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
3. Exhale as you pull and inhale as you extend.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting toward the working side.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about chest height and stand facing away from the anchor.
2. Grip a handle in each hand, arms extended in front at shoulder height, and lean forward with a straight body from head to heels.
3. Brace your core and open your arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend, lowering your chest toward the handles.
4. Drive through your chest to bring your arms back together in front of you.
5. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating the torso.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Step your feet back to increase difficulty and forward to make it easier.
2. Keep a steady slight bend in the elbows throughout.
3. Exhale as you press the handles together, inhale as you open the arms.
4. Keep the core tight to stop the hips from sagging.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and place the top of one foot in a handle behind you.
2. Stand tall on the front leg with your torso upright and core braced.
3. Bend the front knee to lower until the front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
4. Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and the chest up.
5. Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
6. Finish all reps, switch legs, and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep most of your weight on the front leg, not the suspended foot.
2. Control the descent to manage the instability.
3. Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep your front shin near vertical to protect the knee.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and lie on your back with both heels in the handles, legs extended.
2. Place your arms by your sides for support and brace your core.
3. Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from shoulders to heels.
4. Bend your knees to pull your heels toward your glutes while keeping the hips high.
5. Slowly extend your legs back to the straight starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips lifted throughout so the hamstrings stay loaded.
2. Move with a slow, controlled tempo to manage the instability.
3. Exhale as you curl, inhale as you extend.
4. Squeeze your glutes to hold the bridge instead of arching your lower back.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about knee height and sit on the floor with both heels in the handles, legs extended.
2. Place your arms by your sides for support and brace your core.
3. Lift your hips off the floor while keeping your legs straight.
4. Pull your knees toward your chest, stopping just short of contact.
5. Slowly extend your legs back to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core braced to stop your lower back from arching.
2. Start with a smaller range and increase it as control improves.
3. Exhale as you tuck the knees in, inhale as you extend.
4. Move slowly to keep the suspended legs steady.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension handles to about waist height and stand facing the anchor.
2. Grip the handles with palms facing down and lean forward with a straight body from head to heels.
3. Bend your elbows to bring your hands toward your forehead, keeping the upper arms still.
4. Brace your core and press through your hands to extend the elbows fully.
5. Slowly bend your elbows to return to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Step your feet forward to make it harder and back to make it easier.
2. Keep the upper arms fixed so only the elbows move.
3. Exhale as you extend, inhale as you bend.
4. Keep the core tight to hold the body in a straight line.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about waist height and stand facing the anchor.
2. Grip the handles with palms facing down, hands wider than shoulder width.
3. Walk your feet forward and lean back with body straight, heels on the floor and arms extended.
4. Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows out and back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the elbows wide and back to load the rhomboids and rear delts.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
4. Lower your feet to increase difficulty or step them back to make it easier.

instructions:
1. Stand side-on to the net in a balanced ready stance with knees slightly bent.
2. Rotate your hips and trunk back to load the racket on your dominant side.
3. Step forward and drive from the back leg, uncoiling your hips and trunk toward the ball.
4. Swing the racket forward, contacting the ball in front of your body with the wrist firm.
5. Follow through across your body and recover to the ready stance.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Generate power from the ground up: legs, then hips, then trunk, then arm.
2. Keep your eyes on the ball through contact.
3. Brace your core to transfer rotation into the stroke.
4. Finish the follow-through fully rather than cutting the swing short.

instructions:
1. Stand on the treadmill side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
2. Start the belt at a low speed and step on carefully.
3. Increase the speed to a comfortable jogging pace with an upright posture and braced core.
4. Bend your arms to about 90 degrees and swing them naturally at your sides.
5. Land mid-foot with each stride and keep your breathing steady.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head up and gaze forward, not down at your feet.
2. Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce joint impact.
3. Set a pace that lets you hold good form for the full duration.
4. Drive your arms to help maintain rhythm.

instructions:
1. Stand on the treadmill side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
2. Start the belt at a low speed and step on carefully.
3. Increase the speed to a running pace with an upright posture and braced core.
4. Bend your arms to about 90 degrees and swing them naturally at your sides.
5. Land mid-foot with each stride and keep your breathing steady.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head up and gaze forward, not down at your feet.
2. Use a smooth, natural stride to reduce joint impact.
3. Set a pace that lets you hold good form for the full duration.
4. Drive your arms to help maintain rhythm.

instructions:
1. Stand on the treadmill side rails and attach the safety clip to your clothing.
2. Start the belt at a low speed and step on carefully.
3. Increase the speed to a comfortable walking pace with an upright posture.
4. Take natural strides, rolling from heel to toe with each step.
5. Swing your arms gently and keep your breathing relaxed.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your head up and shoulders relaxed.
2. Avoid holding the handrails so your core and posture stay engaged.
3. Add incline to increase glute, hamstring and calf demand.
4. Maintain a steady, comfortable pace throughout.

instructions:
1. Sit on the machine and adjust the seat so your upper arms rest on the pad with elbows bent about 90 degrees.
2. Grasp the handles with a neutral grip, keeping your elbows below the pivot point.
3. Straighten your elbows to push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Keep your upper arms pinned to the pad throughout.
5. Slowly bend your elbows to return to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you return.
2. Drive the movement with your triceps, not your shoulders or back.
3. Keep your upper arms still on the pad for a strict contraction.
4. Control the return rather than letting the weight drop.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to the high pulley of the crossover machine.
2. Grasp the rope with a neutral grip and step back, leaning slightly forward with elbows tucked to your sides.
3. Straighten your elbows to push the rope down, spreading the ends apart at the bottom.
4. Keep your upper arms still and squeeze your triceps at full extension.
5. Slowly let your elbows bend to return to the start. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pin your elbows to your sides so only your forearms move.
2. Exhale as you push down and inhale as you return.
3. Spread the rope apart at the bottom for a fuller contraction.
4. Lean slightly forward to keep tension on the triceps.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Step forward with one foot, rolling from heel to ball of the foot.
3. Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs.
4. Push off the rear foot and bring it through to take the next step.
5. Continue with a steady, natural stride. Repeat.
tips:
1. Swing your arms in opposition to your legs for balance.
2. Keep a steady, comfortable pace.
3. Wear supportive shoes to protect your feet and joints.
4. Stand tall and look ahead rather than down.

instructions:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Step forward briskly, rolling from heel to ball of the foot.
3. Drive your arms in opposition to your legs to add momentum.
4. Push off powerfully from the rear foot to keep the pace high.
5. Continue with a brisk, controlled stride. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a brisk pace that challenges you but stays controlled.
2. Pump your arms to drive your stride.
3. Keep your shoulders relaxed and your core engaged.
4. Wear supportive shoes to protect your joints.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with your legs raised straight toward the ceiling.
2. Place your arms by your sides with palms down for support.
3. Engage your core and push your feet upward, lifting your hips off the floor.
4. Keep your legs vertical throughout the movement.
5. Slowly lower your hips back down with control. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use a smaller range of motion at first and build up as you get stronger.
2. Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower.
3. Lift with your abs, not momentum or a leg swing.
4. Keep your legs as straight as possible to target the lower abs.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and together, arms extended overhead holding an ab roller.
2. Brace your core and lift your straight legs toward the ceiling.
3. At the same time, raise the ab roller toward your toes, curling your upper back off the floor.
4. Slowly lower your legs and the roller back down, stopping just before they touch the floor.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and under control rather than swinging your legs.
2. Keep your lower back from arching as you lower the legs.
3. Reduce the range of motion if you cannot keep your core braced.
4. Exhale as you lift toward your toes.

instructions:
1. Load one end of a barbell into a landmine and kneel on both knees facing it.
2. Hold the bar end at shoulder height with one hand, elbow tucked.
3. Brace your core and press the bar up and forward until the arm is extended.
4. Lower the bar back to your shoulder under control.
5. Repeat with the other arm, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips and torso square; do not let the load twist you.
2. Squeeze your glutes to stay tall through each press.
3. Drive the bar slightly forward, not straight up.
4. Exhale as you press.

instructions:
1. Load one end of a barbell into a landmine and kneel on both knees facing it.
2. Hold the bar end at shoulder height with both hands, elbows tucked.
3. Brace your core and press the bar up and forward until your arms are extended.
4. Lower the bar back to your shoulders under control.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
2. Squeeze your glutes to stay stable on your knees.
3. Press the bar along its natural arc, slightly forward.
4. Exhale as you press.

instructions:
1. Load one end of a barbell into a landmine and kneel on both knees facing it.
2. Hold the bar end with both hands, arms extended in front of your chest.
3. Brace your core and rotate the bar down and across toward one hip.
4. Control the bar back to center, then rotate to the other side.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your core, not your arms.
2. Keep your hips facing forward as the torso turns.
3. Move smoothly and avoid jerking at the end range.
4. Exhale as you twist.

instructions:
1. Load one end of a barbell into a landmine and hold the bar end at your chest.
2. Stand tall with feet together, facing the landmine.
3. Step out to one side and bend that knee, pushing your hips back while keeping the other leg straight.
4. Lower until your bent thigh is near parallel, keeping your chest up.
5. Drive through the bent leg to return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the foot of the working leg flat and toes forward.
2. Push your hips back rather than letting the knee cave in.
3. Keep your chest tall and core braced.
4. Feel a stretch in the inner thigh of the straight leg.

instructions:
1. Place an agility ladder flat on the floor and stand at one end with feet together.
2. Bend your knees slightly and stay on the balls of your feet.
3. Hop forward with both feet into the first square, landing softly.
4. Continue hopping square to square, keeping a quick rhythm.
5. Move back to the start and Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your knees soft and aligned over your toes.
3. Use your arms for balance and rhythm.
4. Brace your core to stay stable on each landing.

instructions:
1. Place an agility ladder flat on the floor and stand at one end.
2. Lift one foot and balance on the other leg.
3. Hop forward on the single leg into the first square, landing softly.
4. Continue hopping square to square on the same leg, keeping control.
5. Switch legs on the way back and Repeat.
tips:
1. Control each landing to protect the ankle and knee.
2. Keep the standing knee tracking over the toes.
3. Engage your hip and core to stop the pelvis from dropping.
4. Keep hops small and quick for better control.

instructions:
1. Place an agility ladder flat on the floor and stand at one end.
2. Stay on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
3. Skip forward, placing one foot in each square as you advance.
4. Drive the opposite knee up with each skip and pump your arms.
5. Keep a quick, light rhythm down the ladder, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay tall and light on the balls of your feet.
2. Drive the knee up to match each skip.
3. Coordinate opposite arm and leg for rhythm.
4. Keep contacts quick and quiet.

instructions:
1. Place an agility ladder flat on the floor and stand at one end.
2. Stay on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
3. Skip forward, placing both feet into each square before advancing.
4. Drive the knee up between skips and pump your arms.
5. Keep a quick, light rhythm down the ladder, then Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep both foot contacts quick and quiet inside the square.
2. Stay tall and on the balls of your feet.
3. Use your arms to keep rhythm and balance.
4. Brace your core to stay controlled at speed.

instructions:
1. Place an agility ladder flat on the floor and stand sideways at one end.
2. Lower into an athletic stance with knees bent and feet wide.
