3. Step laterally into the first square, switching your lead and trail feet.
4. Keep advancing sideways down the ladder, changing your base each square.
5. Repeat the drill leading with the other side.
tips:
1. Stay low in an athletic stance throughout.
2. Push off the outside foot to drive sideways.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways beside an agility ladder laid flat on the floor.
2. Step both feet into the first square one at a time (in, in).
3. Step both feet out to the side of the next square one at a time (out, out).
4. Continue the in-in-out-out pattern while moving laterally down the ladder.
5. Stay low, keep quick light ground contacts, and face the same direction.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay on the balls of your feet for fast, light contacts.
2. Keep knees bent and hips low to control lateral movement.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting as you shuffle sideways.
4. Keep your chest up and look ahead, not down at your feet.

instructions:
1. Stand facing an agility ladder laid flat on the floor.
2. Step both feet into the first square one at a time (in, in).
3. Step both feet out and forward straddling the next square (out, out).
4. Drive one knee up high with each step to add a knee lift.
5. Continue the pattern moving forward down the ladder with quick contacts.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the knee up to hip height with each lift.
2. Stay on the balls of your feet for quick ground contacts.
3. Keep your torso tall and core braced throughout.
4. Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand facing an agility ladder laid flat on the floor.
2. Step both feet into the first square one at a time (in, in).
3. Step both feet out and forward straddling the next square (out, out).
4. Continue the in-in-out-out pattern moving forward down the ladder.
5. Stay low and keep quick, light ground contacts.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay on the balls of your feet for fast, light steps.
2. Keep knees soft and hips low for control.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced through each square.
4. Pump your arms to keep rhythm and balance.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways beside an agility ladder laid flat on the floor.
2. Step both feet into the first square one at a time (in, in).
3. Step the lead foot out to the side of the next square (out).
4. Continue the in-in-out pattern while moving laterally down the ladder.
5. Stay low with quick light contacts and face the same direction.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay on the balls of your feet for fast lateral steps.
2. Keep knees bent and hips low to control side movement.
3. Brace your core to resist twisting as you shuffle.
4. Keep your chest up and eyes forward.

instructions:
1. Stand sideways beside an agility ladder laid flat on the floor.
2. Hop both feet into the first square, then hop in place a second time (double hop).
3. Hop both feet laterally into the next square and double hop again.
4. Continue hopping sideways down the ladder, one square at a time.
5. Land softly on the balls of your feet and stay low.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly through the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep knees bent to cushion each hop.
3. Drive off both feet evenly for balanced lateral hops.
4. Brace your core to stay controlled between squares.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine or a corner.
2. Stand to the side of the bar and grip the loaded end with the near hand.
3. Keep a slight bend in the elbow and brace your core.
4. Raise the bar out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
5. Lower the bar under control to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow, not the hand, to keep tension on the side delt.
2. Avoid shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo on the way down.
4. Keep the torso still and resist leaning toward the bar.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine and hold the loaded end at shoulder height.
2. Step back into a reverse lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor.
3. Drive through the front foot to return to standing.
4. As you rise, press the bar overhead until the arm is extended.
5. Lower the bar back to the shoulder and reset.
6. Repeat, alternating legs.
tips:
1. Brace the core to resist the diagonal pull of the bar.
2. Time the press to finish as you reach standing.
3. Keep the front shin vertical during the lunge.
4. Move smoothly rather than rushing the transition.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine.
2. Lie back on a bench or the floor facing the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands.
3. Start with the arms extended over the chest.
4. Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
5. Extend the elbows to press the bar back to the start.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arms still and let only the forearms move.
2. Lower the bar under control to stretch the long head of the triceps.
3. Keep the wrists firm and neutral.
4. Brace the core to keep the torso stable.

instructions:
1. Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine.
2. Stand facing the bar and hold the loaded end with both hands at chest height.
3. Extend the arms out in front and brace the core.
4. Rotate the bar down and across toward one hip.
5. Control the bar back up and across to the other hip.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from the trunk, not just the arms.
2. Pivot the feet slightly to protect the knees.
3. Move under control to resist the bar's momentum.
4. Keep the arms long and the elbows soft.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and place a foam roller horizontally under your upper back.
2. Cross your arms over your chest and lift your hips off the floor.
3. Push through your feet to roll the roller slowly up and down the upper back.
4. Pause on any tight spot for 20 to 30 seconds.
5. Lower your hips and reset.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay above the mid-back and do not roll over the lower spine.
2. Roll slowly and control the pressure with your feet.
3. Keep the core engaged to protect the neck and spine.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into each tender spot.

instructions:
1. Sit on the floor and place the foam roller under one calf.
2. Cross the other leg over for added pressure and lift your hips off the floor.
3. Slowly roll from just below the knee down to the ankle.
4. Pause on tender spots for a few seconds until tension eases.
5. Roll for about 60 seconds, then switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and keep the rolling controlled.
2. Rotate the leg slightly to reach the inner and outer calf.
3. Breathe steadily and relax into tender areas.
4. Keep pressure firm but tolerable, never sharp pain.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side with the foam roller under the outer thigh.
2. Support your upper body on your forearm and cross the top leg in front for balance.
3. Slowly roll from the hip down toward the knee.
4. Pause on tender spots until tension eases.
5. Roll for about 60 seconds, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the motion slow and controlled.
2. Stop short of the knee joint.
3. Rotate the thigh slightly to cover the full outer quad.
4. Use arm support to manage the pressure on tender spots.

instructions:
1. Lie face down with the foam roller under the front of both thighs.
2. Support your upper body on your forearms.
3. Slowly roll from the hips down toward the knees.
4. Pause on tender spots until tension eases.
5. Roll for about 60 seconds.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and keep the core engaged.
2. Stop short of the knee joint.
3. Roll one leg at a time for deeper pressure.
4. Breathe steadily and relax into tender areas.

instructions:
1. Grip the rings and press up to a support position with arms straight.
2. Keep the rings close to your body and shoulders down.
3. Bend your elbows and lower until your shoulders are below your elbows.
4. Lean the torso slightly forward to engage the chest.
5. Press back up to full elbow extension.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the rings tight against your sides to stay stable.
2. Turn the rings out at the top for shoulder control.
3. Lower under control to manage the unstable rings.
4. Keep the core braced to prevent swinging.

instructions:
1. Set one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand and hold the end of the bar at shoulder height with one hand.
3. Brace your core and keep your feet about shoulder-width apart.
4. Press the bar up and forward until the arm is extended.
5. Lower under control back to the shoulder.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Brace the core to resist twisting toward the loaded side.
2. Press in line with the bar's arc, slightly forward.
3. Keep the shoulder packed down, not shrugged.
4. Keep the ribs down to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand facing the bar with feet hip-width apart and hold the end with both hands.
3. Keep a slight knee bend and push the hips back, lowering the bar along your legs.
4. Stop when you feel a stretch in the hamstrings and your back stays flat.
5. Drive the hips forward to stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Hinge at the hips, do not squat down.
2. Keep the bar close to your legs throughout.
3. Maintain a flat back and neutral neck.
4. Brace your core before each rep.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand side-on to the bar and grip the end with both hands at hip level.
3. Rotate your torso and pivot the rear foot as you swing the bar across your body.
4. Drive through the legs and press the bar up and away to lockout.
5. Reverse the motion under control back to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Generate power from the hips and legs, not the arms.
2. Pivot the back foot to let the hips rotate freely.
3. Brace the core to control the rotation.
4. Move smoothly without jerking the weight.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Stand facing the bar and hold the end with both hands at chest height.
3. Keep the arms slightly bent and the core braced.
4. Rotate the torso to swing the bar in an arc to one side.
5. Control the bar back across to the opposite side.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Move from the trunk, keeping the arms fixed.
2. Let the hips and shoulders rotate together.
3. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
4. Brace the core to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Sit on a bench or the floor facing the bar.
3. Hold the end with one hand at shoulder height.
4. Press the bar up and away until the arm is extended.
5. Lower under control and repeat on the other arm.
6. Repeat, alternating arms.
tips:
1. Brace the obliques to stop the torso twisting toward the load.
2. Keep the shoulder down and away from the ear.
3. Press in a smooth diagonal line.
4. Control the lowering on each rep.

instructions:
1. Place one end of a barbell in a landmine anchor and load the free end.
2. Sit on a bench or the floor facing the bar.
3. Hold the end with both hands at shoulder height.
4. Press the bar up and away until the arms are extended.
5. Lower under control to the starting position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core braced to support the spine.
2. Press in a smooth diagonal line away from the body.
3. Keep the shoulders down, away from the ears.
4. Control the bar on the way down.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench facing the landmine, holding the bar end in one hand at shoulder height.
2. Set your feet flat and brace your core.
3. Press the bar up and slightly forward until your arm is extended.
4. Lower the bar under control back to your shoulder.
5. Complete all reps, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to stop your torso twisting toward the bar.
2. Press in a smooth diagonal arc that follows the landmine path.
3. Keep your wrist straight and stacked over the elbow.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the landmine, holding the bar end in one hand at shoulder height.
2. Set your feet shoulder-width apart and brace your core.
3. Dip slightly by bending your knees.
4. Drive through your legs and press the bar up and forward until your arm is extended.
5. Lower the bar under control to your shoulder, complete all reps, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the leg drive to start the press, then finish with the shoulder.
2. Keep your core braced to resist torso rotation.
3. Keep the dip short and vertical, not a full squat.
4. Exhale as you drive the bar up.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the landmine in a staggered stance, holding the bar end in one hand at shoulder height.
2. Place the opposite-side foot forward and brace your core.
3. Press the bar up and slightly forward until your arm is extended.
4. Lower the bar under control back to your shoulder.
5. Complete all reps, then switch stance and arm.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Use the staggered stance to stop yourself overarching as you press.
2. Keep your core tight to resist torso rotation toward the bar.
3. Press in a smooth diagonal arc following the landmine path.
4. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand facing the landmine, holding the bar end at your chest with both hands.
2. Set your feet shoulder-width apart and brace your core.
3. Squat down by bending your hips and knees until your thighs are parallel.
4. Stand up and press the bar up and forward until your arms are extended.
5. Lower the bar to your chest and return to the squat.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and heels down through the squat.
2. Link the stand and press into one smooth motion.
3. Keep your core braced throughout to protect your lower back.
4. Exhale as you stand and press.

instructions:
1. Place a resistance band around your legs just above the knees or ankles.
2. Set your feet shoulder-width apart and bend slightly into a half-squat.
3. Step one foot out to the side against the band tension.
4. Bring the trailing foot in, keeping tension on the band.
5. Take the set number of steps one way, then return the other way.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep tension on the band at all times, even between steps.
2. Keep your toes pointing forward and knees tracking over your feet.
3. Stay low in the half-squat throughout.
4. Move with control, leading from the hip, not the foot.

instructions:
1. Stand beside a sturdy box about 30 to 50 cm tall, feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your knees and hinge slightly at the hips to load your legs.
3. Swing your arms and push explosively off both feet, jumping sideways onto the box.
4. Land softly on top with knees bent and hips back to absorb the impact.
5. Step down to the start position and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the mid-foot with bent knees to cushion each landing.
2. Keep your chest up and core braced throughout the jump.
3. Step down rather than jumping down to protect your joints.
4. Use a box height you can clear with controlled form.

instructions:
1. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and stand in a staggered stance, opposite foot forward.
2. Hinge forward at the hips and rest your free hand on your front thigh for support.
3. Let the dumbbell hang toward the floor with a slight bend in the elbow.
4. Drive the elbow up and back past your ribs, rotating slightly as if starting a mower.
5. Lower the weight under control to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Pull with your back and elbow, not by jerking with the arm.
2. Keep your spine neutral and core braced through the hinge.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top of each rep.
4. Control the descent rather than dropping the weight.

instructions:
1. Lie on your side on a bench or the floor, holding a dumbbell in the top hand.
2. Rest the dumbbell across the front of your hip with a slight bend in the elbow.
3. Keep your body stacked and core engaged.
4. Raise the dumbbell out and up until your arm reaches shoulder height.
5. Lower it back down under control.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow and keep the wrist neutral.
2. Move slowly and avoid swinging the weight with momentum.
3. Stop at shoulder height to keep tension on the side delt.
4. Use a light weight; this position is harder than a standing raise.

instructions:
1. Set your forearms on the floor and walk them forward so your elbows are ahead of your shoulders.
2. Extend your legs back and rise onto your toes.
3. Tuck your pelvis under and brace your abs hard.
4. Form a straight line from head to heels and keep your glutes tight.
5. Hold the position while breathing steadily.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the pelvis tucked to maximize abdominal tension.
2. Do not let the hips sag or pike up.
3. Move the elbows only as far forward as you can hold with good form.
4. Breathe steadily instead of holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot.
2. Bend the other knee and grasp that ankle or foot behind you.
3. Press the lifted foot into your hand and raise the thigh up and back.
4. Reach the opposite arm forward as your chest lifts.
5. Hold the balance while breathing steadily.
6. Release and repeat on the other side.
tips:
1. Fix your gaze on a still point to hold your balance.
2. Press the foot into the hand to open the chest and hips.
3. Keep the standing leg slightly soft, not locked.
4. Engage your core to stay tall and stable.

instructions:
1. Stand to one side of a low box in an athletic stance, knees soft.
2. Step the lead foot onto the box, then quickly bring the trailing foot up.
3. Step down on the far side and keep moving laterally as fast as you can.
4. Reverse direction and run back across the box.
5. Stay low and keep your feet light and quick.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and weight on the balls of your feet.
2. Drive off the outside leg to change direction sharply.
3. Pump your arms to help maintain rhythm and speed.
4. Keep knees bent to absorb impact and protect joints.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a low box in an athletic stance, knees soft.
2. Tap one foot lightly on top of the box, then quickly switch to the other foot.
3. Alternate feet as fast as possible, staying on the balls of your feet.
4. Keep your torso upright and core braced.
5. Continue for the set duration or count.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stay light on your toes and minimise ground contact time.
2. Keep knees bent and hips low throughout.
3. Drive your arms to match the leg cadence.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced and centred.

instructions:
1. Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck hanging off the edge.
2. Hold a light weight plate against the back of your head with both hands.
3. Lower your chin toward your chest under control.
4. Extend your neck to raise the back of your head toward the ceiling.
5. Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and never jerk the neck.
2. Use a towel between the plate and your head for comfort.
3. Keep the range of motion controlled and pain-free.
4. Start with very light weight and progress gradually.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back on a bench with your head and neck hanging off the edge.
2. Hold a light weight plate against your forehead with both hands.
3. Lower your head back under control to extend the neck.
4. Curl your neck forward, bringing your chin toward your chest.
5. Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and keep the motion smooth.
2. Place a towel between the plate and your forehead for comfort.
3. Keep the range of motion controlled and pain-free.
4. Start with very light weight and build up gradually.

instructions:
1. Stand on the centre of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a handle in each hand with palms facing inward, arms at your sides.
3. Curl one hand toward your shoulder, keeping the elbow tucked.
4. Lower under control to the start.
5. Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and palms facing each other throughout.
2. Keep elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging.
3. Control the band on the way down to keep tension.
4. Squeeze at the top before lowering.

instructions:
1. Stand side-on to a wall about 60 cm away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball with both hands.
2. Rotate your torso away from the wall, bringing the ball across your body.
3. Forcefully rotate back toward the wall and slam the ball into it at hip-to-chest height.
4. Catch or pick up the rebound and reset to the start.
5. Complete the reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your hips and core, not just your arms.
2. Keep your spine tall and avoid rounding your back.
3. Brace your abs throughout to protect the lower back.
4. Exhale sharply as you slam the ball.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at chest height.
2. Lower into a squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
3. Drive up through your heels to stand.
4. As you rise, press the ball overhead until your arms are extended.
5. Lower the ball back to your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest up and core braced through the squat.
2. Press the ball overhead in one fluid motion with the leg drive.
3. Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
4. Breathe out as you stand and press.

instructions:
1. Kneel in a half-kneeling position with one knee up and one knee down.
2. Hold a medicine ball with both hands beside the hip of the down knee.
3. Rotate your torso and lift the ball diagonally across your body toward the side of the raised knee.
4. Control the ball back down to the starting hip.
5. Complete the reps, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the movement from your core, keeping your arms fairly straight.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square and stable in the kneeling position.
3. Exhale as you chop upward.
4. Move with control rather than swinging.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet together, holding a medicine ball at chest height.
2. Jump your feet out wide while pressing the ball overhead.
3. Jump your feet back together while lowering the ball to your chest.
4. Keep a steady, rhythmic pace.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly through the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep your core braced as you press overhead.
3. Coordinate the arm press with the leg movement.
4. Maintain a controlled rhythm rather than rushing.

instructions:
1. Stand close to a large tyre lying flat, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Squat down and grip the bottom edge of the tyre with both hands.
3. Drive through your legs and hips to lift the tyre to a standing position.
4. As it rises, drop one knee under and push the tyre forward to flip it over.
5. Step forward, reset your grip, and continue.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your legs and hips, keeping your back flat.
2. Keep your chest against the tyre as you drive up.
3. Explode through the hips to convert the lift into the flip.
4. Brace your core hard before each lift.

instructions:
1. Stand in front of a tyre with feet about shoulder-width apart.
2. Grip the sledgehammer with both hands, dominant hand near the head.
3. Swing the hammer overhead, sliding the dominant hand down the handle.
4. Drive through the hips and slam the head into the tyre.
5. Reset, alternate the lead hand each set, and Repeat.
tips:
1. Power the swing from your hips and core, not just the arms.
2. Keep your core braced to control the rotation.
3. Maintain a firm grip throughout to absorb the impact.
4. Bend the knees slightly to protect the lower back.

instructions:
1. Load the sled and grip the high posts with arms extended.
2. Lean forward with a flat back and brace your core.
3. Drive through the balls of your feet to push the sled.
4. Take powerful, driving steps to move it forward.
5. Cover the set distance and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms straight and let your legs do the work.
2. Maintain a strong forward lean for better drive.
3. Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
4. Push through the whole foot for steady propulsion.

instructions:
1. Attach a harness or strap from the sled to your body.
2. Drop into a bear-crawl position on hands and feet.
3. Keep your hips low and your back flat.
4. Crawl forward, moving opposite hand and foot together.
5. Drag the sled the set distance and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and knees just off the ground.
2. Brace your core to resist sagging or twisting.
3. Take controlled steps rather than rushing.
4. Keep your shoulders stacked over your hands.

instructions:
1. Set two kettlebells on their sides on a sled or floor.
2. Place a hand on each bell with arms straight out.
3. Lean forward with a flat back and brace your core.
4. Drive through your legs to push the bells forward.
5. Move the set distance with driving steps and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your arms locked and let your legs power the push.
2. Maintain a low, forward body angle for drive.
3. Push evenly with both hands to keep a straight path.
4. Brace your midsection throughout.

instructions:
1. Attach a heavy bag or sled to a harness or hand strap.
2. Face away from the load with straps in hand or on shoulders.
3. Lean forward and brace your core.
4. Drive through your legs to drag the load forward.
5. Take strong steps for the set distance and Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight to protect the lower back.
2. Push through the whole foot on each step.
3. Maintain a steady forward lean against the load.
4. Keep a firm grip if dragging by straps.

instructions:
1. Sit in the horizontal leg press with your back against the pad.
2. Place the ball of one foot low on the platform, heel hanging off the edge.
3. Extend the leg with a slight knee bend and remove the safety stops.
4. Lower the heel to stretch the calf, then press through the ball of the foot to lift as high as possible.
5. Pause at the top, lower under control, and complete all reps before switching legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and pause at the top to maximise calf contraction.
2. Keep the knee angle fixed so the calf does the work, not the quad.
3. Use a full range, getting a deep stretch at the bottom.
4. Keep the foot steady to balance the single-leg load.

instructions:
1. Sit in the horizontal leg press with your back against the pad.
2. Place the balls of both feet low on the platform, heels hanging off the edge.
3. Extend the legs with a slight knee bend and remove the safety stops.
4. Lower the heels to stretch the calves, then press through the balls of the feet to lift as high as possible.
5. Pause at the top and lower under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and pause at the top to maximise calf contraction.
2. Keep the knee angle fixed so the calves do the work, not the quads.
3. Use a full range, getting a deep stretch at the bottom.
4. Keep weight even across both feet.

instructions:
1. Sit in the horizontal leg press with your back flat against the pad.
2. Place one foot in the centre of the platform about shoulder-width position.
3. Extend the leg to lift the weight and remove the safety stops.
4. Lower the platform by bending the knee until it reaches about 90 degrees.
5. Press through the foot to extend the leg without locking it out, then complete all reps before switching.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the foot flat and drive through the whole foot.
2. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
3. Keep your back and hips pressed into the pads.
4. Brace your core to resist twisting on the working side.

instructions:
1. Sit in the horizontal leg press with your back flat against the pad.
2. Place both feet shoulder-width apart in the centre of the platform.
3. Extend the legs to lift the weight and remove the safety stops.
4. Lower the platform by bending the knees until they reach about 90 degrees.
5. Press through the feet to extend the legs without locking them out.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your feet flat and drive through the whole foot.
2. Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
3. Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the pads.
4. Do not let the knees cave inward as you press.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope or strap to a kettlebell and hold the handles or attach to a belt.
2. Set a tall posture with feet hip-width apart and core braced.
3. Lean slightly forward and drive through the front foot to take a step.
4. Continue striding forward, dragging the kettlebell behind or alongside you.
5. Maintain steady tension and walk the set distance.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Take strong, deliberate strides and push hard through each foot.
2. Keep your core tight to protect the lower back.
3. Stay tall and resist twisting at the torso.
4. Use a rope long enough to keep the kettlebell clear of your heels.

instructions:
1. Attach a harness or hold a strap connected to a loaded sled at your side.
2. Stand sideways to the sled with feet about shoulder-width apart.
3. Brace your core and step the lead foot out to the side, away from the sled.
4. Follow with the trailing foot, dragging the sled laterally.
5. Continue stepping for the set distance, then face the other way and return.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest tall and hips level throughout.
2. Drive through the outside edge of the lead foot.
3. Keep the core braced to resist being pulled off balance.
4. Take controlled steps rather than rushing.

instructions:
1. Load the sled and grip the low handles.
2. Lean forward with arms extended and a flat back.
3. Brace your core and drive the sled forward with powerful leg strides.
4. Stay low and keep continuous tension through each step.
5. Push for the set distance.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a strong forward lean to engage the quads.
2. Drive through the balls of your feet for plantarflexion.
3. Keep arms fixed and the back flat, not rounded.
4. Maintain a steady, powerful stride rather than short choppy steps.

instructions:
1. Sit on the pec deck with your back flat against the pad.
2. Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
3. Place forearms on the pads or grip the handles with a slight elbow bend.
4. Squeeze your chest to bring the arms together in front of you.
5. Pause briefly, then return slowly to the stretched position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight constant bend in the elbows throughout.
2. Squeeze the chest at the point of contraction.
3. Control the return; do not let the weight pull your arms back fast.
4. Keep your back and head against the pad to isolate the chest.

instructions:
1. Load the sled and grip the handles or attach a harness.
2. Set a flat back with arms engaged and core braced.
3. Drive the sled forward with strong, continuous leg strides.
4. Extend the hips and knees fully with each push.
5. Cover the set distance maintaining steady power.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the core braced and back flat throughout.
2. Drive through the full foot and finish with the calves.
3. Maintain continuous tension; do not coast between steps.
4. Use a steady rhythm rather than rushing.

instructions:
1. Sit at the row machine with chest against the pad and feet planted.
2. Grip the handles with arms extended and a slight forward reach.
3. Brace your core and pull the handles toward your torso.
4. Drive the elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
5. Return slowly to the stretched start position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end of the pull.
3. Keep the torso upright; avoid swinging for momentum.
4. Control the return to keep tension on the back.

instructions:
1. Attach a single kettlebell to a low sled or drag harness.
2. Place both hands on the sled posts or grip the kettlebell handle low.
3. Lean forward with straight arms and a flat back, core braced.
4. Drive through the balls of your feet and push the sled forward in short powerful strides.
5. Keep moving for the set distance or time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and core tight so you do not feel it in the lower back.
2. Stay low and lean into the push for more quad and glute drive.
3. Take short, fast steps and push through the front of each foot.
4. Keep your arms straight to transfer force efficiently.

instructions:
1. Attach a rope to a loaded sled and sit or stand facing it.
2. Grip the rope with both hands and brace your core.
3. Pull the rope toward you hand over hand, driving your elbows back.
4. Engage your lats and squeeze your shoulder blades on each pull.
5. Continue until the sled reaches you or for the set time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead each pull with your elbows to load the lats, not just the arms.
2. Use a firm but relaxed grip so your forearms last longer.
3. Keep your core braced and back flat throughout.
4. Drive through your legs if standing to move heavier loads.

instructions:
1. Attach handles or a rope to a loaded sled and grip them.
2. Step back into a slight lunge with a flat back and braced core.
3. Drive through your legs to drag the sled while stepping backward.
4. At each step, row the handles to your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades.
5. Continue dragging and rowing for the set distance or time.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pull the handles to your ribs, leading with the elbows for back engagement.
2. Keep your chest up and back flat as you drag.
3. Drive through your heels on the lower-body portion.
4. Brace your core to stay stable against the load.

instructions:
1. Kneel on the floor and extend one leg straight forward, heel down.
2. Slide the front foot forward and the back leg straight behind you.
3. Lower your hips toward the floor as far as flexibility allows.
4. Keep your torso upright and place your hands on the floor or blocks for support.
5. Hold the position and breathe steadily for the set time.
6. Switch legs and repeat.
tips:
1. Warm up the hamstrings and hips before attempting the full split.
2. Use blocks under your hands to control depth and protect the hamstrings.
3. Keep your hips square and facing forward.
4. Ease out slowly and stop if you feel sharp pain in the groin or hamstring.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body straight.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Jump both feet forward toward your chest at the same time.
4. Jump your feet back to the plank position.
5. Continue jumping in and out at a steady pace.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag or pike.
2. Land softly on the balls of your feet to protect your knees.
3. Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
4. Breathe rhythmically and keep a controlled tempo.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet about hip-width apart and place your heels on a low wedge or plates 3 to 5 cm high.
2. Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands cupping the top head.
3. Brace your core and keep your torso upright as you bend your knees and lower into a deep squat.
4. Let your knees travel forward over your toes and descend until your thighs pass parallel.
5. Drive through the balls of your feet to extend your knees and return to standing.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your chest tall and the dumbbell close to your sternum throughout.
2. Let the knees track forward over the toes to load the quads.
3. Control the descent rather than dropping into the bottom.
4. Brace your abs to support the upright torso.

instructions:
1. Kneel on a soft mat with your torso upright and a partner pinning your ankles to the floor.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips and torso in a straight line.
3. Lower your chest toward the floor slowly, resisting with your hamstrings as your knees extend.
4. Catch yourself with your hands when you can no longer control the descent.
5. Push off lightly and pull with your hamstrings to return to the upright position.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lower as slowly as possible to maximise eccentric hamstring load.
2. Keep your hips extended so the line from knees to shoulders stays straight.
3. Use your hands only to catch the bottom, not to do the work.
4. Stop the set once you can no longer control the descent.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg about 30 cm in front of a sturdy box.
2. Dip into a quarter squat on the working leg and swing your arms back.
3. Drive explosively through that leg and jump up onto the box.
4. Land softly on both feet with knees bent to absorb the impact.
5. Step down carefully and reset on the same leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land on both feet with soft, bent knees to decelerate safely.
2. Use a strong arm swing to assist the single-leg drive.
3. Choose a box height you can clear with control.
4. Step down rather than jumping down to protect the joints.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg about 30 cm in front of a sturdy box.
2. Dip into a quarter squat on the working leg and swing your arms back.
3. Drive explosively through that leg and jump up onto the box.
4. Land softly on the same foot with the knee bent to absorb the impact.
5. Step down carefully and reset on the same leg.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly with a bent knee to absorb force.
2. Use a strong arm swing to assist the single-leg drive.
3. Choose a box height you can clear with control.
4. Step down rather than jumping down to protect the joints.

instructions:
1. Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock the position.
3. Lift one arm off the floor and extend it forward without rotating your hips.
4. Hold the position while resisting any twist of the torso.
5. Return the arm and switch sides for an equal hold.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep hips and shoulders square to resist rotation.
2. Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes the whole time.
3. Widen your feet for more stability if the hold is too hard.
4. Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and arms at your sides.
2. Bend the knee and hip to lower into a quarter squat, swinging your arms back.
3. Drive the arms up and explosively extend the leg to jump straight up.
4. Land softly on the same leg, absorbing the impact with a bent knee.
5. Reset your balance, then complete the set and switch legs.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly on the ball of the foot, rolling to the heel to absorb force.
2. Keep the knee tracking over the toes, not caving inward.
3. Use your arm swing to add height and control.
4. Brace your core to stay balanced through each jump.

instructions:
1. Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
3. Lift one arm off the floor and reach it forward or tuck it to your side.
4. Resist any rotation, keeping your hips and shoulders square to the floor.
5. Hold for the set time, then switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and square; do not let them twist toward the lifted side.
2. Widen your feet for a more stable base if needed.
3. Brace as if bracing for a punch to resist rotation.
4. Keep your neck neutral, gaze just ahead of your hands.

instructions:
1. Set up in a push-up position with feet wide for balance and one hand on the floor under your chest.
2. Place the free arm behind your back or along your side.
3. Brace your core and resist rotation, keeping hips square.
4. Bend the working elbow to lower your chest toward the floor.
5. Press through the hand to push back up to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch arms.
tips:
1. Spread your feet wide to create a stable base and reduce twisting.
2. Keep your hips and shoulders square; resist rotating toward the working arm.
3. Keep the working elbow tucked at roughly 45 degrees from the body.
4. Brace the core hard throughout to control the descent.

instructions:
1. Stand holding a medicine ball overhead with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Slam the ball hard to the floor, hinging through the hips and bending forward.
3. Place your hands down and jump or step your feet back into a plank.
4. Lower your chest, then push up and jump the feet back to your hands.
5. Pick up the ball and explosively jump up, pressing it overhead.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the slam with your lats and abs, not just your arms.
2. Keep your core braced when jumping back to protect your lower back.
3. Use a non-bouncing slam ball so it does not rebound into your face.
4. Land softly from each jump with bent knees.

instructions:
1. Lie on your back and raise your legs straight toward the ceiling.
2. Hold a medicine ball with both hands, arms extended overhead.
3. Brace your core and crunch your upper back off the floor.
4. Reach the ball up toward your toes at the top of the movement.
5. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your abs, not by swinging the ball with your arms.
2. Keep your legs as straight and still as possible.
3. Exhale as you crunch up and reach the ball to the toes.
4. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.

instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with a straight spine.
2. Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow and drop the hand behind your neck.
3. Bring your left arm behind your back and reach the hand up toward the right hand.
4. Hook the fingers together or hold a strap between them.
5. Hold the stretch and breathe steadily, keeping the chest open.
6. Release, switch arms and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the top elbow pointing up, not flaring out.
2. Do not force the hands together; use a strap if they do not meet.
3. Avoid arching the lower back to reach further.
4. Breathe slowly into the shoulder stretch.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and body in a line.
2. Lift your hips up and back into a pike, forming an inverted V.
3. Keep legs straight and core braced.
4. Jump both feet wide apart, then jump them back together.
5. Keep the hips high and the arms firm throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your weight evenly between hands and feet.
2. Land softly on the balls of your feet.
3. Hold the pike shape; do not let the hips drop.
4. Breathe out as you jump the feet wide.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours in a tabletop position.
2. Bring your right knee forward toward your right wrist.
3. Slide your left leg straight back and lower the hips toward the floor.
4. Keep the front shin angled and square the hips forward.
5. Hold upright or fold forward over the front leg and breathe steadily.
6. Release, switch sides and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and square to the front.
2. Support the front hip with a folded towel if needed.
3. Do not let the back leg roll outward.
4. Ease into the stretch; never force the depth.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
2. Lift your hips up and back into a pike, forming an inverted V.
3. Brace your core and keep the legs straight.
4. Reach your right hand back to tap your left hip.
5. Return the hand and tap the right hip with the left hand.
6. Repeat, alternating sides.
tips:
1. Keep the hips high and stable as you tap.
2. Resist twisting the torso when one hand lifts.
3. Spread the supporting hand wide for balance.
4. Move with control rather than speed.

instructions:
1. Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
2. Lift your hips up and back into a pike, forming an inverted V.
3. Brace your core and keep the legs straight.
4. Reach your right arm forward and overhead while balancing on the left hand.
5. Return the hand and reach the left arm forward.
6. Repeat, alternating arms.
tips:
1. Keep your hips high and square when one arm lifts.
2. Press firmly through the supporting hand.
3. Resist letting the torso rotate during the reach.
4. Move slowly to keep balance.

instructions:
1. Hold a plank on your forearms or hands with your body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Reach one arm overhead to form an I, then return.
4. Reach the arm out at a 45 degree angle to form a Y, then return.
5. Reach the arm straight out to the side to form a T, then bend the elbow into a W.
6. Switch arms and repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square to the floor and resist twisting as you lift each arm.
2. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back during each reach.
3. Move slowly and with control rather than swinging the arm.
4. Keep your neck long and gaze slightly ahead of your hands.

instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position, then walk your hands back and lift your hips into an inverted V.
2. Keep your legs as straight as possible and your head between your arms.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
4. Press back up to the pike position.
5. Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder while holding the pike, then switch.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Stack your shoulders over your hands to load the deltoids in the pike position.
2. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag during the shoulder taps.
3. Lower under control rather than dropping your head to the floor.
4. Keep your feet planted and resist rotating your torso during the taps.

instructions:
1. Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench with the other leg extended forward.
2. Hold your arms out in front for balance.
3. Bend the standing knee and sit back until your glutes touch the box.
4. Keep the free leg off the floor throughout.
5. Drive through the standing foot to stand back up.
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
tips:
1. Keep the heel of your standing foot flat on the floor.
2. Control the descent rather than dropping onto the box.
3. Keep your chest up and core braced to stay balanced.
4. Track your knee over your toes and avoid letting it cave inward.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank position on your hands or forearms with your body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and set your feet about hip-width apart.
3. Lift one arm and reach it straight out in front of you.
4. Hold briefly without letting your hips rotate.
5. Lower the arm and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips square to the floor and resist twisting toward the lifted arm.
2. Widen your feet for a more stable base if you wobble.
3. Squeeze your glutes and brace your core throughout.
4. Reach in a slow, controlled motion rather than swinging the arm.

instructions:
1. Start in a forearm plank with your body in a straight line.
2. Brace your core and keep your hips level.
3. Press one hand to the floor, then the other, to rise into a high plank.
4. Lower back down one forearm at a time to the starting position.
5. Alternate the leading arm each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips as still as possible and resist rocking side to side.
2. Set your feet wider for more stability.
3. Keep your core braced throughout the transition.
4. Move at a steady pace rather than rushing the up and down.

instructions:
1. Hold a weight plate in each hand and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back.
2. Let both plates rest on the floor at full stretch.
3. Row one plate up to your hip, squeezing the back.
4. Lower it back to a dead stop on the floor.
5. Repeat on the other side, alternating each rep.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Pause fully on the floor each rep to remove momentum.
2. Keep the spine neutral and core braced.
3. Pull with the elbow close to the body, not the arm.
4. Resist twisting the torso as you alternate sides.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and core braced.
2. Hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
3. Extend your arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
4. Rotate the plate like a steering wheel from one side to the other.
5. Keep the arms extended and shoulders stable throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep arms straight and at shoulder height the whole set.
2. Brace the abdomen and exhale through each rotation.
3. Move under control, do not let the plate swing.
4. Keep shoulders down and away from the ears.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a weight plate on the floor between your feet.
2. Hinge and squat down, gripping the sides of the plate.
3. Drive through the legs and pull the plate up to shoulder height.
4. Press the plate overhead until the arms are extended.
5. Lower the plate back to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive with the legs and hips to start the clean, not the arms.
2. Brace the core to protect the lower back.
3. Keep the plate close to the body as it rises.
4. Press straight up with the plate over the midline.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a medicine ball with both hands.
2. Drop into a quarter squat and rotate the ball down toward one hip.
3. Drive up through the legs while sweeping the ball diagonally across the body.
4. Finish with the ball high on the opposite side, pivoting the back foot.
5. Reverse the motion back down to the start.
6. Repeat, then switch sides.
tips:
1. Initiate the rotation from the hips and core, not the arms.
2. Keep the core braced and avoid arching the lower back.
3. Pivot the trailing foot to let the hips rotate freely.
4. Move with control rather than throwing the ball.

instructions:
1. Stand on a rebounder with feet together and knees soft.
2. Bounce and jump your feet out to about shoulder-width.
3. Land softly through the balls of the feet.
4. Bounce again and bring your feet back together.
5. Keep the core braced and bounces controlled.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly through the balls of the feet to absorb impact.
2. Keep the knees soft and tracking over the toes.
3. Brace the core to stay balanced on the unstable surface.
4. Keep bounces low and rhythmic rather than high.

instructions:
1. Stand in the centre of the rebounder with feet together and knees soft.
2. Jump and spread both feet out wide to the edges of the mat.
3. Jump again and bring your feet back together to the centre.
4. Keep a steady bouncing rhythm and stay light on the balls of your feet.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Land softly through the balls of your feet to absorb each bounce.
2. Keep your core braced to stay balanced on the unstable surface.
3. Maintain an even, controlled rhythm rather than jumping as high as possible.
4. Keep knees slightly bent throughout to protect the joints.
